low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 6.
; Checked: y = x + c (measured, %5 -> %7).
; Clean: the old x rail (%4, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t = y - c (%6), both freed.
; Kept: y (%5, measured: a measured rail stays allocated).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; cq_theta on the classical x0 mints alloc_i32(x0) and rotates it in place (rule 2). y = x + c is a mixed Q+C add: the
; classical c is a literal operand of the _hl template and the sum lands in a fresh rail (rule 4). The measurement of
; y is the sink. x is dead after the add and the add is a bijection in x for fixed c, so the old x rail is cleaned (rule 6):
; t = y - c recomputes it, copy_i32 zeroes x, t is uncomputed, both are freed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: t = y - c recomputes the old x (the update is a bijection in it)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %6, i32 %4)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t

; Clean: the old y rail (%6, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t = z - x (%8), both freed.

; each for the other fixed, so rule 6 cleans operand 0 of the IR add (y: t = z - x) and keeps x (its inverse would read

  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: t = z - x recomputes the old y (the update is a bijection in it)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 7, 6, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: n (measured: the carried rail n_K, %20 -> %40; rule 6 leaves it the only n rail).
; Clean: every x-chain trip rail (the compare flags, the products, sums, the next-x selects and every trip predicate
; a_0..a_{K-1}, the K-th body's included), popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the after-trip-K exit test (%26,
; uncomputed at once); the |1> seed (%8, freed directly); the OLD n of every trip (rule 6, in the body: n' = a ? n + 1 : n
; is a bijection in n for every a and the trip predicate does not read n, so the arm's garbage n + 1 is uncomputed first
; and t = a ? n' - 1 : n' is copied onto the old n, uncomputed and both freed; trip 0's old n is the |0> incoming %7).
; Kept: a_K (%27: the exit test x_K > k evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with the predicate of trip K; rule 14:
; a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, observable non-convergence; a loop that exits after exactly K trips
; reads 0); x (%6, the rotated user register, loop-carried through the selects: x * a + b is no bijection in x (a may be
; even) and the trip predicate reads x, so rule 6 does not apply and the x chain is reversed); n (%20, measured). x * a + b
; wraps, so LLVM knows no bound on the trip count and the cutoff is K.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Re-rolled (rule 14): -O1's pre-header guard x > k (%7) is the latch test %14 one trip earlier (SCEV: both test the
; carried x), so it is trip 0 of the loop. Iteration j of the rolled loop evaluates the test on the carried x, forms
; a_j = a_{j-1} & (x_j > k) from the |1> seed, and runs the body (x = x * a + b, n++) under a_j: the select merges
; advance each carried value only where a_j = 1. The loop is cut off after K bodies (K = 4; the literal 4 below is K).
; After the K-th body the exit test is evaluated once more on the final x and a_K = a_{K-1} & (x_K > k) is kept as the
; output rail; that test is uncomputed at once. Each trip pushes its handles on the runtime handle stack; after n is
; copied out, a reverse loop pops them and uncomputes every trip, every trip predicate included (the K-th body's
; predicate is not a_K). The |1> seed is freed directly (rule 7). RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31): a carried value
; whose trip update is a bijection and whose trip predicate does not read it (n here) is cleaned in the body of the same
; trip: the new rail is the only one that survives, it is not pushed, the reverse loop never sees it, and no copy-out is
; needed (the measurement reads n_K). A carried value the exit test reads (x) cannot be cleaned: x = k and x = k + 1 both
; leave `x -= 1 under x > k` at k, so that update is not injective (149, 54, 68).
; Basis check (a = 1, b = 0xFFFFFFFF, i.e. x = x - 1; k = 2): x0 = 6 tests 6, 5, 4, 3 > 2 (four bodies, n = 4) and the
; test after the K-th body reads 2 > 2 = 0, so a_K = 0 (exact-K exit); x0 = 7 tests 7, 6, 5, 4 and then 3 > 2 = 1, so
; a_K = 1 (the loop would run a fifth trip). In both cases trip K's own predicate a_{K-1} is 1 and is uncomputed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_dfl_env: z + f; fenv_narrow_mask: fetestexcept + (int)z; fenv_op_in_arm: fetestexcept + (int)y;
; fenv_quantum_mode: rc + (int)s (each measured, then combined classically).
; Clean: every intermediate rail (dropped flags states, saved masks, gated exception bits, the quantum mode handle and its
; validity flag, the arm values).
; Kept: the user register of each function (x or m) and the final flags rail of each function (an output, rule 23);
; fenv_op_in_arm's merged value rail y and fenv_quantum_mode's result rails are measured.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (fenv_dfl_env, fenv_narrow_mask, fenv_op_in_arm); Ry(th) on m (fenv_quantum_mode).
; Four fenv shapes beyond 80-82, same model (rule 23): the host part goes through the real calls, the quantum part is
; rails; the mode is classical until a quantum value is written into it; the flags rail is sticky and advanced out of
; place; the final flags rail is an output that stays. fenv_dfl_env: fesetenv(FE_DFL_ENV) sets mode 0 and EMPTIES the
; flags rail (the dropped rail is uncomputed in the mirror); feupdateenv(FE_DFL_ENV) restores the default and ORs the
; current flags in, and empty | current is current: no gate. fenv_narrow_mask: fegetexceptflag with mask m saves
; flags & m as the object's quantum part; fesetexceptflag reinstates (current & ~m) | (saved & m) as the new flags rail,
; the previous one dropped. fenv_op_in_arm: a constrained op inside a quantum arm raises only on the arm's branch: its
; exception bits enter the flags through select(pred, exc, 0); the op's value merges by the phi's select (rule 9).
; fenv_quantum_mode: fesetround with an arbitrary quantum argument: valid iff (m & ~0xC00) == 0, mode' = valid ? m : mode
; (a handle from here on), the return value valid ? 0 : 1 is quantum; the classical ops after it take the mode handle
; (_rmq). Mode constants are x86-64's: 0, 1024, 2048, 3072.
source_filename = "fenv_extras.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  %5 = call i32 @fegetround()    ; IR: round.dynamic: the classical entry mode, read once from the host
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm(i32 %4, double %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %5 = constrained.fmul(%4, %2, round.dynamic, strict)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl_rm_exc(i32 %4, double %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %5: its exception bits  [the flags rail]
  %8 = call i32 @fesetenv(ptr @_FE_DFL_ENV)    ; IR: %6 = fesetenv(FE_DFL_ENV)  (host call; mode = 0; the flags rail %e0 is DROPPED: the rail is empty again)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f64_hl_rm(i32 %6, double %2, i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = constrained.fadd(%5, %2, round.dynamic, strict)  [mode = classical 0]

name: 101_longjmp_quantum
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 18, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: r (measured): escaped ? -1 : inner(x, k) + 2.
; Clean: the arm value x*x + 1 + 2, the clone's result and escaped-flag rails (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every
; rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register x; the merged result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; A longjmp under a quantum predicate is a MULTI-FRAME PREDICATED EARLY RETURN (rule 24), 24/35's early return carried
; across the call boundary: the callee's clone computes the longjmp arm's predicate as an ESCAPED flag rail beside its
; normal result (the normal arm's pure ops run unguarded, as every arm's do) and returns { result, escaped } (the
; aggregate ABI of 64); at the setjmp site the two continuations are the phi over the diamond, merged by a select on the
; escaped flag: setjmp's second return IS the escaped branch. Nested frames generalise it: every intermediate clone
; between the longjmp and its setjmp returns its own result beside an escaped flag that is the OR of its callees' flags
; and its own longjmp arms, and its continuation after each call is predicated on not-escaped exactly as 35's early
; return predicates the rest of a body. The host _setjmp/longjmp calls are NOT executed: the control transfer is what is
; lowered, and jb is a classical slot never written (the IR carries it as the global @jb). setjmp's return value on the
; escaped path is longjmp's classical argument (1 here; a quantum argument would be a rail selected by the flag); here
; -O1 already folded icmp eq %5, 0 into the diamond, so the flag is the whole of it. Any classical effect inside the
; longjmp arm would be a tape entry (47); this arm has none.
source_filename = "longjmp_quantum.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@jb = internal global [37 x i32] zeroinitializer, align 16    ; IR: @jb  (classical jmp_buf; never written: setjmp/longjmp are not executed)

define i32 @longjmp_quantum(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q_inner_10(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = setjmp(@jb) (not executed); %8 = call @inner(%4, %2), clone (arg 0 quantum): { result, escaped }
  %6 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 0    ; IR: %8  [result rail of the normal continuation]
  %7 = extractvalue { i32, i32 } %5, 1    ; IR: %6 = icmp eq i32 %5, 0 is false iff the callee longjmp'd  [escaped flag rail]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 2)    ; IR: %9 = add nsw i32 %8, 2  (the normal continuation, unguarded)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %7, i32 -1, i32 %8)    ; IR: %11 = phi [%9, %7], [-1, %3]: escaped ? -1 : %9  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %6, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_inner_10_unc(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %8 and the escaped flag (adjoint of the call)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the escaped flag (|0>)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %9)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %12
}

define internal fastcc { i32, i32 } @__cq_q_inner_10(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: %3 = icmp sgt i32 %0, %1  [predicate of block %4: longjmp(@jb, 1) fires iff set; the host call is not executed]
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (block %5, unguarded)
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %7 = add nuw nsw i32 %6, 1
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [copy the result out]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: block %4 taken  [escaped flag rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %3, i32 %7)    ; IR: copy the escaped flag out
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  %8 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } poison, i32 %6, 0    ; IR: ret i32 %7: the result handle
  %9 = insertvalue { i32, i32 } %8, i32 %7, 1    ; IR: the escaped-flag handle (setjmp's second return)
  ret { i32, i32 } %9    ; IR: ret i32 %7
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_inner_10_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %2, i32 %3)    ; IR: recompute %3
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %2, i32 %2)    ; IR: recompute %6
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: recompute %7
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %0)    ; IR: ret i32 %7  [xor the result out of %out]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %5, i32 %1)    ; IR: xor the escaped flag out of %oesc
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %6, i32 %2, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %2, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  ret void
}

name: 102_effect_tape
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16 (signal table, effect entries), 19 (address rail dispatch, table clones), 20, 24 (unobservable
; volatile), 2, 5, 7, 8, 14; §1.3 (bundle), §1.4 (table clone, activation counter).
; Checked: raise_handled: x (measured) and hit (the load copy of @hit after the join, measured); the cell __cq_sig[30]
; at exit = the address of h (HOST); the cell @hit at exit = (x > k ? 30 : 0), given hit = 0 at entry. raise_default:
; x (measured). remove_cond: x (measured).
; Expected: raise_handled(0, .5, 1): Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of the i32 rail x = 0, each bit 1 with probability
; s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209; P(x > 1) = (1 - s)(1 - (1 - s)^30) = 0.797654. On that branch the cell __cq_sig[30] holds
; the address of h, the one registered function of type void (i32), so its flag is 1, h's _ctl table clone stores 30
; into @hit, and the complement predicate is 0 (the effect entry raise is never performed): (x, hit) = (v, 30) for
; v > 1 and (v, 0) for v <= 1. raise_default(0, .5, 1): nothing is registered at __cq_sig[6] (the cell is 0), so h's
; flag is 0 on every branch and the complement predicate is x > 1: the effect entry raise(6) is performed by the
; backend on the shots where it reads 1 (P = 0.797654), and the default action of SIGABRT terminates there.
; remove_cond(0, .5, 1): the effect entry remove("/tmp/cq_x") is performed where x > 1 (P = 0.797654).
; Clean: raise_handled and raise_default: the dead result of signal (raise_handled only: the load copy of
; __cq_sig[30], un-copied before the store); the arm flag x > k; per candidate of the dispatch: the conjunction
; f & f_i and the |sig> argument seed (uncomputed and freed right after the twin: rule 5 sentence 3, the caller treats
; what it passed by its own rules, as 212), its flag f_i and the complement predicate p_{i+1}, pushed and uncomputed by
; the reverse loop. remove_cond: the predicate flag (x > k).
; Kept: the user register x of each function (rotated, measured); raise_handled: the load copy of hit (measured), by
; rule 5 sentence 3 the tape slot and the value seed (the i64 address of h) of the store into __cq_sig[30];
; raise_handled and raise_default: the load copy of the signal cell under the arm flag (the address rail of the
; dispatch), un-copied under the arm flag after the reverse loop, its last reader, and left allocated (the table clone
; call is a memory version change between, rule 5 sentence 1), per candidate the tape slot of the kept store h's
; _ctl table clone makes (one per candidate call, also under a control that reads 0); the function's tape (each
; function). h: the tape slot and the value seed of its store. __cq_q_h_1_t and __cq_q_h_1_t_ctl keep the tape slot of
; their store; its value and control rails are the caller's formals, which the caller treats by its own rules.
; At the cutoff (not reached here) __cq_q_h_1_t_ctl keeps one overflow predicate rail (rule 14).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each function.
; CLASSICAL EFFECTS UNDER A QUANTUM PREDICATE (rule 16). A host effect cannot happen "in superposition", and executing
; it on a classical reading of the predicate would be a measurement, so a call with no body under a quantum predicate is
; an EFFECT ENTRY on the function's tape: its fields (a classical argument a tape_write_<W>_lit, a pointer its address
; as an i64), then cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(pred, tape, name), name = @.cq.effect.<callee>. When the backend
; performs it is BACKEND_ABI §1.11; the host call itself is never executed by the lowered program. The flag is
; uncomputed after the entry like any flag.
; MEMORY (rules 20, 24). static volatile sig_atomic_t hit is an internal global whose every use is a load or a store
; through it: its volatile is unobservable (rule 24), the qualifier is dropped, and its accesses are bus accesses at
; its host address (rule 20): nothing is allocated, seeded or registered for it, and its initializer 0 is the host
; byte the overlay reads. The later read of hit is a bus load after the join, a rail, measured (rule 2).
; SIGNAL (rule 16, signal table). signal(SIGUSR1, h) has classical arguments and no predicate in scope: the host call
; as it stands, then the bus load of the cell &__cq_sig[30] (its result, unused: un-copied before the store) and a
; kept store of h's address there (an i64 seed at a classical address). Everything is classical-valued, so the store
; writes the host array and the cell stays HOST (§1.3).
; RAISE (rules 16, 19). No handler is tracked at compile time: raise(sig) under the arm flag loads the cell
; &__cq_sig[sig] by the _hl_controlled form and calls through that address rail, a call of function type void (i32)
; with sig as its one actual. The candidates are the functions of that type in the clone table, read at run time
; (__cq_clone_count / __cq_clone_at; a classical loop); candidate i has the flag f_i = (rail == a_i), and its _ctl
; table clone (kind 1) is called under f & f_i with sig as a seed rail and K, its _ctl twin (kind 3) right after it.
; The complement branch is the effect entry raise with sig as its _lit field under p_n, where p_0 = f and
; p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i. raise_handled and raise_default are the same construction: SIGABRT is no longer the abort
; arm of 45 (whether a handler exists is a run-time fact; the default action is the backend's performance of the
; entry). remove(path) has no body: the effect entry remove with the path's address as its _lit field. The results of
; signal/raise/remove are unused: the bare effect form.
; H (rules 5, 19, §1.4). Its address is taken (passed to signal), so it has the four table clones, one row of the
; clone table registered by a module constructor, and an activation counter. hit = s is a store with no load: a kept
; store (rule 5 sentence 3) of the seed alloc_i32(s) in the own symbol, of the formal rail s in __cq_q_h_1_t, and the
; _hl_controlled store under the predicate in __cq_q_h_1_t_ctl. h writes memory, so rule 18 gives it no twin: the
; table twins pop nothing; the _ctl twin counts its activation like the clone.
; CALLER'S RAILS (rule 5 sentence 3). The callee keeps its store; the conjunction f & f_i and the |sig> seed are rails
; the caller minted and passed as the `_ctl` predicate and an argument, so the caller treats them by its own rules: the
; conjunction is uncomputed (and_i1 again: f and f_i are untouched by the call) and freed after the twin, and the seed,
; never written, is freed (a basis state, unentangled), as 212.
; SPEC GAP: rule 16's ordinary-host-call test makes every externally visible function "called after an event" when
; the module contains one; the signal-table bullet asks only for classical arguments and no predicate in scope and
; wins (212): the host call is made as it stands.
; SPEC GAP: rule 16 does not say what raise dispatches. As 212: a call of function type void (i32) with the signal
; number as its one actual (a seed, table clone ABI), the entry raise with the signal number as its one field.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no module-internal name. As in 205, 211 and 212: the activation counter @__cq_act_h, the cut test
; icmp ult d, K, the constructor @__cq_register at priority 65535, the sig string @.cq.sig, effect names
; @.cq.effect.<name>. §6 compares no name.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 gives the complement of the candidate flags no spelling; as 211 and 212 (not_i1 / and_i1 /
; not_i1 per candidate, p_i and f_i pushed and uncomputed by the reverse loop).
; SPEC GAP (corpus convention, §5): the clone-table rows of the externally visible raise_handled, raise_default and
; remove_cond (their _t, _t_ctl and twins) are omitted as in 197, 200, 204, 211 and 212; none has type void (i32).
; SPEC GAP: the table twins take K last, _unc(s, K) and _ctl_unc(pred, s, K), as 212 (BACKEND_ABI §3).
source_filename = "effect_tape.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@hit = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: @hit  (lives at its host address on the bus, rule 20; nothing seeded)
@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [10 x i8] c"/tmp/cq_x\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str
@__cq_sig = external global [65 x i64]    ; IR: the bundle's signal table (§1.3)
@.cq.effect.raise = private unnamed_addr constant [6 x i8] c"raise\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for raise
@.cq.effect.remove = private unnamed_addr constant [7 x i8] c"remove\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for remove
@.cq.sig = private unnamed_addr constant [11 x i8] c"void (i32)\00", align 1    ; IR: the function type of a signal handler, the key of the dispatch and of h's row
@__cq_act_h = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: h's live _ctl activations (§1.4: it has a table clone)
@llvm.global_ctors = appending global [1 x { i32, ptr, ptr }] [{ i32, ptr, ptr } { i32 65535, ptr @__cq_register, ptr null }]    ; IR: the module constructor that registers the clone-table rows

define i32 @raise_handled(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (§5: once, at function entry)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape (effects)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call ptr @signal(i32 noundef 30, ptr noundef nonnull @h)    ; IR: %5 = signal(30, @h): classical arguments, no predicate in scope: the host call as it stands (its host result is not read)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl(i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 30) to i64))    ; IR: %5 = signal(...): the bus load of the cell &__cq_sig[30], the call's result (the previous handler address)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 30) to i64))    ; IR: un-copy %5 (unused; before the store, the next memory version change)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 ptrtoint (ptr @h to i64))    ; IR: %5 = signal(...): the handler address as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 30) to i64), i32 %9)    ; IR: %5 = signal(...): the bus store of the handler address into &__cq_sig[30]  (kept store, rule 5)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp sgt i32 %4, %2  [arm flag f of block %7]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_controlled(i32 %10, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 30) to i64))    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the cell &__cq_sig[30] loaded under the arm flag  [the address rail of the call; un-copied after the reverse loop, not freed]
  %12 = call i32 @__cq_clone_count(ptr @.cq.sig)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): rule 19, the number n of registered functions of type void (i32)
  br label %13
13:
  %14 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %26, %17 ]    ; IR: candidate index i (classical loop over the clone table)
  %15 = phi i32 [ %10, %3 ], [ %25, %17 ]    ; IR: complement predicate p_i  (p_0 = the arm flag)
  %16 = icmp ult i32 %14, %12
  br i1 %16, label %17, label %27
17:
  %18 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %14)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): candidate address a_i
  %19 = ptrtoint ptr %18 to i64    ; IR: a_i as its run-time address
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl(i32 %11, i64 %19)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): f_i = (address rail == a_i)
  %21 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): fresh |0> for the conjunction
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %10, i32 %20, i32 %21)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): f & f_i, the predicate of candidate i
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 30)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the classical actual 30 as a seed (table clone ABI: every formal a handle)
  %23 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %18, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the _ctl table clone of a_i (kind 1)
  call void %23(i32 %21, i32 %22, i32 4)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the handler under f & f_i  [K]  (a memory version change)
  %24 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %18, i32 3)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the _ctl twin of a_i (kind 3)
  call void %24(i32 %21, i32 %22, i32 4)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the twin, called exactly once (no result: right after the call)  [K]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %22)    ; IR: release the seed (|30>, never written; minted here, so by rule 5 sentence 3 the caller treats it by its own rules after the twin, as 212)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %10, i32 %20, i32 %21)    ; IR: uncompute the conjunction (after its last controlled call; rule 5 sentence 3, as 212)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release the conjunction (|0>)
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): fresh |0> for p_{i+1}
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %20)    ; IR: X bracket: NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %15, i32 %20, i32 %25)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %20)    ; IR: X bracket closes
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)    ; IR: p_i for the reverse loop
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %20)    ; IR: f_i for the reverse loop
  %26 = add nuw nsw i32 %14, 1
  br label %13
27:
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i32_lit(i32 %5, i32 30)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): argument 0 of the effect entry, the signal number (classical): a _lit field
  call void @cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(i32 %15, i32 %5, ptr @.cq.effect.raise, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = raise(30): the complement branch (no registered function), the effect entry raise under p_n; bare form, %8 is unused
  br label %28
28:
  %29 = phi i32 [ %12, %27 ], [ %33, %32 ]    ; IR: candidates still to undo, from n down to 0
  %30 = phi i32 [ %15, %27 ], [ %35, %32 ]    ; IR: p_{j+1}, the predicate being undone
  %31 = icmp sgt i32 %29, 0
  br i1 %31, label %32, label %38
32:
  %33 = add nsw i32 %29, -1    ; IR: candidate index j
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: f_j
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: p_j
  %36 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %33)    ; IR: candidate address a_j again
  %37 = ptrtoint ptr %36 to i64    ; IR: a_j as its run-time address
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %34)    ; IR: X bracket: NOT f_j
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %35, i32 %34, i32 %30)    ; IR: uncompute p_{j+1} (after the effect entry, its last use)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %34)    ; IR: X bracket closes
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release p_{j+1} (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl_unc(i32 %34, i32 %11, i64 %37)    ; IR: uncompute f_j (the address rail still holds the loaded value)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release f_j (|0>)
  br label %28
38:
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_controlled_unc(i32 %11, i32 %10, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 30) to i64))    ; IR: un-copy the %8 = raise(30) cell load under the arm flag, after its last reader (the reverse loop); the table clone calls lie between, so it stays allocated (rule 5 sentence 1)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6 (after its last controlled gate; before x is measured)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%4)
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @hit to i64))    ; IR: %11 = load volatile i32, ptr @hit  [unobservable volatile, rule 24: a bus load after the join, a rail]
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %40)    ; IR: %12 = cq_measure_si32(%11)  [the load copy is the measured rail, rule 2]
  %42 = add nsw i32 %41, %39    ; IR: %13 = add nsw i32 %12, %10  (classical: two outcomes)
  ret i32 %42    ; IR: ret i32 %13
}

; the own symbol (the all-zero mask, §1.4): what host code reaches when the host delivers the signal
define internal void @h(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: store volatile i32 %0, ptr @hit: the classical value as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %2, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @hit to i64), i32 %3)    ; IR: store volatile i32 %0, ptr @hit  [unobservable volatile, rule 24: a bus store, kept, rule 5]
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
}

; the table clone (§1.4): every formal a handle, then K; no result, nothing minted, nothing pushed
define internal void @__cq_q_h_1_t(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @hit to i64), i32 %0)    ; IR: store volatile i32 %0, ptr @hit  [s is a rail: the store's value rail; kept store, rule 5]
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
}

; the table clone's twin: h writes memory, so rule 18 gives it no twin; nothing was pushed, nothing to pop
define internal void @__cq_q_h_1_t_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  ret void
}

; the _ctl table clone: the predicate first, every bus access under it
define internal void @__cq_q_h_1_t_ctl(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M
  %5 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: the activation's depth d (§1.4), read on entry
  %6 = add nsw i32 %5, 1
  store i32 %6, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: one more live _ctl activation
  %7 = icmp ult i32 %5, %2    ; IR: rule 14: the body runs while d is below K
  br i1 %7, label %8, label %9
8:
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_controlled(i32 %0, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @hit to i64), i32 %1)    ; IR: store volatile i32 %0, ptr @hit under the predicate  [kept store: tape slot, value rail and control rail stay, rule 5]
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: the activation ends (the counter is d again)
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
9:
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: rule 14, the cut at d = K: fresh |0>
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %0, i32 %10)    ; IR: rule 14: the predicate copied out, the kept overflow predicate (an output rail)
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: the activation ends
  ret void    ; IR: ret void (no result)
}

; the _ctl twin: no rule-18 twin and nothing pushed; it counts its activation like the clone (§1.4)
define internal void @__cq_q_h_1_t_ctl_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: the activation's depth d, read on entry
  %5 = add nsw i32 %4, 1
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: one more live _ctl activation
  store i32 %4, ptr @__cq_act_h, align 4    ; IR: the activation ends
  ret void
}

define i32 @raise_default(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (§5: once, at function entry)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = icmp sgt i32 %4, %2  [arm flag f of block %6]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_controlled(i32 %7, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 6) to i64))    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the cell &__cq_sig[6] loaded under the arm flag  [the address rail of the call; un-copied after the reverse loop, not freed]
  %9 = call i32 @__cq_clone_count(ptr @.cq.sig)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): rule 19, the number n of registered functions of type void (i32)
  br label %10
10:
  %11 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %23, %14 ]    ; IR: candidate index i (classical loop over the clone table)
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %3 ], [ %22, %14 ]    ; IR: complement predicate p_i  (p_0 = the arm flag)
  %13 = icmp ult i32 %11, %9
  br i1 %13, label %14, label %24
14:
  %15 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %11)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): candidate address a_i
  %16 = ptrtoint ptr %15 to i64    ; IR: a_i as its run-time address
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl(i32 %8, i64 %16)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): f_i = (address rail == a_i)
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): fresh |0> for the conjunction
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %7, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): f & f_i, the predicate of candidate i
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 6)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the classical actual 6 as a seed (table clone ABI)
  %20 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %15, i32 1)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the _ctl table clone of a_i (kind 1)
  call void %20(i32 %18, i32 %19, i32 4)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the candidate under f & f_i  [K]  (a memory version change)
  %21 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %15, i32 3)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the _ctl twin of a_i (kind 3)
  call void %21(i32 %18, i32 %19, i32 4)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the twin, called exactly once  [K]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release the seed (|6>, never written; rule 5 sentence 3, as 212)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %7, i32 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: uncompute the conjunction (after its last controlled call; rule 5 sentence 3, as 212)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the conjunction (|0>)
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): fresh |0> for p_{i+1}
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %17)    ; IR: X bracket: NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %17, i32 %22)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %17)    ; IR: X bracket closes
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)    ; IR: p_i for the reverse loop
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)    ; IR: f_i for the reverse loop
  %23 = add nuw nsw i32 %11, 1
  br label %10
24:
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i32_lit(i32 %5, i32 6)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): argument 0, the signal number (classical): a _lit field
  call void @cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(i32 %12, i32 %5, ptr @.cq.effect.raise, i32 1)    ; IR: %7 = raise(6): the complement branch, the effect entry raise under p_n (performed by the backend: SIGABRT's default action terminates); bare form, %7 is unused
  br label %25
25:
  %26 = phi i32 [ %9, %24 ], [ %30, %29 ]    ; IR: candidates still to undo, from n down to 0
  %27 = phi i32 [ %12, %24 ], [ %32, %29 ]    ; IR: p_{j+1}, the predicate being undone
  %28 = icmp sgt i32 %26, 0
  br i1 %28, label %29, label %35
29:
  %30 = add nsw i32 %26, -1    ; IR: candidate index j
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: f_j
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: p_j
  %33 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %30)    ; IR: candidate address a_j again
  %34 = ptrtoint ptr %33 to i64    ; IR: a_j as its run-time address
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %31)    ; IR: X bracket: NOT f_j
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %32, i32 %31, i32 %27)    ; IR: uncompute p_{j+1} (after the effect entry, its last use)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %31)    ; IR: X bracket closes
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %27)    ; IR: release p_{j+1} (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %8, i64 %34)    ; IR: uncompute f_j
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release f_j (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_controlled_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr getelementptr inbounds ([65 x i64], ptr @__cq_sig, i64 0, i64 6) to i64))    ; IR: un-copy the %7 = raise(6) cell load under the arm flag, after its last reader (the reverse loop); the table clone calls lie between, so it stays allocated (rule 5 sentence 1)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %5 (after its last controlled gate; before x is measured)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_si32(%4)
  ret i32 %36    ; IR: ret i32 %9
}

define i32 @remove_cond(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = icmp sgt i32 %4, %2  [predicate of block %6]
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i64_lit(i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @.str to i64))    ; IR: %7 = remove(@.str): argument 0, the path: a pointer is its address, classical: a _lit field (the string is not expanded into fields)
  call void @cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %4, ptr @.cq.effect.remove, i32 1)    ; IR: block %6: %7 = remove(@.str): the effect entry under the predicate, complete after its field; the host call is not executed; bare form, %7 is unused
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_si32(%4)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %9
}

; module constructor: one row per address-taken function (§1.3): fn, sig, _t, _t_ctl, _t_unc, _t_ctl_unc
define internal void @__cq_register() {
  call void @__cq_clone_register(ptr @h, ptr @.cq.sig, ptr @__cq_q_h_1_t, ptr @__cq_q_h_1_t_ctl, ptr @__cq_q_h_1_t_unc, ptr @__cq_q_h_1_t_ctl_unc)    ; IR: h's row (its address is passed to signal)
  ret void
}

name: 103_complex_float_vector
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 3 (lane moves emit no gate; an unread lane gets no gate), 18, 25, 26, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: crealf(q) + cimagf(q) (measured, the result rail %15 -> %16).
; Clean: z's real lane a + 0 (%7), its scaled copy (%8), w's real lane (%10) and the clone's copied-out result lane
; (%13, zeroed by the __cq_q_twicef_10_unc twin), all uncomputed in LIFO order and freed; the clone-internal fadd rail.
; Kept: a (%5, the rotated user register).
; Rotations: (Ry, a, th, 1).
; The x86-64 ABI passes
; and returns `float _Complex` as the fixed vector <2 x float>, so clang emits insertelement, extractelement,
; shufflevector and lane-wise vector fadd. A FIXED 2-LANE VECTOR IS A PAIR OF LANES exactly as the { f32, f32 }
; aggregate of 64: each lane is a rail or a classical value on its own, insertelement/extractelement/shufflevector move
; lanes (no gate: a classical permutation of handles and values), and a vector op is one scalar template per lane that
; is read: in twicef, -O1 computes `%2 = fadd %0, %0` and `%3 = fadd %0, %0` and the shufflevector <0, 3> reads lane 0
; of %2 and lane 1 of %3 only, so %3's quantum lane 0 is dead and gets no template (rule 3), its classical lane 1 is a
; plain fadd; a poison lane is read by nothing and gets no gate either; a bitcast <2 x float> to i64 would be the two
; lanes' bit views (18) shifted and or'ed. Here lane 1 (the imaginary part) stays classical throughout: the clone
; `__cq_q_twicef_10` takes the two lanes as (handle, float) with mask 10 and returns { i32, float } (the quantum lane
; copied out as 64, the classical lane as a plain value); its _unc twin takes the lane-0 handle first.
source_filename = "complex_float_vector.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define float @complex_float(float noundef %0, double noundef %1, float noundef %2, float noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f32(float %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [register a]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = fmul float %2, 0.000000e+00    ; IR: %6 = fmul float %2, 0.0  (classical)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl(i32 %5, float %6)    ; IR: %7 = fadd float %6, %5  (commutative, quantum operand first)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f32_hl(i32 %7, float %3)    ; IR: %8 = fmul float %7, %3
  %9 = fmul float %2, %3    ; IR: %9 = fmul float %2, %3  (classical)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = fadd float %7, %8  [lane 0 of w]
  %11 = fadd float %9, %2    ; IR: %11 = fadd float %9, %2  (classical: lane 1 of w)
  %12 = call fastcc { i32, float } @__cq_q_twicef_10(i32 %10, float %11)    ; IR: %12, %13 = insertelement (lane 0 = %10, lane 1 = %11: no gate); %14 = call @twicef(%13), clone (lane 0 quantum)
  %13 = extractvalue { i32, float } %12, 0    ; IR: %14 lane 0  (handle)
  %14 = extractvalue { i32, float } %12, 1    ; IR: %14 lane 1  (classical)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl(i32 %13, float %14)    ; IR: %15 = shufflevector %14, poison, <1, poison> (lane 0 = %14's lane 1: no gate); %16 = fadd <2 x float> %14, %15: lane 0 = %14[0] + %14[1]  [result rail]; lane 1 is poison (no gate)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_twicef_10_unc(i32 %13, i32 %10, float %11)    ; IR: uncompute %14's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %10, i32 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, float %3)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, float %6)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  %16 = call float @cqrt_measure_f32(i32 %15)    ; IR: %17 = extractelement %16, 0 (the lane-0 rail); %18 = cq_measure_f32(%17)
  ret float %16    ; IR: ret float %18
}

define internal fastcc { i32, float } @__cq_q_twicef_10(i32 %0, float %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = fadd <2 x float> %0, %0: lane 0 (the same rail in both slots)
  %4 = fadd float %1, %1    ; IR: %2: lane 1  (classical)
  %5 = fadd float %1, %1    ; IR: %3 = fadd <2 x float> %0, %0: lane 1 (classical); its lane 0 is read by nothing and gets no template (rule 3)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f32(float 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %4 = shufflevector %2, %3, <0, 3> (lane 0 = %2[0], lane 1 = %3[1]: no gate); ret  [result rail: lane 0]
  call void @cqrt_copy_f32(i32 %3, i32 %6)    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4  [copy lane 0 out]
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: uncompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %7 = insertvalue { i32, float } poison, i32 %6, 0    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4: lane 0, the result handle
  %8 = insertvalue { i32, float } %7, float %5, 1    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4: lane 1, classical
  ret { i32, float } %8    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_twicef_10_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, float %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_fadd_f32(i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: recompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_copy_f32(i32 %4, i32 %0)    ; IR: ret <2 x float> %4  [xor lane 0 out of %out]
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f32_unc(i32 %4, i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %2's lane 0
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  ret void
}

name: 104_fpclass
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fpclass_d: isnan(y) + 2*isinf(y) + 4*isfinite(y) + 8*isnormal(y) for y = x * c; fpclass_f: the
; fpclassify code of x (each measured).
; Clean: every intermediate rail (compares, fabs, zext, the constant selects, the or chain, the inner merges, y).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (fpclass_d, f64); Ry(th) on x (fpclass_f, f32).
; FLOATING-POINT CLASSIFICATION. clang 19 lowers the classification builtins to what suits each: isnan to `fcmp uno`,
; isinf/isfinite to `fcmp oeq/one |y|, inf` over llvm.fabs, isnormal to the intrinsic `llvm.is.fpclass(y, mask)`
; (mask 264 = 0x108: negative normal | positive normal), and __builtin_fpclassify to a chain of branches on compares
; that -O1 leaves as a diamond chain with a four-way phi. Each compare and fabs is its ordinary template (rule 4);
; `llvm.is.fpclass.<W>(y, mask)` is the template cq_template_is_fpclass_<W>_hl(h, mask) with the classical mask (an i1
; rail; the backend tests the bits of the representation against the ten-class mask); the selects on constants are
; select_i32_ll; the phi chain of fpclass_f is the nested select of 23 (condition tree, rule 9), every compare computed
; unguarded. On Darwin the `fpclassify()` macro calls the library's `__fpclassifyf` instead: that is a lifted clone
; (34), not shown.
source_filename = "fpclass.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %4, double %2)    ; IR: %5 = fmul double %4, %2
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_uno_f64_hl(i32 %5, double 0.000000e+00)    ; IR: %6 = fcmp uno double %5, 0.0  (isnan)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i1_to_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %7 = zext i1 %6 to i32

  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %9, i32 2, i32 0)    ; IR: %10 = select i1 %9, i32 2, i32 0
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_one_f64_hl(i32 %8, double 0x7FF0000000000000)    ; IR: %11 = fcmp one double %8, inf  (isfinite)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %11, i32 4, i32 0)    ; IR: %12 = select i1 %11, i32 4, i32 0
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_is_fpclass_f64_hl(i32 %5, i32 264)    ; IR: %13 = llvm.is.fpclass.f64(%5, 264)  (isnormal: mask = negative normal | positive normal)
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %13, i32 8, i32 0)    ; IR: %14 = select i1 %13, i32 8, i32 0
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i32(i32 %14, i32 %7)    ; IR: %15 = or disjoint i32 %14, %7

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 16, 7, 5, 4, 2.
; Checked: *q + *r (measured, %46 -> %47), q = align_down(&a[x & 7], 16), r = align_down(&a[x & 7] + 12 bytes, 16), with
; P = the block's run-time address (16-aligned, __cq_alloc) and c = x & 7: q = P + 16 * (c >> 2) and r = P + 16 *
; ((c + 3) >> 2), so *q + *r = 2v (c = 0), 2v + 4 (c = 1..3), 2v + 8 (c = 4), and for c = 5..7 r = P + 32, one past
; the end of a: *r reads the 4 host bytes there (the C program's own undefined behaviour; 0 per §2 when they are not
; readable host memory), so *q + *r = v + 4 + H with H that host word. Memory: the 8 cells of a hold v .. v + 7 at exit.
; Clean: the pointer-arithmetic rails (x & 7, its zext, the shl by 2; the address rail p; the masked address q; p + 12;
; the masked address r), and the two load copies *q and *r (rule 5 sentence 1: no memory version change follows them).
; Kept: the user register x; the result rail (measured). Rule 5: the 8 seeds v + j (%8, %12, %16, ..., %36, each the
; value rail of a kept store; classical-valued, no qubit) and the tape slots of the 8 i32 stores (backend rails).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: ptrmask_q(0, .5, 3): Ry(.5) on every qubit of x = 0 flips each bit with s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209, so
; P(c = 0) = 0.827384 (result 6), P(c = 1..3) = 0.111407 (result 10), P(c = 4) = 0.053945 (result 14), P(c = 5..7) =
; 0.007264 (result 7 + H, H the host word at P + 32).
; ONE BUS (rule 20): a's alloca has a getelementptr with a tainted index among its users, so it is BUS-RESIDENT: its
; block is __cq_alloc(32, 16) at the alloca's program point (rule 16), no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are
; dropped. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). The eight initializer stores are bus stores at classical
; addresses (the constant getelementptrs stay, spelled ptrtoint as their run-time i64): each stores the seed
; alloc_i32(v + j) (rule 7) and is KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3); every value, address and control is classical-valued, so
; they write the host bytes and the cells stay HOST (§1.3).
; POINTERS ARE INTEGERS (rule 21): p = a + (x & 7) is ONE 64-bit address rail: the index rail (-O1's zext to i64),
; shl_i64_hl by log2 of the element size 4, add_i64_hl of the classical base P (rule 20). llvm.ptrmask(p, -16) is
; rule 4's integer template and_i64_hl(p, -16) on the address rail (rule 21: ptrtoint/inttoptr are identities, so the
; mask acts on the address itself); %24 = p + 12 bytes is add_i64_hl(p, 12) (element size 1, no scale). Nothing is
; known about what p points into: no object, base, extent or provenance is carried, no cell index is rebuilt, no range
; is tested, and the `align 16` on the ptrmask results is never consulted. Each dereference is ONE qram_load_i32 at
; its address rail (rule 21), with no guard and no bounds check.
; UNCOMPUTE (rule 5): the add is the last consumer of both load copies and is measured; no memory version change follows,
; so each copy is un-copied right after the add (at the cells' values at the load) and freed; then each address rail,
; which outlives its load's _unc (rule 20), and the chain below it, in reverse.

name: 106_fork_join
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 20, 16, 18, 5, 7, 3, 4, 2, §1.4.
; Checked: s = a.out + b.out (the add rail, measured) = (x * x + 1) + (c * c + 1). The cells at exit: a.in = x,
; a.out = x * x + 1, b.in = c, b.out = c * c + 1 (bus cells of the two __cq_alloc blocks; not named outputs).
; Clean: per activation of worker (two: job a, job b): the load copy of j->in (un-copied right after the product's
; uncompute, before the activation's store, the next memory version change, rule 5 sentence 1) and the product rail
; j->in * j->in (uncomputed by its _unc after its consumer, the add). fork_join: the load copies of a.out and b.out,
; un-copied right after the add, before the measurement (nothing changes memory after the loads, rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: x (the rotated user register; also the value rail of the a.in store); the sum (measured); and by rule 5 the
; tape slots of the six bus stores (a.in, a.out, b.in, b.out in fork_join; j->out in each worker activation) with
; their value rails: the seeds alloc_i32(0) (a.out), alloc_i32(c) (b.in), alloc_i32(0) (b.out) and, per activation,
; the add rail j->in * j->in + 1 that worker stores into j->out.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; SINGLE-THREAD COLLAPSE (rule 24; Bennett.jl's stance, owner 2026-10-20): a reversible program is a function of its
; inputs, so a thread interleaving that could change the result has nothing to uncompute; data-race-free fork/join
; code gives the same result under every schedule, and the SEQUENTIAL schedule is taken. pthread_create(&t, attr, f,
; arg) is a direct call of the start routine f(arg) at the create site; no host thread is started, the host
; pthread_create is not executed and the pthread_t is never written. pthread_join is nothing (the start routine has
; already returned). Mutex lock/unlock are no-ops (rule 24).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 3). The job structs a and b are passed to a callee (the start routine), a user rule 20 (b) does
; not allow, so both are BUS-RESIDENT: __cq_alloc(8, 4) each at the alloca's program point, no alloca remains and
; their lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Every store into them is a kept bus store at a classical address (the
; gep has no tainted operand and stays), its classical value first a seed (rule 7); a.in's value is x's handle. Every
; load is a bus load and a rail (rule 3): job b's cells hold classical values, and its worker activation computes on
; rails all the same (over-taint, §0: a rail in a basis state costs no qubit). The pthread_t slots ta, tb and the mutex
; m are HOST-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)): once the create, join, lock and unlock calls are rule 24's direct call and
; no-ops, their users are lifetime markers, the mutex initializer's memset of the untainted byte 0 and its classical
; signature store; they stay the plain instructions with their lifetime markers (rule 22: a host-resident destination
; keeps the intrinsic).
; A POINTER IS ONE SCALAR (§1.4, rules 18, 21). worker(&a) and worker(&b) both pass a classical ptr (the address of a
; __cq_alloc block): mask digit 0, so both calls reach worker's OWN symbol with its C parameter list, lowered (its body
; makes bus accesses). Nothing about the pointee (which cells hold rails) crosses the call. worker stores into j->out,
; so it WRITES MEMORY: it has no twin (rule 18) and the store's tape slot and value rail stay (rule 5). The load copy
; of j->in is un-copied inside the activation, before that store. In fork_join the loads of a.out and b.out follow the
; last memory version change (the second worker call), so both copies are un-copied after the add.
; SPEC GAP (rule 24, join): rule 24 names pthread_create and mutexes, not pthread_join. Taken (proposed sentence):
; pthread_create is a direct call of the start routine that writes no pthread_t, and pthread_join is nothing (its retval
; out-parameter is not written). The classical loads of ta and tb that only feed the joins are dead and dropped (they
; would read a never-written host slot).
; SPEC GAP (rule 24 against rule 20 (b)): whether the users of an alloca are counted before or after rule 24 rewrites the
; pthread and mutex calls. Taken (proposed sentence): the pthread_t operand of pthread_create and pthread_join and the
; mutex operand of a lock, unlock or trylock are not users for rule 20 (b); the residency test is asked after these
; calls are rewritten. So ta, tb and m stay host-resident. Counting the calls would make all three bus-resident (the
; memset a rolled loop of 64 kept byte stores, the signature a kept i64 store); no gate on a rail of the program changes.
; SPEC GAP (rule 24 against rule 19, address-taken): worker's address is used only as pthread_create's start routine.
; Taken (proposed sentence): a function whose address is used only as the start routine of a pthread_create with a
; constant callee is not address-taken by that use, so worker has no clone-table row and no _t clone.
; OUT OF SCOPE: condition variables, barriers and busy-waits on another thread's progress need a scheduler and deadlock
; under the sequential schedule. Multi-QPU placement is a backend matter over the handle graph (gates on disjoint rails
; commute); the lowered IR does not change with the number of devices.

  %13 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 4    ; IR: %10 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %4, i64 4  (&a.out; nothing tainted: the gep stays)
  %14 = ptrtoint ptr %13 to i64    ; IR: %10 as its run-time address
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %10: the classical value as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store

  %16 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: the classical value as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store

  %17 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %7, i64 4    ; IR: %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 4  (&b.out; the gep stays)
  %18 = ptrtoint ptr %17 to i64    ; IR: %11 as its run-time address

  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i64 %18, i32 %19)    ; IR: store i32 0, ptr %11  (b.out = 0; kept store)
  call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 8, ptr nonnull %9)    ; IR: call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 8, ptr nonnull %6)  [kept: host-resident]
  call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 8, ptr nonnull %10)    ; IR: call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 8, ptr nonnull %7)  [kept: host-resident]
  call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 64, ptr nonnull %11)    ; IR: call void @llvm.lifetime.start.p0(i64 64, ptr nonnull %8)  [kept: host-resident]
  call void @llvm.memset.p0.i64(ptr noundef nonnull align 8 dereferenceable(64) %11, i8 0, i64 64, i1 false)    ; IR: memset %8  (host-resident destination: the intrinsic stays, rule 22)
  store i64 850045863, ptr %11, align 8    ; IR: store i64 850045863, ptr %8  (host-resident: the plain store, mutex signature)
  %20 = call ptr @worker(ptr noundef %5)    ; IR: %12 = pthread_create(%6, null, @worker, %4): the start routine called here (rule 24); &a is a classical ptr, mask 0: worker's own symbol; no host call
  %21 = call ptr @worker(ptr noundef %7)    ; IR: %13 = pthread_create(%7, null, @worker, %5): the same, for job b; no host call
  ; IR: %14 = load %6; %15 = pthread_join(%14, null); %16 = load %7; %17 = pthread_join(%16, null): nothing (the start routines already ran)
  ; IR: %18 = pthread_mutex_lock(%8): no-op (one thread)

; a[1] + w = 2 + w; x even: b[1] + w = 4 + w; the cells at exit: a = {1, 2}, b = {3, 4}, and u's 8 cells hold the
; address (x & 1 ? &a : &b) + 4.

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 6, 16, 18, 20, 21, 24; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem), §1.4 (own symbol).
; Checked: ctz_q: (unsigned)ctzll(x | 1 << 32) (measured, the trunc rail %6 -> %7); trap_q: x + 1 (measured, %6 -> %8);
; tls_q: tl * 2 (measured, the shl rail %11 -> %12), and the cell tl = x + 1 + c (read from the bus at exit at the
; thread-local's address).
; Clean: ctz_q: the or rail (%4) and the cttz rail (%5), uncomputed and freed; trap_q: the old x rail (%4, rule 6:
; dead after x + 1) and t = r - 1 (%7), both freed; tls_q: the old x rail (%5, rule 6: x + 1 is a bijection in x and x
; is dead after it; the image x + 1 is kept), t = (x + 1) - 1 (%7), and the load copy of tl (%10, un-copied after the
; shl, before the measurement: no memory version change follows the load); touch: the swapped-out old *p (%5, rule 6),
; the inverse t = y' - c (%7) and the rail the cell's |0> went to (%6).
; Kept: x in ctz_q (%3, 64 bits: a rotated user register whose result has no inverse); trap_q's result x + 1 (%6,
; measured) and its abort flag x > k (%5): a noreturn-arm predicate passed to cqrt_abort_i1 stays allocated and the
; backend measures it after the program's last own measurement; tls_q: by rule 5 the tape slot of the store
; `tl = x + 1` (no handle: it is in the backend and holds the displaced tl) and its value rail x + 1 (%6), and the shl
; rail (%11, measured). touch keeps nothing (the in-place form leaves no rail, tape slot or old value).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each of the three functions (an i64 Ry in ctz_q).
; The three intrinsics the CQ musl architecture headers produce when their asm is spelled as
; builtins (LIBC_COVERAGE.md): llvm.cttz (a_ctz_64 = bsf) is the unary template cq_template_cttz_<W> exactly as 56's ctlz,
; the is_zero_poison literal being a promise about the operand, not an operand; llvm.trap (a_crash = hlt) is a noreturn
; under a quantum predicate, 45's abort arm: the predicate rail goes to cqrt_abort_i1 and stays allocated, the backend
; measures it after the program's last own measurement; llvm.threadlocal.address (every __thread access) and
; llvm.thread.pointer (__get_tp = mov %fs:0) are classical host intrinsics kept as they are: ONE THREAD (rule 24), so a
; thread-local object is the one thread's object at its host address, and llvm.threadlocal.address IS that address, a
; classical ptr. The object lives on the bus through the overlay like any global (rule 20): nothing is allocated, seeded
; or registered for it. The Darwin x86-64 backend has no code generation for llvm.thread.pointer, so this host's trace
; cannot exercise it; its lowering is the same as threadlocal.address's (a classical call returning an address), only the
; latter is shown.
; tls_q. `tl = x + 1` is a bus store at the classical address of tl (ptrtoint of the intrinsic's result), a KEPT store
; (rule 5, sentence 3): its tape slot and its value rail x + 1 stay for the shot. Because the image x + 1 now lives, x is
; dead after the add and rule 6 cleans it right after the update (t = (x + 1) - 1, copy, uncompute t, free x).
; touch(&tl, c) passes a classical pointer and a classical int: the all-zero mask (§1.4, rules 18, 21: a pointer is one
; scalar, nothing about the pointee crosses the call), touch's OWN symbol, never inlined. The call is a memory version
; change (touch writes memory). The load of tl after it is a fresh bus-load copy (rule 3); the shl reads it, and the copy
; is un-copied right after the shl, before its measurement (rule 5 sentence 1; no memory version change follows).
; touch. `*p += c` is load, add, store on the same SSA pointer with nothing between: rule 5's IN-PLACE FORM with a rule-6
; bijection (the add of the classical c) as its one step, as 195's bump: swap-out into a fresh |0> rail, y' = y + c with
; the clean of the old rail, swap-in of y', free of the rail that now holds the cell's |0>. The same body serves host
; callers and all-classical calls (§1.3 overlay).
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins) per externally
; visible function. No conforming example of the corpus emits one for a function that is only externally visible; this
; module follows the corpus (197, 200, 204) and registers nothing for ctz_q, trap_q and tls_q.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no calling convention, linkage or attributes for a lowered own symbol; touch keeps -O1's internal
; fastcc (195, 200), and the memory facts of the original (nocapture, memory(argmem: readwrite)) are dropped: the
; lowered body calls the backend.

define i32 @ctz_q(i64 noundef %0, double noundef %1) {

  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i64_hl(i32 %3, i64 4294967296)    ; IR: %4 = or i64 %3, 4294967296
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_cttz_i64(i32 %4)    ; IR: %5 = llvm.cttz.i64(%4, true)  (trailing zeros; the literal is a poison promise, not an operand)
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_trunc_i64_to_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = trunc i64 %5 to i32  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_cttz_i64_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_or_i64_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 %3, i64 4294967296)    ; IR: uncompute %4
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %4 rail (|0>)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %7 = cq_measure_ui32(%6)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %7

define i32 @trap_q(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = icmp sgt i32 %4, %2  [predicate of the noreturn block %6]
  call void @cqrt_abort_i1(i32 %5)    ; IR: block %6: llvm.trap(); unreachable  (noreturn arm flag, kept allocated; measured by the backend at end of shot)
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %4, 1  (block %7, runs uncontrolled)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: t = r - 1 recomputes the old x (the update is a bijection in it)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %4)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the old x rail (|0> after the copy)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_si32(%8)
  ret i32 %8    ; IR: ret i32 %9
}

define i32 @tls_q(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus m (§5: once, at function entry)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: %5 = add nsw i32 %4, 1
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (x + 1) - 1 recomputes the old x (the add is a bijection in it; its image is kept by the store)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the old x rail (|0> after the copy)
  %8 = call align 4 ptr @llvm.threadlocal.address.p0(ptr align 4 @tl)    ; IR: %6 = llvm.threadlocal.address(@tl)  (classical host intrinsic: the one thread's address of tl, rule 24)
  %9 = ptrtoint ptr %8 to i64    ; IR: %6 as its run-time address (the _hl operand)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %4, i64 %9, i32 %6)    ; IR: store i32 %5, ptr %6: tl = x + 1  (kept store at a classical address: tape slot and value rail stay, no _unc)
  call fastcc void @touch(ptr %8, i32 %2)    ; IR: call fastcc void @touch(ptr %6, i32 %2): a classical pointer and a classical int, mask 00 = touch's own symbol (a memory version change)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %4, i64 %9)    ; IR: %7 = load i32, ptr %6: tl  (a fresh copy of the cell after touch's update)
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = shl nsw i32 %7, 1  [result rail]
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %4, i64 %9)    ; IR: un-copy %7 (its last reader %8 is done; no memory version change since the load, rule 5)

define internal fastcc void @touch(ptr %0, i32 %1) unnamed_addr {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus m (§5: once, at function entry)
  %4 = ptrtoint ptr %0 to i64    ; IR: the address p as the _hl operand (classical, run time)

  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: %3 = load i32, ptr %0: swap-out: the rail holds *p, the cell |0>
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %1)    ; IR: %4 = add nsw i32 %3, %1
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %1)    ; IR: rule 6: t = y' - c recomputes the old *p
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: the old rail ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 %1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the old *p rail (|0> after the copy)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 %4, i32 %6)    ; IR: store i32 %4, ptr %0: swap-in: the cell holds *p + c, the rail the cell's |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the rail (|0>): nothing remains of the update
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 18, 20, 16, 22, 14, 3, 7, 8, 9, 5, 6, 2, 21, §1.3, §1.4.
; Checked: smin_q: min(x, c) (measured, %5 -> %6); bswap_q: bswap(x) (measured, %4 -> %6); usub_sat_q: x > c ? x - c : 0
; (measured, %5 -> %6); va_copy_q: sum_twice(2, x, a) = 2 * (x + a) (measured: the clone's returned rule-6 image s + t,
; %10 -> %11 in the caller); vla_loop_q: acc = sum over i < m of x + i (measured: the carried rail, rule 6 left no other
; acc rail; the never-written |0> seed when m <= 0). The bus cells (the variadic block, ap, bp, the VLAs) are no named
; output.
; Clean: in bswap_q the old x rail (%3, rule 6: bswap is a bijection, its own inverse) and t = bswap(r) (%5), both
; freed. In __cq_q_sum_twice_00, per trip of each walk: the slot-address chain (the zext of gp_offset, reg_save_area +
; gp_offset, the select of the slot address), un-copied/uncomputed after the slot's load; the slot's load copy (IR %31 /
; %53, un-copied in the trip: no memory version change between the load and its _unc); the old s / t (rule 6 in the
; body, trip 0's the |0> seed) and its inverse; every carried gp_offset rail (IR %29 / %51) and every carried
; overflow_arg_area rail (IR %28 / %50, the last trip's included): popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop, trip 0's
; against the load copy; after the walks
; t (rule 6: operand 0 of s + t, cleaned from the sum) and its inverse; un-copied but left allocated (rule 5 sentence 1:
; each overtaken by trip 0's stores): the load copies of ap.gp_offset, ap.reg_save_area, ap.overflow_arg_area (IR %4,
; %7, %8), un-copied after the first walk's last undo, and of the same three bp fields (IR %10, %13, %14), un-copied
; after the second walk's. In vla_loop_q, per trip: x + i (IR %17,
; uncomputed after the call it was passed to), the load copy of v[0] (IR %18, un-copied in the trip), the old acc (rule 6
; in the body; trip 0's the |0> seed) and its inverse.
; Kept: x in the other four functions (%4 of smin_q, %4 of usub_sat_q, %5 of va_copy_q, %6 of vla_loop_q: rotated user
; registers whose results have no inverse in them); bswap_q's measured result %4. va_copy_q (rule 5): the tape slots of
; the two stores into the variadic block, the seed of a (the second store's value rail; x is the first's). In
; __cq_q_sum_twice_00 (rule 5 unless named): the four seeds 48, 176, the block address and 0 of va_start and their four
; tape slots; the 24 byte load copies of va_copy (the value rails of its 24 byte stores into bp) and their 24 tape
; slots (rule 22); per trip of each walk the flag
; gp_offset < 41 (control rail of both of its stores), gp_offset + 8 and overflow_arg_area + 8 (value rails) and the two
; tape slots; s (IR %32 of the last trip, rule 6: the operand of s + t that is not cleaned). The result s + t is returned
; (no twin: the clone writes memory, rule 18) and measured. vla_loop_q: per trip the tape slot of put's store (its value
; rail x + i is the caller's, uncomputed); the carried acc (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each of the five functions.
; The last intrinsics of the musl census
; (LIBC_COVERAGE.md), each the width/op variant of an existing family: llvm.smin is 56's smax/umin family
; (cq_template_smin_<W>[_hl]); llvm.bswap is a unary bit permutation like 56's ctlz (cq_template_bswap_<W>, no classical
; operand); llvm.usub.sat is 92's uadd.sat family (cq_template_usub_sat_<W>[_hl|_lh]).
; THE VARIADIC CALL (rule 16, §1.4). va_copy_q stores the two variadic actuals into ONE __cq_alloc(16, 16) block in the
; SysV overflow-area layout (8-byte slots, the promoted i32 at its slot's address): x's rail at block + 0 (a kept store,
; the value rail the user register), a's seed at block + 8 (a kept store with its seed). It calls the block form
; __cq_q_sum_twice_00(i32 poison, ptr block): the fixed formal n (dead, poison, digit 0), then the block address (digit
; 0); no handle and no per-signature clone. The clone keeps sum_twice's linkage and calling convention (internal, C).
; In the clone ap and bp are BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b): va_start and va_copy are users no host-resident case allows):
; __cq_alloc(24, 16) each, the lifetime markers dropped. va_start(ap) is the four kept bus stores {gp_offset = 48,
; fp_offset = 176, overflow_arg_area = block, reg_save_area = 0}; va_copy(bp, ap) of the bus-resident ap is rule 22's
; copy of its 24 bytes (a host loop of 24 byte loads at ap + j, each pushed, then 24 byte stores at bp + i popped, i = 23
; down to 0, all kept; SPEC GAP below); va_end is the -O1 code as it stands (the intrinsic, a no-op on x86-64).
; Every load of a va_list field is a bus load and its value a rail (rule 3: over-taint, a classical-valued rail costs no
; qubit), so each va_arg is quantum control: gp_offset < 41 is a flag (rule 8, always 0 here: gp_offset
; is 48 and every argument is read from the overflow area), the arms' address and offset arithmetic is hoisted and
; computed unguarded, the two field stores stay in their arms as _hl_controlled stores under f and NOT f (X bracket),
; and the three phis are select templates (rule 9): the slot address, the next gp_offset, the next overflow_arg_area.
; The slot is read by a bus load at that address rail. Each walk is a classically bounded loop (n = 2 propagated by
; -O1, the latch tests i == 0). Rule 6 cleans in the body (as 27, 204): s (or t), whose other operand is the slot's load
; copy. The overflow_arg_area's update f ? ovf : ovf + 8 is a bijection in ovf, but nothing reads its final rail after
; the walk, so rule 6 does not clean it per trip: its chain is garbage, undone by the reverse loop. gp_offset's update
; f ? gp + 8 : gp has a condition that reads gp: no rule-6 bijection. So each trip pushes its kept flag, gp + 8 and
; ovf + 8 and (trips i != 0) its old gp and old ovf, and the reverse loop after the walk pops them and uncomputes the
; two selects (trip 0's against the load copies). After both walks s + t is formed and rule 6 cleans operand 0, t;
; the sum is returned directly (an image is never copied out, rule 6). The second walk reads the same block through
; bp's copied overflow_arg_area, so x and a are loaded twice: sum = 2x + 2a.
; THE VLA (rules 16, 20). v is passed to put, a user no host-resident case allows, so the VLA is bus-resident: every trip
; allocates __cq_alloc(4 n, 16) at the alloca's program point; llvm.stacksave/stackrestore are dropped for it. put(v, x +
; i) is the clone __cq_q_put_01(ptr, i32): a classical pointer (digit 0, the ptr itself) and a value rail; put stores the
; rail at the classical address (a kept store), so put writes memory and has no twin. The caller uncomputes x + i after
; the call (a template result it passed, rule 5 sentence 3); trace_check reports that _unc and free as "a value rail
; freed": its docstring names this case legal by rule 5, read by hand. v[0] is a bus load (a rail); acc' = v[0] + acc
; is rule 6 in the body (as 204), the load copy is un-copied before the next trip's __cq_alloc, and the final acc is
; measured directly: no push, no reverse loop.
; SPEC GAP: rule 16 says va_copy is "the -O1 code as it stands", the llvm.va_copy intrinsic, a host copy of ap's 24
; bytes. That reads unspecified bytes wherever ap's cells are QUANTUM (a va_copy after a va_arg's controlled stores),
; and the compiler may never ask whether a cell is HOST (rule 20). Read here: va_copy of a bus-resident va_list is rule
; 22's copy of its 24 bytes from ap to bp (the intrinsic stays only when both are host-resident); va_end stays.

; and the reverse loop pops them (nothing is recomputed). The pushes of the old gp and the old ovf are made on trips
; i != 0 only (trip 0's are the load copies), under a classical branch on the trip index (i == 0, the same compare -O1
; uses as the latch test; no loop peeling); the last undo, against those load copies, follows the reverse loop, and the
; three field load copies are un-copied right after it.

; (%10), uncomputed in LIFO order and freed; bitint_s7: the i7 trunc of x (%5) and the clone's copied-out i7 result (%7,

; C23 _BitInt(N) reaches -O1 IR as the native iN types (i100, i7), with the ordinary opcodes and casts on them. RULE: the handle ABI is
; width-only, so a template exists for EVERY width N on demand: cq_template_<op>_i<N>[_hl|_lh], cq_template_zext_i<M>_to_i<N>,
; cq_template_trunc_i<N>_to_i<M>, cqrt_alloc_i<N>/cqrt_copy_i<N>; the runtime's width set is a generator parameter, not a

; Checked: (float)twice16(h) with h = (_Float16)(f * c + 1) (measured).

; arithmetic, the clone's result rail (zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register f; the result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on f.
; C23 _Float16 reaches -O1 IR as the native half type. On x86-64 clang promotes half arithmetic to float: every op is
; fpext half->float, the float op, fptrunc float->half; only an op inside a function whose ABI keeps half (the callee
; twice16) stays a half op (fadd half). half is one more FP width (rule 25): cq_template_fptrunc_f32_to_f16 /
; fpext_f16_to_f32 are width variants of 19's casts, fadd_f16 of 13's templates, cqrt_alloc_f16/copy_f16 of the handle

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)

name: 112_overflow_fshr_variants
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 6, 2.
; Checked: uadd_overflow_qc: overflow ? c : x + c; usub_overflow_qq: (x - y) + (unsigned long)overflow; rotr_qc:
; rotr(x, k); rotr_qq: rotr(x, k) with a quantum k (each measured).
; Clean: uadd_overflow_qc's wrapped sum and overflow flag; usub_overflow_qq's overflow flag, then by rule 6 its old x
; (operand 0 of the sub; t = d + y); rotr_qc's and rotr_qq's old x (rule 6: a rotate is a bijection in x for any amount;
; t = fshl(r, r, k)); each t uncomputed, all freed.
; Kept: uadd_overflow_qc's x (its select result has no inverse), usub_overflow_qq's y, rotr_qq's k (a rotate is no
; bijection in its amount); the measured result rails (the select, the wrapped difference and
; its zext'd flag, the two funnel shifts).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (uadd_overflow_qc, rotr_qc); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (usub_overflow_qq); Ry(tx) on x and
; Ry(tk) on k (rotr_qq).
; Width and op variants of 92 and 56, the three intrinsics the LLVM libc census (LIBC_COVERAGE.md) reported without an
; example. llvm.uadd.with.overflow and llvm.usub.with.overflow return { iN, i1 }: as in 92 the aggregate is TWO templates
; over the same operands (rule 4), the value is the plain wrapping opcode (add_i32_hl, sub_i64: that IS element 0) and
; the flag is cq_template_u<op>_overflow_<W>[_hl], an i1 rail with its own _unc; extractvalue picks the rail, zext i1 is
; the cast template. llvm.fshr is the three-operand funnel shift of 56 (fshl): a rotate is fshr(x, x, k), the same rail
; read in both value slots (56's same-operand rule), with the _qql form for a classical amount and the all-quantum form
; cq_template_fshr_i32 (three handles, as fma's unsuffixed form) when the amount is a register. Everything not measured
; is uncomputed in reverse order; a dead register whose kept result is a bijection in it is then cleaned by rule 6.
source_filename = "overflow_fshr_variants.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = uadd.with.overflow(%4, %2): element 0, the wrapped sum (%7)
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_uadd_overflow_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5: element 1, the overflow flag (%6)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %6, i32 %2, i32 %5)    ; IR: %8 = select i1 %6, i32 %2, i32 %7  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_uadd_overflow_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_ui32(%8)
  ret i32 %8    ; IR: ret i32 %9

  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_usub_overflow_i64(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %7: element 1, the overflow flag (%8)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i1_to_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = zext i1 %8 to i32  [measured]

; measured rails, q1 in bit 0 of the returned int.

; Bärtschi–Eidenbenz |D^4_2> written as plain C: CNOT = `t ^= c`, CRy = `if (c) cq_theta(&t, a)`, CCRy = `s = 2*a + b;
