; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (`bool q[n]` is a runtime-sized bus-resident alloca: one __cq_alloc(n, 16) block of n byte
; cells, every address classical), 16 (the allocation), 5 (every `q[m-1] ^= q[..]` and every controlled rotation of a
; cell is the in-place form: swap out, update or gate, swap in; every other store is kept, every load copy the form
; overtakes is un-copied after its last reader and left allocated), 6 (the update y' = y ^ x inside the form cleans the swapped-out rail: t = y' ^ x fresh, copy, _unc,
; free), 10 (CRy / CCRy are ry_i1_controlled on the swapped-out rail under the flag, the swaps _controlled), 2 (the
; rotated register is the cell; the measured cells are plain load copies), 14 (classical-bound loops: the m-loop and the
; l-loop stay rolled; every trip-local rail is cleaned or kept inside its trip, so nothing is pushed and there is no
; reverse loop), 21 (addresses are ptrtoint of the classical getelementptrs), 7, 8, 9, 3.
; Checked: the cells q[0..n-1] (the n measured cells: each trip of the measure loop takes a plain load copy of q[i] and
; measures it, IR %101; q[i] in bit i of the returned int, n <= 31).
; Clean: per m-trip, the two swap rails of q[m-1] (IR %36 -> %37, %52 -> %53), their rule-6 temporaries and the two
; rails the cell's |0> went to, and the swap rail of the CRy form on q[m-2] (IR %40 -> %48); per l-trip, the same for
; the two forms on q[m-1] (IR %65 -> %66, %88 -> %89) and the CCRy form on q[m-1-l] (IR %76 -> %84), and the CCRy flag
; chain (IR %68, %72, %73, %74); all uncomputed and freed inside the trip that minted them.
; Kept: the init loop's n seeds (alloc_i8 of `i >= n - k`, IR %19) as the value rails of the n kept stores `store i8 %19`
; and their n tape slots (rule 5); the n measured load copies (rule 2). Left allocated, un-copied (rule 5 sentence 1:
; overtaken, a memory version change lies between the load and its un-copy): per m-trip three load copies, the copy of
; q[m-2] the first xor reads (IR %34), the copy of q[m-1] that is the CRy flag (IR %37, read after the swap-in), the
; copy of q[m-2] the second xor reads (IR %51); per l-trip four: the copy of q[m-1-l] the first xor reads (IR %64), the
; copy of q[m-1] the select reads (IR %66, read after the swap-in), the i8 copy of q[m-l] (IR %71), the copy of q[m-1-l]
; the second xor reads (IR %87). Each is un-copied right after its last reader (the rule-6 _unc of t, the controlled
; swap-in, or the flag chain's _unc).
; Rotations: per trip m = n .. 2: (CRy, the cell q[m-2], 2*acos(sqrt(1/m)), q[m-1] ^ q[m-2]) (the copy of q[m-1] after
; its first xor); then per l = 2 .. min(k, m-1): (CCRy, the cell q[m-1-l], 2*acos(sqrt(l/m)), 2*(q[m-1] ^ q[m-1-l]) +
; q[m-l] == 3) (the flag over the copies of q[m-1] after the block's first xor and of q[m-l]). All angles are computed at
; run time from the classical trip counters m and l.
; Bärtschi–Eidenbenz |D^n_k> with n and k function inputs (113 is the fixed-size N = 4, K = 2 instance, whose classical
; prefix -O1 folded). `bool q[n]` is a VLA: -O1's `alloca i8, i64 %3` has tainted stores among its users, so it is

; remains); -O1's byte getelementptrs over it are classical and stay, and each address is its ptrtoint, the `_hl`
; operand of every access. The init loop stores the classical start value `i >= n - k` into each cell: a kept store
; of the seed alloc_i8 (rules 5, 7; its tape slot takes the zeroed byte). Nothing folds, so every gate appears. Both
; loops have classical bounds and stay rolled exactly as -O1 shaped them: the m-loop (header %28, latch %22) and the
; inner l-loop (header %60, do-while latch `l < kk` %92, entered unless kk < 2 %55).

; no memory version change between its load and its store: rule 5's in-place form at width i1 (Width casts: the loads
; carry !range [0, 2), so the step is xor_i1, SPEC GAP 1). The operand q[..] is a plain load at its own program point
; before the swap-out, overtaken by the form: un-copied after its last reader, not freed. Inside the form the xor into a fresh rail is a rule-6 bijection
; in the swapped-out rail, which is cleaned at once; the result is swapped in and the rail the cell's |0> went to is
; freed. A later reader of the new q[m-1] (the 2-qubit block's `if (q[m-1])`, the 3-qubit block's select) reads a plain
; load taken after the swap-in (rule 5, Readers). The 2-qubit block's arm (block %39: load q[m-2], cq_theta, store
; q[m-2]) is the in-place form on q[m-2] under the flag = that copy (rule 10): the swaps are _controlled, the Ry is

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 21, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 11, 12, 14, 15, 16; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc, qram_swap).
; Checked: m = sum_i cq_measure(x[i]) << i: each measured x[i] is the i1 load copy of cell x + i (IR %82/%83 -> %84).
; The cells of the block x on the bus at exit: the low bit of cell x + i holds the measured outcome of x[i] (its high 7
; bits 0), 0 <= i < n.
; Clean: per H trip, the swap rail of the in-place form (|0> after its swap-in, freed). Per cost trip: the load copies of
; eu[e] and ev[e] (IR %42, %47), their sext rails (%43, %48), the two address rails x + eu[e], x + ev[e] (%44, %49), the
; two i8 cell copies (%45, %50), the compare flag x[eu[e]] == x[ev[e]] (%51), the controlled load copy of gamma[l] (%53)
; and its fneg rail (%54), all uncomputed and freed in the same trip (rule 5 sentence 1: the cost loop has no memory
; version change). Per mixer trip: the reader copy of x[i] before the swap-out (%64/%65), the swap rail, the reader copy
; of the rotated x[i] after the swap-in (%70) and the angle rail 2 beta[l] (%69).
; Kept: the cells x[0..n-1] themselves (the registers live in memory: rotated in place, read through load copies); by
; rule 5 sentence 3 the n kept stores `store i8 0, ptr %23` of the H loop, each with its tape slot and its value seed
; alloc_i8(0) (rule 7; a classical basis state, 8 qubits, unentangled); by rule 5 sentence 1, the p*n load copies of beta[l] (IR %68: each is
; overtaken by its trip's in-place form, a memory version change, before its last reader, the fmul _unc: un-copied
; right after that _unc and left allocated, 64 qubits each); by rule 2, the n measured i1 load copies (IR %83).
; Rotations: (Ry, cell x[i], pi/2, 1) for i = 0..n-1; then per layer l = 0..p-1: for each edge e = 0..ne-1,
; (P, flag, val(A), NOT flag(x[eu[e]] == x[ev[e]])) with A = fneg of the f64 rail loaded from gamma[l] (rz_qangle_controlled
; on the X-bracketed flag); for each i = 0..n-1, (P, copy of x[i], pi/2, x[i]), (Ry, cell x[i], val(B), 1) with B = 2 *
; the f64 rail loaded from beta[l] (ry_i1_qangle on the swap rail), (P, copy of x[i], -pi/2, x[i]).
; QAOA MaxCut on a graph given at run time: the vertex count n, the edge count ne, the edge endpoint arrays eu/ev, the
; layer count p and the angle arrays gamma/beta are all parameters, so every loop is a ROLLED classical loop with a
; runtime bound (rule 14) and no size is fixed at compile time.
; ONE BUS (rules 16, 20, 21). `bool x[n]` is -O1's `alloca i8, i64 n`; it stores a tainted value (the rotated bit), which
; no user of rule 20 (b) allows, so it is BUS-RESIDENT: __cq_alloc(n, 16) at its program point, no alloca remains (rule
; 16: zeroed host memory at an address never reused; the size is classical, no K2). m = __cq_mem() is called once, at
; entry (§5). The cells are the registers: no handle is ever stored (§1.1). eu, ev, gamma and beta are pointer arguments,
; program memory like any other: every load of them is a bus load and a rail (rule 3; over-taint, a basis copy of HOST
; cells: a classical basis state of W qubits, unentangled). Hence the edge endpoints eu[e], ev[e] are i32 rails, -O1's sext is the sext template, and the
; `getelementptr i8, ptr %9, i64 %43` with a tainted index is rule 20's address arithmetic: add_i64_hl(sext, x) into a
; 64-bit address rail (size 1: no scale), and the cell loads at x[eu[e]], x[ev[e]] are qram_load_i8 at an address rail.
; The angles gamma[l] and beta[l] are f64 rails, so every phase and rotation that reads them is rule 15's single qangle
; primitive (rule 11: a value loaded from the bus is a quantum angle).
; Gate shapes:
;  (0) H layer `x[i] = 0; cq_theta(&x[i], pi/2)`: `store i8 0, ptr %23` is a KEPT store of the seed alloc_i8(0) (rules 5
;      sentence 3, 7); -O1 forwarded the stored 0 into the theta (`cq_theta_i1(false, ..)`), and the theta, `zext`, `store
;      i8 %25, ptr %23` is rule 5's in-place form at width i1 (Readers: y is the forwarded value, the interval runs from
;      the first store; Width casts): alloc_i1(0), qram_swap_i1_hl, Ry(pi/2) on the swap rail, qram_swap_i1_hl, free.
;  (1) cost phase `if (x[u] != x[v]) cq_phi(-gamma[l])`: -O1 compares the two cells with `icmp eq i8` of two `load i8` and
;      puts the phase in the ELSE arm. Each load is a bus load at its address rail (i8, the access type; no trunc); the flag

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 20, 21, 22; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, qram_swap).
; Checked: m, the three counting bits x[T-1-j] (the byte cells x + 2 - j of the bus block %2; the measure loop takes a
; plain load copy of each at width i1, %91, and measures it, %92), and y = a^x mod N (the copied-out rail %35 -> %82); the
; result is m | y << 8.
; Clean: per H trip the swap rail of the in-place form on x[j] (|0> after its swap-in); every mod-exp trip rail (the load
; copy of x[j] that is the trip's condition, the product, the remainder and the select of each trip, pushed and popped by
; the mirror loop right after the loop: the select, then the load copy un-copied, then the remainder and the product),
; the rail holding the classical seed y = 1 (%18, popped as %43, never written); in the QFT^-1 the Toffoli flags (one per
; (j, k) pair) with the two load copies each reads (x[T-1-k] plain, x[T-1-j] loaded under x[T-1-k] and un-copied under
; it), the load copy of x[T-1-j] that carries cq_phi(pi) (un-copied before the swap-out) and the swap rail of every
; in-place Ry.
; Kept: the memset value seed (alloc_i8(0), rule 7) and the tape slots of its three byte stores (rule 5 sentence 3,
; rule 22); the three load copies the measure loop measures (rule 2) and the measured y result rail. The cells are the
; registers: entangled with y as |x>|a^x mod N> until measured.
; Rotations: (Ry, cell x[j], pi/2, 1) for j = 0, 1, 2 (H on |0>); then for j = 0, 1, 2 over the logical qubit x[T-1-j]:
; (P, flag, -pi / 2^(j-k), x[T-1-k] & x[T-1-j]) for each k < j, (P, copy of x[T-1-j], pi, x[T-1-j]) (rz_i1 on the bare
; load copy), and (Ry, cell x[T-1-j], pi/2, 1). The mod-exp is a permutation (no rotation).
; Shor order finding for N = 15, a = 7, T = 3 counting qubits, end to end: the three parts are examples 58 (a bool
; array of registers), 62 (the controlled modular multiply in a classical loop) and 60 (the QFT^-1 loops), composed.
; FLAT MEMORY (rule 20). `bool x[T]` stores rails (the cq_theta results), so the alloca is BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)):
; __cq_alloc(3, 1) at its program point (rule 16: zeroed; the lifetime markers are dropped), and every access is a bus
; access at its run-time address (gep, then ptrtoint: classical, _hl). The initializer -O1 turned into a memset is rule
; 22's host loop of byte stores of ONE i8 seed, kept (emitted although the block is zero already: §0). The cells are the
; registers; no handle is ever stored (§1.1). H|0>: each `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext; store i8` on one
; SSA pointer is rule 5's in-place form through the Width-casts clause: alloc_i1(0), qram_swap_i1_hl, ry_i1 on the swap
; rail, qram_swap_i1_hl, free.
; Mod-exp: the condition `if (x[j])` is a plain bus load of x[j] at width i1 (SPEC GAP 1), a BARE RAIL that is its own
; flag (59); the arm's mul/urem are hoisted out of the arm into fresh rails and the phi is one select on that rail; y is
; loop-carried, seeded with a rail holding the classical 1; the classical recurrence ap = ap*ap % N runs beside it and is
; pushed for the mirror. The loop is MIRRORED RIGHT AFTER IT (62's placement): the final y is copied out and every
; trip's rails are uncomputed. The load copy of x[j] is a trip-local rail that rule 5 does not keep: its last reader is
; the select's _unc in the mirror, and the forward loop, the copy-out and the mirror make no memory version change (loads
; only), so it is pushed with the trip's rails and un-copied right after that _unc (rule 5 sentence 1; the reverse trip
; recomputes the classical address from its trip index). After the mirror only the three cells and the y result rail
; remain, entangled: |x>|a^x mod N>.
; QFT^-1: `if (x[T-1-k] && x[T-1-j]) cq_phi` is two nested branches (-O1 keeps the short-circuit): the load of x[T-1-k]
; is plain, the reload of x[T-1-j] sits in the arm of the x[T-1-k] flag and is the _controlled load under it (rule 5);
; the two are ONE Toffoli flag (rule 8), a kickback with the classical angle, un-Toffoli, free, then both copies are
; un-copied (60). `if (x[T-1-j]) cq_phi(pi)` reads y of the in-place Ry that follows (load %36, store %59 through %35):
; rule 5 Readers, a plain load taken before the swap-out; the phase is rz_i1 on that bare copy (a diagonal gate needs
; no flag), the copy is un-copied, then the in-place Ry(pi/2) (H = Ry(pi/2)·Z on a superposed qubit). The measure loop
; takes plain load copies of the cells and measures them; y is measured last. Every load copy before the measure loop is
; un-copied, so the state is the old slot-array lowering's: m uniform on {0, 2, 4, 6}, y in {1, 7, 4, 13} (analytic;
; the replayer of _tools/replay reads the retired slot model and was not re-run on this trace).
; SPEC GAP 1: every read of a _Bool cell here is the program's own `load i8; trunc nuw i8 to i1` with no in-place form
; around it (the mod-exp condition, the QFT^-1 flag loads, the measure loop). Rule 5's Width-casts clause fixes the width
; U only for a reader's plain load of a form. Chosen as 60, 117 and 205: one qram_load_i1_hl at the trunc's width (§1.3:
; the low bit of the cell), not a qram_load_i8 and a trunc template.

  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i1_hl(i32 %1, i64 %13, i32 %14)    ; IR: %5/%6: swap-out: the rail holds x[j], the cell's low bit |0>

name: 118_qft4_demorgan
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 8, 4, 2, 5.
; Checked: c0 (%2 -> %16), c1 (%3 -> %18), c2 (%4 -> %21), c3 (%5 -> %24), all measured and packed into the returned int.
; Clean: every negation rail (NOT c3 %6, NOT c1 %8, NOT c2 %10, NOT c0 %12) and every flag rail (%7, %9, %11, %13, %14,
; %15), each |0> at its free.
; Kept: the four user registers c0..c3 (measured; a measured rail stays allocated).
; Rotations: (Ry, c0, th, 1); (Ry, c1, th, 1); (Ry, c2, th, 1); (Ry, c3, th, 1); (P, c3, pi, c3); (Ry, c3, pi/2, 1);
; (P, flag, -pi/2, c3&c2); (P, c2, pi, c2); (Ry, c2, pi/2, 1); (P, flag, -pi/4, c3&c1); (P, flag, -pi/2, c2&c1);
; (P, c1, pi, c1); (Ry, c1, pi/2, 1); (P, flag, -pi/8, c3&c0); (P, flag, -pi/4, c2&c0); (P, flag, -pi/2, c1&c0);
; (P, c0, pi, c0); (Ry, c0, pi/2, 1). A middle-four control c_i&c_j is the X-bracketed flag NOT(NOT c_i | NOT c_j).
; The 4-qubit QFT^-1 written with `a && b` conditions: -O1 keeps the first and last conjunctions as
; `select i1 a, i1 b, i1 false` (the Toffoli flag of 59/60), but De-Morgans the middle four: it hoists the NEGATIONS as
; values (%9 = xor i1 %8, true = NOT c3, %16 = NOT c1, %20 = NOT c2, %27 = NOT c0 in the -O1 IR), rewrites each condition
; as `select i1 NOT a, i1 true, i1 NOT b` (= NOT(a && b)) and INVERTS the branches, so the phase block runs under the
; negated flag. Lowered as spelled:
;  - a negation value is a fresh rail: cq_template_xor_i1_hl(rail, 1) (out of place; the register is untouched);
;  - the or-select of two rails, `select i1 NOT a, i1 true, i1 NOT b` = NOT a | NOT b, is a branch flag: cqrt_or_i1 of the
;    two negation rails into a fresh |0> flag (rule 8); the phase block runs under NOT of that flag, so it is an X-bracketed
;    kickback (21, 39); the flag is re-applied (self-inverse) and freed right after;
;  - the two `select i1 a, i1 b, i1 false` conjunctions are the Toffoli flag of 59 (cqrt_and_i1), kickback, un-Toffoli;
;  - `if (q) cq_phi(pi)` on a bare register is cqrt_rz_i1 on that rail (115); cq_theta rotates the rail in place.
; A negation rail is uncomputed after its LAST use and before the next in-place gate on its operand, because the
; uncompute needs the operand's value unchanged: NOT c1 (%8) dies before c1's rotation, NOT c0 (%12) before c0's;
; NOT c3 and NOT c2 die at the end (their registers are not rotated again). Every flag is |0> at its free.
; Replayed on alg_test's sim_qpe.py: |+>^4 (th = pi/2) -> |0000> with p = 1, no ancilla left allocated.

  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %10, i32 %8, i32 %11)    ; IR: %21 = NOT a | NOT b into the flag

  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %11)    ; IR: bracket

  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %3, double 0x3FF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %26 = cq_theta_i1(%3, pi/2)  [Ry in place on c1]
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i1_hl(i32 %2, i1 true)    ; IR: %27 = xor i1 %2, true  [NOT c0; read by %28 and %31]
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %28 = select i1 %9, i1 true, i1 %27  [NOT(c3 && c0)]  [fresh flag rail]
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %6, i32 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: %28 = NOT a | NOT b into the flag

; at P = %6) hold the four rotated registers at exit.

; their sum %14, the address rail %15 = &GRID + sum), uncomputed and freed right after the load. register_grid: the swap
; rail of every in-place form (%29 per cell in the first loop, %59 per row in the second, %40 for the cross-row arm),
; |0> after its swap-in.
; Kept: table_2d's registers r (%6) and c (%7) and the measured load copy %16 (rule 2). register_grid: the four cells
; q[i][j] (user registers living in the bus cells, two of them read by measured load copies); the seed %7 and the tape
; slot of the initializer `store i32 0` (a kept store, rule 5 sentence 3; classical-valued, so the cells stay HOST and
; no qubit is spent, §0); the two measured load copies %41 and %48 (rule 2). Left allocated, un-copied (rule 5
; sentence 1: overtaken by an in-place form): per trip of the first loop the angle load copy %28 of theta[2i+j]
; (classical-valued); per row of the second loop the flag %56 (the load copy of q[i][0] that controls the form on
; q[i][1]); the flag %35 (the load copy of q[0][1] taken BEFORE the cross-row form; on the rows == 1 path its un-copy
; reads the rotated cell and the rail keeps garbage).
; Rotations: (Ry, r, tr, 1); (Ry, c, tc, 1) in table_2d; (Ry, the cell q[i][j], the angle rail of theta[2i+j], 1) per
; cell in order; then (Ry, the cell q[i][1], c, copy of q[i][0]) per row i; then (Ry, the cell q[rows-1][1], c, copy of
; q[0][1] taken before the gate) (rows == 1: the same cell as the control's source).
; table_2d: a constant 2-D table read at a quantum row AND a quantum column is ONE bus load at an address rail (rule 20;
; QROM is retired). @GRID is a constant global, but its getelementptr has tainted indices, so the access is no
; host-resident access (rule 20 (a)): the load is cqrt_qram_load_i32 at the address rail, reading the HOST cells of the
; table through the overlay (nothing seeded, nothing registered). The address is -O1's own getelementptr
; [4 x [4 x i32]] @GRID, 0, %8, %10 as 64-bit template arithmetic: each tainted index as -O1 wrote it (and, then zext to
; i64), scaled by its element size (16 bytes a row, 4 a column: mul_i64_hl), summed (add_i64), plus the classical part,
; the run-time address of @GRID (add_i64_hl of `ptrtoint (ptr @GRID to i64)`). Nothing is narrowed, bounded or checked.
; The load copy is measured, so it is never un-copied (rule 2); the access is then the address rail's last reader and
; the whole chain is uncomputed LIFO right after the load (rule 20).
; register_grid: `bool q[2][2]` is an alloca stored tainted values, so it is BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)): one zeroed

; `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext; store i8` through the same pointer is rule 5's in-place form at width

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 15, 16, 20, 21; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc, qram_swap).
; Checked: quantum_strlen's n (the result rail %39 of the after-loop select, through %56, measured into %57);
; quantum_strcmp's `i < cap ? a[i] - b[i] : 0` (the copied-out result %107 -> %108, measured). The cells on the bus
; at exit, read at each block's address: s[i] (strlen), a[i] and b[i] (strcmp) = Ry(th[i]) (resp. Ry(ta[i]),
; Ry(tb[i])) applied to 'a' (97) for i < cap, 0 for cap <= i < 4 (the zero store; zeroed __cq_alloc memory).
; Clean: every trip rail (the trip predicates, exit flags, per-trip selects, strcmp's difference and its sexts), popped
; and uncomputed by the reverse loop; every load copy of a cell in the scan loops (strlen's s[i]; strcmp's a[i], b[i] in
; block %33 and b[i] again in block %37), each pushed with its trip and un-copied in the reverse loop right after its
; last reader's _unc, under the control it was loaded with (rule 5 sentence 1: no memory version change follows the
; fill loop); the swap rail of each in-place form (|0> after the swap-in, freed); the |1> seed and the chain's |0>
; seed rail, freed directly (rule 7).
; Kept: the cells s[i] (strlen) and a[i], b[i] (strcmp): the registers live on the bus, rotated in place by rule 5's
; in-place form. By rule 5 sentence 3, the tape slot of every bus store with its value seed (rule 7): the zero
; initializer `store i32 0` of each block (alloc_i32(0)) and each trip's `store i8 97` (alloc_i8(97)); strcmp's
; OVERLAP path (d = 0, never taken at run time: a and b are distinct blocks) adds the kept store of b[i] with its
; rotated load copy as value rail (frozen, rule 2). By rule 5 sentence 1, the angle load copies th[i], ta[i], tb[i]
; (each overtaken by the in-place form, a memory version change: un-copied after its last reader, the Ry, past the
; form's second swap, and left allocated). The measured result rail. No predicate is kept: the bound cap is classical, so every trip and
; exit predicate, the last trip's a_last included, is a function of the inputs and is uncomputed by the reverse loop
; (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum exit); no bus access is under a predicate that controls a store.
; Rotations: (Ry, s[i], A_i, 1) per trip i of the fill loop, A_i the f64 angle rail loaded from th[i] (rule 15: a loaded
; angle is a rail, rule 3); (Ry, a[i], ta[i] rail, 1), (Ry, b[i], tb[i] rail, 1) per trip i, each in place on its cell
; through the form's swap rail (on strcmp's OVERLAP path, b[i]'s Ry acts on the load copy instead).
; A STRING SEARCH OVER QUANTUM CHARS: -O1 turns `while (n < cap && s[n] != 0) n++` into a classical counted loop over
; cap (the buffer bound) with a quantum EARLY EXIT, and computes n from the classical induction variable in the exit
; block (%28 = trunc %20) merged by the exit phi %30 [0 (cap <= 0), %28 (NUL at trip i), %1 (no NUL)]. So n is never a
; loop-carried quantum value: which EXIT is taken is quantum. The loop stays a classical loop of cap trips (26's shape)
; under the trip predicate a_i = a_(i-1) & NOT z_i (seed |1>), and each exit gets its own predicate: e_i = a_(i-1) & z_i
; for the NUL exit at trip i, a_last for the fall-through exit. These predicates are MUTUALLY EXCLUSIVE and exactly one is
; 1. The exit phi is merged per rule 9: one cq_template_select_i32 per incoming, chained with the complement arm innermost
; into fresh rails: r_i = select(e_i, i, r_(i-1)) in trip i (the literal incoming %28 is the trip index: _lh), seeded by
; a |0> rail (the incoming 0 of the cap <= 0 edge; a seed, rule 7), and after the loop r = select(a_last, cap, r_last),
; the result. Each trip pushes its load copy, its predicates and r_(i-1); a reverse loop pops them, uncomputes r_i by its
; select's _unc, then the predicates and the test, and un-copies the load (the result does not depend on them staying
; alive).
; quantum_strcmp has two quantum exits from one trip into the same exit block %37 (NUL in a, or a[i] != b[i]): the exit
; flag of the trip is x_i = e1_i | e2_i (or_i1 into a fresh flag, rule 8; e1, e2 exclusive), the block's value
; d = a[i] - b[i] (classical trip index i, quantum chars) is computed unconditionally (pure), merged by
; r_i = select(x_i, d, r_(i-1)); d and its two sexts stay alive (pushed with the trip) and the reverse trip uncomputes
; r_i, x_i, d and the sexts in exact LIFO order (rule 5);
; the fall-through exit and the cap <= 0 edge contribute 0, the value of the |0> seed, so no select is spent on them. The
; last trip's r is copied out (alloc + copy, rule 14) and the reverse loop uncomputes every trip's r.
; ONE BUS (rules 16, 20, 21). Each `char x[4]` is stored to with a tainted value (the cq_theta result), a user rule 20 (b)
; does not allow, so it is BUS-RESIDENT: __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program point (zeroed host memory at an
; address never reused), no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Its base is its run-time
; address, a classical i64, and every gep below has untainted indices, so every access is _hl at a classical address.
; m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). th, ta, tb are pointer arguments: their loads are bus loads (rule 20),
; so each angle is an f64 rail and each rotation is cqrt_ry_i8_qangle (rule 15).
; The punned zero initializer `store i32 0, ptr x` is a bus store of the seed alloc_i32(0) (rule 20: a classical value
; is first a seed), kept (rule 5 sentence 3), classical-valued: the cells stay HOST.
; The fill loop: `store i8 97, ptr p; t = load th[i]; y' = cq_theta_c(97, t); store i8 y', ptr p`. The store of 97 is a
; kept store of the seed alloc_i8(97). -O1 forwarded 97 to the cq_theta: by rule 5's Readers clause the interval of the
; in-place form runs from that store to the store of y' on the same SSA pointer, so the cq_theta is the form (rule 2):
; alloc_i8(0), qram_swap_i8_hl (the rail holds 97, the cell |0>), the Ry, qram_swap_i8_hl back, free, emitted at the
; second store's position. The angle load is a load a step reads: a plain load at its own program point, before the
; swap-out, overtaken by the form: un-copied after the second swap and not freed (rule 5, the `*p += *q` case).
; SPEC GAP: rule 2's first sentence ("cq_theta on a classical v mints alloc_<W>(v) then ry") and rule 5's Readers clause
; (y forwarded from the preceding store) both read on `cq_theta_c(97, ...)` stored back through the pointer the 97 was
; stored to. The Readers clause is taken (the form, as 206); the other reading (a fresh seed rotated and a second kept
; store of it) leaves the same cell value and differs only in which rails are kept.
; The angle rail is un-copied after the form (rule 15's 'uncomputed afterwards', rule 5 sentence 1) and, overtaken by
; the form, left allocated.
; In strcmp the interval of b[i]'s form (store 97 to b[i] .. store %22 to b[i]) contains two memory version changes at
; the classical address a[i]: the store of 97 to a[i] and a[i]'s own form. The Readers clause applies with p = &b[i]
; and q = &a[i] (S_p = S_q = 1): d is the AND of the two changes' tests (q - p >= 1 && p - q >= 1, mod 2^64, unsigned),
; computed before the first change; br d around the plain load of b[i] (the copy, taken when d = 0), the changes
; emitted once, then br d at the store's position: d = 1 the form on b[i], d = 0 the Ry on the copy (frozen, rule 2)
; and a kept store. a[i]'s own interval contains no change: its form stands with no test.
; The scan loops: each load of a cell is a bus load (a rail, rule 3) under the predicate of its block at that trip
; (rule 5: every bus access under a quantum predicate is _controlled): strlen's s[i] and strcmp's a[i] under the
; predicate of reaching the trip's test (the |1> seed for trip 0); strcmp's b[i] in block %33 under that block's
; predicate; the reload of b[i] in block %37 (%40) is its own bus load under x_i, the predicate of block %37 (no bus
; access is hoisted: the old shared handle of %35 and %40 is gone). The reverse loop recomputes each address from
; the trip index and pops the load copies.

; Checked: quantum_bitfield's updated word w (the new word %14 -> %15, measured); bitfield_through_pointer's f.c (the
; lshr-8 result %12 -> %13, measured); the 4 cells of f at exit (read from the bus): w + (d << 8) mod 2^32.
; Clean: quantum_bitfield's field chain (a %7, a + v %8, b %9, the flag %10, the shifted and masked new field %11, %12,
; the cleared word %13); bitfield_through_pointer's field-a rail %10, its flag %11 and the load copy of f (%9),

; the in-place form (the swap rail %6, the rule-6 inverse %8, the updated rail %7), all freed.

; the kept store f = w) and the measured result rail; by rule 5 the tape slot of the store of w into f. The in-place
; form in bump_c keeps nothing.

; field access as integer arithmetic on that word. A read of field b is `lshr`+`and`, a write is the read-modify-write
; `(word & ~mask) | ((v << off) & mask)`: two `and`s and a disjoint `or`, each a fresh rail (nothing in place). When the
; struct is a local whose bytes never escape, SROA dissolves it and the word is an SSA value (first function; -O1 even
; forwards f.b from the computed field instead of re-reading the new word): no bus access. The condition on the field
; just written is a phase arm on that field's compare flag. The garbage of the RMW (the two masked halves and the field
; computation) is uncomputed after the disjoint or; the new word is measured. Uncompute order is dependency order (rule
; 5): the cleared word (%13) reads only w and is independent of the field chain, so it is undone last; the chain is
; undone in reverse.

; argument is a user that demotes it): one __cq_alloc(4, 4) block at its program point, the lifetime markers dropped

; c = `lshr 8` read that copy, and the copy is un-copied after its last reader (the `and`'s _unc and the lshr), before
; the measurement of c (rule 5 sentence 1). Nothing asks whether the cells at p are the cells of f.

name: 123_enum_switch_fallthrough
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 13, 8, 9, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: y (the result rail %16 -> %17, measured) and m (%5 -> %18, measured), summed.
; Clean: the four case flags e0..e3 (%6..%9), the two OR predicates (%11, %12), the GREEN-body select %14 and the BLUE
; product %15, each |0> at its free.
; Kept: the enum register m (%5, rotated and measured) and the result rail y (%16, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, m, th, 1); (P, e0, p, m == 0); (P, e3, -p, m == 3).
; The scrutinee is a quantum enum (enum mode * matches unsigned int * in cq_theta's _Generic: an enum is its compatible
; integer type, i32 in IR). Each case label gets one equality flag; the flags are mutually exclusive, and the missing
; default is the implicit no-op arm (a value outside 0..3 runs no case, so its predicate is the complement and needs no
; flag). Fallthrough is not a C-level notion in IR: it is a block reached from several switch edges, so a block's
; predicate is the disjoint OR of the case flags that reach it:
;   block %6 (RED body)   e0              -> phase arm: kickback cq_phi(p) onto e0
;   block %7 (GREEN body) e0 | e1         -> value: %8 = y0 + 1 (classical: y0 is a parameter)
;   block %9 (BLUE body)  e0 | e1 | e2    -> value: %10 = phi selects %8 when entered from %7 (e0|e1), y0 from the switch (e2)
;   block %12 (ALPHA)     e3              -> phase arm: kickback cq_phi(-p) onto e3
; The two OR predicates are cqrt_or_i1 into fresh |0> flags (rule 8; the edge flags are disjoint); the second reuses the
; first. The phase of the RED body is fired once, on e0 alone, not on the OR: the phase belongs to the block where cq_phi
; stands, and the value code it falls into is shared (method matches arm class: the phase goes to a flag, the values
; merge by select). %10 has two classical data operands (select _ll); the final merge %15 is the quantum %11 when the
; BLUE block ran (e0|e1|e2) and the classical y0 otherwise (select _hl; the ALPHA and no-case edges both carry y0).
; Everything but the result and the enum register is uncomputed LIFO; the enum register is rotated, so it stays (frozen)
; and is measured.
source_filename = "enum_switch_fallthrough.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 0)    ; IR: switch i32 %5: i32 0 -> %6  [RED]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: switch i32 %5: i32 1 -> %7  [GREEN]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 2)    ; IR: switch i32 %5: i32 2 -> %9  [BLUE]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 3)    ; IR: switch i32 %5: i32 3 -> %12  [ALPHA]
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %6, double %3)    ; IR: block %6: cq_phi(%3)  [kickback onto the RED flag only]
  %10 = fneg double %3    ; IR: %13 = fneg double %3  (classical)
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %9, double %10)    ; IR: block %12: cq_phi(%13)  [kickback onto the ALPHA flag]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %7 = (%5 == 0) | (%5 == 1)  (RED falls into GREEN)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %11)    ; IR: OR of the (disjoint) edge flags %6 -> %7 and switch -> %7
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of block %9 = pred(%7) | (%5 == 2)  (GREEN falls into BLUE)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %11, i32 %8, i32 %12)    ; IR: OR of the (disjoint) edge flags %7 -> %9 and switch -> %9
  %13 = add nsw i32 %2, 1    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %2, 1  (classical: y0 + 1)
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %11, i32 %13, i32 %2)    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ %2, %4 ], [ %8, %7 ]  (entered from %7 iff e0|e1)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %14, i32 3)    ; IR: %11 = mul nsw i32 %10, 3
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 %15, i32 %2)    ; IR: %15 = phi i32 [ %2, %4 ], [ %2, %12 ], [ %11, %9 ]  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %14, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %14, i32 %11, i32 %13, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %11, i32 %8, i32 %12)    ; IR: uncompute pred(%9) (self-inverse)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %6, i32 %7, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute pred(%7) (self-inverse)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %5, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute the ALPHA flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %5, i32 2)    ; IR: uncompute the BLUE flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute the GREEN flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute the RED flag
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %16)    ; IR: %16 = cq_measure_si32(%15)
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %17 = cq_measure_ui32(%5)
  %19 = add nsw i32 %18, %17    ; IR: %18  (classical)
  ret i32 %19    ; IR: ret i32 %18
}

name: 124_callee_controlled_ry_in_loop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19, 10, 8, 14, 18, 20, 21, 5 (in-place form; Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 2, 7, 16; §1.3 (the bus, qram_swap), §1.4.
; Checked: r + x + b (measured). r is the 4 cells at P, the address of the bus-resident r, read after the loop by the
; load copy %21 -> %22; the cells at P at exit hold r after every trip.
; Clean: inside every trip's clone call: the callee flag f = (x > k + i) (%8), the composed flag g = b & f (%9) and the
; swap rail of the in-place form (%10, |0> after its swap-in on both branches of g).
; Kept: the user registers x and b (control and compare inputs only, measured). r is the cell at P (rotated in place
; under control, rule 10 on a memory cell). Rule 5 sentence 3: the tape slot of the store r = r0 and its value rail, the
; seed alloc_i32(r0) (%13). Rule 2: the load copy of r (%21), measured, never un-copied.
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x; Ry(tb) on b; for each trip i = 0..n-1 (classical, n > 0): Ry(t) on the cell at P (r) under
; b & (x > k + i).
; A CONTROLLED RY UNDER A COMPOSED CONTROL, ACROSS A CALL, INSIDE A CLASSICAL LOOP THAT SITS IN A QUANTUM ARM. Three
; pieces, each from an existing example:
;   (1) -O1 fuses the outer `if (b)` with the loop guard `n > 0` into one `and i1 %10, %11`. One operand is the bare
;       _Bool rail b (a rail is a condition by itself), the other is classical. A classical conjunct is split off as
;       a classical branch (rule 8): when it is false nothing runs, when it is true the predicate IS b. No AND flag is
;       computed in the caller, and the trip counter, the bound and `k + i` all stay classical (rule 14, classical
;       bound: no trip-local rail remains in the caller, so nothing is pushed and there is no reverse loop).
;   (2) `step(&r, ...)` takes r's ADDRESS, a call user, so the alloca of r is bus-resident (rule 20 (b)):
;       __cq_alloc(4, 4) at its program point, P = its run-time address (a classical i64), no alloca remains and the
;       lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). `r = r0` is a bus store of the seed alloc_i32(r0) at P, a kept store
;       (rules 5, 7). The call to step runs under the quantum predicate b, and step has a rotation and bus accesses, so
;       it becomes a CONTROLLED CLONE with the predicate as its first parameter (rule 19: __cq_q_<fn>_<mask>_ctl). A
;       pointer is one scalar (§1.4, rules 18, 21): &r is a classical ptr (not computed from a rail), digit 0, and the
;       formal stays the C ptr; x is quantum, digit 1; k and t are classical: __cq_q_step_0100_ctl. Nothing about the
;       pointee crosses the call. The clone writes memory (an in-place form), so it has no twin, it has no result, and
;       each call is a memory version change (rules 5, 18).
;   (3) Inside the clone, the callee's own condition x > k becomes a flag f, and the composed control pred AND f is a
;       Toffoli into a fresh |0> flag g (rule 8). `*r = cq_theta(*r, t)` is `load p; cq_theta; store p` on the same
;       SSA pointer with no memory version change between: rule 5's in-place form at the classical address
;       p = ptrtoint %1, under g (rule 10 on a memory cell): swap-out into a |0> rail under g, Ry(t) under g on that
;       rail, swap-in under g, free (g = 0: nothing touched, the rail stays |0>). The cell is the register. Then g is
;       uncomputed with the same Toffoli (pred and f are unchanged) and f with its compare's _unc; both are freed
;       provably |0>. One clone call per trip; g, f and the swap rail are trip-local, so nothing survives the loop.
; After the loop `cq_measure(r)` reads r through a plain bus load at P (rule 3): the copy is the measured rail (rule 2).
; Nothing non-diagonal touches a user register except the in-place form on r's cell at P: the controlled swap pair and
; the controlled Ry between them, all under g.
; b and x are only control or compare inputs, so they are left untouched and measured by the user.
; SPEC GAP (corpus convention, §5): §1.3 / rule 19 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their
; twins) per externally visible function. As in 61, 200, 204, 211 and 212 nothing is registered for
; callee_controlled_ry_in_loop (its address is never taken here); the omission is not part of the pinned lowering.

; One then-arm carries three arm classes at once, and each keeps its own method over ONE flag f = (x > k): the phase
; cq_phi(a) is kickback on f and cq_phi(b) kickback on NOT f (X-bracketed); the value y += 1 is computed unconditionally
; into a fresh rail and merged by a select into a fresh |0> result rail y' (never in place on y: the else value is y
; itself); the rotation of r is an in-place cqrt_ry_i32_controlled on f (r starts as the classical %5 in both arms, so it
; is a fresh register, then frozen). None of the three may borrow another's method: a basis copy of the phase arm would
; drop the phase, a phase on y would not change its label, a select merge of the rotated r would copy a label of an Ry
; superposition.

name: 126_invert_controlled_loop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 17, 14, 10, 8, 12, 5, 2, 3, 11, 15, 20, 21; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem).
; Checked: r + x (measured).
; Clean: the hoisted chain d = sext(x) - k, every trip flag f_i = (i < d) and every trip's controlled load copy A_i of
; th[i], each uncomputed (un-copied) and freed inside the region.
; Kept: the user register x; r (rotated in place under control, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x; then, as the backend emits the region: for i = n-1 down to 0 (classical n > 0): P(-ph) on the
; flag (i < x - k), Ry(-val(A_i)) on r under (i < x - k), A_i the f64 rail loaded from th[i] under that flag.
; A CLASSICAL LOOP WHOSE BODY IS A QUANTUM ARM, INSIDE cq_invert (rule 17). The region is lowered as it would be anywhere
; else (rule 14, classical bound: the loop stays a classical loop; each trip computes its flag, loads th[i], rotates r in
; place under the flag, kicks the phase back on it and uncomputes it; the LICM-hoisted chain d = sext(x) - k is computed
; once before the loop and uncomputed once after it) and sits between cqrt_invert_begin() and cqrt_invert_end() (§1.3).
; The backend, which builds the circuit as this program runs (§0), emits the gates recorded between the two calls
; reversed with each gate inverted; so the trips come out in reverse order (the adjoint of U_{n-1}...U_0 is
; U_0^dag...U_{n-1}^dag, and the trips do not commute: each rotates r by a different angle under a different flag), every
; angle is negated, the controls stay, and inside a trip the Ry and the kickback swap places. Each compute/uncompute pair
; (the hoisted chain, each f_i, each A_i: a load un-copied inside the region reverses into itself, rule 17 Memory)
; reverses into itself, so the backend recomputes and uncomputes it inside the adjoint; the frees it recorded are
; performed after the reversed list. The compiler reverses no loop and negates no angle. -O1 spelled `x > k + i` as
; `i < x - k` with `sext x` and `x - k` hoisted; the compare is `i < d` with the classical i first, and a compare never
; takes _lh (§1.2), so it is spelled by flipping the predicate: `d > i` (icmp_sgt_i64_hl). r is a loop-carried phi
; (%22/%29 in the -O1 IR) whose arm rotates in place, so its handle never changes and both phis are that handle. The two
; empty asm memory fences that CQ.h's markers carry are compiler fences with no gate and are dropped with the markers.
; THE ANGLE th[i] (rules 3, 20, 21, 11, 15). th is a pointer argument, program memory like any other: `load double` of
; th[i] is a bus load and its result is an f64 rail (rule 3; over-taint: a basis copy of HOST cells, no qubit). The
; getelementptr has a classical base and the classical index i, so it stays, and the address is its run-time i64
; (ptrtoint, the _hl operand). The load sits in the arm block %24 and a bus access is never hoisted (rule 9): it is
; qram_load_f64_hl_controlled under the trip flag, |0> on the flag-0 branch (rule 5). An angle loaded from the bus is a
; quantum angle (rule 11), so the controlled Ry is rule 15's single primitive ry_i32_qangle_controlled(f, r, A). Its last
; reader is that rotation and no memory version change follows in the trip (no store, swap, allocation or host call), so
; the copy is un-copied right after it under the same flag (rule 5 sentence 1) and freed, before the flag's own _unc.
; m = __cq_mem() is called once, at function entry (§5).
; Regenerated 2026-11-02 (the first version constructed the reversed loop at compile time); regenerated 2026-11-05 for
; the flat memory model (th[i] is a bus load and a quantum angle).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 6 (witness: bijective update of a dead value, both outcomes), 3, 5, 18, 2, 4.
; Checked: x2 = f(x, y) ^ z (the final x, %8 -> %10, measured).
; Clean: y = x0 + 1 (%5), z = x0 * c (%6), the clone's result x1 (%7, |0> after the rule-6 copy), the inverse t (%9), and
; the clone's internal rails, all freed.
; Kept: x0 (%4, the rotated register: its composite update has no inverse, so it stays allocated, entangled with the
; result) and x2 (%8, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x0, th, 1).
; x has three forward consumers (y, z, the call), so it is a fan-out source; it is the Ry-prepared user register.
; `x = f(x, y)` and `x ^= z` rebind the NAME x: x0 (the register) -> x1 = f(x0, y) = (y + 1) * x0 (the clone's copied-out
; result, rule 18; -O1 rewrote f's body to (b + 1) * a) -> x2 = x1 ^ z (a fresh rail, rule 4). Rule 6 is asked once per
; dead rail, after the rails that read it are uncomputed:
;   x1 is dead once x2 exists and x2 = x1 ^ z is a bijection in x1 for fixed z, so the old rail is cleaned by rule 6:
;   t = x2 ^ z recomputes x1 into a fresh rail, copy_i32(t, x1) zeroes it, t is uncomputed, x1 is freed. Nothing calls
;   the clone's _unc twin, so it is not defined (§1.4).
;   x0 is needed to uncompute z and y, so those are uncomputed first (LIFO: z, then y). Then rule 6 does NOT apply: the
;   composite update x2 = ((x0 + 2) * x0) ^ (x0 * c) is not a bijection in x0 for the other operand c (c = 0 sends x0 and
;   -2 - x0 to the same value), so no inverse exists and x0 stays allocated (garbage policy, 0): it is entangled with the
;   measured result and is never freed.
source_filename = "inplace_fanout_reassign.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x0]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %5 = add nsw i32 %4, 1  [y]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = mul nsw i32 %4, %2  [z]
  %7 = tail call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_f_11(i32 noundef %4, i32 noundef %5)    ; IR: %7 = call @f(%4, %5), quantum clone of f (both args quantum)  [x1]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i32(i32 %7, i32 %6)    ; IR: %8 = xor i32 %7, %6  [x2, fresh result rail]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i32(i32 %8, i32 %6)    ; IR: rule 6: t = x2 ^ z recomputes x1 (xor is its own inverse in x1 for fixed z)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %9, i32 %7)    ; IR: rule 6: x1 ^= t: the dead x1 rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_xor_i32_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the old x1 rail (|0> after the copy)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6 (reads x0)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %5 (reads x0)

name: 128_measure_then_reuse

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 10, 4, 3.
; Checked: measure_then_reuse: cq_measure(x) + m, m the first measurement of x; measure_entangled_rotate_other:
; cq_measure(x) + m, m the measurement of y = x + c.
; Clean: none (no garbage rail is minted).
; Kept: measure_then_reuse: the measured x rail (never reused, uncomputed or freed), the then-arm's fresh rotated
; register and the else-arm's classical-value rail (one of them measured at the join); measure_entangled_rotate_other:
; x (rotated in place, measured) and the measured y rail (not provably |0> once x is rotated).
; Rotations: measure_then_reuse: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on a fresh register seeded with m, under the classical condition
; m > k. measure_entangled_rotate_other: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on x under the classical condition m > k.
; A measurement is the one place where a NAME and its register diverge (rule 2): after `m = cq_measure(x)` the source
; keeps reading x, and every later read of %5 denotes m, a classical value. So the branch on m is ordinary classical
; control (a real br, handle phi at the join, no flag), the then-arm rotation is a fresh register seeded with m and
; rotated, and the else-arm `x += 1` is classical m + 1, put on a rail only because the join merges it with a quantum
; value. The measured rail itself is never reused, uncomputed or freed (it is not provably |0>). In
; measure_entangled_rotate_other the MEASURED name is y; x is never measured, so x keeps naming its own rail (collapsed
; to m - c by the measurement of y, but the compiler never derives that) and the classical-controlled rotation fires in
; place on it. The measured y rail stays allocated: uncomputing y = x + c against x is only valid until x is rotated,
; and a measured rail is never touched.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

; Checked: r + (acc > 0.0), r and acc measured.
; Clean: every trip's load copy c[i] (un-copied by the mirror after the product's _unc, under the predicate it was loaded
; with: no memory version change follows any load, rule 5 sentence 1), product rail c[i] * x, u_i, break flag e_i,
; carried acc_i and predicate a_i (popped and uncomputed by the mirror), the |1> seed predicate (minted after the
; zero-trip test, never on the skip path; rule 14) and the 0.0 seed of acc (rule 7), and the final flag acc > 2 lim.
; Kept: the user register x; the copied-out acc rail (measured); r (rotated under control, frozen, measured). No store,
; no tape slot: the function never writes the bus.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x; Ry(tr) on the fresh |0> rail r under (acc > 2 lim), acc the copied-out loop result.
; Three mechanisms composed: the loop-carried fp rail of 28 (one unfused multiply-add per trip, §2: an fmul product
; rail c[i] * x and an fadd into u_i, both pushed on the handle stack; the mirror after the copy-out), the quantum break
; of 26, and the controlled Ry of 39 conditioned on the loop's RESULT (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum break).
; MEMORY. c is a host pointer parameter: nothing is known about what it points to (rule 21), so the load c[i] is a BUS
; LOAD and its value a rail (rule 3; the cells are HOST, so the copy is c[i] when trip i runs and +0.0 when it does
; not: under a_{i-1} it is a which-path copy entangled with x, a 64-qubit rail un-copied by the mirror), and the
; product is the two-rail fmul (IR order: c[i], x). m = __cq_mem() once at function entry. The gep has
; an untainted base and the classical induction i, so it stays and its ptrtoint is the classical _hl address (rule 20).
; The load sits in trip i's body, which runs iff a_{i-1}: it is _hl_controlled under a_{i-1} (rule 5: a trip C would not
; run touches no cell and no host byte; the exit test reads it, and a_{i-1} is the predicate of reaching that test,
; rule 14). The load copy is trip-local garbage that rule 5 un-copies (the loop has no memory version change), so it
; is pushed with the trip's other rails; the mirror recomputes the address from the trip index and un-copies it after
; the product's _unc (its last reader), under the same control a_{j-1}, still live at that point.

; classical half %19 keeps the loop a classical loop over all n trips, the quantum half becomes the trip predicate: trip

; roundings) computed unguarded (pure; on a trip that does not run the load is |0> = +0.0 and u_i is discarded by the
; select), and the carried value is acc_i = a_{i-1} ? u_i : acc_{i-1}. After the last trip acc_n is the exit phi %22 for
; every break point. WHICH-PATH RAILS: every trip predicate a_i and break flag e_i is entangled with x and is
; uncomputed by the mirror, together with u_i, its product rail, the load copy and acc_i, while x still holds the value
; the trips read; nothing of the loop survives except the copied-out acc. The mirror runs BEFORE the controlled Ry
; (62/116 placement), so the Ry's flag is computed from the copy: f = acc > 2 lim, Ry(tr) on the fresh |0> rail r under
; f, f uncomputed, r and acc measured. n <= 0 takes the classical edge: acc is the seed rail (0.0), the same tail runs

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 13, 14 (classical bound), 7, 9, 2, 4, 5.
; Checked: acc (the copied-out result %26 -> %44, measured; where the loop never runs the seed rail %5 -> %8 is measured).
; Clean: every trip rail (the scrutinee, the three equality flags, the three arm values and the select chain of each
; trip, and the old acc), popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the seed rail holding the classical 1 (%5, popped
; as %40), never written and freed directly.
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register) and the measured result rail.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; The loop is a classical loop with no predicate chain (25, 57; the trip count n is classical, only the switch inside
; the body is quantum). The quantum switch is the 22/49 value switch in its body, and acc is loop-carried and seeded
; CLASSICAL (a rail holding 1 before trip 0, as 62). The default label is `unreachable` (-O1 proved `& 3` covers 0..3),
; so case 3 is the complement: no flag, it is the innermost select operand, i.e. acc carried unchanged. Each trip
; computes the scrutinee, three equality flags, the three arm values from the carried acc and merges them by a select
; chain into a fresh rail (the next acc); the old acc and every intermediate are pushed, as in 57. The classical trip
; index is not pushed: the reverse trip j is the forward trip i = j and recomputes it. After the last trip the result is
; copied out, the reverse loop pops and uncomputes each trip LIFO, and the seed rail (the classical 1, never written) is

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 11, 15, 9, 8, 5, 2.
; Checked: phi_angle_select and nested_angle_select: x; theta_angle_select and shared_angle_select: r + x (measured).
; Clean: every select flag (x > k, x > k1, x > k2), every angle rail A and nested_angle_select's inner angle rail, all
; uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; r (rotated by the angle rail, measured) in theta_angle_select and
; shared_angle_select.
; Rotations: phi_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1) with A = select(x > k, a, b). theta_angle_select:
; (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = select(x > k, a, b). nested_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1)
; with A = select(x > k1, a, select(x > k2, b, c)). shared_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1);
; (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with the one A = select(x > k, a, b).
; An ANGLE SELECT is a QUANTUM ANGLE (rule 11): the angle depends on a quantum flag, so it is computed into an f64 rail
; by the ordinary select template (rule 9; the arms a, b, c are runtime-classical doubles, so cq_template_select_f64_ll,
; and a select of selects nests: the inner select's rail is the else arm of the outer one, select_f64_lh), and ONE
; primitive consumes the rail (rule 15): cqrt_rz_qangle(A) for cq_phi (register-free; no quantum predicate is in scope,
; so the phase e^{i val(A)} lands on each branch of A and stays on the branches of x when A and the flag are
; uncomputed) and
; cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) for cq_theta on the seeded register r. The compiler never expands the select into per-arm
; controlled rotations; the N-bit ladder is the backend's. One select read by two consumers (shared_angle_select) is
; one angle rail read by both primitives and uncomputed once, after the second. Each angle chain is uncomputed LIFO and
; freed (rule 5), then the flags.

; prep_beside_phase: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t) on r under (x > k) after xorc(r0) under the same flag; P(p) on NOT (x > k).
; prep_twice: Ry(th) on x; Ry(t1) on r under (x > k1) after xorc(r0) under it; Ry(-t1) on r under (x > k1) & (x < k2),
; then xorc(r0) on r under the same conjunction; xorc(r0) on r under (x < k2); Ry(t2) on r under (x < k2).
; A STATE PREP under a quantum condition is a controlled Ry on the variable's own rail (39, rule 10); when the arm first
; RESETS the variable (r = 0) and the straight-through value is something else (7, r0, or an earlier prep), the reset
; is a controlled XOR with the value the rail holds there: cqrt_xorc_<W>_controlled(flag, r, v) takes r from v to 0

; the kickback under NOT the flag (39/21). OVERWRITING a register that an earlier arm may have prepared: where both
; conditions hold the earlier prep must be undone first, by its own adjoint under the conjunction flag (Ry(-t1), then

name: 136_callee_measure
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 2, 4, 5.
; Checked: m + cq_measure(y), m = max(cq_measure(x), k) returned classically by the callee, y = x + c (y is a classical
; read by rule 2; its value is witnessed by the output).
; Clean: the y rail (%6): computed before x's measurement, it collapses with it (rule 2) and is uncomputed at the collapse
; point against x's rail, which holds the outcome; then freed.
; Kept: the user register x (measured inside the clone, never freed).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; Classical reads (rule 2): 1 (cq_measure(y): y is classical after x's measurement, no gate).
; A callee that MEASURES its quantum argument is not a pure function and has no _unc twin (rule 18): its clone measures
; the handle where the source measures the value, and from there on the callee is classical (the smax is classical
; arithmetic on the outcome). The clone returns the classical int, not a handle, so the caller's call result is
; classical: nothing to copy out, nothing to uncompute. The measurement is the user's: it collapses x and, through
; y = x + c, the entangled y.
; CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2, ruling 2026-10-29): y's only quantum source is x, and x is measured when the clone returns,
; so y is classical from there on although its rail was computed before the measurement. The clone returns smax(m, k),
; not m, so the caller RE-READS x's rail (cqrt_measure_i32 on a measured rail is a classical re-read of the outcome, not
; a measurement: rule 2, ABI 1.3; the backend logs no event), uncomputes y against that rail (which still holds m) and
; recomputes y = m + c by a classical add. The user's cq_measure(y) is a classical read and emits no gate. The argument
; rail is consumed by the measurement and is never freed.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %7 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_readout_10(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = call @readout(%5, %2), quantum clone (arg 0 quantum): measures x inside, returns a CLASSICAL int

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 8, 5, 2.
; Checked: printf_double: cq_measure(x) > 0.0; printf_compound_cond and printf_nested_cond: x + y (measured).
; Clean: the compare flags (x > k), (y > m) and the conjunction flags (compound: (x > k) & (y > m); nested: the inner
; predicate outer & inner).
; Kept: the user registers x (and y); the tape rails (never freed; the backend prints the entries whose predicate
; measured 1).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (printf_double); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (printf_compound_cond, printf_nested_cond).
; Expected tape: printf_double prints "%f" of x unconditionally; printf_compound_cond prints "both x y" iff
; x > k && y > m; printf_nested_cond prints "inner y" iff x > k && y > m, then "outer x" iff x > k.
; 47's tape with three widenings (rule 16). A quantum DOUBLE field is a copy like an integer field: cqrt_tape_write_f64
; appends a fresh write-only f64 rail (the f64 angle rail of rule 15 concerns rotation angles, not data). A COMPOUND
; condition (-O1: select i1 %a, i1 %b, false) is the conjunction flag of 23, built by Toffoli into a |0> rail (rule 8);
; the entry and its fields are controlled by that flag, which is uncomputed after the entry. A NESTED condition is the
; depth-2 predicate of 08: the inner entry is controlled by outer & inner, the outer entry by the outer flag alone, in
; program order. The tape rails are never freed (47).

; Checked: acc (the copied-out result %33 -> %55, measured; where no trip runs the |0> seed %7 -> %12 is measured).
; Clean: every inner trip's rails (the xor %22, the unguarded sum %23, the break flag %24, the carried select %25, the
; old acc %19 and EVERY predicate a_j, the inner chain's last a_{m-1} included), popped and uncomputed by the nested
; reverse loop; each outer trip's |1> seed (%16) and the |0> seed of acc (%7), never written and freed directly.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register) and the measured result rail. No predicate is kept: both bounds are classical, so
; every predicate is a function of the inputs and the mirror uncomputes it (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum exit).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; 27's nested rolled loops composed with 26's quantum break, the break confined to the INNER loop. -O1 tests the break
; after the body and folds it with the classical exit into `select i1 %22, i1 %24, i1 false`; the classical half keeps
; the inner loop a classical loop over all m trips, the quantum half is the trip predicate: inner trip j of outer trip i
; runs iff a_{j-1} (no break before it in THIS inner loop), u_j = acc_{j-1} + (x ^ (i + j)) is computed unguarded
; (pure), the break flag is e_j = u_j > lim, the carried value is acc_j = a_{j-1} ? u_j : acc_{j-1}, and
; a_j = a_{j-1} AND NOT e_j. Each outer trip starts a fresh predicate chain (a_{-1} = |1>): the break resets with the
; inner loop, the outer loop continues. Every trip's rails are pushed and the nested reverse loop pops them (27). If
; n <= 0 or m <= 0 no inner trip ever runs: one classical edge, acc is the seed rail. Both bounds are classical: no K.
; No output rail (rule 14, classical bound with a quantum exit): each outer trip's inner chain pushes its LAST
; predicate a_{m-1} (%26 of inner trip m-1, pushed by block %29 and popped as %37 = %42 of the first inner reverse trip),

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 1, 2, 4, 6.
; Checked: fadd_qc's x + c (%5 -> %6), fsub_qq's x - y (%7 -> %8), fmul_qq's x * y (%7 -> %8), fdiv_cq's c / x
; (%5 -> %6), fneg_q's -x (%4 -> %6), each the function's measured return.
; Clean: fneg_q: the old x rail (%3, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and t = -(-x) (%5), both freed.
; Kept: the rotated f64 register(s) of the other functions (FP arithmetic has no inverse) and every measured result rail.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in fadd_qc, fdiv_cq and fneg_q; (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1) in fsub_qq and fmul_qq.
; Floating-point arithmetic on a quantum double is the f64 width variant of rule 4: each tainted fadd/fsub/fmul/fdiv/fneg
; is one cq_template_<op>_f64 into a fresh rail. A classical operand is a literal: the handle-first form is _hl (x + c)
; and the classical-first form is _lh (c / x, where the order is not commutative); a quantum-quantum op takes two handles.
; The measurement is the sink. fneg is a bijection (a sign-bit flip, NaN included), so in fneg_q the dead x is cleaned by
; rule 6; the rounding ops keep their registers.

; Clean: the condition flag x > k (%8), uncomputed before the measurement and freed.
; Kept: x (%7, the rotated register, measured) and r (%9, rotated by a different angle in each arm and never measured:
; frozen, never reverse-played, never freed).

; The source has two return arms that never meet; at -O1 clang merges every return, so the IR reconverges in a phi of
; the two MEASURED values (%17) under the quantum condition. What remains to lower: the dead register r is rotated by a
; different angle in each arm (the controlled Ry of 39 and its NOT-bracketed twin) and never measured, so it stays
; allocated (frozen). Both arms measure x at the same point, so by rule 2 the two cq_measure calls are ONE unconditional
; measurement of x (the second a classical re-read). The merge phi %17 is then decided by rule 2's CLASSICAL COLLAPSE:
; its condition %8 = (x > k) is computed only from the measured rail x and the classical k, so it is classical. Its rail
; is uncomputed while x still holds the outcome's source state (here before the measurement, right after the last
; controlled Ry it guards), the condition is recomputed from the outcome by an ordinary `icmp sgt` (%11), and the merge
; is a classical `select` (%13); no quantum mux and no select template. No measurement is inserted: the user measures x
; in both arms, and that one measurement decides the return.

  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: %8 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %2  [path predicate of %9; its negation is the predicate of %12]
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %3)    ; IR: %10 / %13 = cq_theta_si32(%3, ...)  [register r, starts as %3 in both arms]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %8, i32 %9, double %4)    ; IR: block %9: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %4)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket: block %12 runs under NOT %8
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %8, i32 %9, double %5)    ; IR: block %12: %13 = cq_theta_si32(%3, %5)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 11, 15, 9, 13, 20, 21, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: r + x (measured) in each function.
; Clean: every flag (x > k1, x > k2; the case flags (x & 3) == 0, 1, 2), every angle rail (the inner selects and A; in
; theta_table_angle A is the bus load copy, un-copied after its last reader, rule 5 sentence 1), the scrutinee / index
; x & 3 (theta_switch_angle, theta_table_angle) and the address chain of &tab[x & 3] (zext / mul / add), all
; uncomputed and freed.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; r (seeded with r0, rotated by the angle rail, measured). No tape slot
; and no load copy is kept: theta_table_angle makes no store.
; Rotations: theta_nested_angle_select: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = select(x > k1, a, select(x > k2,
; b, c)). theta_switch_angle: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = select((x & 3) == 0, p0, select((x & 3) == 1,
; p1, select((x & 3) == 2, p2, p3))). theta_table_angle: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = tab[x & 3],
; tab = {0.1, 0.2, 0.3, 0.4}.
; A MULTI-WAY ANGLE for cq_theta is a QUANTUM ANGLE (rule 11): whatever picks the angle, it is computed into an f64 rail
; by ordinary templates and ONE cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) consumes it (rule 15); the compiler never expands it into
; per-arm controlled Ry, the N-bit ladder is the backend's. The three sources of the angle: a select of selects nests
; its selects (rule 9: the inner select on the inner flag, computed unguarded, is the else arm of the outer one;
; runtime-classical arms are literals, select_f64_ll / _lh); a switch over a quantum scrutinee is the select chain over
; its case eq flags (rule 13; the default is unreachable, so the last case 3 is the complement, needs no flag and is the
; innermost arm, as 49); a constant table read at a quantum index is ONE BUS LOAD at an address rail (rules 20, 21):
; the constant global lives at its host address (HOST cells through the overlay, nothing seeded or registered), and
; the getelementptr with a tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic, the index rail x & 3 brought to i64 by -O1's
; zext, mul_i64_hl by the element size 8 and add_i64_hl of the classical part, the table's address ptrtoint
; (ptr @theta_table_angle.tab to i64) (the constant index 0 contributes 0). The load is qram_load_f64 at that rail,
; m = __cq_mem() once at entry (§5); nothing is known about what the address points to, and no index is narrowed,
; bounded or checked. Its copy A is read only by the rotation and no memory version change follows, so it is un-copied
; right after the rotation (load _unc, free) and the address rail, which outlives the access's _unc (rule 20), is then
; uncomputed LIFO with the index. The register r keeps its classical seed via cqrt_alloc and is rotated once.
; Afterwards the angle chain is uncomputed LIFO and freed, then the flags and the scrutinee (rule 5).
source_filename = "theta_angle_multiway.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18, 9, 15, 2, 10, 5.
; Checked: call_result_as_target's y (the clone's result rail %8 -> %9) and x (%7 -> %10); call_result_as_theta_angle's r
; (%10 -> %11) and x (%6 -> %12); call_result_as_phi_angle's x (%5 -> %9), all measured.
; Clean: every clone-internal rail; call_result_as_theta_angle's and call_result_as_phi_angle's clone result v (%7; %6,
; zeroed by the _unc twin), its uitofp (%8; %7) and the angle register A = fl(s * v) (%9; %8), all freed.
; Kept: x in each function (the rotated register, measured); call_result_as_target's y (%8, rotated in place, frozen,
; measured); call_result_as_theta_angle's r (%10, rotated by the angle rail, frozen, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1); (Ry, y = pick(x, k, a, b), t, 1) in call_result_as_target; (Ry, x, th, 1);
; (Ry, r, val(A), 1) with A = fl(s * pick8(x, k)) in call_result_as_theta_angle; (Ry, x, th, 1); (P, A, val(A), 1) with
; the same A in call_result_as_phi_angle.
; call_result_as_target: the lifted clone __cq_q_pick_1000 (mask left to right, §1.4) hoists both arms, merges them by
; ONE cq_template_select_i32 on the compare flag (rule 9), copies the merge out as the result rail and uncomputes the
; merge and its operands; the caller's second cq_theta is then a plain Ry on the RESULT RAIL: no alloc (the register
; exists), and y is frozen afterwards (rule 10). A QUANTUM-VALUED ANGLE (rule 15, as 79): the angle s * v is computed
; into an f64 REGISTER by ordinary templates (uitofp of the clone's result, fmul_hl by the classical s: the program's
; IEEE double, bit-exact), and the rotation is ONE gate primitive reading that register: cqrt_ry_i32_qangle(r, A) for
; cq_theta, cqrt_rz_qangle(A) for cq_phi (a relative phase, kicked back onto the sources by A's uncompute). The backend
; supplies the N-bit ladder; the IR never spells it. The angle register is only read, so the LIFO spine uncomputes it,
; then the clone's _unc twin (__cq_q_pick8_10_unc) zeroes the result rail as in 07. (Laddering the integer result
; directly, s*2^k per bit, would realize s*v over the reals, not the rounded double fl(s*v).)

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%8, %5): Ry on the result rail itself (no alloc, the register exists)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%9)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 6, 2, 3, 4, 5, 8.
; Checked: y' + x (measured).
; Clean: the compare flag f = (x > k), its zext z, the rule-6 inverse t = y' - z and the OLD y rail (|0> after the
; copy), all freed.
; Kept: none (x and y' are user registers).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1); (Ry, y' = y + [x > k], t, 1).
; -O1 folds `if (x > k) y += 1` into `y + zext(x > k)` (no branch, no phi): the value arm is an ordinary out-of-place add of
; the zext rail into a fresh rail y'. y' then becomes the register of the second cq_theta (rule 2: a rotation of an
; existing handle is in place). Rule 6: the old y rail is dead and y' = y + z is a bijection in y for fixed z, so before the
; non-diagonal Ry on y' the old rail is cleaned: t = y' - z is computed fresh, copy_i32(t, y_old) zeroes y_old, t is
; uncomputed and both are freed; then z and f are uncomputed (their sources x, f are unchanged). Nothing dirty survives
; into the rotation, so no record of the pre-rotation value of y' can dephase it.

target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

name: 145_swap_test
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 6, 9, 2, 4, 5.
; Checked: c | (a' << 1) | (b' << 8) (measured).
; Clean: the two rule-6 inverse rails and the OLD a and b rails (|0> after the copies), all freed.
; Kept: none (c, a', b' are user registers).
; Rotations: (Ry, a, ta, 1); (Ry, b, tb, 1); (Ry, c, pi/2, 1); (Ry, c, -pi/2, 1).
; The swap `if (c) { t = a; a = b; b = t; }` reaches -O1 as two selects on the _Bool rail c: b' = c ? a : b (%8) and
; a' = c ? b : a (%9). Rule 9: each merge is one cq_template_select_i32 into a fresh rail; the condition is the bare i1
; rail c (rule 8). Rule 6: the pair update (a, b) -> (a', b') is a bijection (a controlled swap) and the old values are
; dead, so the old rails are cleaned BEFORE the second rotation of c: a_old = c ? b' : a' and b_old = c ? a' : b' are
; recomputed fresh from the swapped pair, copied onto the old rails (which become |0>), the two inverse rails are
; uncomputed LIFO and everything is freed. Only then is c rotated back by -pi/2: were the old rails still allocated, they
; would hold a which-way record of c and the interference that gives P(c = 0) = (1 + |<a|b>|^2) / 2 would be lost.
source_filename = "swap_test.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [register b]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %3)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [register c, the swap control]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %7, double 0x3FF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %7, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %8 = select i1 %7, i32 %5, i32 %6  [b after the swap, fresh]

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 9, 6, 7, 5.
; Checked: x + n (measured: x as the copied-out x_K, %26 -> %42; n as the carried rail n_K, %18 -> %43, measured directly
; because rule 6 leaves it the only n rail).
; Clean: every x-chain trip rail except a_K (the products, sums, next-x selects, the tests and the predicates a_1..a_{K-1}),
; popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop; the |1> seed is freed directly; the OLD n of every trip (rule 6, in the body:
; n' = a ? n + 1 : n is a bijection in n for every a and the trip predicate reads x, never n, so the arm's garbage n + 1 is
; uncomputed first and t = a ? n' - 1 : n' is copied onto the old n, uncomputed and both freed; trip 0's old n is the |0>
; incoming %7, and trip 0's predicate is the |1> seed, so there t = n' - 1 = 0).
; Kept: a_K, the predicate computed by the last trip's test (the first rail popped by the reverse loop; rule 14: a_K
; = 1 means a fifth body would have run, which is observable). The user register x (%6) stays allocated: x = x * a + b is
; no bijection in x (a may be even) and the exit test reads x, so rule 6 does not apply and the x chain is pushed and
; reversed (x_K is copied out for the measurement).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; A do-while: the body runs before the test, so trip 0's body is unconditional (its predicate is the |1> seed) and the
; test at the END of trip j produces the predicate of trip j+1: a_{j+1} = a_j & (x_{j+1} > k), on the CARRIED value
; (where the loop has already exited the carried x is frozen and a_j = 0 absorbs the test). The loop is re-rolled to K = 4
; bodies and K tests; both carried values advance by a select on a_j (rule 9). Each trip pushes its x-chain rails; x_K is
; copied out (alloc + copy) and a reverse loop pops and uncomputes every trip LIFO, skipping a_K on its first
; iteration. RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31, as in 05): a carried value whose trip update is a bijection and whose
; trip predicate does not read it (n here) is cleaned in the body of the same trip: the new rail is the only one that
; survives, it is not pushed, the reverse loop never sees it, and no copy-out is needed (the measurement reads n_K). The
; do-while changes nothing: trip 0's clean-up is the same code under the |1> seed. A carried value the exit test reads (x)
; cannot be cleaned: x = k and x = k + 1 both leave `x -= 1 under x > k` at k, so that update is not injective (05, 149,
; 54, 68).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
