  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %9  [n before trip 0: trip 0's old n, freed by rule 6 in the body]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of trip 0's body (a do-while body runs unconditionally once)
  br label %9

9:
  %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %23, %9 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %17, %9 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %11, %7 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %5 ], [ %18, %9 ]    ; IR: %9 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %12, %7 ]
  %13 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %22, %9 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip's body
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %10 = mul nsw i32 %8, %2
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %14, i32 %3)    ; IR: %11 = add nsw i32 %10, %3
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: %12 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 1
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %15, i32 %11)    ; IR: next %8 = a ? %11 : %8
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %16, i32 %12)    ; IR: next %9 = a ? %12 : %9  [n_{j+1}: the only n rail after this trip]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %12, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: the arm's garbage %12 is uncomputed first (its _unc reads the old n)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release %12 (|0>)
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %18, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: n' - 1
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %19, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: t = a ? n' - 1 : n' recomputes the old n (the composite update n' = n + a is a bijection in n)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %20, i32 %12)    ; IR: rule 6: old n ^= t: |0> (trip 0: the |0> incoming %7, unchanged; its predicate is the |1> seed, so t = n' - 1 = 0)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %20, i32 %13, i32 %19, i32 %18)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %20)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %19, i32 %18, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute n' - 1
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %19)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: rule 6: release the old n rail (|0> after the copy); it is not pushed
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 %4)    ; IR: %13 = icmp sgt i32 %11, %4  (on the carried x)
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next trip's body
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %13, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %13 taken: a_{j+1} = a_j & cond
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %14)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  %23 = add nuw nsw i32 %10, 1
  %24 = icmp ult i32 %23, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %13, label %7, label %14  [K]
  br i1 %24, label %9, label %25

25:
  %26 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %15 = cq_measure_si32(%11): the carried x  [copied-out result; n needs none: rule 6 left n_K the only n rail]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %17, i32 %26)    ; IR: %11 of the last trip
  br label %27

27:
  %28 = phi i32 [ 0, %25 ], [ %39, %38 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %29 = phi i32 [ %17, %25 ], [ %35, %38 ]    ; IR: %8 written by this trip
  %30 = phi i32 [ %22, %25 ], [ %34, %38 ]    ; IR: predicate produced by this trip's test
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %36 = icmp eq i32 %28, 0    ; IR: reverse index 0 is trip K-1: the predicate its test produced is a_K, the output rail (rule 14)
  br i1 %36, label %38, label %37

37:
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %34, i32 %31, i32 %30)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate produced by this trip (trips 0..K-2)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %38

38:
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %29, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %29, i32 %34, i32 %32, i32 %35)    ; IR: uncompute next %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release next %8 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %32, i32 %33, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release %11 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %33, i32 %35, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release %10 (|0>)
  %39 = add nuw nsw i32 %28, 1
  %40 = icmp ult i32 %39, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %40, label %27, label %41

41:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  %42 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %26)    ; IR: %15 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  %43 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %18)    ; IR: %16 = cq_measure_si32(%12)  [n_K, the carried rail: rule 6 left no other n rail, so no copy-out; the |0> incoming %7 was freed as trip 0's old n]
  %44 = add nsw i32 %43, %42    ; IR: %17 = add nsw i32 %16, %15  (classical)
  ret i32 %44    ; IR: ret i32 %17
}

name: 151_return_in_kloop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 8, 9, 7, 5.
; Checked: i (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail, every trip predicate (the K-th included) and the after-trip-K return test; the |1> seed and
; the i seed are freed directly.
; Kept: a_K (%22: the return test x_K == k evaluated after the K-th body, negated and ANDed with trip K's predicate;
; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, i.e. the return was not taken within K trips nor at the
; test after them, which is observable; a loop whose return is taken at that test reads 0). The user register x stays
; allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; `for (;;) { if (x == k) return cq_measure(i); ... }` is a loop whose only exit is the return, tested at the top of each
; trip (-O1: the pre-header `x == k` is trip 0's test, the latch `x/2 == k` the next trip's). It is re-rolled to K = 4 trips
; under the chain a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT(x_j == k): the exit flag is X-bracketed into the Toffoli (rule 8). The returned
; value is the carried i, which the selects on a_j freeze at the trip where the return was taken (rule 9), so the
; fall-through after K trips and every early return read the same copied-out rail. After the K-th trip the return test
; is evaluated once more on x_K and a_K = (predicate of trip K) & NOT(x_K == k) is kept (rule 14); the test is uncomputed
; at once. Each trip pushes its rails; the mirror pops and uncomputes LIFO, every trip predicate included.

define i32 @return_in_kloop(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {

  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %10 / %7  [i before trip 0]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the first test in %3 (always 1)
  br label %7

7:
  %8 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %18, %7 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %9 = phi i32 [ %4, %3 ], [ %16, %7 ]    ; IR: %11 = phi i32 [ %12, %9 ], [ %4, %3 ]
  %10 = phi i32 [ %5, %3 ], [ %17, %7 ]    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ %13, %9 ], [ 0, %3 ]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %3 ], [ %13, %7 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = icmp eq i32 %4, %2 (trip 0) / %14 = icmp eq i32 %12, %2  [the return flag]
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip's body (block %9)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %12)    ; IR: bracket: the trip runs when the return is NOT taken
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %11, i32 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: br i1 %5 / %14 not taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT e
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %12)    ; IR: bracket
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_lshr_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 1)    ; IR: %12 = lshr i32 %11, 1
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 1)    ; IR: %13 = add nuw nsw i32 %10, 1
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %14, i32 %9)    ; IR: next %11 = a ? %12 : %11
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %13, i32 %15, i32 %10)    ; IR: next %10 / %7 = a ? %13 : %10  (frozen once the return was taken)

  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %10)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %14)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)

  %19 = icmp ult i32 %18, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %14, label %6, label %9  [K]
  br i1 %19, label %7, label %20

  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %16, i32 %2)    ; IR: %14 = icmp eq i32 %12, %2 after trip K: the return test that would decide a (K+1)-th trip
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & NOT that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %13, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %14 not taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %21, i32 %16, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %21)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %23 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %13, %9 ]  [copied-out result: the carried i]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %17, i32 %23)    ; IR: %7
  br label %24

24:
  %25 = phi i32 [ 0, %20 ], [ %35, %24 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %26 = phi i32 [ %16, %20 ], [ %34, %24 ]    ; IR: %11 written by this trip
  %27 = phi i32 [ %17, %20 ], [ %33, %24 ]    ; IR: %10 written by this trip

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %26)    ; IR: release next %11 (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release %12 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %31)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %32, i32 %31, i32 %28)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; a_K is a separate rail)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %31)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %34, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %5 / %14
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release %5 / %14 (|0>)
  %35 = add nuw nsw i32 %25, 1
  %36 = icmp ult i32 %35, 4    ; IR: K  [K]

37:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release incoming 0 of phi %10 (never written, |0>)
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %23)    ; IR: %8 = cq_measure_si32(%7)
  ret i32 %38    ; IR: ret i32 %8
}

name: 152_phase_in_kloop
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (quantum-dependent exit, cutoff K), 8, 10, 12, 9, 7, 5.
; Checked: r + x (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail and every trip predicate, the K-th included (the phase-arm flags are uncomputed inside their
; trip); the after-trip-K exit test; the |1> seed is freed directly.
; Kept: a_K (%24: the exit test x_K > k evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with trip K's predicate; rule 14: a_K = 1
; iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0). r is a user register: it
; is rotated in place under a_j every trip and FROZEN (rule 10: never reverse-played, never freed), then measured. The
; user register x stays allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); for each trip j = 0..3: (P, h_j, p, a_j && (x_j & 1) != 0), (Ry, r, t, a_j) where a_j =
; AND_{i<=j} (x_i > k) and x_i = x >> i.
; The loop is 05's K-loop (trip j runs under a_j = a_{j-1} & (x_j > k)) with two gates in its body. The phase arm `if (x & 1)
; cq_phi(p)` is a nested quantum branch inside the trip: its path predicate a_j & NOT(x_j & 1 == 0) is one X-bracketed
; Toffoli into a fresh |0> flag h_j (rule 8; -O1 tests the FALSE edge `== 0`), the phase is a kickback on h_j (rule 12),
; and h_j, the compare and the `and` are uncomputed right after the kickback, inside the trip (rule 5: their sources x_j
; and a_j are unchanged, so no push is needed). The in-place cq_theta(&r, t) under the trip is rule 10:
; cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(a_j, r, t) on the one r rail seeded with the classical 0; nothing reads r, so a_j can still be
; uncomputed afterwards (it reads x only). The carried x advances by a select on a_j; after K trips it is copied out and the
; mirror pops and uncomputes LIFO, every trip predicate included. Before the copy the exit test is evaluated once more
; on x_K and a_K = (predicate of trip K) & (x_K > k) is kept (rule 14); the test is uncomputed at once.

  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %9 / %20  [register r: the classical 0, rotated in place below, frozen]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the loop guard in %5 (always 1)
  br label %9

9:
  %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %5 ], [ %20, %9 ]    ; IR: trip index, bounded by K  [K]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %19, %9 ]    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ %16, %14 ], [ %6, %5 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %14, %9 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = icmp ugt i32 %6, %2 (trip 0) / %17 = icmp ugt i32 %16, %2
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip (block %8)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %13, i32 %14)    ; IR: br i1 %7 / %17 taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & cond_j
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 1)    ; IR: %11 = and i32 %10, 1
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 0)    ; IR: %12 = icmp eq i32 %11, 0  (block %13 is its FALSE edge)
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: path predicate of block %13 = a_j & NOT %12  [fresh |0> flag]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket: block %13 runs under NOT %12
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %16, i32 %17)    ; IR: br i1 %12 inside the trip, false edge
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %17, double %3)    ; IR: block %13: cq_phi(%3)  [kickback on the path predicate]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %16, i32 %17)    ; IR: uncompute the %13 predicate (a_j, %12 unchanged)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %16)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)    ; IR: release the %13 predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %15, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %12

  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %11, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %14, i32 %7, double %4)    ; IR: block %14: %15 = cq_theta_si32(%9, %4)  [Ry in place on r under a_j; r frozen]
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_lshr_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 1)    ; IR: %16 = lshr i32 %10, 1
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %14, i32 %18, i32 %11)    ; IR: next %10 = a ? %16 : %10
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %11)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %13)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  %20 = add nuw nsw i32 %10, 1
  %21 = icmp ult i32 %20, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %17, label %8, label %18  [K]
  br i1 %21, label %9, label %22

22:
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl(i32 %19, i32 %2)    ; IR: %17 = icmp ugt i32 %16, %2 after trip K: the exit test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip
  %24 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %14, i32 %23, i32 %24)    ; IR: br i1 %17 taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %23, i32 %19, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %23)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %19 = phi i32 [ %6, %5 ], [ %16, %14 ]  [copied-out result: the carried x]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %19, i32 %25)    ; IR: %19
  br label %26

26:
  %27 = phi i32 [ 0, %22 ], [ %34, %26 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %28 = phi i32 [ %19, %22 ], [ %33, %26 ]    ; IR: %10 written by this trip
  %29 = phi i32 [ %14, %22 ], [ %32, %26 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %30 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %28, i32 %29, i32 %30, i32 %33)    ; IR: uncompute next %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release next %10 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_lshr_i32_hl_unc(i32 %30, i32 %33, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %16  (the controlled Ry on r is frozen: not reverse-played)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release %16 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %32, i32 %31, i32 %29)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; it reads x only, never r)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_ugt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %33, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %7 / %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release %7 / %17 (|0>)
  %34 = add nuw nsw i32 %27, 1
  %35 = icmp ult i32 %34, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %35, label %26, label %36

36:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %21 = cq_measure_si32(%20): the r rail itself
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %25)    ; IR: %22 = cq_measure_ui32(%19)
  %39 = add i32 %38, %37    ; IR: %23 = add i32 %22, %21  (classical)

}

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (nested quantum-dependent exits, cutoff K, chain seeded by the arm flag), 9, 8, 7, 5.
; Checked: s (measured).
; Clean: every trip rail of both loops and every trip predicate, the K-th of each chain included; the after-trip-K exit
; tests (uncomputed right after their output rail is formed); the else-arm value, the arm flag and the s seed are freed.
; Kept: (rule 14) A_K (%40: the outer exit test x_K > k evaluated after outer trip K, ANDed with that trip's
; predicate) and, per outer trip, B_K (%33: the inner exit test z_K > k evaluated after inner trip K, ANDed with that
; trip's predicate; minted in the outer latch, never pushed): 5 output rails in all. A_K = 1 iff the outer loop would run
; a (K+1)-th trip; a B_K = 1 iff that outer trip's inner loop would; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0.
; The user registers x and y stay allocated.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; Two nested K-loops inside the then-arm of `if (x > c)`. The arm flag F = (x > c) SEEDS the outer chain (rule 14: a loop
; in an arm takes the arm flag instead of |1>): A_i = A_{i-1} & (x_i > k) with A_{-1} = F, so where the arm is not taken
; nothing in the loops changes. Each outer trip's inner chain is seeded by that trip's predicate: B_j = B_{j-1} & (z_j > k)
; with B_{-1} = A_i (-O1's hoisted guard %13 is inner trip 0's test); z_0 is the user register y. Every carried value (s, z,
; x) advances by a select on its chain's predicate (rule 9). The arm itself merges by one select on F between the loops'
; final s (the seed 0 where no trip ran, covering the [0, %10] incoming) and the else-arm value x + y, computed unguarded;
; the merge is a fresh result rail, so nothing is copied out. The mirror is 139's nested reverse: pop the outer trip's
; rails, run the inner reverse (every inner predicate uncomputed), uncompute the outer predicate and its compare.
; F is uncomputed last, after the chain it seeded has been torn down.

; lifted clone __cq_q_f_10 (rule 18, §1.4 mask: x quantum, c classical): the clone computes x * c + 1 out of place,

; XORs the result out and uncomputes, after which the caller frees the result rail. The compare is one flag E on the
; result rail; the phase block's path predicate F & E is one and_i1 into a fresh |0> flag G (rule 8), the phase is a
; kickback on G (rule 12: a quantum predicate is in scope). Teardown is LIFO: G, E, the call result (twin), F, all before

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 5, 8, 9.
; Checked: the returned int R = m + x_m with m = (x_m > k) ? y_m : c (classical: x and y measured).
; Clean: the flag F = (x > k) and the select rail m, uncomputed after x's measurement (classical collapse, rule 2).
; Kept: the user registers x and y (both measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; A cq_measure INSIDE A QUANTUM ARM (rule 2). A measurement is never conditioned on quantum data: the cq_measure of y
; is executed UNCONDITIONALLY at its program point, so y is collapsed on the F = 0 branch as well, a deviation from the
; C program's branch-conditioned measurement that is the user's responsibility (the compiler may warn). The flag F is
; never measured. At the arm's merge F still reads the unmeasured x, so m = F ? y_m : c is a quantum select (rule 9)
; into a fresh rail. Then x is measured. From that point F and m depend only on measured rails and classical values,
; so CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2) applies: m's select and F's compare are uncomputed while x's rail still holds its
; outcome (§1.3: a measured rail may be read as an operand), and F, m and R are recomputed by ordinary classical
; instructions from the outcomes. The function returns a plain int; no handle escapes. 140 is the same collapse with
; the measurement before the merge.

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %4)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %4  [flag F: path predicate of block %10]
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: block %10: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%8)  [executed unconditionally (rule 2): never conditioned on F]
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %9, i32 %10, i32 %5)    ; IR: %13 = phi i32 [ %11, %10 ], [ %5, %6 ]  [m = F ? y_m : c, a quantum select while x is unmeasured]

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 21, 5, 7, 4, 3, 2; §1.3 (the bus and its overlay).
; Checked: r = table[(i + 1) & 7] + c (measured, %18 -> %19); the cells of table at exit, read from the bus at
; &table + 4 j: table[j] = (j == (i & 7)) ? v : 0 (its initial host bytes, the zeroinitializer, elsewhere).
; Clean: the store's address chain (and / zext / mul / add: %7..%10), uncomputed and freed right after the store; the
; load's address chain (add / and / zext / mul / add: %12..%16) and the load copy %17, un-copied and uncomputed before
; the measurement.
; Kept: the register i (%6, frozen); the store's tape slot (it holds the displaced 4 cells of table[i & 7]: their prior
; content, 0 on every branch for a first call, earlier calls' values otherwise) and its value rail, the seed %11 = |v> (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 7: a basis state, no qubit); the measured
; result rail %18. One tape slot per call: the kept slots grow with the number of calls.
; Rotations: (Ry, i, ti, 1).
; Expected for global_qram(0, .5, 9, 4): (i + 1) & 7 never equals i & 7, so the load reads a cell the store did not
; write, which still holds its initial 0 on every branch, and r = 4 with probability 1; the 4 bytes at
; &table + 4 (i & 7) hold 9 on each branch of i.
; ONE BUS (rule 20): `static int table[8]` is an ordinary global at its host address. Nothing is allocated, seeded or
; registered for it (no constructor, no handle cell, no QRAM of its own): its cells are on the one bus M through the
; overlay and start HOST, holding the zeroinitializer's host bytes. m = __cq_mem() is fetched once at function entry.
; @table is not isConstant, so it is not host-resident and both accesses are bus accesses (rule 20); the indices are
; tainted, so each address is a rail and the plain (not _hl) forms are used. Nothing is known about an
; address at compile time: each getelementptr with a tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic into an address
; rail: the index rail brought to i64 (-O1's zext nneg, the zext template), scaled by mul_i64_hl(., 4) and added to

; value is always a handle). It is KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3): no _unc exists, its tape slot and its seed stay. The

; together with the chain that produced it (its last reader is the store).

name: 161_opaque_callee
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 27, 19, 18, 7, 2, 4, 5, §1.1 (escaped rail), §1.4 (table clones), §0.
; Checked: the returned rail ext_fn(x, c) + m, where m = cq_measure(x) (an UNMEASURED quantum result: the ret carries
;          its handle, §1.1, checked as that rail's basis value).
; Clean: the clone result r when the twin zeroes it (the twin frees it, §1.4; the caller frees no result of a table
;        clone); the seed of the classical c (never written, freed directly after the twin, rule 7).
; Kept: the register x (measured), the returned rail (escapes with the return; never freed), and r where ext_fn's
;       twin does not zero it (no rule-18 twin: KEPT; a FROZEN result, rule 19), as §1.4 states.
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x.
; ext_fn has no body in this module, so rule 27 applies: the call becomes a call to the DECLARED clone, which is the
; table clone of §1.4, named from the callee's C signature alone: __cq_q_ext_fn_11_t, every mask digit 1, no _b
; bounds. Every scalar actual is a handle: x is its register, the classical c is minted as a seed alloc_i32(c)
; (rule 7). K follows as a trailing classical i32 (here the corpus default 4): the clone's quantum-exit loops run
; min(K, B) trips. The result r is a handle; its twin __cq_q_ext_fn_11_t_unc(r, x, c_seed, K) always exists and pops
; what the clone pushed. Both use the default C calling convention. Whatever is linked defines them; if nothing
; does, linking fails with an undefined symbol. The call is a memory version change (rule 5); no other memory
; version change follows it, so the twin runs at its rule-18 position (rule 19): after r's last use, the add.
; r is quantum, so r + m is the out-of-place add_hl with the classical outcome m as the literal (rule 4). x is
; measured by then, which is allowed (§1.3: a measured rail may still be read as an operand); after the measurement
; every branch holds r = ext_fn(m, c), which the twin recomputes and XORs out.
source_filename = "opaque_callee.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @opaque_callee(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = call @ext_fn(%4, %2): the classical c as a seed (rule 7; rule 27: every actual a handle)
  %6 = call i32 @__cq_q_ext_fn_11_t(i32 %4, i32 %5, i32 4)    ; IR: %5 = call @ext_fn(%4, %2): the declared (table) clone, two handles and K (rule 27); a memory version change; result r is a handle  [K]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %4)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_si32(%4)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: %7 = add nsw i32 %6, %5  (r quantum, m classical: commutative, spelled _hl)
  call void @__cq_q_ext_fn_11_t_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %5, i32 4)    ; IR: twin of %5: r to |0> and freed by the twin (its last use was %7; rule 19 at its rule-18 position)  [K]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the seed c (never written, rule 7)
  ret i32 %8    ; IR: ret i32 %7  (the handle of the returned rail, §1.1)
}

name: 162_quantum_return_entry

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: §1.1 (escaped rail), 19, 18, 2, 4, 5, 6, §0.
; Checked: quantum_return_consumer's measured q * 2. quantum_return_entry returns an UNMEASURED quantum value: its
;          `ret i32` carries the HANDLE of the x + c rail (§1.1), checked as that rail's basis value.
; Clean: in the entry the old x rail (%4, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and t = r - c (%6), both freed; in the consumer
;        nothing (its only garbage-free rail is the frozen result of the call).
; Kept: quantum_return_entry: the returned rail (escapes with the return; never freed).
;       quantum_return_consumer: the rail the call returns (FROZEN: the rule-6 image of the register x the callee minted
;       and rotated; never uncomputed, never freed) and the measured rail.
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x in the entry (reached once per consumer call).
; An ENTRY function keeps its C signature (i32), and a quantum value returned through it is the i32 handle of the rail:
; the rail escapes to the caller and is never freed by the callee. The register x is dead after the add, a bijection in x
; for fixed c, so rule 6 cleans it before the return: a caller may rotate the returned rail, and a kept x would dephase it.
; Inside the entry the body is the ordinary rule-4 chain: one add_hl into a fresh rail, returned directly. The CONSUMER
; calls the entry (rule 19, ruling 2026-11-02: the compiler never inlines; a callee reached with no quantum argument whose
; body reaches a rotation is called as it is). The callee's result record says the returned handle is a FROZEN rail: the
; rule-6 image of the register x minted inside, so no twin exists for it and the consumer keeps it exactly as it would keep
; a register of its own. q * 2 (-O1: shl 1) is a fresh rail, measured; the returned rail stays allocated. A clone
; __cq_q_quantum_return_entry_000 would have the entry's own signature and body (no quantum argument, no extra result: the
; minted register was absorbed by rule 6), so the entry IS the clone and the call targets it (§1.4). Until 2026-11-02 this
; consumer inlined the entry's body (x minted here, q uncomputed against it); same rotation, same qubit count kept.
source_filename = "quantum_return_entry.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @quantum_return_entry(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = add nsw i32 %4, %2  [the result rail]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: t = r - c recomputes the old x (the update is a bijection in it)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %6, i32 %4)    ; IR: rule 6: x ^= t: the dead x rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the old x rail (|0> after the copy)
  ret i32 %5    ; IR: ret i32 %5  (the i32 is the HANDLE of the x + c rail: an escaped rail, never freed; x was cleaned by rule 6)

  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 1)    ; IR: %5 = shl nsw i32 %4, 1  [result rail]
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_si32(%5)
  ret i32 %6    ; IR: ret i32 %6  (the returned %4 rail stays allocated: frozen, never freed)

name: 163_sret_return
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 16, 18, 20, 21, 26; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc), §1.4.
; Checked: r.a + r.b + r.c (the add rail %16, measured -> %17) = ((x + c) + (x * c) + c) mod 2^64; the cells of r on
; the bus at exit: r.a = x + c, r.b = x * c, r.c = c (8 bytes each at offsets 0, 8, 16).
; Clean: sret_return: the three load copies r.a, r.b, r.c (%8, %11, %15; un-copied, no memory version change follows
; the loads) and the partial sum r.b + r.a (%12). __cq_q_mk_010: nothing (every rail it makes is the value rail of a
; kept store).
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register), the sum rail %16 (measured); by rule 5 sentence 3 the three tape slots of the
; clone's stores `store i64 %4, ptr %0`, `store i64 %6, ptr %5`, `store i64 %2, ptr %7` and their value rails: the add
; rail x + c (%6 in the clone), the mul rail x * c (%9 in the clone) and the seed c (%12 in the clone, rule 7).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected for the driver sret_return(0, .5, 3): Ry(.5) flips each of the 64 bits of x independently with probability
; s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087; x unchanged (= 0, probability (1 - s)^64 = 0.0176) measures (0 + 3) + 0 * 3 + 3 = 6.
; SRET IS A POINTER FORMAL LIKE ANY OTHER (rule 26, §1.4): mk(sret &r, x, c) is the clone of mask 010 (the sret pointer
; a classical ptr, x a rail, c classical), __cq_q_mk_010(ptr, i32, i64); nothing about the pointee (its fields, their
; kinds, the struct type) appears in the name or the parameter list and no handle crosses the call through memory.
; The sret attribute stays on the formal and the call, an ABI note, spelled with the literal type { i64, i64, i64 }
; (renumber_locals.py would read a named %struct.big as a local value). mk's own symbol has no caller left: dropped.
; THE ALLOCA IS BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 b): r is a call argument, so it is __cq_alloc(24, 8) at the alloca's program point,
; no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). -O1's byte-offset geps (8, 16) have nothing tainted
; and stay as they are: the struct keeps its C layout in memory, and every field access is ONE i64 bus access at the
; classical address (rule 20 store size; S = 8 cells).
; WHAT THE CLONE STORES IS KEPT (rules 5, 18). Each of the three stores is a kept bus store at a classical address
; (qram_store_i64_hl): its tape slot stays for the shot and so does its value rail. r.a = x + c and r.b = x * c are
; therefore not uncomputed in the clone, and the classical c is stored as a seed alloc_i64(c) kept with its store
; (rule 7): every store is a bus store and its value always a handle (§1.3). mk writes memory, so __cq_q_mk_010 has NO
; twin and returns nothing (void). The caller's loads come after the call (a memory version change) and are bus loads
; whose results are rails (rule 3), r.c included: the last add is rail + rail (cq_template_add_i64), not _hl.
; LOAD COPIES (rule 5 sentence 1): r.c's copy (%15) is un-copied right after its last reader, the measured add %16,
; which is never uncomputed and so has no _unc to wait for; then the partial sum %12 is uncomputed and the copies of
; r.b and r.a are un-copied after its _unc, all before the measurement (the sentence's convention), with no memory
; version change after the loads.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no calling convention, linkage or attributes for a clone called by name; it keeps the callee's
; (internal fastcc, unnamed_addr) as 31, 195 and 200 do, and the memory, capture and nullness facts of mk (noalias,
; nocapture, writable, writeonly, dead_on_unwind, memory(argmem: write), nofree, willreturn) are dropped (§1.4).
; Regenerated 2026-11-05 for the flat memory model: the previous version (one handle cell per quantum field, a twin
; that zeroed copy rails through the slot) belonged to the retired model.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

name: 164_byval_large
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 22, 20, 21, 16, 18, 5 (in-place form, Readers clause), 7, 2, 3, 4; §1.3, §1.4.
; Checked: sum3(p, c) = p.a + p.b * c + p.c (the clone's copied-out result rail, measured, both entries); the cells of
; the caller's block of p at exit (read from the bus at its address): a = the rotated register, b, c as stored (_two: b
; the rotated register too); the cells of the byval copy at exit: the same 24 bytes. Both paths of each run-time
; disjointness test d (below) give these values.
; Clean: on each DISJOINT path (d = 1) the swap rail of the in-place form (|0> after its swap-in, freed); inside
; __cq_q_sum3_00 (both calls): the three load copies p.a, p.b, p.c (un-copied after their last reader,
; no memory version change follows them in the clone, rule 5 sentence 1) and the template rails b * c, the two adds
; (uncomputed by their _unc after the copy-out, rule 18).
; Kept: on each DISJOINT path the cell that holds the rotated register (p.a in _one; p.a and p.b in _two: rotated in
; place, rule 5's in-place form); on each OVERLAP path (d = 0) the load copy of the cell taken before the first
; intervening store (rotated, so a FROZEN register, rule 2; the value rail of the kept store) and that kept store's tape
; slot (rule 5 sentence 3); the measured result rail (rule 2; no twin is called); by rule 5 (sentence 3) and rule
; 7: the three seed stores of the initializer {x0, b, c} / {x0, y0, c} with their seeds (tape slot + seed rail each);
; by rule 22: the 24 byte load copies of
; the byval copy, each the value rail of a kept byte store, and the 24 byte stores' tape slots.
; Rotations: byval_large_one: DISJOINT (Ry, p.a, tx, 1); OVERLAP (Ry, the load copy of p.a, tx, 1).
; byval_large_two: (Ry, p.a, tx, 1) on DISJOINT d_a, (Ry, the load copy of p.a, tx, 1) on OVERLAP d_a; then (Ry, p.b,
; ty, 1) on DISJOINT d_b, (Ry, the load copy of p.b, ty, 1) on OVERLAP d_b. Each path is chosen by a CLASSICAL run-time
; branch, never a control.
; Expected (driver): the three cells of one 24-byte block never overlap, so every d is 1 and every OVERLAP block is
; emitted and never runs. byval_large_one(0, .5, 2, 3) measures a + 2 * 3 + 3 = a + 9, a = 0 with every bit flipped
; independently with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 (P(9) = (1 - p)^64 = 0.0176); byval_large_two(0, .5, 1, .25, 3) measures
; a + 3 * b + 3, b = 1 with every bit flipped with q = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544 (the unflipped branch a = 0, b = 1 gives 6 with (1 - p)^64 (1 - q)^64 = 0.0064).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21, 26). A 24-byte struct passed BY VALUE travels as a `byval` pointer to a caller-made copy. The
; caller's alloca %struct.big is BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b): a store of a tainted value and the call are among its
; users), so it is __cq_alloc(24, 8) at its program point and its lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). The struct
; initializer is three ordinary kept bus stores at the run-time addresses p, p + 8, p + 16, each value a seed (rule 7).
; cq_theta(&p.a, tx) is, after -O1, cq_theta_sl on the parameter x0 forwarded from the store to cell a, followed by
; `store %8, ptr %5` to the same cell: rule 5's IN-PLACE FORM on the cell, whose interval runs from the store of x0
; (rule 5, Readers: the forwarded y). The same for p.b in _two (y0 forwarded from the store to cell b).
; READERS (rule 5). The interval of each form holds memory version changes: in _one the stores to b and c lie between
; the store of x0 and the rotation; in _two the form on a has the stores to b and c in its interval, and the form on b
; has the store to c and the form (or kept store) on a in its. Every change is a bus store or in-place form at a
; classical address (S_q = 8 cells) and every cell address is a getelementptr/ptrtoint chain over the block's address,
; computable before the first change (the lowered code computes the chain of c there, ahead of where -O1 places it).
; So d is the AND of one test per change, q - p >= 8 && p - q >= 8 (mod 2^64, unsigned, S_p = 8), computed ONCE
; immediately before the first change of the interval, where the one copy is taken, and branched on TWICE: `br d`
; around a plain load of p (the copy, taken when d = 0), the changes emitted once, then `br d` at the rotation's store:
;   DISJOINT (d = 1): the cell still holds the forwarded value; the in-place form stands: alloc_i64(0),
;   qram_swap_i64_hl (the rail holds the cell, the cell |0>), the Ry on the rail, qram_swap_i64_hl back, free.
;   OVERLAP (d = 0): the Ry acts on the copy (frozen from there on, never un-copied) and the store is an ordinary kept
;   store of it.
; The copy's handle reaches the second branch through a classical phi whose d = 1 incoming is poison. The rotated value
; has no SSA reader (the byval copy reads the block through the bus), so no join phi of handles follows the form.
; In _two the two intervals interleave: d_a and a's copy come before the store to b, d_b and b's copy after it and
; before the store to c; a's second branch precedes b's (the program order of the two rotations).
; THE BYVAL COPY (rule 26): at the call the caller makes the copy, q = __cq_alloc(24, 8) (the byval's size and align),
; and a rule-22 bus copy of 24 bytes from p to q: a host loop of 24 qram_load_i8_hl at p + j, each handle pushed, then a
; host loop of 24 qram_store_i8_hl at q + j popping them (bytes 23 down to 0); every byte store is kept with its load
; copy as value rail (rule 22). The call passes q as a PLAIN pointer: no `byval` on a lowered call, and the callee is
; the plain-ptr form of §1.4, spelled by the clone grammar even with the all-zero mask: q is a classical ptr (digit 0)
; and c classical (digit 0), so both entries call the ONE clone __cq_q_sum3_00. Nothing about the pointee (which fields
; are quantum) crosses the call. sum3's own symbol keeps the C signature for host callers; it is internal and has no
; caller left, so it is dropped (§1.4).
; THE CLONE (rules 3, 18): every load is a bus load and its result is a rail, also in the all-zero mask, so all three
; fields are rails whatever the caller stored (over-taint, §0: a classical-valued rail costs no qubit), and the result
; is a rail. It forms the sum out of place (mul_i64_hl, then two add_i64 of rails), copies the result into a fresh
; rail and uncomputes its chain; each load copy is un-copied right after its last reader (the _unc of its consumer).
; The clone writes no memory, so a twin could exist; the caller measures the result (rule 2: the measured rail stays),
; so no twin is called and none is defined (§1.4).
; SPEC GAP (rule 26, byval): the copy is made at the call's program point, immediately before the call: __cq_alloc,
; then rule 22's load loop over the source and its store loop into q.

define i64 @byval_large_one(i64 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i64 noundef %2, i64 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (§5: once, at function entry)
  %6 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 24, i64 8)    ; IR: %5 = alloca %struct.big, align 8: bus-resident (rule 20), one zeroed block (rule 16); llvm.lifetime.start dropped
  %7 = ptrtoint ptr %6 to i64    ; IR: %5 as its run-time address (cell a)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %0)    ; IR: store i64 %0, ptr %5: the classical value as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i64 %0, ptr %5  (kept store, rule 5); the interval of the form on cell a starts here (x0 is forwarded)
  %9 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 8    ; IR: %6 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 8  (nothing tainted: the gep stays)
  %10 = ptrtoint ptr %9 to i64    ; IR: %6 as its run-time address (cell b)
  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 16    ; IR: %7 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 16  (computed here, before the first change: rule 5, Readers)
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %11 to i64    ; IR: %7 as its run-time address (cell c)
  %13 = sub i64 %10, %7    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p mod 2^64, p = cell a, q = cell b (the first change)
  %14 = icmp uge i64 %13, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p >= S_p, S_p = 8 cells
  %15 = sub i64 %7, %10    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q mod 2^64
  %16 = icmp uge i64 %15, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q, S_q = 8 cells
  %17 = and i1 %14, %16    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: cells a and b disjoint
  %18 = sub i64 %12, %7    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p mod 2^64, q = cell c (the second change)
  %19 = icmp uge i64 %18, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p >= S_p
  %20 = sub i64 %7, %12    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q mod 2^64
  %21 = icmp uge i64 %20, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q
  %22 = and i1 %19, %21    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: cells a and c disjoint
  %23 = and i1 %17, %22    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: d = the AND of the tests of both changes, computed immediately before the first of them
  br i1 %23, label %26, label %24    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: d = 1 DISJOINT: no copy is taken; d = 0 OVERLAP: the copy below

24:
  %25 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: the forwarded %0 as a rail: a plain load of %5 taken before the memory version changes (rule 5, Readers)  [OVERLAP path only]
  br label %26    ; IR: (no instruction)

26:
  %27 = phi i32 [ poison, %4 ], [ %25, %24 ]    ; IR: (no instruction) the copy's handle on the OVERLAP path (classical phi; poison, never read, on the DISJOINT path)
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %2)    ; IR: store i64 %2, ptr %6: the seed (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %10, i32 %28)    ; IR: store i64 %2, ptr %6  (kept store; a memory version change in the interval, emitted once)
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %3)    ; IR: store i64 %3, ptr %7: the seed (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %12, i32 %29)    ; IR: store i64 %3, ptr %7  (kept store; a memory version change in the interval, emitted once)
  br i1 %23, label %30, label %32    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: the same d, at the store's position: DISJOINT: the form stands; OVERLAP: the step acts on the copy

30:
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 0)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_sl(%0, %1); store i64 %8, ptr %5: %0 is forwarded from the store to the same cell: in-place form, the swap rail (|0>)  [DISJOINT path]
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %31)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_sl(%0, %1): swap-out: the rail holds the cell's %0 (untouched by the changes), the cell |0>
  call void @cqrt_ry_i64(i32 %31, double %1)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_sl(%0, %1)  [Ry in place on p.a]
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %31)    ; IR: store i64 %8, ptr %5: swap-in: the cell holds register p.a
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release the swap rail (|0>)
  br label %33    ; IR: (no instruction)

32:
  call void @cqrt_ry_i64(i32 %27, double %1)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_sl(%0, %1)  [Ry on the load copy: a frozen register from here on, rule 2]  [OVERLAP path]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %27)    ; IR: store i64 %8, ptr %5  (a kept store: no _unc, its tape slot and its value rail stay, rule 5 sentence 3)
  br label %33    ; IR: (no instruction)

33:
  %34 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 24, i64 8)    ; IR: %9 = call @sum3(byval(%struct.big) align 8 %5, ...): the byval copy q (rule 26)
  %35 = ptrtoint ptr %34 to i64    ; IR: q as its run-time address
  br label %36    ; IR: the byval copy: a rule-22 bus copy of 24 bytes from %5 to q (load all, then store all)

36:
  %37 = phi i64 [ 0, %33 ], [ %40, %36 ]    ; byte index of the load loop (classical)
  %38 = add i64 %7, %37    ; the source byte's address (classical)
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl(i32 %5, i64 %38)    ; IR: byval copy  [source byte j: a bus load; the copy is the value rail of byte j's store, KEPT (rule 22)]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %39)    ; the handle outlives its SSA value (§1.1, rule 22)
  %40 = add nuw nsw i64 %37, 1
  %41 = icmp eq i64 %40, 24
  br i1 %41, label %42, label %36

42:
  %43 = phi i64 [ 24, %36 ], [ %44, %42 ]    ; bytes left to store (classical)
  %44 = add nsw i64 %43, -1    ; byte index of this store: 23 down to 0 (the pop order)
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; the load copy of byte %44
  %46 = add i64 %35, %44    ; the destination byte's address (classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %5, i64 %46, i32 %45)    ; IR: byval copy  [destination byte: a kept store (rule 22)]
  %47 = icmp eq i64 %44, 0
  br i1 %47, label %48, label %42

48:
  %49 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_sum3_00(ptr noundef %34, i64 noundef %3)    ; IR: %9 = call fastcc @sum3(ptr byval %5, i64 %3): the plain-ptr form (§1.4, rule 26), mask 00 (classical q, classical c); the result rail
  %50 = call i64 @cqrt_measure_i64(i32 %49)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_sl(%9)  (the measured rail stays allocated; no twin, rule 2)
  ret i64 %50    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end(%5) dropped (rule 16); ret i64 %10
}

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_sum3_00(ptr noundef %0, i64 noundef %1) unnamed_addr {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (§5: once, at function entry)
  %4 = ptrtoint ptr %0 to i64    ; IR: %0 as its run-time address (mask digit 0: the formal is the C ptr)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl(i32 %3, i64 %4)    ; IR: %3 = load i64, ptr %0  [p.a: every load is a bus load, a rail (rule 3)]
  %6 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %0, i64 8    ; IR: %4 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %0, i64 8  (nothing tainted: the gep stays)
  %7 = ptrtoint ptr %6 to i64    ; IR: %4 as its run-time address

  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %0, i64 16    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %0, i64 16
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %11 to i64    ; IR: %8 as its run-time address

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %3, i64 %4)    ; IR: un-copy %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, i64 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %3, i64 %7)    ; IR: un-copy %5

define i64 @byval_large_two(i64 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i64 noundef %2, double noundef %3, i64 noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (§5: once, at function entry)
  %7 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 24, i64 8)    ; IR: %6 = alloca %struct.big, align 8: bus-resident (rule 20), one zeroed block (rule 16); llvm.lifetime.start dropped
  %8 = ptrtoint ptr %7 to i64    ; IR: %6 as its run-time address (cell a)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %0)    ; IR: store i64 %0, ptr %6: the seed (rule 7)

  %12 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %7, i64 16    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 16  (computed here, before the first change of a's interval: rule 5, Readers)
  %13 = ptrtoint ptr %12 to i64    ; IR: %8 as its run-time address (cell c)
  %14 = sub i64 %11, %8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers (form on a): q - p mod 2^64, p = cell a, q = cell b (the first change)

  %16 = sub i64 %8, %11    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q mod 2^64
  %17 = icmp uge i64 %16, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q, S_q = 8 cells
  %18 = and i1 %15, %17    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: cells a and b disjoint

  %22 = icmp uge i64 %21, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q

  %24 = and i1 %18, %23    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: d_a = the AND of the tests of both changes, computed immediately before the first of them

  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %2)    ; IR: store i64 %2, ptr %7: the seed (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %11, i32 %29)    ; IR: store i64 %2, ptr %7  (kept store; a change in a's interval, emitted once); the interval of the form on cell b starts here (y0 is forwarded)
  %30 = sub i64 %13, %11    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers (form on b): q - p mod 2^64, p = cell b, q = cell c (the first change)
  %31 = icmp uge i64 %30, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p >= S_p, S_p = 8 cells
  %32 = sub i64 %11, %13    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q mod 2^64
  %33 = icmp uge i64 %32, 8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q, S_q = 8 cells
  %34 = and i1 %31, %33    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: cells b and c disjoint
  %35 = sub i64 %8, %11    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p mod 2^64, q = cell a (the second change: a's form or kept store)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 18, 1, 3, 4, 5, §1.4.
; Checked: r.a + r.b (struct_i64_i32_one, measured); r.a and r.b (struct_i64_i32_both, each measured).
; Clean: struct_i64_i32_one: the sext rail and the result rail r.b (zeroed by the twin, freed by the caller), the
;        clone's chain. struct_i64_i32_both: the clone's chain (both result rails are measured and stay).
; Kept: the rotated registers (p.b; p.a and p.b), frozen; the measured rails.
; Rotations: Ry(tb) on p.b; Ry(ta) on p.a and Ry(tb) on p.b.
; A 12-byte struct { long, int } is coerced to the two-register aggregate { i64, i32 } at the C ABI, in and out: here
; -O1 needs no shifts or masks, the fields already arrive as separate SSA values. Under rule 26 the aggregate is a
; tuple of fields: a quantum field is an i32 handle, a classical one keeps its C type, and extractvalue / insertvalue
; on it are classical (no gate). The clone takes the fields in order (§1.4, one digit per field of the aggregate, then
; c): __cq_q_bump_010(i64 a, i32 b handle, i32 c) returns { i64 classical r.a, i32 handle r.b } (the classical field
; r.a = a + c is ordinary host arithmetic inside the clone); __cq_q_bump_110(i32 a handle, i32 b handle, i32 c) returns
; { i32, i32 } of two handles (r.a = a + sext(c) is an add_hl of the i64 handle by the classical sign-extended c). Each
; clone copies its quantum results into fresh rails and uncomputes its chain (rule 18). struct_i64_i32_one sign-extends
; the handle r.b by a cast template, adds the classical r.a (commutative: handle first), uncomputes the cast, runs the
; twin to zero r.b and frees it. struct_i64_i32_both measures both result rails directly: no twin runs (51 / 71) and
; the final add of the two outcomes is classical.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 18, 8, 9, 4, 5, 7, 13, 14, 19, 23, 24 (and 3, 1).
; Checked: complex_div_q_c: creal(q) + cimag(q) (measured); complex_div_c_qq: creal(q) and cimag(q) (two measurements, classical sum).
; Clean: every rail but the registers (re; c and d), the measured result rails and the one Kept rail below; this includes
;   the fenv rails of the strictfp ilogb clone (the caller's empty flags rail, the two INVALID selects, the two ORed flags
;   states, the flags phi of logb and both clones' returned flags copies: fenv state the program never reads, dropped).
; Kept: a_K of __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl (ilogb's subnormal-loop exit test i<<1 >= 0 evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with
;   trip K's predicate a_4; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run a (K+1)-th trip, an exact-K exit reads 0; the shl
;   recurrence has no LLVM range bound below K, so it is kept; the clone's predicate seeds the chain, so a_K reads 0
;   where logb does not call ilogb): one rail per ACTIVATION of the loop (rule 14, as a nested
;   loop keeps one inner a_K per outer trip): __cq_q___divdc3_0011 runs __cq_q_logb_1 forward once and its twin once, and
;   the twin re-runs the forward ilogb clone (strictfp ilogb cannot be inlined into it), so complex_div_c_qq keeps two;
;   __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl_unc itself keeps nothing).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on re (first entry); Ry(tc) on c, Ry(td) on d (second entry). The clones hold no rotation.
; Complex division has no inline fast path: clang always calls __divdc3, the compiler-rt body reproduced in the .c file, so the
; whole divide is one lifted call (rule 18). The two entries reach it with different taint: mask 1000 (a = creal(z) quantum,
; b, c, d classical) and mask 0011 (c, d quantum), one clone each; every classical op of the body stays classical IR and every
; op with a handle operand is an out-of-place template (rule 4, the _hl/_lh shapes with the classical value as a literal). The
; libm calls inside the body follow the same taint: logb/scalbn with classical arguments are the plain calls of the O1.ll,
; a quantum argument makes them clones of the injected musl bodies (rule 18): __cq_q_scalbn_10 and __cq_q_scalbn_11
; (musl scalbn.c), __cq_q_logb_1 (musl logb.c) and __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl (musl ilogb.c). The PINNED SOURCE AS BUILT is normative
; for every function the .c does not define (owner ruling 2026-10-29, cq-ezan): the bundle's clang -O1 IR of musl b1efda5,
; whose values the `; IR:` comments of the clones name. ilogb.c carries `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON`, so its IR is
; strictfp: it cannot be inlined into logb (no pragma) and its clone follows 82's fenv ABI (rule 23): the caller's mode
; and flags rail as two trailing parameters, { result, flags' } returned, both copied into fresh rails before the body is
; uncomputed, the _unc twin taking both returned handles first. __divdc3 has no FENV_ACCESS, so its environment is the
; default: __cq_q___divdc3_0011 passes the mode literal 0 (FE_TONEAREST) and mints an EMPTY flags rail (|0>, rule 7) that
; it frees directly after the twins; the returned flags are fenv state the program never reads and are dropped (uncomputed
; by the twin, freed). logb calls ilogb only in its finite-nonzero block, under a quantum predicate. ilogb holds a
; quantum-exit loop whose a_K is kept, so the callee is its _ctl clone (rule 19): __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl(P, x, mode, flags)
; with P the predicate of logb's block %11 (!%3 & !%7), and the twin __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl_unc(P, outs, args). P only seeds
; the loop's chain; the templates and the copy-out run unguarded (§1.4) and are merged, so logb's result phi AND its
; flags phi are the same nested
; selects, the flags arms of the blocks that do not call ilogb being the caller's flags. In __cq_q_ilogb_1_ctl the subnormal
; loop `for (e = -0x3ff; i>>63 == 0; e--, i<<=1);` has a quantum exit: it is rule 14's ROLLED loop of K = 4 trips (lines
; tagged [K]: the trip counter against the literal 4), its chain seeded by P & the arm predicate (e == 0 & i<<12 != 0),
; the pre-header guard %12 being trip 0 of the latch test %21, so each trip is test then body (as 05). i advances by a
; select on the trip predicate. e is an affine induction (start -1023, step -1): its value in a trip is the classical
; -1023 - (trip index + 1), recomputed from the trip index in the forward and in the reverse loop and never pushed; only
; its exit value is a carried rail, advancing by a select on the trip predicate (rule 14). Each trip pushes the handles
; its _uncs read; the reverse loop pops K trips. After the K-th body the latch test is evaluated once more and
; a_K = a_4 & test is kept; that test is uncomputed at once, and every
; trip predicate a_1..a_4 (the K-th body's included) by the reverse loop. The two FORCE_EVAL(0/0.0f) of ilogb (the zero arm,
; block %13 under S0 & i<<12 == 0, and the inf/nan arm, block %22 under S2047) are constrained.sitofp(0) = 0.0f and
; constrained.fdiv(0.0f, 0.0f): two literals, so the quotient is a classical NaN stored volatile to a dead local (no gate,
; rule 24), and its INVALID bit is fenv state: flags' = flags | select(pred, FE_INVALID = 1, 0) (65's spelling); the mode
; is passed but not read (a NaN in every rounding mode). The `switch` on the exponent field is one equality flag per case
; and the default is the complement (rule 13). fabs/fmax(maxnum)/copysign/fptosi/sitofp and every fcmp predicate (ueq = !isfinite, une, ord, uno) are templates.
; Every tainted branch is a flag (rule 8): `select i1 %a, i1 true, i1 %b` is the disjunction or_i1, `and i1` the

; Path predicates of the nested if/else-if ladder (P37, P41, P45, P57, P71, P78) are and_i1 chains; the two five-incoming
; phis of %94 are three select templates each on the disjoint path predicates P57, P78, P41 with the complement value (%31 /
; %26, the plain result) innermost (rule 9); the two-incoming phis merge on the local flag with the arms in flag order.

; into a fresh rail; the product is uncomputed by its fmul _unc right after the sum it fed and freed (rule 5). A classical
; product (both factors classical, quantum addend) is a classical fmul and an fadd_hl with the addend's handle first
; (commutative); otherwise the product factors are commutable, so a handle is put first (fmul _hl). Each clone copies its two results into fresh rails,

; two copies directly (c_qq: nothing calls a twin of __cq_q___divdc3_0011, so none is defined (§1.4); the copies are the

; before the measurement (rule 5).

; rint(x) (%4 -> %5), fmax(x, c) (%5 -> %6), each the function's measured return.

; Kept: each function's rotated f64 register x and its measured result rail.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18 (the musl hypot body is inlined by clang, so it lowers in the entry), 20, 3, 4, 5, 8, 9 (and 1).
; Checked: cabs_quantum_re: hypot(re, im) (measured, %60 -> %61); cabs_quantum_both: hypot(re, im) with both quantum
; (measured, %62 -> %63).
; Clean: every flag, select and arithmetic rail of both entries, all freed before the measurement.
; Kept: the registers (re %4; re %5 and im %6) and the two measured result rails (%60, %62).
; Rotations: (Ry, re, tr, 1) in cabs_quantum_re; (Ry, re, tr, 1), (Ry, im, ti, 1) in cabs_quantum_both.
; cabs is hypot; musl's body is static and clang -O1 inlines it, so no clone appears: the whole function is
; straight-line templates in the entry. The `union { double f; unsigned long long i; }` views are SSA values (rule 20):
; a bitcast template between f64 and i64, the exponent read is lshr + trunc, and fabs clears the sign. The conditional
; swap `if (ux.i < uy.i)` is one icmp flag and two selects (rule 9). Every `return` of the if ladder is an exit edge:
; the four-incoming phi of %63 is three nested selects on the local branch flags (%18: return y; %22 = or_i1 of the two
; equality flags: return x; %25: x + y), innermost the sqrt path, so each select is dominated by the previous flag's
; false case and no path conjunction is needed; the three-incoming phis of %38 (the scaling by 2^+-700 and z) are two
; nested selects on %29 and %34 the same way. The split x = hx + lx goes through fptrunc / fpext templates, the two
; llvm.fmuladd sums (lx, ly) UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14): an fmul into a fresh product rail, then an fadd of product and
; addend, the product uncomputed after the sum, and sqrt is a template. In the second entry the compare, the selects and
; the sum are two-handle templates (both operands quantum). Everything but the result rail is uncomputed LIFO and freed
; before the measurement.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (bool x[nq] stores rails (the cq_theta results): a BUS-RESIDENT runtime-sized alloca,
; __cq_alloc(nq, 16) at its program point (rule 16: one zeroed block, a classical size); every access is a bus access at
; the cell's run-time address, gep then ptrtoint, classical: _hl), 5 / 2 (each `cq_theta(x[i])` stored straight back is
; the in-place form at width i1 (Width casts: alloc_i1(0), qram_swap_i1_hl, ry_i1 on the swap rail, qram_swap_i1_hl,
; free; 205's bool_cell_rotate): the cells are the registers and no handle is ever stored (§1.1); the init loop's
; `store i8 0` is a kept store of a seed (rules 5, 7) and opens the interval of the first form, whose y is the false -O1
; forwarded from it (rule 5, Readers)), 5 sentence 1 (every other read of x[i] is a plain bus load at width i1: the
; parity loop's copies are un-copied by the reverse loop after the parity _unc that reads them, the default arm's copy
; right after its kickback, the measure loop's copies are measured and stay), 14 (every loop has the classical bound nq
; and stays a ROLLED classical loop; the case-2 parity loop is a classical-bound loop with a quantum body: each trip loads
; x[i] and computes the next parity into a fresh rail, pushes the previous parity and the load copy, and a reverse loop
; pops and uncomputes them after the kickback), 7 (the |0> parity seed is freed directly; each `store i8 0` seed is kept
; with its store), 13 / 8 (the `switch` on the classical selector stays a classical switch; the one quantum branch
; `br i1 %24` is a flag kickback per incoming arm), 4 (p ^= x[i], -O1's `icmp ne i8 cell, zext(p)` on two i1-valued i8s
; (!range [0,2)), is cq_template_xor_i1 into a fresh rail, as 113: the zext i1 -> i8 of the parity rail is that rail's
; i1-valued view, no gate), 12 (the case-1 edge reaches cq_phi(pi) under no quantum predicate at any depth: a global
; phase, deleted; the other two edges are under the quantum flag and kick back), 21 (the cell addresses are classical
; integers; inbounds is never consulted).
; Checked: m = sum x[i] << i, x[i] the cells x + i of the bus block (read by the measure loop's load copies).
; Clean: the case-2 parity rails (nq of them), the parity seed and the nq load copies of x[i] the parity loop takes; the
; default arm's load copy of x[0]; the swap rail of every in-place form (2 nq of them, |0> after the swap-in).
; Kept: per cell, the seed alloc_i8(0) of `store i8 0` and that store's tape slot (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 7; nq each);
; the nq load copies of x[i] the measure loop measures (rule 2). The cells are the registers.
; Rotations: Ry(pi/2) on the cells x[0..nq-1] (control 1); then exactly one of (classical switch on sel):
;   sel == 0: nothing;  sel == 1: nothing (global phase deleted);
;   sel == 2: P(pi) on flag(x0 ^ ... ^ x[nq-1])   [control predicate: the parity of x; nothing when nq <= 0];
;   default:  P(pi) on the load copy of x[0]     [control predicate x0: a basis copy of the cell, un-copied at once];
; then Ry(-pi/2) on the cells x[0..nq-1] (control 1).

;   slots are classical |0> records (the cells hold 0 when the store is made), every load copy that a phase or a parity
;   reads is un-copied before the next swap of its cell, and the default arm's P(pi) on a basis copy of x[0] is P(pi) on
;   the cell; so the outcomes are unchanged (analytic, not replayed; the trace stubs compute nothing).

; case 2 to the parity loop (guarded by nq > 0; nq <= 0 goes to the join with p = false), and the default to a load of
; x[0]; the two quantum arms meet in `phi i1 %24` and `br i1 %24` guards the phase block. The handle phi under classical
; control is not emitted: its only consumer is the kickback, which is emitted per arm because the case-2 arm must
; uncompute its own parity rails and load copies, and the default arm its load copy. The parity loop's carried
; `phi i1 %13`, seeded by the literal false, is a carried rail seeded by alloc_i1(0) (rule 7). No memory version change
; lies between a parity load and its _unc (the loop and its mirror only load), so sentence 1 un-copies them all; the
; same holds for the default arm's load.
; The init loop: `store i8 0, ptr %27; %28 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2); %29 = zext; store i8 %29, ptr %27`. The
; cq_theta's operand is the value -O1 forwarded from the store of 0 to the same SSA pointer, and nothing lies between
; that store and the store of %29: the in-place form, emitted at the second store's position (the swap-out reads the 0
; the cell holds).
; SPEC GAPS (marked at the line):
;  1. The forwarded y of rule 5's Readers clause is here a classical literal (false, from `store i8 0`), not a rail and
;     not a `load; trunc`, and rule 2 says a cq_theta of a classical v mints alloc_<W>(v). Chosen: the in-place form at
;     width i1 (the cell is the register). The mint read would rotate a fresh rail and make `store i8 %29` a kept
;     store of it: the cell would then hold a CNOT copy of a kept register, and the later in-place Ry(-pi/2) on the cell
;     would act on a dephased qubit (DJ would no longer give m == 0 iff f is constant).

7:; IR: block %6

9:; IR: block %25  (x[i] = false; H^n: the Ry(pi/2) loop, classical bound nq)

  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 %10    ; IR: %27  (the cell x[i])
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %11 to i64    ; IR: %27 as its run-time address (classical)

  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i64 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: store i8 0, ptr %27  (a kept store: no _unc, its tape slot and its seed stay, rule 5 sentence 3)
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %28 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2): in-place form at width i1 on the value forwarded from that store (rule 5, Readers, Width casts), the swap rail (|0>)  SPEC GAP 1: a forwarded classical literal opens the form (not rule 2's mint)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i1_hl(i32 %3, i64 %12, i32 %14)    ; IR: %28: swap-out: the rail holds x[i] (0), the cell's low bit |0>
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %14, double 0x3FF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %28 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [Ry(pi/2) on x[i]]

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the swap rail (|0>)
  %15 = add nuw nsw i64 %10, 1    ; IR: %30  (classical)
  %16 = icmp eq i64 %15, %8    ; IR: %31  (classical)
  br i1 %16, label %17, label %9    ; IR: br i1 %31, label %8, label %25

17:; IR: block %8

    i32 0, label %46
    i32 1, label %46
    i32 2, label %18
  ]

18:; IR: block %9  (case 2: f = parity of x)
  %19 = icmp sgt i32 %0, 0    ; IR: %10  (classical)
  br i1 %19, label %20, label %46    ; IR: br i1 %10, label %11, label %33  (nq <= 0: p = false, no phase)

20:; IR: edge %9 -> %11
  %21 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: incoming false of phi %13  [p before trip 0: a |0> seed rail]
  br label %22    ; IR: br label %11

22:; IR: block %11  (p ^= x[i], classical bound nq)
  %23 = phi i64 [ %29, %22 ], [ 0, %20 ]    ; IR: %12  (classical i)
  %24 = phi i32 [ %28, %22 ], [ %21, %20 ]    ; IR: %13 = phi i1 [ %17, %11 ], [ false, %9 ]  (the carried parity rail)
  %25 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 %23    ; IR: %14  (the cell x[i])
  %26 = ptrtoint ptr %25 to i64    ; IR: %14 as its run-time address (classical)
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i1_hl(i32 %3, i64 %26)    ; IR: %15 = load i8, ptr %14  (!range [0,2): a plain bus load of the form's cell, taken at width i1, rule 5 Width casts)
  %28 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i1(i32 %27, i32 %24)    ; IR: %16 = zext i1 %13 to i8 (a view, no gate); %17 = icmp ne i8 %15, %16  [= x[i] ^ p on i1-valued i8s: the next parity, a fresh rail]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %24)    ; IR: trip-local rail on the handle stack (rule 14): the previous parity
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %27)    ; IR: trip-local rail on the handle stack (rule 14): the load copy of x[i] (un-copied by the mirror, rule 5 sentence 1)
  %29 = add nuw nsw i64 %23, 1    ; IR: %18  (classical)
  %30 = icmp eq i64 %29, %4    ; IR: %19  (classical)
  br i1 %30, label %31, label %22    ; IR: br i1 %19, label %23, label %11

31:; IR: block %23 reached from %11  (%24 = phi i1 [ %17, %11 ]; br i1 %24 -> block %32)
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %28, double 0x400921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %24 = phi i1 [ %17, %11 ]; br i1 %24 -> block %32: cq_phi(pi)  [kickback on the parity flag]
  %32 = add nsw i64 %4, -1    ; IR: (mirror of the parity loop: undoes trip nq-1 down to 0; classical)
  br label %33    ; IR: (mirror)

33:; IR: reverse loop over the parity trips
  %34 = phi i64 [ %32, %31 ], [ %40, %33 ]    ; IR: i of the trip being undone  (classical)
  %35 = phi i32 [ %28, %31 ], [ %37, %33 ]    ; IR: %17 of the trip being undone
  %36 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the trip's load copy of x[i] (%15)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the trip's incoming parity (%13)
  call void @cq_template_xor_i1_unc(i32 %35, i32 %36, i32 %37)    ; IR: uncompute %17 of that trip
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %38 = getelementptr i8, ptr %5, i64 %34    ; IR: (the cell x[i], recomputed from the trip index)
  %39 = ptrtoint ptr %38 to i64    ; IR: (its run-time address, classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i1_hl_unc(i32 %36, i32 %3, i64 %39)    ; IR: un-copy %15 of that trip after its last reader (rule 5 sentence 1: the cells unchanged since the load)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %40 = add nsw i64 %34, -1    ; IR: (classical)
  %41 = icmp eq i64 %34, 0    ; IR: (classical)
  br i1 %41, label %42, label %33    ; IR: (classical)

42:; IR: end of the mirror

43:; IR: block %20  (default: f = x[0])
  %44 = ptrtoint ptr %5 to i64    ; IR: %4 as its run-time address (classical)
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i1_hl(i32 %3, i64 %44)    ; IR: %21 = load i8, ptr %4; %22 = trunc nuw to i1  (a plain bus load of x[0] at width i1, rule 5 Width casts)
  call void @cqrt_rz_i1(i32 %45, double 0x400921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %24 = phi i1 [ %22, %20 ]; br i1 %24 -> block %32: cq_phi(pi)  [phase on the bare rail %22 itself: a diagonal gate on a basis copy of the cell, no flag]
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i1_hl_unc(i32 %45, i32 %3, i64 %44)    ; IR: un-copy %21 right after its last reader (rule 5 sentence 1)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %45)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %46    ; IR: br label %23 -> br label %33

46:; IR: block %33 (the join)
  %47 = icmp sgt i32 %0, 0    ; IR: %34  (classical)

48:; IR: block %35

50:; IR: block %37

  br i1 %51, label %52, label %61    ; IR: br i1 %38, label %39, label %50

52:; IR: block %39

54:; IR: block %41  (H^n: the Ry(-pi/2) loop, classical bound nq)
  %55 = phi i64 [ 0, %48 ], [ %59, %54 ]    ; IR: %42  (classical i)
  %56 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %5, i64 %55    ; IR: %43  (the cell x[i])

  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %58, double 0xBFF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %46 = cq_theta_i1(%45, -pi/2)  [Ry(-pi/2) on x[i]]
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i1_hl(i32 %3, i64 %57, i32 %58)    ; IR: %47 = zext; store i8 %47, ptr %43: swap-in: the cell holds %46
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %58)    ; IR: release the swap rail (|0>)

  %60 = icmp eq i64 %59, %49    ; IR: %49  (classical)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (bool x[nq] is -O1's `alloca i8, i64 nq`; it stores tainted values, so it is BUS-RESIDENT:
; __cq_alloc(nq, 16), every access a bus access at its run-time address), 5 (each cq_theta of a cell is the in-place form
; through the Width-casts clause; Memory sentences 1 and 3), 2 (the cq_theta's own width i1; the measured load copies),
; 21 (gep, then ptrtoint: classical addresses, _hl), 16 (__cq_alloc), 14 (the H^n loop, the value loop, the H^n loop and
; the measure loop have the classical bound nq and stay ROLLED classical loops; the value loop pushes its four trip-local
; rails per trip, the load copy included, and a reverse loop pops and uncomputes them), 7 (v's |0> seed is freed directly;
; on the nq <= 0 path the literal 0 reaching `phi i32 %20` is materialised as a seed rail too, so the phi is all handles;
; the seed of each `store i8 0` is that kept store's value rail), 4 (v is zext_i8_to_i32 / shl_i32_hl / or_i32 into
; fresh rails; the oracle is and_i32_hl against the runtime s, ctpop_i32, and_i32_hl 1, icmp_eq_i32_hl 0, every one a
; fresh rail), 8 (the compare rail is the branch flag; the phase arm sits on the FALSE edge of `parity == 0`, so it is the
; X-bracketed kickback), 12 (the cq_phi is under a quantum predicate: not deleted); §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc).
; Checked: m = sum x[i] << i: each measured x[i] (the i1 load copy of cell i, IR %60/%61 -> %62). The cells of the block on
; the bus at exit: the low bit of x[i] holds the measured outcome of x[i] (its high 7 bits 0), 0 <= i < nq.
; Clean: per H^n trip (both loops), the swap rail of the in-place form (|0> after the swap-in, freed); per value trip, the
; i8 load copy of x[i] (IR %29, un-copied by the reverse loop after the zext _unc, before H^n swaps the cells: rule 5
; sentence 1) and the zext, shl and or rails; the flag, the three oracle rails (and, ctpop, and) and the seed of v.
; Kept: the cells x[0..nq-1] themselves (the registers live in memory: rotated in place, read through load copies); by
; rule 5 sentence 3, per trip of the FIRST H^n loop only (the second H^n loop stores nothing: its store is the in-place
; form's swap-in), the tape slot of the kept store `store i8 0, ptr %14` and its value seed alloc_i8(0) (classical-valued,
; no qubit, rule 7); by rule 2, the nq measured i1 load copies (IR %60).
; Rotations: Ry(pi/2) on cell x[i], i = 0..nq-1 (control 1); P(pi) on NOT flag(popcount(v & s) & 1 == 0)  [control
;   predicate: the parity of x & s is odd, i.e. (-1)^{x.s}]; Ry(-pi/2) on cell x[i], i = 0..nq-1 (control 1); each Ry in
;   place on its cell through the form's swap rail.
; Expected: m = s mod 2^nq with probability 1 (analytic: the cells are the registers and nothing outside them stays
;   entangled with them when H^n runs the second time). bernstein_vazirani(4, 11) -> m = 11; bernstein_vazirani(5, 19)
;   -> m = 19; every free hits |0>.
; -O1 keeps the source structure: H^n as a rolled loop that stores 0 into x[i] and calls cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2) (the
; 0 forwarded from that store), v as an nq-trip accumulator loop (zext nneg i8 -> i32 of the cell, shl by the trip index,
; or into the carried i32 seeded by the literal 0), the oracle as `and`, ctpop, `and 1`, `icmp eq 0` with the cq_phi
; block on the FALSE edge, H^n again as `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext; store i8`, and the measure loop
; as `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_measure_i1`. Each loop is guarded by its own `nq > 0` test.
; ONE BUS (rules 16, 20, 21). The alloca's users include stores of a tainted value (the rotated bit), which rule 20 (b)
; does not allow: the block is __cq_alloc(nq, 16) at its program point (zeroed, an address never reused) and no alloca
; remains. The size is classical (nq is a parameter): no K2, no overflow predicate. Every gep has an untainted index and
; stays; its ptrtoint is the classical _hl address. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). No handle is ever
; stored (§1.1): the cells hold the qubits.
; THE FIRST H^n LOOP. `store i8 0, ptr %14` is an ordinary bus store of a classical value: the seed alloc_i8(0) and
; qram_store_i8_hl, KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3; value, address and control classical-valued, so the cell stays HOST). The
; cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2) rotates the value -O1 forwarded from that store to the same SSA pointer %14, and its result is
; stored back through %14 (zext to i8) with no memory version change between: rule 5's in-place form (Readers: y is the
; forwarded value; Width casts: the form at width i1): alloc_i1(0), qram_swap_i1_hl, ry_i1 on the swap rail,
; qram_swap_i1_hl, free (SPEC GAP 1).
; THE VALUE LOOP is the accumulator of 117's value(x): a bus load of the i8 cell (qram_load_i8_hl), zext_i8_to_i32, shl,
; or into fresh rails; the trip's previous accumulator, load copy, zext and shl rails are pushed. Its mirror runs after
; the kickback and before H^n swaps the cells, and only when the value loop ran (the same classical nq > 0 test): the
; load copy's last reader is the zext _unc in the mirror, and no memory version change lies between the load and that
; point, so it is un-copied there (rule 5 sentence 1). `v & s` has a quantum and a classical operand: the _hl template
; with the runtime literal s; ctpop is the unary intrinsic template of 56. The kickback P(pi) under `parity odd` is the
; phase oracle (-1)^{x.s}, so H^n (-1)^{x.s} H^n |0> = |s>.
; THE SECOND H^n LOOP: `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1(-pi/2); zext; store i8` on one SSA pointer is the in-place
; form through the Width-casts clause, as 58 and 117.
; THE MEASURE LOOP: each `load i8; trunc nuw to i1` is a plain bus load at width i1 (SPEC GAP 2, as 117, 205), measured
; and kept (rule 2: a measured load copy is never un-copied).
; SPEC GAP 1: rule 5's Readers clause forwards y from "the preceding store to p", and its Width-casts clause starts from
; `load T p; trunc T to U`. Here -O1 forwarded the stored i8 0 as the i1 literal false straight into cq_theta (no load,
; no trunc). Chosen: the in-place form at width i1 from the kept store's position (the cell holds the forwarded 0), not
; rule 2's mint alloc_i1(false) + a kept store of its zext copy, which would leave the register's rail and the store's
; value rail entangled with the cell.
; SPEC GAP 2: the measure loop's `load i8; trunc nuw i8 to i1` is no reader of a form's SSA value (another loop). Chosen
; as 117 and 205: one qram_load_i1_hl at the trunc's width (§1.3: the low bit of the cell), no trunc template.
