name: 180_teleport
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2 (three cq_theta on classical false mint |0> rails and rotate them; `cq_theta(&a, -pi/2)` and
; `cq_theta(&c, -theta)` rotate existing rails in place; the three cq_measure_i1 are measure_i1 and every dominated use of the
; measured value is classical), 4 (`b = a ^ b` is cq_template_xor_i1 OUT OF PLACE into a fresh rail, the CNOT fan-out that
; makes the Bell pair; the X correction `c ^ m1` is cq_template_xor_i1_hl out of place with the classical m1 as literal),
; 6 (the old c rail after the X correction is dead and xor is a bijection in c for fixed m1: cleaned and freed),
; 8 (`if (m2 && c)`: the classical conjunct m2 is a classical branch around the quantum part; the quantum part is the bare
; rail c, so the phase is rz_i1 on c itself), 12 (cq_phi(pi) is under the quantum predicate c: not deleted),
; 3 (`c = b ^ 0` was folded by -O1: %3 is ONE rail that is both b and c until the CNOT; after it, %4 is b and %3 stays c).
; Checked: c (the final measured rail, %7; the return value).
; Clean: the old c rail %3 (rule 6: t = c' ^ m1 recomputes it, copy_i1 zeroes it, t is uncomputed) and t (%8), both freed.
; Kept: a (%2) and b (%4), measured and therefore never freed; c (%7, the corrected rail), measured at the end. The old b
;   rail after `b = a ^ b` is NOT a dead value to clean by rule 6: it IS the register c (c = b ^ 0 == b), read by the X
;   correction. Were it dead, rule 6 would clean it right after the CNOT, before the H on a (the inverse reads a).
; Rotations: Ry(theta) on a (control 1); Ry(pi/2) on b (control 1); Ry(-pi/2) on a (control 1);
;   [after the measurements, classical control:] P(pi) on c (%7) under the classical m2 (control predicate: m2 & c, with
;   c the bare rail); Ry(-theta) on c (%7, control 1). The X correction is a basis permutation (xor_i1_hl), not a rotation.
; Expected: teleport(0.7): the final measurement is 0 with probability 1 on every one of the four (m1, m2) branches, each
;   branch having probability 1/4 (state-vector replay of the trace with scripted outcomes: fidelity 1 on 00, 01, 10, 11,
;   every cqrt_free on |0>).
; What -O1 did: `c = b ^ c` with c = 0 is c = b, so %3 (the Ry(pi/2) rail) is both names; `b = a ^ b` is `%4 = xor i1 %2, %3`;
; `if (m1) c = !c` became `%8 = xor i1 %3, %6` (c xor the measured bit); `m2 && c` became `select i1 %7, i1 %8, i1 false` with
; the cq_phi block under it; the final cq_theta reads %8. Lowering: %4 is a fresh rail, so the state after it is
; sum_a amp(a) |a>_a |a ^ b>_b' |b>_c with (b, c) the Bell pair: the textbook circuit. H on a is Ry(-pi/2) in place. Both
; Bell outcomes are classical from their measurement on. `%8 = xor i1 %3, %6` has the classical m1 as an operand, so it is
; the _hl template into a fresh rail (rule 4, no branch: m1 is the literal), and the old c rail is cleaned by rule 6.
; `%9 = m2 && c` is a classical branch on m2 around the quantum predicate c itself, under which cq_phi(pi) is rz_i1 on c
; (the bare-rail phase of 118). The recipient's Ry(-theta) is in place on c; the measurement follows.
source_filename = "teleport.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @teleport(double noundef %0) {
  %2 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %2 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [register a, from |0>]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %2, double %0)    ; IR: %2 = cq_theta_i1(false, %0)  [Ry(theta): the state to send]
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [register b, from |0>; also c: `c = b ^ 0` is c = b, one rail for both names until the CNOT]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %3, double 0x3FF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_i1(false, pi/2)  [Ry(pi/2) on b]
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i1(i32 %2, i32 %3)    ; IR: %4 = xor i1 %2, %3: b = a ^ b out of place (rule 4) into a fresh rail  [register b from here on; %3 remains c: the CNOT fan-out is the Bell pair (b, c) followed by CNOT a -> b]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %2, double 0xBFF921FB54442D18)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_i1(%2, -pi/2)  [H on a: Ry(-pi/2) in place; %5 is a's rail]
  %5 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %4)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_i1(%4)  [m1; b's rail stays allocated]
  %6 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = cq_measure_i1(%5)  [m2; a's rail stays allocated]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i1_hl(i32 %3, i1 %5)    ; IR: %8 = xor i1 %3, %6: c ^ m1 OUT OF PLACE (rule 4) with the measured, classical m1 as the literal operand (rule 2)  [register c from here on]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i1_hl(i32 %7, i1 %5)    ; IR: rule 6: t = %8 ^ m1 recomputes the old c (xor is its own inverse in c for fixed m1)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %8, i32 %3)    ; IR: rule 6: old c ^= t: the dead %3 rail is now |0>
  call void @cq_template_xor_i1_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, i1 %5)    ; IR: uncompute t

  call void @cqrt_ry_i1(i32 %7, double %11)    ; IR: %13 = cq_theta_i1(%8, %12)  [Ry(-theta) in place on c: the recipient un-rotates]
  %12 = call i1 @cqrt_measure_i1(i32 %7)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_i1(%13)
  %13 = zext i1 %12 to i32    ; IR: %15  (classical)

}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 18 (the musl atan body is static and inlined by clang -O1, so it lowers in the entry), 20 (two bus loads at address rails), 21, 5, 8, 9, 3, 4 (and 1, 2), section 2.
; Checked: atan(x) * c (measured, %74 -> %75).
; Clean: every flag, select and arithmetic rail of the entry; the two address rails of atanhi[id] and atanlo[id] and
; their scaled-index rails; the conjunction flag of block %59; the two bus load copies (un-copied: no memory version
; change follows them); all uncomputed and freed before the measurement.
; Kept: the register x (%4) and the measured result rail %74. No store, no tape slot, no kept load copy.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; A transcendental whose body is SHOWN (175 only declares its exp/atan2 clones): musl's atan (FreeBSD msun s_atan.c
; lineage) reproduced as the static atan_musl in the .c. clang -O1 inlines it into the entry, so the O1.ll holds no call
; and no clone __cq_q_atan_musl_1 exists: the whole body is straight-line templates here (what a clone would hold, minus the
; copy-out). The `union { double f; unsigned long long i; }` view is a bitcast template, ix = the high word masked (lshr,
; trunc, and), and the `ix` range tests are compare flags on that i32 bit view (rule 8): %9 (ix >= 0x44100000), %15
; (ix < 0x3fdc0000), %17 (ix < 0x3e400000), %20 (ix < 0x3ff30000), %22 (ix < 0x3fe60000), %32 (ix < 0x40038000). The huge
; branch's `sign ? -z : z` with z = atanhi[3] + 0x1p-120f is const-folded by -O1 to copysign(pi/2, x), a copysign_f64_lh
; template; `x != x` is the fcmp uno flag %11. The four `id` arms (block %23/%27/%33/%37) are pure: computed unguarded (fmul,
; fadd and fdiv templates, each llvm.fmuladd UNFUSED by section 2 into an fmul product rail and an fadd, the product
; uncomputed by its fmul _unc right after the sum; fdiv totalised by section 2) and merged by selects nested like the if tree (rule 9): on %22 and %32
; innermost, then %20, then %15 for the %16 edge that carries x itself. `id` is the same select tree over literals at
; the phi's own type: -O1 typed the phi i64 (the sext of int id into the GEP index folded into the incomings, with
; 4294967295 for the id = -1 edge), and no index is narrowed (rule 20), so the id rail is i64 (select_i64_ll /
; select_i64_lh with 4294967295 on that edge).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21): `atanhi[id]` and `atanlo[id]` are constant tables read at a QUANTUM id. Nothing is known about
; an address at compile time and nothing is allocated or seeded for a global: each table lives at its host address and
; is read through the bus as HOST cells. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (section 5). Each getelementptr has a
; tainted index, so it is 64-bit template arithmetic into an address rail: the i64 id rail scaled by mul_i64_hl(id, 8),
; then add_i64_hl of the classical part, the constant expression ptrtoint (ptr @atanhi to i64) (the constant index 0
; contributes 0); the two getelementptrs share the id rail and each emits its own scale and add. Each load is ONE
; qram_load_f64 at its address rail. A bus access is never hoisted or speculated (rules 5, 9): the loads stay at their
; program point in block %59 as the _controlled form under the block's predicate, the conjunction NOT %9 AND NOT %15
; (rule 8: and_i1 into a fresh |0> inside an X bracket on both flags), computed just before the first load and
; uncomputed right after the last load _unc. Under predicate 0 (the paths that return earlier, the id = -1 edge among
; them) no cell is read and the load rail stays |0>, which the select tree discards. No memory version change (a store,
; an allocation, a memory-writing call; rule 5) follows the loads, so both copies are un-copied (rule 5, Memory) with their control at its load value,
; LIFO after their last reader's _unc; each address rail outlives its load's _unc and is uncomputed right after it
; (rule 20). The aT[] coefficients were folded into fmuladd literals by clang (the literals of the fmul/fadd templates)
; and are classical. `br i1 %15` at %39 is -O1's rewrite of `id < 0` (on every path into %39, id < 0 iff %15), so the two
; early returns and the final merge are selects on the same flags: %73 = select(%9, select(%11, x, %13), select(%15,
; select(%17, x, %58), %71)), one select per distinct incoming with the complement arm innermost. sign (%70 = the bit
; view < 0) selects the negated result. Everything but the result rail is uncomputed LIFO before the measurement.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 15, 8, 11, 12, 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 14, 16, 20, 21, 22; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc, qram_swap).
; Checked: out = sum_j c[j] << (t-1-j) | sum_i k[i] << (t+i): each measured c[j] is the i1 load copy of cell c + j of the
; bus block %8 (the first measure loop), each measured k[i] the i1 load copy of cell k + i of the block %6 (the second
; measure loop). The cells of both blocks on the bus at exit: the low bit of cell c + j (k + i) holds the measured outcome
; of c[j] (k[i]), its high 7 bits 0.
; Clean: the kv accumulator walk (its |0> seed and per trip the zext, shl, or rails, pushed and uncomputed by the mirror
; loop), its sitofp rail (or, for nk <= 0, the 0.0 seed rail of the phi), the angle base A = fl((2 pi / 2^nk) * (double)kv)
; (the program's fmul), the per-trip angle rail A_j = fl(A * 2^j) (one per trip of the phase loop) and the QFT^-1 Toffoli
; flags c[m] & c[j] (one per (m, j) pair), each |0> (or its seed value) at its free; the swap rail of every in-place form
; (the eigenstate Ry, H^t, the QFT^-1 Ry; |0> after its swap-in); the load copy of c[j] that controls the phase primitive
; of trip j, the two load copies of c[m] and c[j] each QFT^-1 flag reads (the c[j] copy loaded under c[m]) and the load
; copy of c[j] that carries the phase cq_phi(pi): all un-copied right after their last reader (rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: the two memset value seeds alloc_i8(0) and the tape slots of the nk + t byte stores of the memsets (rules 5
; sentence 3, 7, 22); by rule 5 sentence 1, un-copied after their last reader but left allocated, the nk load copies
; of tk[i] (each overtaken by its trip's in-place form, a memory version change, before its last reader, the qangle
; primitive; un-copied right after the swap-in: HOST cells, classical-valued, no qubit) and the nk i8 load copies of
; k[i] of the kv walk (overtaken by the H^t in-place forms before their last reader, the zext _unc in the mirror, and
; un-copied right after it); by rule 2 the t + nk measured i1 load copies. The cells
; are the registers: no handle is ever stored (§1.1).
; Rotations: (Ry, cell k[i], val(T_i), 1) for i = 0..nk-1, T_i the f64 rail loaded from tk[i] (ry_i1_qangle on the swap
; rail); (Ry, cell c[j], pi/2, 1) for j = 0..t-1; then for j = 0..t-1: (P, A_j, val(A_j), copy of c[j]) with
; A_j = fl(fl((2 pi / 2^nk) * (double)kv) * 2^j), kv = sum_i k[i] << i [the controlled U^(2^j), U = diag(e^{i 2 pi kv /
; 2^nk}), applied by ONE primitive on the angle rail]; then the QFT^-1: for j = t-1..0: (P, flag, -pi / 2^(m-j),
; c[m] & c[j]) for m = t-1..j+1, (P, copy of c[j], pi, c[j]) (rz_i1 on the bare load copy), (Ry, cell c[j], pi/2, 1).
; Expected: for basis kv the counting field reads kv * 2^(t-nk) exactly when t >= nk (c[0] is its top bit); in
; superposition every kv branch reads its own estimate and k is left unchanged. The k copies (un-copied, left allocated)
; are basis copies of a register that no non-diagonal gate touches after its preparation and that is measured: they change no outcome
; distribution. Analytic (not re-replayed in the bus model; val(T_i) = tk[i] exactly, pi and pi/2 lie on the Ry grid):
; call 1 (nk = 2, t = 2, tk = {pi, 0}: kv = 1) reads c = 01, k = (1, 0) with p = 1.0000; call 2 (nk = 3, t = 4,
; tk = {pi/2, pi/2, pi}: kv uniform on {4, 5, 6, 7}) reads c = 2 kv (1000, 1010, 1100, 1110) jointly with its own k,
; p = 0.25 each, nothing else.
; QPE whose phase comes from a QUANTUM angle register, general size: nk, t and the preparation angles tk[] are inputs, so
; every loop has a classical runtime bound (rule 14). ONE BUS (rules 16, 20, 21). `bool k[nk], c[t]` are -O1's
; `alloca i8, i64 n`; each stores a tainted value (a cq_theta result), which no user of rule 20 (b) allows, and c is also
; read under a quantum predicate (the QFT^-1 c[j] load in the arm of c[m]): both are BUS-RESIDENT, __cq_alloc(n, 16) at
; their program points (rule 16: zeroed, a classical size, no K2), and every access is a bus access at its run-time
; address (gep with an untainted index stays, then ptrtoint: classical, _hl). m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry.
; The zero-fills -O1 turned into memsets are rule 22's host loop of byte stores of ONE i8 seed, kept (emitted although
; the block is zero already: §0). tk is a pointer argument, program memory like any other: tk[i] is a bus load and an
; f64 rail (rule 3; over-taint, a basis copy of HOST cells), so cq_theta(&k[i], tk[i]) rotates by a QUANTUM ANGLE: ONE
; primitive cqrt_ry_i1_qangle (rules 11, 15). Each `load i8; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext; store i8` on one SSA
; pointer is rule 5's in-place form at width i1 (Width casts): alloc_i1(0), qram_swap_i1_hl, the rotation on the swap
; rail, qram_swap_i1_hl, free; tk[i] is a plain bus load at its own program point, before the swap-out.
; kv = sum k[i] << i is the quantum accumulator of 28 over the cells (a bus load of k[i] at the access type i8, zext from
; i8, shl, or into fresh rails, pushed per trip). -O1 turns (double)kv into `sitofp` at the loop exit and merges it with
; the literal 0.0 of the nk <= 0 path; that incoming is a seed rail cqrt_alloc_f64(0.0), so the phi is a handle on both
; edges. The kv seed alloc_i32(0) is allocated before the guard and is also the kv rail of the nk <= 0 path. -O1 hoists
; 2 pi / 2^nk (classical) and its product with (double)kv out of the phase loop: cq_template_fmul_f64_hl gives the f64
; REGISTER A holding the program's IEEE double, bit-exact (rule 15, as 79 and 143). Each trip multiplies A by the
; classical (double)(1 << j) into the trip rail A_j, computed UNGUARDED (pure arm code is hoisted, rule 9), and
; `if (c[j]) cq_phi(phi)` is ONE primitive cqrt_rz_qangle_controlled(q_j, A_j), q_j the plain i1 load copy of c[j]:
; e^{i val(A_j)} on the branch where c[j] is 1 (rule 15; the backend supplies the N-bit ladder, the IR never spells it;
; the phase is RELATIVE in k, never a deletable global one, rule 12). q_j is un-copied right after the primitive (the
; phase loop has no memory version change); A_j is only read, so it is uncomputed and freed right after. After the loop
; A, the sitofp rail and the kv walk are uncomputed in LIFO order before the QFT^-1 (no non-diagonal gate ever touches
; k). The mirror's zext _unc reads the trip's k[i] load copy, which the H^t swaps overtook: its handle is pushed with
; the trip's rails (SPEC GAP 2), and the mirror un-copies it right after that _unc and leaves it allocated (rule 5
; sentence 1). The QFT^-1 is 117's caller loop: the
; nested branches c[m], c[j] are one Toffoli flag of two load copies, the c[j] load sitting in the arm of c[m] and so
; controlled by it (rule 5); `if (c[j]) cq_phi(pi)` is cqrt_rz_i1 on a plain load copy of c[j] taken before the swap-out
; of the in-place Ry (rule 5 Readers: another reader of y). The measure loops are plain load copies, measured (rule 2),
; and the packing is classical.
; SPEC GAP 1: every read of a _Bool cell here that is `load i8; trunc nuw i8 to i1` with no in-place form around it (the
; phase-loop control, the QFT^-1 flag loads, the measure loops; the cq_phi(pi) reader is a reader of the in-place form
; and is taken at i1 by rule 5 Width casts) has its width fixed by rule 5's Width-casts clause
; only for a reader's plain load of a form. Chosen as 115 and 117: one qram_load_i1_hl at the trunc's width (the low bit
; of the cell), not a qram_load_i8 and a trunc template. The accumulator's `load i8; zext nneg i8 to i32` has no trunc
; and is qram_load_i8_hl with zext_i8_to_i32.
; SPEC GAP 2: rule 14 pushes "every trip-local rail that rule 5 does not keep (and any classical per-trip value its
; _uncs need ...)", and rule 22 names only its hand-over and rule 19's dispatch loop as pushes of kept rails. The kv
; mirror's zext _unc needs each trip's overtaken k[i] load copy. Chosen: its handle is pushed as that per-trip classical
; value, and the mirror pops it for the zext _unc and the copy's own _unc after it (the copy is never freed).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 21, 16, 5, 14, 8, 9, 4, 2.
; Checked: the packed array a[0] | a[1] << 2 | a[2] << 4 | a[3] << 6 after one bubble pass over the cells
; a[k] = (x >> 2k) & 3 (measured), and m = max(a[0..3]) after the pass (copied out, measured); the classical result is
; pack | m << 8. Memory: the four cells of the block (P + 4k) hold the sorted a[k] at exit (not a named output).
; Clean: the three shift rails (x >> 2, x >> 4, x >> 6); every scan trip's load copy of a[k] and its umax rail (pushed,
; popped and uncomputed by the reverse scan loop; the load is un-copied there, rule 5 sentence 1); the load copy of a[0]
; read after the sort; the three post-loop load copies a[1..3], the three shl rails and the two inner ors of the pack.
; Nothing of the sort loop is pushed and it has no reverse loop.
; Kept: the user register x; the four cell rails (x & 3, (x >> 2) & 3, (x >> 4) & 3, (x >> 6) & 3), the value rails of
; the four initializer stores, with their four tape slots (rule 5 sentence 3); per sort trip the two load copies of
; a[i] and a[i+1] (the value rails of the trip's two controlled stores), the flag a[i] > a[i+1] (their control rail)
; and the two tape slots; the pack result rail and the copied-out maximum (both measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; ONE BUS (rule 20): `a` is stored tainted values, so the alloca is BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)): one zeroed block
; __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the alloca's program point, no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16).
; m = __cq_mem() once at function entry. Every index is classical (the constant initializer offsets, the trip counter i
; and i + 1, the scan counter k, the fixed post-loop reads), so -O1's getelementptrs stay classical instructions and
; every access is _hl at their ptrtoint (rules 20, 21). The four initializer stores are KEPT bus stores of the cell
; rails (rule 5 sentence 3), which makes the cells QUANTUM; each cell rail is a store's value rail and stays allocated,
; so only the shift rails beneath them are uncomputed, each right after its `and` (its last reader; rule 5).
; The swap `if (a[i] > a[i+1]) { t = a[i]; a[i] = a[i+1]; a[i+1] = t; }`: both loads are bus loads (rails), the flag is
; the icmp template over the two load copies (rule 8), and the arm's only content is two stores. A bus access is never
; hoisted (rule 9): each store stays in its arm as qram_store_i32_hl_controlled under the flag (rule 5), so a[i] <- a[i+1]
; and a[i+1] <- a[i] happen on the flag = 1 branch only and each displaced cell goes to its own tape slot. Neither store
; is an in-place form (each stores the value loaded through the OTHER pointer), so both are kept stores: their value
; rails (the two load copies) and their control rail (the flag) are KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3). The trip therefore has no
; trip-local rail that rule 5 does not keep: nothing is pushed and the classical loop has no reverse loop (rule 14).
; After the sort no memory version change follows (the lifetime end is dropped), so every later load is un-copied after
; its last reader (rule 5 sentence 1). -O1 folded the scan's `if (a[i] > m) m = a[i]` into llvm.umax (one template per
; trip, rule 4); m is a loop-carried value seeded by the load copy of a[0], copied out after the scan (alloc + copy), and
; the reverse scan loop pops each trip's load copy and old m, uncomputes the umax, then un-copies the load at the
; address recomputed from the trip index (rule 14: no inbounds/nsw in the reverse loop). The pack is straight-line
; (rule 4) and uncomputed down to its result rail, each post-loop load copy un-copied after its shl's _unc; the load
; copy of a[0] (read by the scan's trip 1, whose umax _unc runs in the reverse scan loop, and by the pack's last or) is
; un-copied right after that or. Both measurements read result rails only and are placed after the cleanup, in program
; order.

; m = 3: result 0x3e1. For every basis x the pass moves the maximum to a[3], so m = a[3].

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 22, 21, 16, 14, 5, 6, 7, 4, 2.
; Checked: histogram: h[0] | h[1] << 4 | h[2] << 8 | h[3] << 12 with h[b] = #{i < 4 : (x >> 2i) & 3 == b} (measured).
; gather_scatter: s = sum over i < 4 of t[(x >> 3i) & 7] (the carried rail, measured) and out[0] | out[1] << 8 |
; out[2] << 16 | out[3] << 24 after out[(x >> 2i) & 3] = v0 + i for i = 0..3 in order (measured); the classical result
; is their sum. The cells of the two blocks at exit (h[b], out[b] at the block's address + 4b) are not named outputs.
; Clean: histogram: per trip the shift rail, the bucket index rail, its zext, the scaled index and the address rail
; (uncomputed and freed right after the in-place form's second swap), the in-place form's old-count rail (rule 6:
; t = new - 1 copied onto it, t uncomputed) and its new-count rail (|0> after the swap-in); after the loop the four
; fixed-address load copies, the three shl rails and two inner ors. gather_scatter, per trip: the table chain (shift,
; index, zext, scaled index, address rail), the load copy of t[j] (un-copied in the trip, before the scatter store),
; the old s (rule 6 in the body; trip 0's old s is the |0> seed) and its rule-6 rail t, the scatter chain (shift, index,
; zext, scaled index, address rail, uncomputed right after the store); after the loop the same pack garbage as
; histogram. Nothing is pushed and neither function has a reverse loop.
; Kept: histogram: the user register x and the pack result rail (measured); by rule 5 the 16 tape slots of the memset's
; byte stores and their one value seed (i8 0). gather_scatter: x, the final s (measured), the pack result rail
; (measured); by rule 5 the 16 memset tape slots with their seed (i8 0), and per trip the scatter store's tape slot and
; its value seed v0 + i (rule 7: a basis state, no qubit).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1) in each entry.
; ONE BUS (rule 20): h and out are indexed by a rail, so each alloca is BUS-RESIDENT: one __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the
; alloca's program point, no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). m = __cq_mem() once at entry.
; The `= {0}` memset is rule 22's ONE host loop of 16 kept byte stores qram_store_i8_hl of one seed alloc_i8(0) at the
; classical addresses base + j (classical-valued: the cells stay HOST); it is emitted although the block is already
; zero (§0). Each getelementptr with a tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic: -O1's zext of the index as
; zext_i32_to_i64, mul_i64_hl by the element size 4, add_i64_hl of the classical base (the block's run-time address,
; or ptrtoint (ptr @t to i64)). No index is narrowed, bounded or checked.
; histogram: h[idx]++ is load, add 1, store on the same SSA pointer with no memory version change between, so it is
; rule 5's IN-PLACE FORM at the address rail (rule 6, a memory cell): alloc_i32(0), qram_swap_i32 out, the add into a
; fresh rail, rule 6's clean of the old rail (t = new - 1), qram_swap_i32 in, free. No copy of the cell, tape slot or
; old count remains, so the trip pushes nothing; the address chain is template garbage, uncomputed after the second
; swap. The four post-loop reads are bus loads at classical addresses (the block + 0, 4, 8, 12); no memory version
; change follows them, so each is un-copied after its last reader's _unc, before the measurement (rule 5 sentence 1).
; gather_scatter: t is a constant global, but its getelementptr has a TAINTED index, so it is not host-resident there
; (rule 20 (a) covers untainted indices only): t[j] is a bus load qram_load_i32 at an address rail over the HOST cells
; of @t (no QROM, nothing seeded). s is a carried accumulator, s' = t[j] + s a bijection in s that no trip predicate
; reads, so rule 6 cleans the old s in the body (as 27, 204): t = s' - t[j], copied onto the old s, uncomputed, both
; freed; the final s is measured directly, no copy-out. Its other operand, the load copy, is then un-copied after the
; clean (its last reader) and before the trip's next memory version change, the scatter store (rule 5 sentence 1). The
; scatter out[k] = v0 + i is a KEPT store at an address rail of the seed alloc_i32(v0 + i) (rules 5, 7): a later store
; to the same cell displaces the earlier value onto its own tape slot, so the cell ends with the LAST value written to
; it, as in C. -O1 measures s before reading out; s is measured at that program point.
; Basis check: x = 0x1b = 0b00_01_10_11 (buckets 3, 2, 1, 0): h = {1, 1, 1, 1}, result 0x1111. For gather_scatter with
; x = 0x1b and v0 = 10: table indices 3, 3, 0, 0 give s = 1 + 1 + 3 + 3 = 8; out[3] = 10, out[2] = 11, out[1] = 12,
; out[0] = 13, pack = 0x0a0b0c0d; result 8 + 0x0a0b0c0d.
; Rule 5 sentence 1: the consumer of the t[j] copy (%32, the carried s) is a rule-6 image with no _unc, so the copy's last
; reader is rule 6's inverse (sub_i32_unc), and the copy is un-copied right after it, before the scatter store. Rule 6
; 'Both operands dead': the copy is a bus load copy that sentence 1 un-copies, so rule 6 cleans the other operand, the old s (195).
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins) per externally
; visible function. The corpus emits a row only for an address-taken function; this module follows it and registers
; nothing for histogram and gather_scatter (neither address is taken).

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 14, 16, 20, 21.
; Checked: list_search: p ? i : -1, the index of the first node whose v equals key, else -1 (the copied-out result,
; measured). calloc_aligned: r = s[j & 1] + 1 (measured).
; Clean: list_search: every trip rail (the load copy of p->v, the found flag, the body predicate, the address rail
; p + 8, the load copy of p->next, the null flag, the trip's exit value, the carried result and pointer selects, the
; predicates A[1]..A[K-1]) popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop (no memory version change follows the stores, so
; both loads of every trip are un-copied, rule 5 sentence 1), plus the three seeds (p = the address of a, the result
; 0, the |1> predicate) freed directly. calloc_aligned: the address chain of a[k & 3] (k & 3, its zext, the scaling by
; 4, the add of a's address), uncomputed right after its store; the load copy s[j & 1], un-copied after its last
; reader (no memory version change follows it).
; Kept: list_search: x and y (rotated; also the value rails of the kept stores a->v = x, b->v = y); the seed value
; rails of the kept stores a->next = b, b->next = c, c->v = 7, c->next = NULL (rule 7) and the tape slots of all six
; stores (rule 5 sentence 3); the result (measured) and the output predicate A[K] (rule 14: LLVM knows no bound of
; the trip count, the loop ends on a 0 read from memory; A[K] is 0 on every branch here, since the list has three
; nodes, but the compiler cannot prove it). calloc_aligned: k and x (rotated; x is also the value rail of the kept
; store a[k & 3] = x); the load copy a[1] (the value rail of the kept store s[0] = a[1]: overtaken by it, rule 5);
; the rail x + 1 (the value rail of the kept store s[1] = x + 1); the tape slots of the three stores; r (measured).
; Rotations: list_search: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1). calloc_aligned: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Driver: list_search(3, .5, 4, .25, 4): on the all-unflipped branch x = 3, y = 4, the key sits in b and the
; measured value is 1; list_search(3, .5, 4, .25, 9): no node holds 9, c->next = NULL ends the scan and the value is
; -1; calloc_aligned(1, .5, 7, .25, 1): r = s[1] + 1 = x + 2 = 9 on that branch.
; list_search. ALLOCATION (rule 16): each malloc(16) is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at its program point (zeroed, never
; reused, alignment 16: the call names none); nothing is known about the three blocks at compile time, and nothing in
; the lowering asks which node a pointer addresses. A pointer is its run-time i64 (rule 21): a, b, c are classical
; addresses (ptrtoint). Every store is a bus store (rule 20; heap blocks are never host-resident): p->v at the block
; address, p->next at address + 8 (the classical getelementptr spelled as the add of its byte offset), a classical
; value first minted as a seed (alloc_i32(7), alloc_i64 of b's and c's addresses, alloc_i64(0) for NULL: a pointer in
; memory is an i64 cell value, rule 21) and kept with its store (rules 5, 7).
; LOOP: the exit p->v != key reads a value loaded from the bus, and p itself is loaded from the bus after trip 0, so
; the loop is a K-loop (rule 14, cutoff K = 4: no range bound B exists) and p is ONE 64-bit address rail (rule 21),
; carried by select on the next-trip predicate. A trip is one execution of the header %14; trip j runs under A[j]
; (A[0] = |1> seed), the body %19 under B[j] = A[j] & NOT found[j], and the next header under A[j+1] = B[j] & NOT
; null[j]. Trip 0's p is a classical start and enters as the seed alloc_i64(a) (rule 14). Each dereference is ONE bus
; access at the address rail, with no guard and no bounds check (rule 21): p->v is qram_load_i32 at p, p->next is
; qram_load_i64 at the address rail add_i64_hl(p, 8), and the loaded i64 is the next p as it stands. Both loads are
; read by an exit test, so each is _controlled under the predicate of REACHING that test (rule 14): p->v under A[j],
; p->next under B[j]; a trip C would not run touches no cell. The NULL test is icmp_eq_i64_hl(next, 0) (rule 21:
; NULL is the literal 0). i is the induction variable %16 = j (SCEV), a classical trip index. The exit phi %25 is
; carried as the result rail r: trip j sets r = found[j] ? j : -1 under A[j] (an exit at %14 yields j, a continue sets
; the provisional -1 that the NULL exit at %19 keeps). After K trips r is copied out, and the reverse loop pops each
; trip: the selects, the null flag, the p->next load (un-copied under B[j], which is still allocated), its address
; rail (it outlives the load's _unc, rule 20), B[j], the found flag and the p->v load (un-copied under A[j]); on
; reverse index 0 (trip K-1) it keeps A[K] (rule 14: the test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip). free is never
; called by the program; it would be nothing (rule 16).
; SPEC GAP (rule 14, two exit tests per trip): rule 14 spells a_K for one exit test per trip. Chosen, as before the
; memory regeneration: a trip is header test, body, latch test; A[K] is the predicate of reaching the header after
; the K-th latch test (the latch test after the K-th body, under B[K-1]); no header test of a (K+1)-th trip is made.
; calloc_aligned. calloc(4, 4) is __cq_alloc(16, 16) (size n·s, zeroed, so nothing is written for calloc's zero fill)
; and aligned_alloc(16, 16) is __cq_alloc(16, 16) (rule 16). a[k & 3] = x: the getelementptr has a tainted index, so
; it is 64-bit template arithmetic into an address rail (zext of k & 3, mul by 4, add of a's address; rule 20) and the
; store is qram_store_i32 at that rail, a kept store; the address chain is uncomputed right after it. s[0] = a[1]: the
; load qram_load_i32_hl at the classical address a + 4 and a kept store qram_store_i32_hl at s; the load copy is the
; store's value rail and is kept. s[1] = x + 1: the template, then a kept store at s + 4; the rail x + 1 is kept with
; it. s[j & 1]: the getelementptr has a classical run-time index, so it stays and its address is the _hl operand of
; qram_load_i32_hl; its copy is un-copied right after its last reader, the add r = s[j & 1] + 1 (rule 5 sentence 1:
; no memory version change follows). free(a) and free(s) are nothing (rule 16).

  %9 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 16, i64 16)    ; IR: %8 = malloc(16): a
  %10 = ptrtoint ptr %7 to i64    ; IR: %6 as its run-time address (classical)
  %11 = ptrtoint ptr %8 to i64    ; IR: %7 as its run-time address (classical)
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %9 to i64    ; IR: %8 as its run-time address (classical)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %13, double %1)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [register y]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %14, double %3)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: store i32 %9, ptr %8: a->v = x  [kept store: its slot and its value rail x stay]
  %15 = add i64 %12, 8    ; IR: %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 8  (classical)
  %16 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %11)    ; IR: store ptr %7, ptr %11: the stored address of b as a seed rail, kept with its store (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %15, i32 %16)    ; IR: store ptr %7, ptr %11: a->next = b  [kept store]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %11, i32 %14)    ; IR: store i32 %10, ptr %7: b->v = y  [kept store]
  %17 = add i64 %11, 8    ; IR: %12 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %7, i64 8  (classical)
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %10)    ; IR: store ptr %6, ptr %12: the address of c as a seed rail (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %17, i32 %18)    ; IR: store ptr %6, ptr %12: b->next = c  [kept store]
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 7)    ; IR: store i32 7, ptr %6: the seed 7 (rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %10, i32 %19)    ; IR: store i32 7, ptr %6: c->v = 7  [kept store]
  %20 = add i64 %10, 8    ; IR: %13 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 8  (classical)
  %21 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 0)    ; IR: store ptr null, ptr %13: NULL as the seed 0 (rules 7, 21)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %20, i32 %21)    ; IR: store ptr null, ptr %13: c->next = NULL  [kept store]
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %12)    ; IR: %15 = phi ptr [ %8, %5 ]: p before trip 0, the classical start a as a seed (rule 14)
  %23 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: the result before trip 0 (never read: A[0] = 1)  [seed]
  %24 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the header in trip 0 (always 1)

  %27 = phi i32 [ %22, %5 ], [ %39, %25 ]    ; IR: %15 = phi ptr [ %8, %5 ], [ %22, %19 ]: p, a 64-bit address rail
  %28 = phi i32 [ %23, %5 ], [ %38, %25 ]    ; IR: the exit value %25 so far
  %29 = phi i32 [ %24, %5 ], [ %36, %25 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching the header %14 in this trip

  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %29, i32 %31, i32 %32)    ; IR: br i1 %18 not taken: B = A & NOT found
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %31)    ; IR: bracket

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21, 22; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc), §1.4.
; Checked: alias_params: a[0] after addto (the load copy, measured): 2 * a0 when x & 1 == 0 (q aliases p), a0 + a1 when
; x & 1 == 1; the cells of a at exit: a[0] = that value, a[1] = a1.
; qram_2d: g[1][2] + g[r & 3][0] (the add rail, measured): v * [r & 3 == 1 && c & 3 == 2] + v * [c & 3 == 0]; the cells
; of g at exit: g[r & 3][c & 3] = v, every other cell 0.
; Clean: alias_params: the address chain of q = &a[x & 1] (x & 1, its zext, the scaled index, the address rail),
; uncomputed by the caller after the call (the clone stored through p; rule 5 sentence 3) and freed; in the clone the
; three rails of the in-place form (the swap rail holding the old *p, the rule-6 inverse t, the updated rail after the
; swap-in). qram_2d: the address chain of the store &g[r & 3][c & 3] (both scaled indices, their sum, the address rail),
; uncomputed right after the store, then c & 3 and its zext; the two load copies g[1][2] and g[r & 3][0], un-copied
; after the add, before the measurement; the address chain of the load &g[r & 3] (the scaled row index, the address
; rail), uncomputed after that load's un-copy, then r & 3 and its zext.
; Kept: alias_params: x (rotated register), the load copy a[0] (measured), and by rule 5 for the shot: the tape slots of
; the two initializer stores with their seed value rails a0, a1. Left allocated, un-copied: in the clone the load copy
; of *q (un-copied after the swap-in; overtaken by the in-place form, a memory version change, so not freed: rule 5
; sentence 1). The in-place form itself keeps nothing. qram_2d: r, c (rotated registers),
; the sum (measured), and by rule 5: the 64 tape slots of the memset's byte stores with their one value seed (i8 0), the
; tape slot of the store g[r & 3][c & 3] = v with its seed value rail v.
; Rotations: alias_params: (Ry, x, tx, 1). qram_2d: (Ry, r, tr, 1); (Ry, c, tc, 1).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21). Every load is a bus load (a rail), every store a bus store, at the pointer's run-time i64 address
; (_hl) or at a 64-bit address rail; m = __cq_mem() once at the entry of every function that accesses the bus (§5).
; alias_params: the alloca a has a gep with a tainted index and a call among its users, so it is bus-resident (rule 20
; (b)): __cq_alloc(8, 4) at its program point, no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). The
; initializer is two kept stores at the classical addresses a and a + 4, each of a seed (rule 7). q = a + (x & 1) is
; 64-bit template arithmetic (rule 20): zext (as -O1 wrote it), mul by the element size 4, add of the classical base
; address: ONE address rail (rule 21). A POINTER IS ONE SCALAR (§1.4): addto(p, q) passes the classical ptr a (digit 0)
; and the address rail q (digit 1): the clone __cq_q_addto_01(ptr, i32). Nothing about the pointee, no object, tag or
; cell index crosses the call, and nothing asks whether p and q are equal. In the clone `*p += *q` is load q, load p,
; add, store p on the same SSA pointer p with no memory version change between the load of p and the store: rule 5's
; IN-PLACE FORM at the classical address p, with the add (a rule-6 bijection in *p) as its one step. The load of *q a
; step reads is a plain bus load at its own program point, before the swap-out, so when q == p it copies the old *p and
; the update is 2 * a0, exactly C's result; that copy is overtaken by the form: un-copied after its last reader (rule
; 6's _unc of t), placed after the swap-in (no bus access inside the form), and not freed (rule 5 sentence 1; when
; q == p the un-copy reads the updated cell and the rail keeps garbage, no rule asks which). The form is emitted at the store's position: swap-out into a fresh |0> rail, y' = y + *q with rule 6's
; clean of the old rail (t = y' - *q), swap-in of y', free. addto writes memory, so the clone has NO TWIN (rule 18) and
; returns nothing; addto's own symbol has no caller left and is dropped (§1.4). The caller uncomputes the address rail
; it passed after the call (rule 5 sentence 3). The load of a[0] after the call (a memory version change) is a fresh
; copy, measured: rule 2's measured rail, never un-copied.
; qram_2d: g is indexed by rails, so it is bus-resident: __cq_alloc(64, 16). -O1's llvm.memset(g, 0, 64) is rule 22's
; ONE host loop of 64 kept byte stores of one i8 seed at the classical addresses g + j (never unrolled, emitted although
; the block is already zero). Each tainted getelementptr is its own address arithmetic (rule 20): %11 = &g[r & 3] is
; zext(r & 3) * 16 + g; %14 = &g[r & 3][c & 3] emits its own scale of the shared zext rail, zext(c & 3) * 4, their sum and
; + g. g[1][2] is -O1's classical gep g + 24 (it stays) and a _hl load. The store of v is a kept store at the address
; rail %14; its address chain is uncomputed right after it (the store is its last reader). The load g[r & 3][0] at the
; address rail %11 is un-copied after the add, so %11 outlives that _unc (rule 20).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19, §1.1 (escaped rail), 6, 4, 5, 2, 9.
; Checked: narrow_bool_consumer: (x > k) ? 5 : 2 (measured); narrow_short_consumer: (short)((s + c) * 2) (measured);
;          wide_long_consumer: (x ^ c) + 1 (measured). The three entries return UNMEASURED quantum values: each `ret`
;          carries the HANDLE of the result rail (§1.1, rule 19), checked as that rail's basis value.
; Clean: narrow_return_short: the old s (rule 6: s + c is a bijection in s, s is dead) and t = r - c; wide_return_long: the
;        old x (rule 6: x ^ c) and t = r ^ c; narrow_bool_consumer: the flag x > k (uncomputed after the select, freed);
;        narrow_short_consumer: the sum s + c (uncomputed against s after the shift, freed; rule 6 does NOT apply to s: the
;        composite update (s + c) << 1 is no bijection, so s must stay to uncompute the sum); wide_long_consumer: the old x
;        and the old x ^ c (two rule-6 clean-ups, each a bijective update of a dead value) and their inverses.
; Kept: each entry's returned rail (escapes with the return; never freed); narrow_return_bool's x (the compare is no
;       bijection, so the rotated register stays, frozen); narrow_bool_consumer's x; narrow_short_consumer's s; every
;       measured rail.
; Rotations: Ry(tx) on x / Ry(ts) on s in each function.
; RETURN TYPE OF AN ENTRY RETURNING A QUANTUM VALUE (rule 19, ruling 2026-10-31). Every quantum value is an i32 handle
; (§1.1). A C return type that cannot hold an i32 (`_Bool`: `zeroext i1`; `short`: `signext i16`; `char`; every floating
; or pointer type) is replaced at the external signature by i32: truncating the handle would name another rail, and the
; compiler never measures a value the program does not measure. The parameter list keeps the C ABI (`i16 signext`
; parameters stay). An integer return type of 32 bits or more keeps its C type and carries the handle zero-extended
; (162: i32 as is; wide_return_long: `zext i32 %h to i64`). In-module callers see the entry inlined (rule 19; here by

define i32 @narrow_return_short(i16 noundef signext %0, double noundef %1, i16 noundef signext %2) {

define i32 @narrow_short_consumer(i16 noundef signext %0, double noundef %1, i16 noundef signext %2) {

; copies are measured directly (as 169's c_qq), so none is defined (§1.4); __cq_q___muldc3_1000_unc is defined and called.
; Inside the clones every op with a handle operand is an out-of-place template into a fresh rail (rule 4; _hl/_lh with the
; classical value as the literal, a commutative op with the handle first, compares never _lh), every op on classical
; operands only stays classical IR, and a phi whose two arms are both classical values but whose edge is a quantum flag is
; a select_f64_ll into a fresh rail (rule 9: %32-%34 of __muldc3). llvm.fmuladd is UNFUSED (§2, cf. 14, 69, 169): an fmul
; into a fresh product rail, then an fadd of the product and the addend. The fcmp predicates (uno, ord-free here: uno,
; oeq, olt, ueq, une) are templates; `select i1 %a, i1 true, i1 %b` is the disjunction or_i1 and `select i1 %a, i1 %b,

; (`[false, %53], [false, %72], [true, %60]`) is the flag %59 & !%71. A flag read as data (%16, %38, %40 feed uitofp i1)
; is the compare's own rail. llvm.ctlz.i64 (zero-is-poison: the template is total, §2), llvm.sadd.sat.i32 and llvm.smax.i32
; on handles are the ctlz_i64, sadd_sat_i32 and smax_i32_hl templates. Merges follow the CFG: an if/else-if ladder into one
; exit nests its selects on the local flags, the deepest else innermost (rule 9: the %35 logb merge on %14/%16/%18, the
; four scalbn merges %88/%137/%192/%244 on their %47-shaped / %64 / %70 flags, the %135 merge on %37); the five-incoming
; phis of %302 (__divdc3) and %85/%99 (__muldc3) whose arms sit on disjoint path predicates (P254, P288, P270; P72; P91)

name: 195_bus_fixed_address
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 16, 18, 19, 20, 21; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc), §1.4 (own symbol).
; Checked: bus_global_cell: cell + y = x + y (measured, %9 -> %11), and the cell `cell` = x (read from the bus at exit).
;          bus_escaped_local: w = x + 1 (the load copy %7, measured -> %8), the cell w = x + 1.
;          bus_rotate_cell: reg (the load copy %4, measured -> %5), the cell `reg` = the rotated 2.
; Clean: bus_global_cell: the old y rail (%7, rule 6: cell + y is a bijection in y, y is dead), the inverse t = sum - cell
;        (%10) and the load copy of cell (%8, un-copied: its last consumer precedes every memory version change).
;        bump: the swapped-out old *p (%4, rule 6), the inverse t = y' - 1 (%6) and the rail the cell's |0> went to (%5).
;        bus_rotate_cell: the swap rail (%3, |0> after the swap-in).
; Kept: bus_global_cell: x (%6: rotated, and the value rail of the kept store, rule 5), the tape slot of the store
;       `store i32 %5, ptr @cell` (no handle: it is in the backend and holds the displaced `cell`), the sum (%9, measured).
;       bus_escaped_local: x (%6: rotated, value rail of the kept store), the tape slot of the store `store i32 %4,
;       ptr %3` (no handle), the load copy of w (%7, measured). bus_rotate_cell: the load copy of reg (%4, measured).
;       bump keeps nothing (the in-place form leaves no rail, tape slot or old value).
; Rotations: bus_global_cell: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1). bus_escaped_local: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
;            bus_rotate_cell: (Ry, the cell reg, tr, 1).
; Expected (Ry(th) acts on every qubit of an i32 rail, so each of the 32 bits flips with probability s(th) = sin^2(th/2),
;   independently: P(v) = s^d (1 - s)^(32 - d), d the Hamming distance of v from the start value):
;   bus_global_cell(3, .5, 4, .25): x from 3 with s = 0.0612087, y from 4 with s = 0.0155438; the measured sum is the
;     convolution mod 2^32, mode 7 with probability 0.080597 (0.080259 of it from x = 3, y = 4).
;   bus_escaped_local(3, .5): w = x + 1, x from 3 with s = 0.0612087: mode 4 with probability 0.132498 (x unchanged); each
;     single-bit flip of x has probability 0.008639.
;   bus_rotate_cell(.75): reg from 2 with s = 0.1341556: 2 with probability 0.009956, each single-bit neighbour 0.001543.
; ONE BUS, CLASSICAL ADDRESSES (rule 20). All memory is the bus m = __cq_mem(), called once at the entry of every function
; that accesses the bus (§5). A global lives at its host address: nothing is allocated, seeded or registered for `cell`
; and `reg`, and the address operand of the _hl forms is the pointer's run-time i64 (ptrtoint). Every store is a bus
; store and every load a bus load whose result is a rail (rule 3), whatever the cell holds.
; bus_global_cell. `cell = x` is a KEPT store (rule 5, sentence 3): no _unc exists, its tape slot stays for the shot and
; so does its value rail x. The load of cell is a fresh copy of the cells. cell + y is an add of two rails that are both
; dead after it: the load copy is garbage rule 5 uncomputes anyway, so rule 6 cleans y first (its inverse t = sum - cell
; reads the copy), and then the copy is un-copied (sentence 1: its consumers and their uncompute precede every memory
; version change; the cells still hold what they held at the load) and freed. The sum is measured.
; bus_escaped_local. The alloca of w has a store of a rail and a call among its users, so it is bus-resident (rule 20 b):
; it is __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program point (rule 16), no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped.
; `int w = x` is a kept store at the block's address. bump is called with a classical pointer: mask 0, bump's OWN symbol
; (§1.4, rule 19), never inlined. The call is a memory version change (bump writes memory); the load of w after it is a
; fresh copy, measured, so it stays as rule 2's measured rail.
; bump. `*p += 1` is load, add, store on the same SSA pointer with nothing between: rule 5's IN-PLACE FORM with a rule-6
; bijection as its one step (rule 6, "a memory cell"). Swap-out into a fresh |0> rail, y' = y + 1 with the clean of the
; old rail, swap-in of y', free of the rail that now holds the cell's |0>. Nothing remains: no copy, no tape slot.
; The same body serves host callers and all-classical calls: on a classical-valued cell every rail here is
; classical-valued and the swaps write host bytes (§1.3 overlay).
; bus_rotate_cell. cq_theta(&reg, tr) is `load @reg; cq_theta; store @reg` straight back through the same pointer: rule
; 2's rotation of a cell, the in-place form with the Ry as its step. The gate acts on the cell's content while it sits in
; the swap rail; the swap-in returns it and the rail is freed. cq_measure(reg) reads the stored value y' (-O1 forwarded
; it): a later reader of y' is a plain load taken after the swap-in (rule 5, Readers), and that copy is measured.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@reg = local_unnamed_addr global i32 2, align 4
@cell = local_unnamed_addr global i32 0, align 4

define i32 @bus_global_cell(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3) {

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 22, 21, 16, 5, 4, 2.
; Checked: r = a[j & 3] (measured, %34 -> %35); the cells of a at exit, read from the bus at the block's address:
; a[i] = (i == (k & 3)) ? x : i + 1.
; Clean: the two address chains, each and / zext / mul / add (%26..%29 for the store, %30..%33 for the load),
; uncomputed and freed right after their access.
; Kept: k, j, x (%10, %11, %12, the rotated registers; x is also the value rail of the kept store, rule 5); the 16
; byte load copies of the initializer (%16 per trip), each the value rail of a kept byte store (rule 5, sentences 1
; and 3; classical-valued, so no qubit, §0); the tape slots of the 16 byte stores and of the i32 store (backend
; rails, rule 5); the load copy r (%34, measured, rule 2).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, j, tj, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: bus_quantum_address(1, .5, 2, .25, 9, .75). Each Ry acts on all 32 qubits of its register and everything
; after the three rotations is a basis permutation, so r is distributed as the C program on independent bit flips:
; a bit of k flips with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209, of j with q = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544, of x with s = sin^2(.375) =
; 0.134156. k & 3 = 0, 1, 2, 3 with 0.057462, 0.881329, 0.003747, 0.057462; j & 3 = 0, 1, 2, 3 with 0.015302,
; 0.000242, 0.969154, 0.015302. The two indices meet with probability 0.005602 and r is then x = 9 ^ e, each e with
; s^|e| (1 - s)^(32 - |e|) (x = 9: 0.009956); otherwise r = (j & 3) + 1. In total P(r = 3) = 0.965524, P(r = 1) =
; 0.014432, P(r = 4) = 0.014423, P(r = 2) = 0.000029, P(r = 9) = 0.000056, and 0.005536 over the other values of x.
; ONE BUS (rule 20): the alloca is BUS-RESIDENT, because a getelementptr with a tainted index is among its users, so
; no alloca remains: its block is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the alloca's program point (rule 16) and the lifetime markers
; are dropped. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). Nothing is known about an address at compile time: the
; base is the block's run-time address as a classical i64, and each getelementptr with a tainted index is 64-bit
; template arithmetic into an address rail: the index rail (-O1's zext to i64), mul_i64_hl by the element size 4,
; add_i64_hl of the classical part (the base; the constant indices contribute 0). The store is ONE qram_store_i32 at
; the address rail and the load ONE qram_load_i32 at the other; no index is narrowed, bounded or checked. The store is
; kept (no _unc, its tape slot and its value rail x stay); its address rail is template garbage, uncomputed after the
; store. The load copy is measured, so it is never un-copied; its address rail is uncomputed after the load.
; THE INITIALIZER (rule 22): llvm.memcpy of 16 bytes into a bus-resident destination is a byte copy on the bus, a
; host loop of 16 qram_load_i8_hl at the source address and then a host loop of 16 qram_store_i8_hl at the block,
; never widened into word accesses. The source is the constant global at its host address (HOST cells through the
; overlay, nothing seeded); every value, address and control is classical-valued, so the stores write the host bytes
; and the cells of a stay HOST until the store at the address rail makes the cells it can reach QUANTUM (§1.3). A
; handle is never stored in program memory (§1.1), so the load loop pushes its 16 handles and the store loop pops
; them: the stores run from byte 15 down to byte 0 (a copy has no direction).

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release the %13 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %28, i32 %27, i64 4)    ; IR: uncompute %13 (the scaled index)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the scaled-index rail (|0>)

  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %31, i64 4)    ; IR: %16 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %7, i64 0, i64 %15  [the tainted index scaled by the element size (rule 20)]
  %33 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %32, i64 %9)    ; IR: %16 = getelementptr  [+ the run-time base: the address rail of &a[j & 3]]

name: 197_bus_mutable_table
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (witness: an address-rail load of a constant global and of a mutable global are the same bus
; load), 19 (witness: an all-classical function is lowered under its own symbol), 5, 7, 2, 3, 4, 21; §1.3 (the overlay).
; Checked: tab_set: the cell tab[i & 3] = v, read from the bus at exit at &tab + 4 (i & 3) (HOST cells: the host
; bytes). bus_mutable_table: v = ROM[k & 3] + tab[k & 3] (measured, the add rail %13 -> %14).
; Clean: tab_set: nothing to clean. bus_mutable_table: the index rail k & 3 (%5), its zext (%6), the two scaled indices
; (%7, %10), the two address rails (%8, %11) and the two load copies (%9, %12), all uncomputed and freed before the
; measurement.
; Kept: tab_set: the store's tape slot (it holds the displaced tab[i & 3]) and its value rail, the seed %8 = |v>
; (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 7). bus_mutable_table: k (%4, the rotated register) and the sum (%13, measured).
; Rotations: tab_set: none. bus_mutable_table: (Ry, k, tk, 1).
; Expected for the driver tab_set(1, 9); bus_mutable_table(1, .5): tab = {2, 9, 1, 8} when the second call runs, so the
; sum is 5, 10, 5, 9 at k & 3 = 0, 1, 2, 3. Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of k = 1: with c = cos^2(.25) = 0.938791 and
; s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209, bit 0 reads 1 with probability c and bit 1 reads 1 with probability s, so k & 3 = 0, 1, 2,
; 3 has probability sc, cc, ss, cs and the measured value is 10 with p = c^2 = 0.881329, 5 with p = s = 0.061209 and
; 9 with p = cs = 0.057462. Without the tab_set call the 10 would read 8: the load sees the byte the store wrote.
; ONE BUS (rule 20): nothing is known about an address, so @ROM (isConstant) and @tab (mutable) are not told apart at
; an address rail. Both globals stay ordinary LLVM globals at their host addresses; nothing is allocated, seeded or
; registered for them, and their cells are HOST: each load reads the host bytes at the access (§1.3). A constant
; global is host-resident only through getelementptrs with UNTAINTED indices; here the index is the rail k & 3, so the
; ROM read is the bus load like the tab read. No QROM exists.
; ADDRESS ARITHMETIC (rule 20): each getelementptr with a tainted index is emitted: the i64 index rail (-O1's zext,
; one rail for both geps, as it is one SSA value) scaled by mul_i64_hl(., 4) and added to the classical base's
; run-time address by add_i64_hl(., ptrtoint @G). The two address rails are rule-5 garbage that outlive their loads'
; _unc.
; UNCOMPUTE (rule 5 sentence 1): no memory version change follows the loads in this function, and their only
; consumer, the add, is measured and never uncomputed, so both copies are un-copied right after the add (the cells
; still hold what the loads read) and freed; then the address chains, the ROM chain last in first out after the tab
; chain, the shared zext and the and.
; tab_set (rule 19, §1.4): the all-zero mask is the function's OWN symbol with its C parameter list, and its body is
; lowered although nothing in it is quantum: @tab is not host-resident (not isConstant), so the store is a bus store
; (rule 20). The getelementptr has nothing tainted and stays; the address is its run-time i64 and the value is the seed
; alloc_i32(v) (rule 7). Address, value and (absent) control are classical-valued, so the backend writes the four host
; bytes and the cells stay HOST (§1.3): host code and the later bus load both see v. The store is a kept store.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins) per externally
; visible function. No conforming example of the corpus emits one; this module follows the corpus and registers
; nothing for tab_set and bus_mutable_table: no table clone, no constructor. Neither function's address is taken.
; SPEC GAP: rule 5 sentence 1 asks for the uncompute of the load's last consumer. Here the consumer (the add) is the
; measured rail, which has none; read as satisfied (as 204 reads it): the copy is un-copied after its last reader,
; before the next memory version change.
; SPEC GAP: rule 20 does not say whether two getelementptrs on one index rail share the scaled index. Emission is per
; getelementptr instruction: each emits its own mul_i64_hl and add_i64_hl; only what is one SSA value at -O1 (the
; zext) is one rail.
; SPEC GAP: rule 20 gives no spelling for a classical address. It is ptrtoint of the pointer: the instruction for an
; instruction-valued pointer (tab_set's %7), the constant expression ptrtoint (ptr @G to i64) for a global, also as
; an _hl literal (as 195, 196).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@tab = local_unnamed_addr global [4 x i32] [i32 2, i32 7, i32 1, i32 8], align 16
@ROM = internal unnamed_addr constant [4 x i32] [i32 3, i32 1, i32 4, i32 1], align 16

define void @tab_set(i32 noundef %0, i32 noundef %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: (none)  [m: the one bus, fetched once at function entry]
  %4 = and i32 %0, 3    ; IR: %3 = and i32 %0, 3  [classical, unchanged]
  %5 = zext nneg i32 %4 to i64    ; IR: %4 = zext nneg i32 %3 to i64  [classical, unchanged]
  %6 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr @tab, i64 0, i64 %5    ; IR: %5 = getelementptr @tab, 0, %4  [nothing tainted: the gep stays]
  %7 = ptrtoint ptr %6 to i64    ; IR: store i32 %1, ptr %5  [the classical address as its run-time i64]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %1)    ; IR: store i32 %1, ptr %5  [the value is always a handle: the seed |v>, kept with the store]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i32 %1, ptr %5  [bus store at a classical address; all classical-valued: the host bytes are written, the cells stay HOST; kept, no _unc]
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
}

define i32 @bus_mutable_table(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: (none)  [m: the one bus, fetched once at function entry]
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register k]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %3 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: %4 = and i32 %3, 3
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64(i32 %5)    ; IR: %5 = zext nneg i32 %4 to i64  [the index rail, shared by both geps]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 4)    ; IR: %6 = getelementptr @ROM, 0, %5  [index scaled by sizeof(i32)]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %7, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @ROM to i64))    ; IR: %6 = getelementptr @ROM, 0, %5  [address rail: &ROM + 4 (k & 3)]
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32(i32 %3, i32 %8)    ; IR: %7 = load i32, ptr %6  [bus load at an address rail; HOST cells of a constant global]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 4)    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr @tab, 0, %5  [index scaled by sizeof(i32)]
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %10, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @tab to i64))    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr @tab, 0, %5  [address rail: &tab + 4 (k & 3)]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32(i32 %3, i32 %11)    ; IR: %9 = load i32, ptr %8  [the same bus load; HOST cells of a mutable global]
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %12, i32 %9)    ; IR: %10 = add nsw i32 %9, %7
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_unc(i32 %12, i32 %3, i32 %11)    ; IR: un-copy %9 (no memory version change since the load)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_hl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %10, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @tab to i64))    ; IR: uncompute the address rail of %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %8 address rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %6, i64 4)    ; IR: uncompute the scaled index of %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the scaled index (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_unc(i32 %9, i32 %3, i32 %8)    ; IR: un-copy %7 (no memory version change since the load)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @ROM to i64))    ; IR: uncompute the address rail of %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %6 address rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i64 4)    ; IR: uncompute the scaled index of %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the scaled index (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64_unc(i32 %6, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %4
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %4 rail (|0>)
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %13)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%10)
  ret i32 %14    ; IR: ret i32 %11
}

name: 198_bus_pointer_cell
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 6, 7, 16, 20, 21.
; Checked: a + b (the add rail %37, measured -> %38), and the cells of a, b and slot read from the bus at exit:
; with i = k & 1 and j = (k >> 1) & 1: slot[0] = &a, slot[1] = &b; *slot[i] = v; *slot[j] += 3.
;   i = 0, j = 0: a = v + 3, b = x          i = 0, j = 1: a = v, b = x + 3
;   i = 1, j = 0: a = 4,     b = v          i = 1, j = 1: a = 1, b = v + 3
; so a + b = v + 3 + x when bit 0 of k is 0 and v + 4 when it is 1, whatever bit 1 of k is.
; Clean: both address chains (k & 1, its zext, the scaling by 8, the add of slot's address: %20..%23; k >> 1, & 1,
; zext, scaling, add: %26..%30), uncomputed and freed right after the un-copy of the load they address; the three rails of the
; in-place form (the swap rail %32, the rule-6 inverse %34, the updated rail %33); the load copies of a and b (%35,
; %36), un-copied after the add: no memory version change follows them.
; Kept: k (%10) and x (%11), the rotated registers (x is also the value rail of the kept store b = x); the sum (%37,
; measured); by rule 5, for the shot: the tape slots of the five stores (a = 1, b = x, slot[0] = &a, slot[1] = &b,
; *p = v) and their seed value rails %13 (1), %16 (&a), %19 (&b), %25 (v); left allocated after their un-copy (rule 5
; sentence 1, overtaken): the load copy p = slot[k & 1] (%24), the address rail of the store *p = v, un-copied after
; that store; the load copy *pp = slot[(k >> 1) & 1] (%31), the address rail of the in-place form, un-copied after
; its second swap. The in-place form itself keeps nothing.
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: bus_pointer_cell(1, .5, 4, .25, 9): Ry(.5) on every qubit of k = 1 leaves bit 0 of k at 1 with probability
; cos^2(.25) = 0.9388, and then the measured value is v + 4 = 13; with probability sin^2(.25) = 0.0612 it is
; 12 + x mod 2^32 for the value x the rotated register holds (x = 4, measured value 16, has probability
; cos^2(.125)^32 = 0.6057 within that branch: 0.0371 in all). Bit 1 of k (1 with probability sin^2(.25)) decides only
; which cell took the + 3, never the sum.
; A POINTER IS AN INTEGER (rule 21). a, b and slot are bus-resident (rule 20 (b)): the addresses of a and b are
; stored as VALUES (not a store through them) and slot is indexed by a rail, so each alloca is one __cq_alloc block at
; its program point and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Every store is a bus store and every load a bus
; load. &a and &b enter their cells as i64 seed rails holding the run-time address (rule 7). The load at the address
; rail &slot[k & 1] (the getelementptr spelled as zext, mul by 8, add of slot's run-time address) is qram_load_i64:
; its result is ONE 64-bit rail, the pointer p, and it is the address operand of the next access as it stands: no
; object, no tag, no guard. *p = v is the plain qram_store_i32 at that rail: a kept store, and the rail p, a load
; copy, is overtaken by it: un-copied after it and not freed (rule 5, sentences 1 and 3). **pp += 3 is load ptr; load i32; add; store i32
; through the same SSA pointer %20 with no memory version change between: the in-place form (rules 5, 6) at the
; address rail *pp, emitted at the store's position: the cell is swapped out into a fresh rail, updated there with
; rule 6's clean of the previous rail, and swapped back; no copy of the cell, tape slot or old value remains. The
; rail *pp is a load copy and the form is a memory version change: un-copied after the second swap, not freed. Nothing in the lowering asks
; whether p and *pp are equal, or which of a and b either addresses.
source_filename = "bus_pointer_cell.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @bus_pointer_cell(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3, i32 noundef %4) {
  %6 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus M (called once, at function entry)
  %7 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 4, i64 4)    ; IR: %6 = alloca i32, align 4: a is bus-resident (its address is stored as a value)
  %8 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 4, i64 4)    ; IR: %7 = alloca i32, align 4: b is bus-resident
  %9 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 16, i64 16)    ; IR: %8 = alloca [2 x ptr], align 16: slot is bus-resident (indexed by a rail)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register k]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %10, double %1)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %11, double %3)    ; IR: %10 = cq_theta_si32(%2, %3)  [Ry]
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %7 to i64    ; IR: the run-time address of a (classical)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 1)    ; IR: store i32 1, ptr %6: the value seed (rule 7; kept with the store)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %12, i32 %13)    ; IR: store i32 1, ptr %6: a = 1  (kept store, classical address)
  %14 = ptrtoint ptr %8 to i64    ; IR: the run-time address of b (classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %14, i32 %11)    ; IR: store i32 %10, ptr %7: b = x  (kept store; the value rail is the register x)
  %15 = ptrtoint ptr %9 to i64    ; IR: the run-time address of slot (classical)
  %16 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %12)    ; IR: store ptr %6, ptr %8: the pointer &a is its address, an i64 seed (rules 7, 21; kept with the store)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %15, i32 %16)    ; IR: store ptr %6, ptr %8: slot[0] = &a  (kept store of an i64 cell value)
  %17 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %9, i64 8    ; IR: %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %8, i64 8  (classical)
  %18 = ptrtoint ptr %17 to i64    ; IR: the run-time address of slot[1] (classical)
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i64(i64 %14)    ; IR: store ptr %7, ptr %11: the pointer &b, an i64 seed (kept with the store)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i64_hl(i32 %6, i64 %18, i32 %19)    ; IR: store ptr %7, ptr %11: slot[1] = &b  (kept store)
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 1)    ; IR: %12 = and i32 %9, 1
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64(i32 %20)    ; IR: %13 = zext nneg i32 %12 to i64

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 7, 16, 20, 21.
; Checked: r = w' + lo (measured, %22 -> %23), lo = byte (k & 3) of x read BEFORE the byte store, w' = x with byte
; ((k >> 2) & 3) replaced by c, bytes counted little-endian (byte 0 = the low 8 bits), the sum mod 2^32. Memory: the
; four cells of w hold w' at exit.
; Clean: the two address chains (k & 3, its zext, the address rail P + (k & 3); k >> 2, the and, its zext, the address
; rail P + ((k >> 2) & 3)), the first uncomputed and freed right after the _unc of its load, the second right after its
; store; the word load copy %20 (rule 5 sentence
; 1: un-copied by its load _unc, no memory version change follows the load); the zext of lo.
; Kept: k and x (rotated; x is also the value rail of the i32 store), r (measured). Rule 5: the tape slot of the i32
; store (4 cells) and of the i8 store (1 cell), the seed c (%19, the i8 store's value rail), the byte load copy lo
; (%14: un-copied after its last reader, the zext _unc, but not freed: the i8 store, a memory version change, lies
; between the load and that point).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: bus_byte_view(1, .5, 0x04030201, 0, 0xAA): Ry(0) leaves x = 0x04030201 (bytes 1, 2, 3, 4), and Ry(.5) on
; every qubit of k = 1 flips each bit with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 (q = 1 - p), so i = k & 3 and j = (k >> 2) & 3 are
; independent: P(i = 1) = P(j = 0) = q^2 = 0.881329, P(i = 0) = P(i = 3) = P(j = 1) = P(j = 2) = pq = 0.057462,
; P(i = 2) = P(j = 3) = p^2 = 0.003747. r = (x with byte j := 0xAA) + (i + 1), 16 distinct values with P(i) P(j):
;   j = 0: 0x040302AB 0.050643, 0x040302AC 0.776741, 0x040302AD 0.003302, 0x040302AE 0.050643   (i = 0, 1, 2, 3)
;   j = 1: 0x0403AA02 0.003302, 0x0403AA03 0.050643, 0x0403AA04 0.000215, 0x0403AA05 0.003302
;   j = 2: 0x04AA0202 0.003302, 0x04AA0203 0.050643, 0x04AA0204 0.000215, 0x04AA0205 0.003302
;   j = 3: 0xAA030202 0.000215, 0xAA030203 0.003302, 0xAA030204 0.000014, 0xAA030205 0.000215
; (worked by hand from the C program; no simulator). For tx != 0 the same table holds per basis value of x, weighted
; by the product distribution of its 32 bits.
; w: its address is the base of two getelementptrs with a tainted index and it is stored a tainted value, so the
; alloca is bus-resident (rule 20): __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program point, no alloca remains, the lifetime
; markers are dropped (rule 16). P = its run-time address, a classical i64.
; STORE SIZE (rule 20, §1.3): every access is ONE call of the type and at the address its instruction names. The word
; store is qram_store_i32_hl(m, P, x): the 4 cells P..P+3, little-endian, so cell P + n holds byte n of x. b[k & 3] is
; ONE qram_load_i8 at the address rail P + (k & 3): one cell, whichever of the four the branch of k names. The byte
; store is ONE qram_store_i8 at the address rail P + ((k >> 2) & 3) of the seed c: it displaces one cell of the word
; into its tape slot. The final qram_load_i32_hl(m, P) reads the same 4 cells as one i32: three bytes of x and the
; byte c at position j. No access is split into bytes or widened to the object, and nothing is asked about what the
; cells hold or which object the address lies in.
; ADDRESS ARITHMETIC (rule 20): the gep's tainted index is already i64 (-O1's zext, emitted as the template), the
; element size is 1, so the address rail is add_i64_hl(index, P): the classical base is the _hl literal. The mul by
; the element size 1 is the identity and is not emitted (§6 compares semantics).
; UNCOMPUTE (rule 5): lo's copy is overtaken by the byte store: it is un-copied after its last reader, the zext _unc,
; and stays allocated; its address chain is template garbage that stays alive until that _unc and is uncomputed after it. The byte store is KEPT
; (slot and seed); its address chain is uncomputed after the store. The word load %20 has one consumer, the add r, and
; no memory version change follows the load, so it is un-copied right after the add (cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc: the
; cells still hold w') and freed; then the zext is uncomputed against lo, and lo is un-copied. Rule 6 is not used: both operands
; of the add are rule-5 garbage.

; Checked: bus_pointer_arg: a[0] + a[1] (the add rail, measured) = 5 + ((k & 3) == 0 ? x : 0); the cells a[0..3] at
; exit: a[k & 3] = x, then a[2] = x, then a[1] = 5. bus_pointer_result: tab[1] (the load copy, measured) =
; ((k & 3) == 1 ? v : 0); the cells tab[0..3] at exit: tab[k & 3] = v. For the driver (k0 = 1, tk = .5, Ry on every
; bit of k): P(k & 3 = 0) = 0.0575, P(1) = 0.8813, P(2) = 0.0037, P(3) = 0.0575. bus_pointer_arg(1, .5, 9, .25)
; measures 5 with p = 0.9425 and 5 + x with p = 0.0575 (x the rotated 9: 14 with p = 0.0575 * 0.6057 = 0.0348);
; bus_pointer_result(1, .5, 9) measures 9 with p = 0.8813 and 0 with p = 0.1187 (tab is zero at the first call).
; Clean: bus_pointer_arg: the address chain of &a[k & 3] (k & 3, its zext, the scaled index, the address rail), each
; uncomputed by its template's _unc after the store in the clone and freed; the two load copies a[0] and a[1],
; un-copied after the add, before the measurement (no memory version change follows the loads) and freed.
; bus_pointer_result: the address rail __cq_q_slot_1 returned, zeroed by the twin __cq_q_slot_1_unc after the store
; and freed; every rail inside __cq_q_slot_1 and its twin.
; Kept: bus_pointer_arg: k and x (rotated registers; x is also the value rail of both clones' stores), the sum
; (measured), and by rule 5: the 16 tape slots of the memset's byte stores with their one value seed (i8 0), the tape
; slot of the store in __cq_q_put_11, the tape slot of the store in __cq_q_put_01, the tape slot and the value seed
; (i32 5) of the store in put. bus_pointer_result: k (rotated), the load copy of tab[1] (measured), and by rule 5 the
; tape slot and the value seed (i32 v) of the store.
; Rotations: bus_pointer_arg: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1). bus_pointer_result: (Ry, k, tk, 1).
; A POINTER IS ONE SCALAR (§1.4, rules 1, 21). put(&a[k & 3], x) passes an address rail and a value rail: the clone
; __cq_q_put_11(i32 address rail, i32 value rail), mask digit 1 for the pointer, nothing about the pointee in the name
; or the parameter list. put(&a[2], x) passes a classical ptr and a value rail: the clone __cq_q_put_01(ptr, i32 value
; rail), mask digit 0 for the pointer, which stays the C ptr (no handle, no seed) and is the _hl address of the store.
; put(&a[1], 5) passes a classical ptr and a classical int: the all-zero mask, which is put's OWN symbol with its C
; parameter list, lowered (its store is a bus store at the run-time address, the value a seed).
; slot(k) returns a pointer computed from a rail: __cq_q_slot_1 returns ONE i32 handle to a 64-bit address rail; slot's
; own symbol has no caller left and is dropped (§1.4).
; A CLONE THAT STORES HAS NO TWIN (rules 5, 18): put writes memory, so none of __cq_q_put_11, __cq_q_put_01 and put
; has an _unc and each store's tape slot stays. The caller treats the rails it passed by its own rules: the address
; rail is a template result and is uncomputed after the call (the store is over), x is a user register. slot writes
; nothing and loads nothing, so its twin exists and runs after the result's last consumer, the store through it.
; THE ALLOCA IS BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20): a[] is indexed by a rail and passed to a callee, so it is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at
; its program point, no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Its memset is rule 22's host
; loop of 16 kept byte stores of one i8 seed at the classical addresses a + j (the cells are HOST and stay HOST).
; The gep with a tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic on the run-time base: zext (as -O1 wrote it), mul by the
; element size, add of the classical base address (rule 20); tab is a mutable global and lives at its host address.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins) per externally
; visible function. No conforming example of the corpus emits one; this module follows the corpus and registers
; nothing for bus_pointer_arg and bus_pointer_result (host code, no gate: §6 cannot tell the two readings apart).
; SPEC GAP: rule 5 sentence 1 speaks of the last consumer's uncompute; here the consumer (the add) is measured and has
; none. The load copies are un-copied right after the add, before the measurement, as a template operand of a
; measured result is (29, 195).
; SPEC GAP: rule 5 sentence 3 names two producers of a store's address rail (a template, a bus load). Here one address
; is the result of a twinned clone: it follows rule 18, twin after the store, then free. The other is a template
; result passed INTO a storing clone: the caller uncomputes it after the call, as it would after its own store.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no calling convention, linkage or attributes for a clone called by name or a lowered own symbol;
; they keep the callee's (internal fastcc), as the corpus does (07, 195), and every memory, capture, nullness and
; purity fact of the original (nocapture, writeonly, nonnull, memory(argmem: write), memory(none), nofree, willreturn)
