; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 22, 20, 21, 5, 2, 3, 4, 7, 14.
; Checked: r = a[k & 7] after the realloc (the load copy at the address rail, measured): x when k & 4 == 0 (the cell
; a[k & 3] the first store wrote, carried over by the copy), 2 when k & 7 == 7, else 0 (zeroed __cq_alloc memory).
; Clean: both address chains (and, zext, mul, add: uncomputed right after their access), min(s, 32) and the header load
; copy s (un-copied before the first copy store: its only consumer umin and that consumer's _unc precede the next memory
; version change, rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: k and x (rotated; x is also the value rail of the kept store a[k & 3] = x); the tape slot of that store; for
; each of the 32 copy trips the predicate p_j = (min(s, 32) > j), the controlled load copy of byte j (the value rail
; of its kept store) and that store's tape slot (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 22); the seed 2 and the tape slot of a[7] = 2
; (rule 7); r (the load copy, measured: rule 2).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Driver bus_heap(1, .5, 9, .25): Ry acts on every qubit of a register, so each bit of k flips with probability
; p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 and each bit of x with q = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544, independently. The header at P0 - 8
; reads 16, so p_0..p_15 are 1 and p_16..p_31 are 0: 16 bytes are copied. Measured r: k & 4 == 0 (1 - p = 0.938791)
; gives r = x, so r = 9 with (1 - p)(1 - q)^32 = 0.568662 and each single-bit neighbour of 9 with
; (1 - p) q (1 - q)^31 = 0.008979; k & 7 == 7 gives r = 2 with p^2 (1 - p) = 0.003517 (0.003519 with x = 2);
; k & 4 != 0 and k & 7 != 7 gives r = 0 with p - p^2 (1 - p) = 0.057692 (0.057833 with x = 0).
; ALLOCATION (rule 16). malloc(16) is __cq_alloc(16, 16) (alignment 16: the call names none): zeroed host memory at an
; address never reused, its size as an i64 in the 8 bytes before it. Nothing is known about the block at compile time.
; realloc(p, 32) with a classical p is q = __cq_alloc(32, 16), s = the i64 bus load at p - 8 (_hl: a classical
; address; a rail all the same, rule 3) and a rule-22 copy of min(s, 32) bytes from p to q: the length is the rail
; umin_i64_hl(s, 32), so the copy is the quantum-length form, its trip bound the new block's size 32 (not K2; no
; overflow predicate: min(s, 32) <= 32), byte j loaded and stored under p_j = icmp_ugt_i64_hl(min(s, 32), j) by the
; _hl_controlled forms at the classical addresses p + j and q + j. The copy loads all its bytes, then stores all of
; them. Nothing is done for p: the old block stays, and free(a) emits nothing. A pointer is its run-time i64 (rule 21):
; p and q are classical here, and nothing else is known about them. The size is always the bus load, never a host read
; of the header, also for a classical p and n: the header cells are bus cells and may be QUANTUM (rule 3).
; The cells of the old block are QUANTUM after the address-rail store (it can reach all 16), so the 16 copied bytes
; are quantum data although every address and predicate of the copy is classical-valued here.
; SPEC GAP (rule 22, carrier): how the byte rails of the load loop reach the store loop is not stated. Chosen: the load
; loop pushes p_j, then the byte rail, on cqrt_push (a handle that outlives its SSA value, §1.1; never stored in program
; memory) and the store loop pops them, so it stores bytes 31 down to 0 (a copy has no direction). These pushes are the
; carrier between the two loops, not rule 14's reverse-loop pushes: the rails are kept (rule 5) and no reverse loop
; follows, so rule 14's "a kept trip rail is not pushed" does not apply to them.
; SPEC GAP (rule 22, quantum length): whether the store loop computes its own p_j is not stated. Chosen: ONE p_j per
; byte, computed in the load loop; it controls byte j's load and byte j's store and is kept as that store's control
; rail (rule 5). The length rail and what produced it (min(s, 32), s) then have their last consumer in the load loop
; and are uncomputed between the two loops, before the first store; a second set of p_j computed in the store loop
; would keep s (overtaken by the stores) and uncompute 32 more flags.
; SPEC GAP (rule 16, realloc): the template of min(s, n) is not named. Chosen: the length rail is umin_i64_hl(s, n)
; and p_j compares that rail; the trip bound is the new block's size in place of min(K2, B) (so no loop-cutoff tag on any line), and there is
; no overflow predicate, since the length never exceeds the bound.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 5 (Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 20, 22, 21, 16, 14, 8, 12, 4, 2, 7.
; Checked: a[0] at exit = ((k & 3) == 0 ? y : 1), measured through load 3 (%38 -> %39); the cells a[0..3] on the bus at
; exit: a[k & 3] = y, each other cell a[i] = i + 1 (its initializer value).
; Clean: the address chain of load 1 and of the store (k & 3 %25, its zext %26, the scaled index %27, the address rail
; A1 %28: one chain, -O1 reuses the gep %12), uncomputed after the STORE; the copy L1 (%29) of load 1 and its flag L1 >
; 2 (%30), uncomputed and freed before the store; the address chain of load 2 (k >> 2, & 3, zext, scaled index, A2:
; %31..%35), uncomputed right after the un-copy of L2; the flag L2 > 2 (%37), uncomputed after its phase.
; Kept: k (%10) and y (%11) (rotated registers; y is also the value rail of the kept store). Rule 5 sentence 3: the tape
; slot of the store a[k & 3] = y, and the 16 tape slots of the initializer's byte stores with their 16 value rails, the
; load copies of the source bytes (%15, one per trip of the load loop, handed to the store loop by cqrt_push /
; cqrt_pop; rule 22: never un-copied, never freed). Rule 5 sentence 1: the copy L2 (%36) of load 2 (the store
; overtakes it before its consumer %22: un-copied after %22's uncompute, left allocated). Rule 2: L3 (%38, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1); (P, flag, p1, INIT[k & 3] > 2); (P, flag, p2, INIT[(k >> 2) & 3] > 2), with
; INIT = {1, 2, 3, 4}: the predicates are bit 1 of k and bit 3 of k. Both phases read the cells BEFORE the store.
; Expected for the driver bus_kept_and_uncopied(1, .5, 9, .25, .125, .375) (analytic, not replayed): Ry(t) flips each
; qubit of a basis register with probability sin^2(t/2). The result is y iff bits 1..0 of k are 00: k0 = 1, so bit 0
; must flip and bit 1 must not, probability sin^2(.25) cos^2(.25) = sin^2(.5) / 4 = 0.057462; otherwise it is 1
; (0.942538). Given the store hit a[0], the result is y0 = 9 with each of its 32 bits flipped independently with
; probability s = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544. So P(1) = 0.942538 + 0.057462 s (1 - s)^31 = 0.943088, P(9) = 0.057462 (1 -
; s)^32 = 0.034807, and P(v) = 0.057462 s^d (1 - s)^(32 - d) for any other v at Hamming distance d from 9. The two
; phases are diagonal and precede no rotation: they do not change this distribution. On the unrotated branch (k = 1)
; load 2 reads a[0] = 1 and the store hits a[1]; on every branch where bits 3..2 of k equal bits 1..0 the two hit the
; same cell, and t is the initializer value there (before the store), never y.
; NOTHING IS DEFERRED. The bus is one linear value and no two accesses commute for the compiler (rule 5): whether load 1
; and the store hit the same cell is never asked, although here they share the SSA address %12. A load copy has exactly
; two fates, decided by where its last consumer and that consumer's uncompute lie relative to the next memory version
; change. Load 1 (%13): its only consumer is the flag %14, whose last controlled gate is the phase p1 in block %15; the
; flag is uncomputed, then the copy is un-copied (cqrt_qram_load_i32_unc, the cells still hold what the load read) and
; freed, all before the store. Load 2 (%21): its consumer %22 follows the store, so the copy is un-copied after the
; flag's uncompute (at the same address rail A2, which stays alive until then) and left allocated: the store came
; between. The store is a kept store: no _unc exists, its tape slot holds the displaced cell content, and
; its value rail y is never freed. Its address rail A1 is a template result and is uncomputed AFTER the store; A2 is
; uncomputed right after L2's un-copy, its last reader.
; MEMORY. a is bus-resident (a getelementptr with a tainted index reaches it, rule 20): no alloca remains, the block is
; __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the alloca's program point, and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). The initializer

; %12 and %20 are 64-bit template arithmetic on the run-time base (rule 20): zext, mul by sizeof(int), add of the

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 3, 14, 16, 5, 6, 7, 8, 4, 2.
; Checked: plain_local: x + c[j & 3] (measured, %12 -> %14). overtaint_kloop: x after the scan, x0 + the sum of the leading
; nonzero cells of c (measured: the carried rail x_K, %18 -> %41; rule 6 leaves it the only x rail).
; Clean: plain_local: the old x rail (%6, rule 6: |0> after the copy) and the inverse t (%13), both freed.
; overtaint_kloop: every trip's load copy (%14), exit test (%15) and trip predicate a_0..a_{K-1} (%16, the K-th body's
; included), popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop (no memory version change follows ext_fill, so every load is
; un-copied, rule 5 sentence 1); the after-trip-K load and test (%26, %27, undone at once); the |1> seed (%7, freed
; directly, rule 7); the OLD x of every trip (rule 6 in a rolled loop: x' = a ? x + v : x is a bijection in x and the
; trip predicate reads only memory, so the arm's garbage x + v is uncomputed first and t = a ? x' - v : x' is copied
; onto the old x; trip 0's old x is the rotated rail %6 itself, |0> after the copy and freed).
; Kept: plain_local: the sum (%12, measured). overtaint_kloop: x_K (%18 of the last trip, measured: the rotated
; register's rule-6 image) and a_K (%28, rule 14: the exit test c[K] != 0 evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with the
; predicate of trip K; no bound of the trip count is known: the loop ends on a 0 read from memory, and the array's
; extent [4 x i32], the inbounds gep and the undefined behaviour of a fifth read are never a bound, rule 21). No store,
; no tape slot: neither function writes the bus (plain_local's stores are plain host stores, ext_fill writes host
; bytes).
; Rotations: plain_local: (Ry, x, tx, 1). overtaint_kloop: (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; plain_local. c is a HOST-RESIDENT alloca (rule 20 (b)): its size is untainted and its every transitive user, through
; getelementptrs with untainted indices (the induction %15, the classical j & 3), is a load with no quantum predicate
; in scope, a store through it of an untainted value (n * i + 1) with no quantum predicate in scope, or a lifetime
; marker. So the alloca, the store loop, the gep and the load stay the plain LLVM instructions, the lifetime markers
; stay with them, the loaded c[j & 3] is CLASSICAL (rule 3) and the function never calls __cq_mem. x + c[j & 3] is
; then example 01: a mixed add with the run-time classical value as the _hl literal, and rule 6 cleans the old x.
; overtaint_kloop. The same array is passed to a bodiless callee: a call is no user rule 20 (b) allows, so c is
; BUS-RESIDENT: __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the alloca's program point (rules 16, 20: zeroed, no alloca remains, the
; lifetime markers are dropped). ext_fill has classical arguments, no quantum predicate in scope and no tape or abort
; event before it: an ORDINARY HOST CALL (rule 16), made as it stands with the block's address. It writes host bytes,
; which the bus sees through the overlay (the cells stay HOST; nothing is seeded or copied). It is a memory version
; change, the last one of the function. Every load of c is a bus load and its value a rail, whatever ext_fill wrote
; (rule 3: over-taint is accepted, such a rail costs no qubit), so the exit test c[i] != 0 reads a rail and the loop
; is a K-LOOP (rule 14, K = 4; the literal 4 below is K). Re-rolled: -O1's pre-header guard (load c[0], == 0) is the
; latch test (load c[i + 1], == 0) one trip earlier, the same load at the affine address {c,+,4}, so it is trip 0.
; Trip j loads c[j] under the predicate of REACHING its test (a_{j-1}; the |1> seed for trip 0), forms
; a_j = a_{j-1} & (c[j] != 0) (the IR's flag is the == 0 exit edge, so the conjunction sits in an X bracket, rule 8)
; and runs the body x += c[j] under a_j through the select merge. The address is an AFFINE INDUCTION with a classical
; start: &c[j] is the classical i64 of the gep at the classical trip index, so every access is _hl; it is
; _hl_controlled because a trip C would not run must touch no cell and no host byte, and its _unc takes the same
; control. Nothing is loaded before the loop on its behalf. After the K-th body the test is evaluated once more
; (c[K], under a_{K-1}: one cell past the block, read only on the branch where C reads it too; no bound is checked,
; rule 21) and a_K is kept. The reverse loop recomputes each address from its trip index and pops the load copy, the
; test and the reach predicate of each trip.
; Basis check (driver: plain_local(3, .5, 2, 1); overtaint_kloop(3, .5, 2) with a host ext_fill that writes
; c = {n, n + 1, 0}, i.e. {2, 3, 0, 0}): Ry(.5) acts on each of the 32 qubits of x0 = 3, so x = 3 ^ e with
; P(e) = p^|e| (1 - p)^(32 - |e|), p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209, |e| the number of flipped bits. plain_local: c = {1, 3,
; 5, 7}, c[1] = 3, the measured value is (3 ^ e) + 3 mod 2^32: 6 with probability (1 - p)^32 = 0.132498, each of the

name: 204_bus_lifetime_reuse
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 16, 14, 18, 5, 6, 7, 9, 21, 3, 8, 19, 4, 2.
; Checked: bus_scope_reuse: s = sum over i < n of a[0] + a[1] after trip i's stores (the carried rail, measured). With
; b_i = (k >> i) & 1: a[0] = b_i ? i : x, and a[1] = x when b_j = 1 for some j <= i, else 0 (never written: the zeroed
; block). bus_recursion: walk(k, x, d) = sum over levels j = d..0 of ((k >> (d - j)) & 1) ? j : x (the outermost
; clone's result rail, measured). The cells of the blocks are not named outputs.
; Clean: bus_scope_reuse, per trip: the address chain lshr / and / zext / mul / add (uncomputed and freed right after
; the store), the load copies of a[0] and a[1] (un-copied and freed in the trip: no memory version change lies between
; a load and its _unc), the old s, the intermediate image s + a[0] and the two rule-6 rails t (rule 6 in the body, as
; 27; trip 0's old s is the |0> seed). __cq_q_walk_110, per activation: the address chain and / zext / mul / add, the
; argument rail k >> 1 (after the call), the inner activation's result below (rule 6, cleaned from a[0] + below; on the
; d == 0 path the |0> seed that stands for below, freed by the same clean-up), the rule-6 rail t and the load copy of
; a[0] (un-copied before the return).
; Kept: bus_scope_reuse: k and x (rotated; x is also the value rail of every trip's address-rail store, rule 5); per
; trip the seed i (value rail of the classical-address store, rule 5: a basis state, no qubit) and the two tape slots
; (backend rails, rule 5); s (measured: the last trip's image, or the seed itself when n <= 0).
; bus_recursion: k and x (rotated; x is the value rail of every activation's address-rail store); per activation the
; two seeds d and 0 and the three tape slots (rule 5); the outermost result (measured). No result rail of an inner
; activation stays: each is cleaned by its caller (rule 6).
; Rotations: bus_scope_reuse: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1). bus_recursion: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: each Ry acts on all 32 qubits of its register and everything after the rotations is a basis permutation,
; so the measured value is the C program on independent bit flips: a bit of k flips with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209,
; a bit of x with q = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544 (x = 9 ^ e with q^|e| (1 - q)^(32 - |e|); x = 9: 0.605738).
; bus_scope_reuse(1, .5, 9, .25, 2): trip 0 adds x on either branch of b_0 (x lands in a[0] or in a[1], the other cell
; is 0). Trip 1 adds 1 + x when b_1 = 1 and x + a[1] when b_1 = 0, where a[1] is what trip 0 left: x when b_0 = 1, else
; 0. Bits (b_0, b_1) = (1, 0), (1, 1), (0, 0), (0, 1) with 0.881329, 0.057462, 0.057462, 0.003747 give s = 3x, 2x + 1,
; 2x, 2x + 1 (at x = 9: 27, 19, 18, 19).
; bus_recursion(1, .5, 9, .25, 2): bits (k0, k1, k2) of k; the levels d = 2, 1, 0 read a[0] = k0 ? 2 : x, k1 ? 1 : x,
; k2 ? 0 : x. (1,0,0): 2x + 2 with 0.827379 (x = 9: 20); (1,0,1): x + 2, (1,1,0): x + 3, (0,0,0): 3x with 0.053945
; each; (1,1,1): 3, (0,0,1): 2x, (0,1,0): 2x + 1 with 0.003517 each; (0,1,1): x + 1 with 0.000229.
; LIFETIME MARKERS ARE DROPPED (rules 16, 20). bus_scope_reuse: a[] is declared in the loop body, but -O1 has ONE
; alloca outside the loop with llvm.lifetime.start/end inside it. A getelementptr with a tainted index is among its
; users, so the alloca is BUS-RESIDENT: it is ONE __cq_alloc(8, 4) block at the alloca's program point, no alloca
; remains, and the markers emit nothing. The cells therefore carry over from trip to trip: nothing is undone at the
; end of a trip. Trip i's store a[0] = i is an ordinary kept store whose tape slot takes whatever trip i - 1 left in
; a[0] (x on one branch of k); its address and value are classical-valued, but the cell may be QUANTUM from the trip
; before: nothing is asked, it is the same qram_store_i32_hl of a seed. a[1] is written by no initializer, so its load
; reads what the block holds.
; THE CARRY-OVER IS A NAMED-OUTPUT DIFFERENCE: on the branch (b_0, b_1) = (1, 0), the dominant one of the driver call,
; trip 1 reads in a[1] the x that trip 0 stored there and s = 3x. A compiler that allocates a fresh zeroed block per
; trip (or zeroes the block at a lifetime marker) gives 2x there. C calls that read indeterminate; the reference takes
; the value the cell holds on the bus (SPEC GAP below).
; THE LOOP (rule 14, classical bound): it stays the classical loop. Every trip rail is either kept by rule 5 or
; uncomputed in the trip, so nothing is pushed and there is no reverse loop: the address chain goes right after its
; store; s1 = a[0] + s is a bijection in s and s' = s1 + a[1] one in s1, the other operand of each is a load copy, so
; rule 6 cleans the old s and then s1 in the body (as 27), each right after its update, and each copy is un-copied
; after the clean-up that reads it, before the next memory version change, which is the next trip's first store. The
; carried s is measured directly.
; THE RECURSION (rules 14, 18): the depth d is classical, so the recursive call is an ordinary call of the ONE clone
; __cq_q_walk_110 (mask left to right: k, x quantum, d classical) under the classical branch d != 0; no predicate, no
; _ctl clone, hence no activation counter (§1.4) and no cutoff. Every activation runs __cq_alloc(8, 4) once: its own
; zeroed block at an address never reused, so the inner activation's stores cannot reach the cells the outer one
; loads after the call. The clone writes memory, so it has NO twin and no caller calls one. Its result a[0] + below is
; a rule-6 bijection in below whose other operand is the load copy: below (the inner activation's result, dead after
; the add) is cleaned from the sum, and the sum, the rule-6 image, is returned directly with no copy-out (a copy could
; not be followed by the image's uncompute, which would read the cleaned below). The phi of the call's result against
; the literal 0 is a classical phi over handles (rule 9), the 0 a seed (rule 7) minted on its edge and released by
; the same clean-up as the call path's below (as trip 0's old rail of a rolled loop). The unlifted walk has no caller
; left and is dropped (§1.4).
; SPEC GAP: rule 6 names no exception for a call result, rule 18 says the result of a callee without a twin is KEPT
; by the caller and gives the clone the copy-out form. Read here: KEPT only means that no twin is called, so rule 6
; cleans below like any other rail; a clone whose result is a rule-6 image returns the image rail directly; a seed
; that is a classical phi incoming of the cleaned value is freed by the same clean-up, not under a second classical
; branch.
; SPEC GAP: §6 says an indeterminate value the C program reads is 0 for the reference. By rule 20 a block-scoped
; bus-resident object is one block whose cells carry over, so from trip 1 on a[1] holds what the trip before left
; (x). Read here: the reference takes what the cell holds on the bus, 0 only for a cell never written.
; SPEC GAP: rule 5 sentence 1 asks for the uncompute of the load's last consumer. In both functions the consumer (an
; add) is a rule-6 image (the carried s, the clone's result), which has none; read as for a template operand (27's
; g): the copy is un-copied after its last reader (rule 6's t), before the next memory version change.
; SPEC GAP: rule 6 "both operands dead" does not say that a bus load copy is "garbage that rule 5 uncomputes anyway".
; It is read so (the copy's un-copy is possible here), so rule 6 cleans the other operand (the old s, below) although
; the copy is operand 0.
; SPEC GAP: rule 9 says a classical phi over handles needs no gate; where its literal incoming is minted is not
; stated. The seed is minted in a block on its edge (in the pred it would stay allocated on the call path).
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins) per externally
; visible function. The corpus emits a row only for an address-taken function (212); no example registers a function
; that is only externally visible, and this module follows that: nothing is registered for bus_scope_reuse and
; bus_recursion.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no calling convention or linkage for a clone called by name; the clone keeps the callee's
; (internal fastcc), as the corpus does (07, 33).

name: 205_quantum_depth_one_clone
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 6, 8, 9, 14, 18, 19, 20; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem), §1.4 (Recursion: one _ctl clone, the activation counter).
; Checked: quantum_depth_one_clone: down(n, a) with the recursion cut at K = 4 (the copied-out result %5, measured -> %6).
;          bool_cell_rotate: flag (the load copy %4, measured -> %5), the cell `flag` = the rotated bit.
;          theta_add_cell: acc (the load copy %7, measured -> %8), the cell `acc` = the rotated 5, plus d.
; Clean: in __cq_q_down_10, in every activation of __cq_q_down_10_ctl that runs its body and of its twin: the base-case
;        flag c, n - 1, the conjunction p & !c (_ctl and twin only), the callee's result (zeroed by the twin, then freed;
;        a |0> rail at the cut), the difference and the merge. bool_cell_rotate: the swap rail (%3). theta_add_cell: the
;        rotated old rail (%4, rule 6), the inverse t = y' - d (%6) and the rail the cell's |0> went to (%5).
; Kept: quantum_depth_one_clone: the user register n (%4), the result rail of __cq_q_down_10 (%5, measured), and ONE
;       overflow rail per cut activation of __cq_q_down_10_ctl (rule 14): each a copy_i1 of that activation's predicate,
;       [n >= 5]; 2^K = 16 of them in one call of the entry (see SPEC GAP 4). bool_cell_rotate: the load copy of flag (%4,
;       measured). theta_add_cell: the load copy of acc (%7, measured). No tape slot: both cell updates are in-place forms.
; Rotations: quantum_depth_one_clone: (Ry, n, th, 1). bool_cell_rotate: (Ry at width i1, the cell flag, th, 1).
;            theta_add_cell: (Ry, the cell acc, th, 1).
; Expected (Ry(th) acts on every qubit of a rail, so each bit flips with probability s(th) = sin^2(th/2), independently):
;   quantum_depth_one_clone(2, .5, 1): n from 2 with s = 0.0612087. With the cut, down(n, 1) is 1 for n <= 0, -1 for
;     n = 1, 2 for n = 2, -2 for n = 3, 3 for n = 4, and 3 for every n >= 5 (the cut activation returns |0>, so the
;     deepest running level returns a + 4 and the levels above give -1, a + 3, -2, a + 2; C would give another value
;     there, and every overflow rail reads 1). Measured: 3 with probability 0.788452 (0.787889 of it from n >= 5,
;     0.000563 from n = 4), 2 with 0.132498 (n unchanged), 1 with 0.069848 (n < 0: 0.061209, n = 0: 0.008639), -2 with
;     0.008639, -1 with 0.000563. P(overflow rails = 1) = 0.787889.
;   bool_cell_rotate(.5): flag from 0 with s = 0.0612087: 1 with probability 0.0612087, 0 with 0.9387913.
;   theta_add_cell(.25, 3): acc from 5 with s = 0.0155438: the measured acc + 3 is 8 with probability 0.605738 (acc
;     unchanged); each single-bit flip of acc has probability 0.009564.
; RECURSION WITH QUANTUM DEPTH, ONE CLONE (§1.4, rule 14). down's base-case test reads the rail n, and its recursive call
; sits in the arm n > 0: a call under a quantum predicate of a function on a call cycle, so the callee is the _ctl clone
; (rule 19), __cq_q_down_10_ctl(pred, n, a): mask 10 at every depth (a + 1 stays classical), ONE clone whatever the
; depth, and no depth is passed. The entry calls down with no predicate in scope: __cq_q_down_10(n, a), the rule-18 clone
; of mask 10. down's own symbol has no remaining use and is dropped (§1.4).
; The clone body (all three definitions share it). c = (n < 1) is the base-case flag. The recursive arm's pure code
; (n - 1; a + 1 is classical) is hoisted and computed unguarded (rule 9); the call stays in its arm, under NOT c: an X
; bracket on c in __cq_q_down_10 (rule 8: the false edge), and in the _ctl clone the conjunction f = p & !c in a fresh
; rail (and_i1 inside the X bracket), which is the callee's predicate. The call is not tail: a - r is computed after it
; (sub_lh, unguarded: r is read by nothing when c holds), and the phi merges by select on c (rule 9). The clone copies
; the merge out, uncomputes select and sub, zeroes r by the callee's twin __cq_q_down_10_ctl_unc(pred, r, n - 1, a + 1)
; under the same predicate value (the same bracket, or f before its teardown), frees r, and uncomputes f, n - 1 and c.
; The twin recomputes the same chain, XORs the merge out of the result rail and uncomputes; the caller frees the result.
; __cq_q_down_10 has no twin (nobody calls one, §1.4): its result is measured by the entry.
; THE ACTIVATION COUNTER AND THE CUT. down lies on a call cycle, so it has one module-internal classical counter of its
; live _ctl activations, @__cq_act_down (§1.4). __cq_q_down_10_ctl and its twin read it on entry (the depth d), add 1,
; and subtract 1 at their return. A classical branch on d decides: while d < K = 4 [K] the body runs; at d = K the
; clone returns at once, its result a |0> rail, and a copy_i1 of its predicate into a fresh rail is the kept overflow
; predicate (rule 14: one per cut activation; no range fact bounds n, so it is kept). The twin makes the same cut: it
; returns at once and touches nothing (the result it would zero is |0> already). __cq_q_down_10 is no _ctl clone and
; does not count, so the activations are: __cq_q_down_10 on n, then _ctl at d = 0..3 on n - 1..n - 4, and the cut at
; d = 4, whose predicate is n >= 1 & n >= 2 & .. & n >= 5 = [n >= 5]. The host recursion gives every activation its own
; rails. Cost: each body calls the next level's clone and its twin, so 2^(d+1) bodies run at depth d and 2^K = 16
; forward activations reach the cut.
; bool_cell_rotate. `load i8 @flag (!range [0, 2)); trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext to i8; store i8 @flag` is rule 5's
; in-place form through the Width-casts clause: the form at width i1 (rule 2: <W> is the cq_theta's own width, not the
; cell's access type): qram_swap_i1_hl, ry_i1, qram_swap_i1_hl, free. The high 7 bits of the cell never leave it.
; cq_measure reads the rotated value %4, a second reader of a value at the cq_theta step: it reads a plain load taken
; after the swap-in (rule 5, Readers), and that copy is measured and stays (rule 2).
; theta_add_cell. `load @acc; cq_theta_si32; add %1; store @acc` is ONE in-place form with two steps: the Ry on the
; swap rail, then the rule-6 bijection y' = y + d with the clean of the previous (rotated) rail, then the swap-in of y'.
; Nothing remains: no copy of the cell, no tape slot, no old value. cq_measure reads y' = %5, which the store also
; reads: a plain load taken after the swap-in, measured.
; SPEC GAPS (each marked at its line; the choice is the one that needs least from an implementer):
;  1. The activation counter has no name in §1.4. Chosen: internal global i32 @__cq_act_<fn>, zero-initialised, as in
;     211; "adds 1" / "subtracts 1" are load, add, store on it. It is compiler state, not program memory: no bus access,
;     no memory version change (rule 5), and it does not make down a function that writes memory (so the twin exists).
;  2. The parameter order of a _ctl clone's twin. Chosen: _ctl_unc(pred, outs.., args..), the predicate first as for
;     _t_ctl_unc (§1.4) and as in 211.
;  3. "_ctl controls every gate" (§1.4) for a clone that returns a value: the controlled arithmetic grid is retired, so
;     the templates run unguarded (rule 9) and the copy-out is the plain copy_<W> of rule 18's one form; the result under
;     pred = 0 is then not |0>, and the caller's select (rule 9) never reads it there. Only the callee's predicate (the
;     conjunction) and the overflow copy read pred.
;  4. Whether the forward _ctl clone called from a twin's recomputation keeps an overflow rail again. Rule 14 says one
;     per cut activation and rule 18's _pure removes phases only, so every forward cut activation keeps one (16 here,
;     all copies of the same predicate) and the twin's own cut keeps none.
;  5. The type of the Readers clause's plain load under the Width-casts clause. Chosen: the form's width U
;     (qram_load_i1_hl, §1.3: loaded from the low bit), not a load at the cell type followed by a trunc template.

  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 5 (in-place form, Readers clause; Memory, sentences 1 to 3), 2, 6 (a memory cell), 20, 21, 3, 7; §1.3 (the bus, qram_swap).
; Two functions, ONE construction: theta_twice_store_between (p = &cell, q = &g: two globals) and
; theta_twice_store_between_ptr (p, q = the pointer arguments). Below, "the cell" is the 4 cells at p, "the other cell"
; the 4 cells at q; the value names in parentheses are those of the first function / of the _ptr function.
; Checked: the returned value = the cell after both rotations (measured: the phi %22 -> %23 / %26 -> %27); the cell at
; exit (read from the bus) holds that same value; on the DISJOINT path the other cell at exit = its old value + 1.
; Clean: the swap rail of the first form (%4 / %8, |0> after its swap-in); of the increment: the swapped-out old value
; (%14 / %18, rule 6), the inverse t = g' - 1 (%16 / %20) and the rail the cell's |0> went to (%15 / %19). On the DISJOINT
; path also the swap rail of the second form (%18 / %22, |0> after its swap-in).
; Kept: on the DISJOINT path: the load copy of the cell taken after the second swap-in (%19 / %23, measured, rule 2);
; nothing else: three in-place forms keep no rail, no tape slot and no old value. On the OVERLAP path: the load copy of
; the cell (%11 / %15: rotated by the second cq_theta, so a FROZEN register, rule 2; it is also the value rail of the
; kept store and the measured rail) and the tape slot of the kept store (rule 5 sentence 3).
; Rotations: DISJOINT path: (Ry, the cell, t1, 1); (Ry, the cell, t2, 1). OVERLAP path: (Ry, the cell, t1, 1); (Ry, the
; load copy of the cell, t2, 1). The path is chosen by a CLASSICAL run-time branch, never a control.
; Expected for the driver (analytic, not replayed; the trace stubs compute nothing, so each call is stated for the
; content v the cell holds when the call starts; s1 = sin^2(t1/2) = 0.0612087, s2 = sin^2(t2/2) = 0.0155438):
;   theta_twice_store_between(.5, .25) and theta_twice_store_between_ptr(&cell, &g, .5, .25): distinct objects, the
;   DISJOINT path. The trace shows swap, Ry(t1), swap, free on P0; the increment between two swaps on the other
;   address; swap, Ry(t2), swap, free on P0; qram_load_i32_hl(P0), measure of that copy; no qram_store. Ry(.5) then
;   Ry(.25) on every qubit of the cell is Ry(.75) on every qubit: each of the 32 bits of v flips independently with
;   probability s = sin^2(.375) = 0.1341556. P(v') = s^d (1 - s)^(32 - d), d the Hamming distance of v' from v:
;   P(v) = 0.009956, each single-bit neighbour 0.001543 (first call: v = 1, neighbours 0, 3, 5, 9, ...). The increment
;   does not change this; g is one larger after each of the two calls (a HOST cell while address and content are
;   classical-valued, so the swaps write the host bytes, §1.3).
;   theta_twice_store_between_ptr(&cell, &cell, .5, .25): q == p, the OVERLAP path. The trace shows swap, Ry(t1), swap,
;   free on P0; qram_load_i32_hl(P0) BEFORE the increment; the increment between two swaps on P0 itself; Ry(t2) on the
;   load copy; ONE qram_store_i32_hl(P0, the copy); measure of the copy; no second form and no later load. The copy is
;   a basis copy of the cell after Ry(t1), taken before the increment, and Ry(t2) acts on the copy alone: each bit of
;   the measured value differs from v with probability f = s1 (1 - s2) + (1 - s1) s2 = 0.0748497 (NOT Ry(t1 + t2):
;   the cell's own qubits stay entangled with the copy), so P(v) = (1 - f)^32 = 0.082946, each single-bit neighbour
;   0.006711. The kept store puts the copy into the cell (the incremented content goes to the tape slot), so the cell
;   at exit holds the measured value. C gives this call no meaning (two restrict pointers to one object, both written);
;   the lowered code never consults restrict/noalias (rule 21) and is defined for every pair of addresses.
; THE THREE UPDATES (first function; the _ptr function is the same with %0, %1 for @cell, @g and its values two/four
; higher). (1) `%3 = load @cell; %4 = cq_theta(%3, t1); store %4, @cell`: the rotation of a cell, rule 5's in-place
; form with the Ry as its one step (rule 2); the store closes the form, emitted at the store's position.
; (2) `%5 = load @g; %6 = add %5, 1; store %6, @g`: the in-place form with a rule-6 bijection as its step (rule 6, "a
; memory cell"), at the classical address &g. It is a MEMORY VERSION CHANGE. (3) `%7 = cq_theta(%4, t2); store %7, @cell`:
; the operand %4 is the value -O1 forwarded from store (1) to the same SSA pointer, so the interval of this form runs
; from that store (rule 5, Readers), and the change (2) lies inside it. %4 is the result of form (1) and has no rail of
; its own: it lives in the cell. The second cq_theta is the first step of the next form on the same SSA pointer, not
; "another reader" that would end form (1) with a load copy.
; READERS. Nothing is known at compile time about the two addresses: not for @cell and @g (rule 20; §0 "no pointer is
; resolved") and not for the restrict arguments (rule 21: noalias is never consulted). So whether (2) touches the cells
; of p is asked at RUN TIME: the change is an in-place form at the classical address q (S_q = 4 cells), p is classical
; (S_p = 4), and the classical i1 d tests q - p >= 4 && p - q >= 4 (mod 2^64, unsigned): exact for the circular cell
; ranges of §1.3, where p + S_p may wrap.
;   DISJOINT (d = 1): the cell still holds %4 at (3), so no copy is taken and the form stands: swap-out, Ry(t2),
;   swap-in, free. The reader cq_measure(%7) is a later reader of y': a plain load taken after the swap-in, measured.
;   OVERLAP (d = 0): before the change the lowered code takes a plain load of p as %4's copy. The second cq_theta
;   rotates that copy (rule 2: frozen from there on, never un-copied), `store %7, p` is an ordinary kept store of it,
;   and cq_measure(%7) measures the copy rail itself (no second load: that would be a second kept copy).
; d is computed ONCE, immediately before the change, and branched on TWICE; nothing is duplicated: `br d` around the
; copy load, then the change (2) emitted once, then `br d` at the second store's position choosing the form or the
; steps on the copy with the kept store. The copy's handle reaches the second branch through a classical phi whose
; d = 1 incoming is poison (never read on that path); the measured rail is a classical phi of two handles.
; Two distinct globals never overlap, so the first function's OVERLAP blocks are emitted and never run; the _ptr
; function's third driver call runs them.

define i32 @theta_twice_store_between(double noundef %0, double noundef %1) {

  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %3 = load i32, ptr @cell: in-place form (1), the swap rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64), i32 %4)    ; IR: %3 = load i32, ptr @cell: swap-out: the rail holds the cell, the cell |0>

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the swap rail (|0>)
  %5 = sub i64 ptrtoint (ptr @g to i64), ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64)    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: q - p mod 2^64, p = the address of @cell, q = that of @g

  %7 = sub i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64), ptrtoint (ptr @g to i64)    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q mod 2^64
  %8 = icmp uge i64 %7, 4    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: p - q >= S_q, S_q = 4 cells
  %9 = and i1 %6, %8    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: d: the cells at p and at q are disjoint (classical, run time), computed immediately before the change
  br i1 %9, label %12, label %10    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: d = 1 DISJOINT: no copy is taken; d = 0 OVERLAP: the copy below

10:
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64))    ; IR: the forwarded %4 as a rail: a plain load of @cell taken before the memory version change (rule 5, Readers)  [OVERLAP path only]
  br label %12    ; IR: (no instruction)

  %13 = phi i32 [ poison, %2 ], [ %11, %10 ]    ; IR: (no instruction) the copy's handle on the OVERLAP path (classical phi; poison, never read, on the DISJOINT path)
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %5 = load i32, ptr @g: in-place form (2), the swap rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @g to i64), i32 %14)    ; IR: %5 = load i32, ptr @g: swap-out: the rail holds the cell at q, that cell |0>  (the memory version change inside the interval, emitted once)
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %14, i32 1)    ; IR: %6 = add nsw i32 %5, 1
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: t = g' - 1 recomputes the old value
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %16, i32 %14)    ; IR: rule 6: the old rail ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %15, i32 1)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the old-value rail (|0> after the copy)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @g to i64), i32 %15)    ; IR: store i32 %6, ptr @g: swap-in: the cell at q holds the sum, the rail that cell's |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the rail (|0>): nothing remains of the increment
  br i1 %9, label %17, label %20    ; IR: (no instruction) Readers: the same d, at the second store's position: DISJOINT: form (3) stands; OVERLAP: the steps act on the copy

17:
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%4, %1): in-place form (3) on the forwarded %4, the swap rail (|0>)  [DISJOINT path]
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64), i32 %18)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%4, %1): swap-out: the rail holds %4 (the cell was not touched by the change), the cell |0>
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %18, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%4, %1)  [Ry on the cell's content]
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64), i32 %18)    ; IR: store i32 %7, ptr @cell: swap-in: the cell holds %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %18)    ; IR: release the swap rail (|0>)
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64))    ; IR: the reader of %7: a plain load of @cell taken after the swap-in (rule 5, Readers)
  br label %21    ; IR: (no instruction)

20:
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %13, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%4, %1)  [Ry on the load copy: a frozen register from here on, rule 2]  [OVERLAP path]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @cell to i64), i32 %13)    ; IR: store i32 %7, ptr @cell  (a kept store: no _unc, its tape slot and its value rail stay, rule 5 sentence 3)
  br label %21    ; IR: (no instruction)

  %22 = phi i32 [ %19, %17 ], [ %13, %20 ]    ; IR: (no instruction) the rail of %7 for its reader: the load after the swap-in or the copy itself (classical phi of handles)
  %23 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %22)    ; IR: %8 = cq_measure_si32(%7)  (the measured rail stays allocated, rule 2)

  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %6, i32 %22)    ; IR: %9 = cq_theta_si32(%6, %3): swap-out: the rail holds %6 (the cell was not touched by the change), the cell |0>

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2 (a cq_theta of a loaded value that is not stored straight back), 3, 5 (Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 10 (frozen), 20; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem).
; Checked: the measured value = src (the second load copy %4, measured -> %5); the cell `dst` = the rotated copy of src
;          and the cell `src` = 3, unchanged (both read from the bus at exit).
; Clean: nothing. No rail of this function is uncomputed or freed: it mints two load copies and both stay.
; Kept: the first load copy of src (%3): rotated, so a FROZEN register (rules 2, 10: never un-copied), and the value rail
;       of the kept store dst = v (rule 5 sentence 3); that store's tape slot (in the backend, holding the displaced
;       `dst`); the second load copy of src (%4, measured: rule 2's measured rail).
; Rotations: (Ry, the load copy of src, th, 1).
; Expected for the driver theta_of_load_copy(.5) (analytic, not replayed): the return value is 3 with probability 1. The
;   cell src is never written, so it stays HOST and holds 3; the second load copies it and the measurement reads 3
;   whatever the rotation did. The cell dst: Ry(th) acts on every qubit of the i32 copy, so each of its 32 bits flips
;   independently with probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087: dst = 3 with probability (1 - s)^32 = 0.132498, each
;   single-bit neighbour of 3 with probability s (1 - s)^31 = 0.008639, P(v) = s^d (1 - s)^(32 - d) at Hamming distance d.
; THE ROTATION ACTS ON THE LOAD COPY (rule 2, the fallback). cq_theta(&v, th) on `int v = src` is, in the -O1 code,
; `load @src; cq_theta_si32; store @dst`: the result is stored through ANOTHER pointer, so this is not rule 5's in-place
; form (no qram_swap: the gate must not reach the cell src) and the Ry acts on the fresh rail the load made, as the C
; program says (v is a copy of src). From the rotation on, that rail is a frozen register: it is never un-copied
; (cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc would need the rail to still hold the cell's value) and never freed. `dst = v` is an ordinary
; kept store of it at the classical address of dst: no _unc exists, its tape slot and its value rail stay for the shot.
; The cell dst is QUANTUM from here on (its content is not classical-valued); the cell src is untouched and stays HOST.
; THE SECOND LOAD. `cq_measure(src)` loads src again: in the -O1 code the opaque call cq_theta_si32 lies between the two
; loads and may write @src for all clang knows, so the first load is not forwarded (the store to @dst alone would not
; prevent it: clang knows the two globals are distinct). The lowering asks nothing of the kind: the IR has a second load,
; so it is a second bus load at the same classical address, a fresh copy of the cell, measured. It reads the cell, not
; the rotated copy. A measured load copy is never un-copied, although no memory version change follows it here: it is
; rule 2's measured rail and stays allocated (no _unc, no free).
; ONE BUS, CLASSICAL ADDRESSES (rule 20). src and dst are globals at their host addresses: nothing is allocated, seeded
; or registered for them; the address operand of the _hl forms is the pointer's run-time i64 (ptrtoint).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 22, 21, 20, 14, 9, 5, 2, 4, 7.
; Checked: the return value r1 + r2, r1 = q[1] and r2 = q[2] after the realloc (the load copies at the classical
; addresses q + 4 and q + 8, each measured; the sum is classical, rule 2). k & 1 == 1 (p = a): the header at a - 8
; reads 8, bytes 0..7 of a are copied, so r1 = a[1] = x and r2 = 0 (bytes 8..11 of q are not written: zeroed
; __cq_alloc memory). k & 1 == 0 (p = b): the header at b - 8 reads 16, bytes 0..15 of b are copied, so r1 = b[1] = 5
; and r2 = b[2] = 7. r1 witnesses the address rail (which block is read), r2 the length predicate p_j = (j < min(s, 24))
; for j = 8..11: a copy of all 24 bytes, or of a fixed 16, would read on the p = a branch the 4 bytes at a + 8, which
; here are the low half of b's size header (b = a + 16 in the bump arena), and return x + 16.
; Clean: k & 1, the flag (k & 1) == 0 and the address rail p = select(flag, b, a) (uncomputed after p's last reader,
; the _unc of p - 8); the address rail p - 8 (after the un-copy of s, which reads it); the header load copy s and
; min(s, 24) (s is un-copied before the first copy store: its only consumer umin and that consumer's _unc precede the
; next memory version change, rule 5 sentence 1); for each of the 24 copy trips the source address rail p + j
; (uncomputed right after its load, before the next trip).
; Kept: k and x (rotated; x is also the value rail of the kept store a[1] = x); the tape slot of that store; the seeds
; 5 and 7 and the tape slots of b[1] = 5 and b[2] = 7 (rule 7); for each of the 24 copy trips the predicate
; p_j = (min(s, 24) > j), the controlled load copy of byte j (the value rail of its kept store) and that store's tape
; slot (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 22); the two load copies r1 and r2 (measured: rule 2).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Driver realloc_pointer_rail(1, .5, 9, .25): Ry acts on every qubit of a register, so each bit of k flips with
; probability p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 and each bit of x with q = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544, independently; everything
; after the two rotations is a basis permutation. k & 1 == 1 (1 - p = 0.938791): the address rail holds a, s = 8,
; p_0..p_7 are 1 and p_8..p_23 are 0, 8 bytes are copied, r1 = x, r2 = 0 and the function returns x: 9 with
; (1 - p)(1 - q)^32 = 0.568662, each single-bit neighbour of 9 with (1 - p) q (1 - q)^31 = 0.008979. k & 1 == 0
; (p = 0.061209): the address rail holds b, s = 16, p_0..p_15 are 1, 16 bytes are copied, r1 = 5, r2 = 7 and the
; function returns 12 whatever x is (0.061350 with x = 12 on the other branch, two bit flips from 9). The other values
; of x share 0.369988.
; REALLOC OF A POINTER RAIL (rule 16). Both mallocs are __cq_alloc(size, 16) (classical host code; alignment 16: the
; call names none), each with its size as an i64 in the 8 bytes before the block. The pointer select on the quantum
; flag is select_i64_ll (rule 21: both incomings classical, entering as their run-time i64 addresses), so p is ONE
; 64-bit address rail and nothing about a or b belongs to it. realloc(p, 24) is, in this order, q = __cq_alloc(24, 16),
; CLASSICAL (the new block does not depend on p); s = the i64 bus load at the address rail p - 8 (add_i64_hl(p, -8),
; rule 20's address arithmetic; the plain load form, an address rail); the length rail umin_i64_hl(s, 24); and a
; rule-22 copy of min(s, 24) bytes from p to q. The length is a rail, so the copy is the quantum-length form, its trip
; bound the new block's size 24 (not K2; no overflow predicate: min(s, 24) <= 24). Byte j is loaded under
; p_j = icmp_ugt_i64_hl(min(s, 24), j) by qram_load_i8_controlled at the address rail add_i64_hl(p, j) and stored
; under the same p_j by qram_store_i8_hl_controlled at the classical address q + j. The copy loads all its bytes, then
; stores all of them. A trip C would not run touches no cell: on the k & 1 == 1 branch the loads at a + 8 .. a + 23,
; beyond the 8-byte block, are under p_j = 0. Nothing is done for p: both old blocks stay.
; No compile-time pointer knowledge is used: the old size is read from the bus on each branch of the address rail,
; and which block is copied is decided by the QRAM query alone.
; The header cells are HOST (written by __cq_alloc, read through the overlay); a[1] is QUANTUM after the store of x.
; SPEC GAP (rule 22 against rule 14, as in 201): rule 22 calls the two copy loops rule-14 K-loops, and rule 14 says a
; predicate that controls a kept store and every trip rail rule 5 keeps is NOT pushed; then the store loop cannot
; name p_j or the byte rail. Chosen, as the one exception to that sentence: the load loop computes ONE p_j per byte
; and pushes, per trip, p_j and then the byte rail on cqrt_push (a handle is never stored in program memory, §1.1);
; the store loop pops them (byte rail first, then p_j), so it stores bytes 23 down to 0 under the same p_j (a copy has
; no direction). There is no reverse loop: both rails are kept. With one p_j per byte, min(s, 24), s, p - 8 and p are
; dead before the first store and are cleaned between the two loops.
; SPEC GAP (rule 22): byte 0 of an address rail r. The rule spells every byte address add_i64_hl(r, j); chosen: j = 0
; too (add_i64_hl(p, 0), a fresh rail uncomputed and freed right after its access like the others), so the trip body
; is uniform and p itself is never the address operand of an access.
; SPEC GAP (rule 16, realloc): neither the template of p - 8 nor the order of the allocation and the header load is
; stated. Chosen: add_i64_hl(p, -8) (rule 20 forms every address with add_i64_hl), and the allocation FIRST: it is a
; memory version change (rule 5), so a header load made before it would be overtaken and s KEPT; made after it, s is
; un-copied before the copy's first store.

name: 209_host_call_behind_printf
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 19, 7, 4, 2; BACKEND_ABI §1.11 (the event sequence).
; Checked: host_call_behind_printf: x (%5, measured -> %7).
; Clean: mark: the |1> predicate seed of its effect entry (%3: never written, freed directly, rule 7).
; Kept: host_call_behind_printf: x (%5: rotated, measured), its tape (%4) and the write-only tape rail of the printf
; field (%6: a copy of x, entangled with it, never freed). mark: its tape (%2). The putchar entry has no result rail
; (the program does not read the result: the bare form).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: host_call_behind_printf(3, .5, 10): Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of the i32 rail x = 3, so each of its 32
; bits flips with probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 and the measured value v is 3 with probability
; (1 - s)^32 = 0.132498, 3 ^ (1 << b) with probability (1 - s)^31 s = 0.008639 for each bit b, and in general
; 3 ^ e with probability s^|e| (1 - s)^(32 - |e|). The tape rail is a copy of x, so the output of the shot is the
; decimal of that same v followed by the byte 10: "<v>\n", in this order on every shot.
; THE ORDINARY-HOST-CALL CONDITION (rule 16). printf("%d", x) has a rail field: a format entry (47), an OUTPUT call
; with a quantum field, which the backend defers to the end of the shot (BACKEND_ABI §1.11). mark(c) is called by
; name after that tape event in its only caller, so mark is a function CALLED AFTER AN EVENT, and its putchar(c),
; although every argument is classical and no quantum predicate is in scope, is NOT an ordinary host call: made as it
; stands it would write its byte before the deferred printf. It is an EFFECT ENTRY: tape_alloc, the argument as a
; _lit field, then cqrt_tape_effect_controlled under a cqrt_alloc_i1(true) seed with the host name "putchar" (the
; bare form: the result is unused). The entry is behind an unresolved event, so the backend defers it too and
; performs both at the end of the shot in sequence order: the printf, then the putchar. The lowered program asks
; nothing; it emits the same one call whatever the backend will do. The property is static (the least fixpoint over
; calls by name), so mark's body is the effect entry for every call of it; mark is internal and has one caller.
; A second clause of rule 16 gives the same answer here: host_call_behind_printf is externally visible in a module
; that contains an event, so it is itself called after an event and mark, its callee, is too (the least fixpoint),
; whatever the position of mark(c) relative to the printf. Both clauses yield this text.
; THE SEED IS FREED WHILE THE ENTRY IS DEFERRED. The backend captures an entry's predicate when the entry is opened
; (as 47 relies on for its uncomputed x > k flag), so the |1> seed is a rule-7 seed: freed directly after the effect
; call, although the putchar is performed only at the end of the shot.
; mark itself is reached with a classical argument: the call is to its OWN symbol (§1.4, the all-zero mask), fastcc
; and internal as -O1 left it; nothing is inlined (rule 19). Neither function touches the bus (no __cq_mem).
source_filename = "host_call_behind_printf.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [3 x i8] c"%d\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str
@.cq.effect.putchar = private unnamed_addr constant [8 x i8] c"putchar\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for putchar (a host string): @.cq.effect.<name>, one per host callee, after the module's own globals

define i32 @host_call_behind_printf(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  call void @cqrt_tape_fmt(i32 %4, ptr @.str)    ; IR: %5 = printf(@.str, %4): the format entry (no predicate in scope; the count %5 is unused)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i32(i32 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: %5 = printf(..., %4): field 0, the rail x copied onto a fresh tape rail (kept): the entry is deferred by the backend
  call fastcc void @mark(i32 %2)    ; IR: call fastcc void @mark(i32 %2): classical argument, the own symbol; called after the tape event above
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_si32(%4)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %6
}

define internal fastcc void @mark(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape, allocated once at entry as in 47 (mark records an entry: it is called after an event, so its putchar is not an ordinary host call)
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: %2 = putchar(%0): no predicate in scope, the |1> seed
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i32_lit(i32 %2, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = putchar(%0): argument 0, classical: a _lit field, <W> the width token of the argument's IR type at the call (i32)
  call void @cqrt_tape_effect_controlled(i32 %3, i32 %2, ptr @.cq.effect.putchar, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = putchar(%0): the effect entry, complete after its fields; bare form, the result is unused
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the seed (|1>, never written: freed directly, rule 7); the backend captured the predicate at the effect call (BACKEND_ABI §1.11), so the deferred entry does not read this rail again
  ret void    ; IR: ret void
}

name: 20_nested_value_arms
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 9, 8, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: r (measured, %13 -> %14).
; Clean: the outer flag %8 = (x > k1), the arm value %9 = x + c, the inner flag %10 = (r < k2), the all-classical select
; %11 = (%10 ? s : 1) and the product %12, all uncomputed LIFO and freed before the measurement.
; Kept: x (%7, the rotated register) and the result rail %13 (measured); nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Nested value arms (rule 9): both arms are pure, so their code is hoisted and computed unguarded into fresh rails. -O1
; folds the inner `if (r < k2) r = r * s` into `r * (r < k2 ? s : 1)`: that all-classical select on the inner flag is one
; select_i32_ll template (both data operands literals), the product is a two-handle mul, and the outer merge
; `x > k1 ? product : x` is one select_i32 template into the fresh result rail %13. No gate fires under control; every
; intermediate is uncomputed by its template's _unc in reverse order and freed.
source_filename = "nested_value_arms.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @nested_value_arms(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, i32 noundef %4, i32 noundef %5) {
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %7 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: %8 = icmp sgt i32 %7, %2
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 %4)    ; IR: %9 = add nsw i32 %7, %4
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %3)    ; IR: %10 = icmp slt i32 %9, %3
  %11 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %10, i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: %11 = select i1 %10, i32 %5, i32 1  (both arms classical)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %11, i32 %9)    ; IR: %12 = mul nsw i32 %11, %9
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %8, i32 %12, i32 %7)    ; IR: %13 = select i1 %8, i32 %12, i32 %7  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %12, i32 %11, i32 %9)    ; IR: uncompute %12
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %11, i32 %10, i32 %5, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %7, i32 %4)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)

name: 210_input_behind_output
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 20, 5, 7, 4, 3, 2; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc); BACKEND_ABI §1.11 (the INPUT rows).
; Checked: buf[0] (the load copy %18, measured -> %19, returned sign-extended), read from the bus at buf's address.
; Clean: the length rail n & 7 (%14, uncomputed after the entry that copied it and freed) and the |1> predicate seed of
; the fgets entry (%15: never written, freed directly, rule 7).
; Kept: n (%10) and x (%11), the rotated registers (x is only printed, never measured by the program); the tape (%7)
; and its two write-only tape rails, the printf field (%13, a copy of x) and the fgets length field (%16, a copy of
; n & 7); the store `buf = {0}`: its tape slot (in the backend) and its value rail, the seed %12 (rules 5, 7); the
; load copy of buf[0] (%18, measured: rule 2's measured rail). The fgets entry has no result rail (the program does
; not read fgets' result: the bare form).
; Rotations: (Ry, n, tn, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: input_behind_output(3, .5, 4, .25, stdin). Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of the i32 rail n = 3, so each bit
; flips independently with probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087; the length is the low three bits of n (011 at the
; start). C's fgets(buf, len, f) stores at most len - 1 bytes of the next input line and a NUL, so with c the first
; byte of that line buf[0] = c iff len >= 2, i.e. unless bits 2 and 1 of n are both 0: the measured value is c with
; probability 1 - (1 - s) s = 0.942538 and 0 with probability 0.057462 (0 on every shot when the stream is at end of
; file: buf was zeroed). For c != 0 the measurement leaves n on the matching side of `(n & 6) != 0`. The stream loses
; the whole next line (up to K2 - 1 bytes) on every branch, not the at most 2 bytes C reads at n = 3. The output of
; the shot is the decimal of x and a newline, x from 4 with s' = sin^2(.125) = 0.0155438 per bit: "4\n" with
; probability (1 - s')^32 = 0.605738; it is printed at the end of the shot, after the input was read.
; INPUT IS NEVER HELD BEHIND A DEFERRED OUTPUT (rule 16, BACKEND_ABI §1.11). printf("%d\n", x) has a rail field: a
; format entry (47), an OUTPUT call with a quantum field, which the backend defers to the end of the shot. fgets is a
; stream call with a pointer argument and a rail argument: an EFFECT ENTRY, and it is the same ONE call it would be
; anywhere else: its three arguments as fields in order (the buffer's address as an i64 literal, the length rail as a
; tape_write_i32 field, the stream's address as an i64 literal), then cqrt_tape_effect_controlled under a
; cqrt_alloc_i1(true) seed with the host name "fgets". The lowered program does not say that the call is an input
; call, does not test what precedes it and names no K2: the backend knows by `name` that fgets is an INPUT call, which
; field is the buffer and which the length, and performs it AT THE CALL although the printf entry before it is
; unresolved: ONE host call at its own bound K2 into a temporary classical buffer, then for each value v the length
; rail can take the bytes fgets with length v would have stored from that input (the first min(v - 1, len) bytes and
; a NUL for v >= 1, nothing for v = 0), bus-stored under n & 7 = v (stores the backend makes: the cells of buf become
; QUANTUM, entangled with n). The input consumed is that of the K2 call on every branch (a stated deviation from the
; C program). Only the order of outputs is kept.
; The tape is the function's: one tape_alloc at function entry, both entries on it in call order; an entry's fields
; are those written since the previous entry. The |1> seed is read by the backend at the effect call like `name`
; (never again), so it is rule 7's seed and is freed directly after the call.
; buf. The alloca has a call among its users, so it is bus-resident (rule 20 b): __cq_alloc(8, 8) at the alloca's
; program point, no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are dropped. `char buf[8] = {0}` is -O1's one `store i64 0`:
; one kept bus store of the seed alloc_i64(0) at the block's address (rule 5 sentence 3, rule 7). The effect entry is
; a memory version change; `buf[0]` after it is a plain bus load, a rail whatever the cell holds (rule 3), measured.
source_filename = "input_behind_output.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [4 x i8] c"%d\0A\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str

name: 211_fnptr_rail_measuring
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21; §1.3 (clone table), §1.4 (table clones).
; Checked: r = ops[k & 1](x) (the copied-out result of the merge, measured): x + 1 where k & 1 = 0 (inc), x where
; k & 1 = 1 (peek); the cells of ops are unchanged.
; Clean: the address chain of &ops[k & 1] (the and, its zext, the scaled index, the address rail), uncomputed right
; after the un-copy of fp (after the reverse loop) and freed; per candidate: the flag f_i (fp == a_i), the complement rail p_{i+1} and the select rail
; out_{i+1}, popped and uncomputed by the reverse loop and freed; the outer select rail (after the copy-out); the
; seeds p_0 (|1>) and out_0 (|0>), never written and freed directly (rule 7); inc's result rail x + 1, zeroed and
; freed by its twin __cq_q_inc_1_t_ctl_unc.
; Kept: k and x (the rotated registers); fp, the load copy of ops[k & 1] (rule 5 sentence 1: un-copied after its last
; reader, the reverse loop's last flag _unc, but left allocated: the dispatch, a memory version change, lies between); per candidate the copy c_i of its
; result (rule 19: the result is kept across the next memory version change as a copy); peek's measured rail t (the
; controlled copy of x, rule 19; measured, rule 2); the result rail r_e of the complement's effect entry, its two
; tape field rails and the tape (rule 16); the copied-out result R (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, k, tk, 1); (Ry, x, tx, 1).
; Expected: fnptr_rail_measuring(1, .5, 4, .25). Each Ry acts on all 32 qubits of its register: a bit of k flips with
; p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209, a bit of x with s = sin^2(.125) = 0.015544. k & 1 = 1 (peek) with 0.938791 and 0 (inc)
; with 0.061209; x = 4 ^ e, each e with s^|e| (1 - s)^(32 - |e|) (x = 4: 0.605738; one given bit flipped: 0.009564).
; r = x on the peek branch and x + 1 on the inc branch: P(r = 4) = 0.568662 (peek, x = 4; plus inc, x = 3: 1.5e-7),
; P(r = 5) = 0.046055 (inc, x = 4: 0.037076; peek, x = 5: 0.008979), P(r = 6) = 0.009564, P(r = 0) = 0.008979, and
; 0.385283 in total over the values other than 4 and 5. The measurement inside peek's clone reads t = x on the peek
; branch and 0 on the inc branch (P(t = 0) = 0.070187): it tells the branches apart, where the C program measures x
; only when peek is called, and it leaves r's distribution as the C program's. Both cells of ops hold registered
; functions of type i32 (i32), so one flag is 1 on every branch, the complement predicate is 0 and the effect entry is
; never performed (deferred by the backend, its r_e is |0>).
; A FUNCTION POINTER LOADED AT AN ADDRESS RAIL (rules 19, 20, 21). ops is a constant global at its host address: HOST
; cells seen through the overlay, nothing seeded and no derived table. The gep with the tainted index is 64-bit
; template arithmetic (the zext as -O1 wrote it, mul by the element size 8, add of the classical base) and the load is
; ONE qram_load_i64 at the address rail: fp is a 64-bit rail holding the callee's host address.
; THE DISPATCH. Which functions fp can denote is never analysed: the candidates are the registered functions of the
; call's function type, read from the clone table at run time. The module constructor registers one row for each
; address-taken function (inc, peek): its host address, the type string "i32 (i32)", its table clone and that clone's
; _ctl, _unc and _ctl_unc. The dispatch is a classical loop (rule 14: i < __cq_clone_count(sig), registration order).
; Trip i takes a_i = __cq_clone_at(sig, i), the flag f_i = icmp_eq_i64_hl(fp, a_i), and calls the _t_ctl clone of a_i
; (kind 1) under f_i with the table ABI: predicate first, every formal a handle (x), then K = 4, the K of this
; function. The caller has no record of a callee: every call is a memory version change, so the result is copied into
; a fresh rail c_i that is KEPT, and the twin (kind 3, same flag) is called right after, before the next memory
; version change (the next candidate's call, or the effect entry). The trip then extends the complement p_{i+1} =
; p_i & NOT f_i (an X bracket on f_i around and_i1 into a fresh rail, rule 8; p_0 is a |1> seed, no predicate being in
; scope) and the merge out_{i+1} = select_i32(f_i, c_i, out_i) (rule 9; out_0 is a |0> seed), and pushes p_i, out_i,
; c_i and f_i. After the loop p_n says "fp is no registered function": fp is host code there, and p_n itself is the
; predicate of the effect entry with a null name, fp its first field and x its second, result rail r_e. The call's
; value is select_i32(p_n, r_e, out_n): the complement's r_e where no candidate matched, else the candidates' merge.
; It is copied out (rule 14), the outer select is uncomputed, the reverse loop pops the trips and uncomputes each
; select, each p_{i+1} and each flag (a_i again from the table), the seeds are freed and the copy is measured.
; THE TABLE CLONES (§1.4). Each takes handles and K, returns one handle and pushes nothing (neither function mints a
; register). inc is one template: its clones return the template's rail, its twins are that template's _unc and the
; free (the caller frees no result of a table clone). A _ctl clone guards gates, and inc has only a template, so
; __cq_q_inc_1_t_ctl computes unguarded (rule 9) and the caller's select does the rest. peek measures, so it has no
; rule-18 twin: both its twins do nothing and its result stays allocated. In __cq_q_peek_1_t a kept copy of the
; argument rail is measured (t = alloc_i32(0); copy_i32(v, t); measure_i32(t), §1.4; the caller's rail is never a
; measured rail) and the outcome returned as a seed rail. In __cq_q_peek_1_t_ctl the measurement is of a CONTROLLED COPY
; (rule 19): t = alloc_i32(0); copy_i32_controlled(pred, v, t); measure_i32(t). x is not collapsed where the flag is 0,
; and t, which holds the tainted outcome, is the result. Every _t_ctl clone and _t_ctl_unc twin reads its function's
; activation counter d on entry, adds 1 and subtracts 1 at its return (§1.4); at d >= K the clone returns a |0> rail
; and keeps a copy_i1 of its predicate as the overflow rail, and the twin frees that |0> rail (rule 14). Nothing
; re-enters here, so d is 0 at every call and no activation is cut.
; THE OWN SYMBOLS. inc and peek stay, at the host addresses the cells of ops hold (the table's keys). inc has no bus
; access, no cq_* call and no call: it is its own lowering. peek's cq_measure of a classical value is that value.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a clone-table row per externally visible function too. fnptr_rail_measuring gets
; none here (as in 195-203): its type is not the call's, so the dispatch does not see the difference.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 does not say how the complement predicate and the select chain are built for a candidate count
; known only at run time. Rule 9's chain with the complement innermost needs r_e, hence every flag, before the first
; select; over the one push/pop stack (§1.1) that takes four loops and every flag twice. Chosen instead, as in 212:
; ONE loop and its reverse. The loop carries the complement p (p_0 = the predicate in scope, here an alloc_i1(true)
; seed; p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i: not_i1(f_i), and_i1(p_i, f_i, fresh), not_i1(f_i)) and the merge out (out_0 =
; alloc_i32(0)). The effect entry is made under p_n and one outer select on p_n takes r_e, else out_n: the complement
; is an arm of the outermost select, not the innermost arm of one chain. The flags are pairwise exclusive (distinct
; addresses), so the value is the same on every branch. With a predicate P in scope a candidate's control would be
; and_i1(P, f_i, fresh), uncomputed after the twin (212).
; SPEC GAP: neither rule 16 nor BACKEND_ABI §1.11 says that an effect entry captures its predicate. p_n is uncomputed
; and freed after the entry like any flag (138, 212; rule 8 keeps only a flag that controls a kept store), so the
; backend must capture it at the call.
; SPEC GAP: no name is fixed for the module constructor, the type-string global or the activation counters; the
; counters are plain module-internal i32 globals, read and written by plain instructions.
; SPEC GAP: rule 18's clone copies each result into a fresh rail; a measured rail cannot be uncomputed, so
; __cq_q_peek_1_t_ctl returns the measured rail t itself. Whether t is a "register it minted" to push (§1.4) is not
; said; it is not pushed (its twin does nothing).
; SPEC GAP: rule 2 does not spell cq_measure of a value that never was a rail (peek's own symbol): the value itself.
; SPEC GAP: §1.4 lets every _ctl_unc twin count an activation; a twin with nothing to do (peek's) does so too.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16 (signal table, effect entry), 19 (address rail dispatch, table clones), 2, 5, 6, 7, 8, 14, 20;
; §1.3 (bundle), §1.4 (table clone, activation counter).
; Checked: signal_table: x (%6, measured -> %39) and hit (the load copy %40, measured -> %41); the cell __cq_sig[30]
; at exit = the address of on_usr1 (HOST); the cell hit at exit = (x > k ? 30 : 0), given hit = 0 at entry.
; Expected: signal_table(0, .5, 1): Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of the i32 rail x = 0, so each bit is 1 with
; probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209. x > 1 (signed) iff bit 31 is 0 and one of bits 1..30 is 1:
; P(x > 1) = (1 - s)(1 - (1 - s)^30) = 0.797654. On that branch the cell __cq_sig[30] holds the address of on_usr1,
; the one registered function of type void (i32), so its flag is 1, on_usr1 runs once and hit = 30; the complement
; predicate is 0 on every branch and the effect entry raise is never performed. The two measurements are perfectly
; correlated: (x, hit) = (v, 30) for v > 1 and (v, 0) for v <= 1; P(hit = 30) = 0.797654, P(hit = 0) = 0.202346
; (x = 0: 0.132498; x = 1: 0.008639; x < 0: 0.061209). The function returns v + 30 (v > 1) or v: 0 with p = 0.132498,
; 2^b + 30 with p = (1 - s)^31 s = 0.008639 for each bit b in 1..30.
; Clean: signal_table: the dead result of signal (%8: a load copy with no consumer, un-copied before the store);
; the arm flag x > k (%10); per candidate of the dispatch: its flag (%20), the conjunction with the arm flag (%21),
; the |30> argument seed (%22) and the complement predicate of the chain (%25), the chain popped and uncomputed by
; the reverse loop; un-copied under the arm flag but left allocated (rule 5 sentence 1: the table clone call, a
; memory version change, overtakes it): the load copy of the cell __cq_sig[30] (%11, the address rail of the
; dispatch), un-copied after the reverse loop, its last reader the last flag's _unc. __cq_q_on_usr1_1_t_ctl: the swapped-out old hit (%9), the sum (%10), the inverse of the composite
; update (%12, %13) and the rail the cell's |0> went to (%11). on_usr1 and __cq_q_on_usr1_1_t: the same without the
; composite.
; Kept: signal_table: x (rotated, measured); the load copy of hit (measured); by rule 5 sentence 3 the tape slot and the value seed (%9, the i64 address of on_usr1)
; of the store into __cq_sig[30]; the function's tape (%5). The clones keep nothing: hit += s is the in-place form.
; At the cutoff (not reached here) __cq_q_on_usr1_1_t_ctl keeps one overflow predicate rail (rule 14).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; SIGNAL (rule 16, signal table). signal(SIGUSR1, on_usr1) has classical arguments and no predicate in scope: the host
; call is made as it stands, then the cell &__cq_sig[30] is loaded (the call's result: the previously registered
; address) and the handler's address is stored there, a kept store of an i64 seed at a classical address. Everything
; is classical-valued, so the store writes the host array and the cell stays HOST (§1.3).
; RAISE (rules 16, 19). raise(SIGUSR1) sits in the arm of x > k: the cell is loaded by the _hl_controlled form under
; the arm flag (rule 5: no access is hoisted; the rail is |0> where the flag is 0) and the call goes through that
; address rail. No handler is tracked: the candidates are the functions of type void (i32) in the clone table, read
; at run time (__cq_clone_count / __cq_clone_at; a classical loop). Candidate i has the flag f_i = (rail == a_i);
; its _ctl table clone (__cq_clone_resolve(a_i, 1)) is called under f & f_i with the signal number as a seed rail and
; K, and its _ctl twin (kind 3) once, right after it (no result to keep). The complement branch is the effect entry
; "raise" with the signal number as its _lit field, under p_n, where p_0 = f and p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i.
; ON_USR1 (rules 5, 6, 19, §1.4). Its address is taken, so it has the four table clones and one row of the clone
; table, registered by a module constructor. hit += s is load, add, store on one pointer with no memory version
; change between: the in-place form on the cell (swap-out, add, rule-6 clean of the old rail, swap-in). In the _ctl
; clone the swaps are _hl_controlled and the update is the composite c ? hit + s : hit. on_usr1 writes memory, so
; rule 18 gives it no twin: the table twins do nothing (nothing was pushed). The _ctl clone and its twin count the
; live _ctl activations in a module-internal counter and the clone is cut at K (§1.4, rule 14).
; SPEC GAP: rule 16's ordinary-host-call test makes every externally visible function "called after an event" when
; the module contains one (here the effect entry raise), which would turn this signal call into an effect entry; the
; signal-table bullet asks only for classical arguments and no predicate in scope. The bullet wins (the signal table
; is a class below "effect entry"): the host call is made as it stands whatever precedes it, and the
; ordinary-host-call test is not asked for signal.
; SPEC GAP: the result of signal is unused. Rule 16 says signal IS the load and the store; the load is emitted and
; un-copied at once (rule 5 sentence 1, no consumer). Omitting a dead load is semantically equal (§6).
; SPEC GAP: rule 16 does not say what raise dispatches. Here: a call of function type void (i32) (C's handler type)
; with the signal number as its one actual (a seed, table clone ABI), and the entry raise has the signal number as
; its one field. The result of raise is unused here, so the bare effect form is used (rule 16: the _<W> form only
; when the program reads the result; BACKEND_ABI §1.11's "a callee without a result" is the narrower wording). A
; result the program reads would be the _i32 entry's rail under the complement and 0 under every candidate flag.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no module-internal name. As in 205 and 211: the activation counter is the internal global
; i32 @__cq_act_<fn>, the cut test icmp ult d, K, the constructor internal void @__cq_register() at priority 65535,
; the sig string private @.cq.sig (the LLVM 19 type print of the function type); effect names are @.cq.effect.<name>
; (102, 209). §6 compares no name.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 gives the complement of the candidate flags no spelling. Used: p_0 = the predicate in scope,
; p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i (not_i1(f_i), and_i1(p_i, f_i, fresh), not_i1(f_i)) in the candidate loop, p_n the entry's
; predicate; p_i and f_i are pushed and the reverse loop uncomputes them (rule 14's classical loop). Each
; candidate's conjunction is and_i1 of the arm flag and f_i. 211 spells it the same way (not_i1 / and_i1 /
; not_i1 per candidate).
; SPEC GAP: CR does not say whether an effect entry's predicate rail is kept; it is uncomputed after the entry (102,
; and rule 8: only a flag that controls a kept store is kept).
; SPEC GAP (corpus convention, §5): §1.3 / rule 19 ask for a clone-table row per externally visible function too
; (signal_table: its _t, _t_ctl and twins with the angle as an f64 rail). The example never takes that address, so
; the row, its table clones and twins are omitted as in 197, 200, 204 and 211; the compiler emits them, and the

; SPEC GAP: §1.4 makes the _ctl twin read and restore the activation counter even where the twin does nothing else

; argument: the table twins take K last, _unc(s, K) and _ctl_unc(pred, s, K).

; Checked: r = a[j & 1] (the load copy at the classical run-time address p + 4 * (j & 1), measured): x for j & 1 == 0

; predicate o = (n > K2).
; Clean: nothing is computed that has to be cleaned: the address of both accesses is classical (no address chain).
; Kept: n (rotated); x (rotated; also the value rail of the kept store a[0] = x) and that store's tape slot (rule 5
; sentence 3); o = icmp_ugt_i64_hl(n, K2), the overflow predicate, an output rail (rule 16, §0, §6); r (the load
; copy, measured: rule 2).
