; it the only acc rail).
; Clean: every inner trip's xor rail g = x ^ (i * c + j) (uncomputed in place after the add and the rule-6 clean-up; its
; _unc reads x, not acc) and the OLD acc of every inner trip (rule 6, in the body: acc' = acc + g is a bijection in acc for
; every g and nothing reads the old acc after the add, so t = acc' - g is computed fresh, copied onto the old acc,
; uncomputed and both freed; trip (0, 0)'s old acc is the |0> incoming %7).
; Kept: the user register x (%6); acc (%26, measured). Nothing is pushed, so there is no mirror.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; Both bounds are classical (rule 14): the lowering is the same nested classical loop. The quantum body computes g and
; acc' = acc + g, then RULE 6 IN A ROLLED LOOP (2026-10-31, as 05): a carried value whose trip update is a bijection and whose
; trip predicate (none here: classical bounds) does not read it is cleaned in the body of the same trip: t = acc' - g is
; copied onto the old acc, uncomputed and freed, the old acc is freed, and the garbage g is uncomputed in place (its _unc
; reads x and the classical i * c + j). The new acc rail is the only one that survives each trip, nothing is pushed, no
; reverse loop is needed and no copy-out: the measurement reads the carried acc directly. n <= 0, and n > 0 with m <= 0,
; take the classical edges and measure the seed rail itself.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 4, 5 (Memory, sentence 1), 20, 21, 3, 2.
; Checked: s = Horner evaluation of coef[0..n-1] at x (measured).
; Clean: every trip's accumulator rail and product rail s * x (both popped and uncomputed by the mirror, the sum
; before the product it read) and every load copy of coef[i] (popped by the mirror and un-copied right after the sum's
; _unc, its last reader); the load copy of coef[0] (the incoming accumulator, un-copied after the mirror, whose last
; reader is trip 1's fmul _unc, the mirror's final step). No memory version change occurs in the function, so every load copy whose
; consumer is uncomputed is un-copied (rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: the user register x; the copied-out result rail (measured); on the n <= 1 path the load copy of coef[0]
; (measured directly: rule 2's measured rail, never un-copied).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x.
; MEMORY. coef is a pointer PARAMETER: nothing is known about the object it addresses (rule 21), so every load through
; it is a bus load and its value a RAIL (rules 3, 20), although the program only reads classical host bytes (over-taint
; is accepted; such a rail costs no qubit). m = __cq_mem() is taken once at entry, and the run-time address of %2 once
; after it, as the classical i64 of the _hl form (rule 20). The index i is a classical induction, so &coef[i] is the
; classical getelementptr's ptrtoint (no inbounds: rule 21) and every access is cqrt_qram_load_f64_hl. coef[0] is the
; incoming accumulator: a load copy, not a seed. clang contracts s * x + coef[i] into llvm.fmuladd.f64, which is
; UNFUSED (§2): each trip is an fmul into a fresh product rail and an fadd of the product and the loaded coef[i] rail
; (both operands rails now: cq_template_fadd_f64, rule 4) into a fresh accumulator rail. The accumulator chain is a
; classical loop with the handle stack (rule 14, classical bound): each trip pushes the old accumulator, its product
; rail and its load copy, and the mirror (after the result is copied out) pops them, uncomputes the sum, un-copies the
; load at the address recomputed from the trip index (rule 14: classical, never pushed), then uncomputes the product
; (rule 5, dependency order). n <= 1 takes the classical edge and measures the coef[0] load copy itself.

  %30 = ptrtoint ptr %29 to i64    ; IR: its run-time address
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: that trip's load copy %17
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: that trip's product rail
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: that trip's %15
  call void @cq_template_fadd_f64_unc(i32 %28, i32 %32, i32 %31)    ; IR: uncompute %18 [sum]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %28)    ; IR: release the %18 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_f64_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %5, i64 %30)    ; IR: un-copy %17: the sum's _unc was its last reader, no memory version change since (rule 5 sentence 1)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release the %17 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fmul_f64_unc(i32 %32, i32 %33, i32 %7)    ; IR: uncompute %18 [product]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release the product rail (|0>)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 21, 5, 4, 2, 3; §1.3 (the overlay).
; Checked: v = TABLE[x & 7] (measured, the load copy %9 -> %10).
; Clean: the index rail %5 = x & 7, its zext %6, the scaled index %7 and the address rail %8, uncomputed and freed
; right after the load, before the measurement.
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register) and the load copy %9 (measured, rule 2: never un-copied, it stays allocated);
; no bus store, so no tape slot.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; ONE BUS (rule 20): a table of classical data read at a quantum index is an ordinary bus load at an ADDRESS RAIL; no
; QROM exists. @TABLE is a constant global, but it is host-resident only through getelementptrs with UNTAINTED indices;
; here the index is the rail x & 7, so the read is the bus load qram_load_i32 at the address rail. @TABLE stays an
; ordinary LLVM global at its host address; nothing is allocated, seeded or registered for it, and its cells are HOST:
; the load reads the host bytes at the access (§1.3). m = __cq_mem() is called once, at function entry (§5).
; ADDRESS ARITHMETIC (rule 20): the getelementptr with a tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic: -O1's zext to i64
; (zext_i32_to_i64), scaled by mul_i64_hl(., 4) (sizeof(int)) and added to the classical base by
; add_i64_hl(., ptrtoint @TABLE) (the constant index 0 contributes 0). No index is narrowed, bounded or checked.
; UNCOMPUTE (rules 5, 20): the load copy is measured, so the load is the address rail's last reader and the address
; chain (add, mul, zext) is uncomputed right after it, then the and that fed the zext; the rotated register x stays.

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 16, 18, 20, 21, 26; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc), §1.4.
; Checked: lo + hi (the add rail %10, measured -> %12) = ((x >> k) + (x & ((1 << k) - 1))) mod 2^32, the shift
; arithmetic and k taken mod 32 (§2); the cell hi on the bus at exit = x >> k.
; Clean: pointer_out_param: the clone's result rail lo (%8, rule 6: lo + hi is a bijection in lo and lo is dead), the
; inverse t = sum - hi (%11) and the load copy of hi (%9, un-copied: its last reader precedes every memory version
; change). __cq_q_split_100: the masked rail (%9), uncomputed after its copy-out and freed.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register), the sum rail %10 (measured); by rule 5 sentence 3 the tape slot of the store
; cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(%4, %5, %6) in __cq_q_split_100 (source `*hi = v >> k`) and its value rail, the shifted
; rail %6 (x >> k). Nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected for the driver pointer_out_param(0, .5, 3): Ry(.5) flips each of the 32 bits of x independently with
; probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087; the measured value is (x >> 3) + (x & 7): x unchanged (= 0, probability
; (1 - s)^32 = 0.132498) gives 0, as do x = -7m, m = 1..7 (dozens of flipped bits each, negligible).
; A POINTER IS ONE SCALAR (§1.4, rules 18, 21, 26). &hi is a classical ptr: split(x, k, &hi) is the clone of mask 100
; (v a rail, k classical, the out-parameter a classical ptr), __cq_q_split_100(i32, i32, ptr); nothing about the pointee
; appears in the name or the parameter list, and no handle crosses the call through memory. The out-parameter is an
; ordinary pointer formal: the clone stores through it and the caller loads it (as rule 26 says for sret).
; THE ALLOCA IS BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 b): hi is a call argument, so it is __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program
; point, no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). The clone's store is a bus store at the
; classical address (qram_store_i32_hl), the caller's load a bus load whose result is a rail (rule 3).
; WHAT THE CLONE STORES IS KEPT (rules 5, 18). The store `*hi = v >> k` is a kept store: its tape slot stays for the
; shot and so does its value rail, the ashr result, which is therefore not uncomputed in the clone. split writes
; memory, so __cq_q_split_100 has NO twin: its result lo is KEPT by rule 18 in the sense that no twin is called, and is
; cleaned by rule 6 like any other rail (rule 6, Dead: a call result that rule 18 keeps). lo + hi has both operands
; dead: the load copy of hi is garbage that rule 5 sentence 1 un-copies (no memory version change follows the load), so
; rule 6 cleans lo first (t = sum - hi reads the copy), then the copy is un-copied and freed, then the sum is measured.
; SPEC GAP: rule 5 sentence 1 asks for the last consumer's uncompute; the consumer (the add) is measured and has none.
; The load copy is un-copied after rule 6's clean, before the measurement, as in 195 and 200.
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no calling convention, linkage or attributes for a clone called by name; it keeps the callee's
; (internal fastcc, unnamed_addr) as 195 and 200 do, and the memory, capture and purity facts of split (nocapture,
; writeonly, memory(argmem: write), nofree, willreturn) are dropped (§1.4).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 24, 20, 16, 21, 5 (Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 6, 4, 2.
; Checked: y = tmp * 2 (measured, %11 -> %12); the cell tmp on the bus at exit holds x + c.
; Clean: the old x rail (%7, rule 6: x + c is a bijection in x, the add is x's only reader, and x is not itself the
; value rail of the kept store, so a clean-up point exists: right after the add, t = (x + c) - c recomputes x fresh,
; copy_i32(t, x) zeroes x, t is uncomputed, and both are freed); the load copy of tmp, un-copied and freed after its
; last reader (the shl), before the measurement.
; Kept: the sum rail x + c, the value rail of the kept store to tmp, and that store's tape slot (rule 5 sentence 3);
; the result rail (measured). Nothing else.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: Ry acts on all 32 qubits of x and everything after it is a basis permutation, so the measured value is
; the C program on independent bit flips of x with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209: volatile_local(0, .5, 3) measures
; 2 * ((0 ^ e) + 3) mod 2^32 for the flip pattern e, 6 with (1 - p)^31 = 0.141137 (e = 0, or e = 1<<31: 2 * (2^31 + 3) wraps to 6).
; THE VOLATILE IS UNOBSERVABLE (rule 24): its pointer operand is the alloca %4, whose only uses are the volatile store
; and load through it, lifetime intrinsics aside (rule 24), so the qualifier is dropped and both accesses are rule 20's.
; THE SLOT IS BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)): the store writes the rail x + c, a tainted value, so the alloca fails the
; host-resident test. It is __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program point (rule 16), no alloca remains, and the
; lifetime markers are dropped. Its address is the classical i64 ptrtoint of the block (rule 21), so the store is
; qram_store_i32_hl and the load qram_load_i32_hl. No rule forwards the stored value to the load: the load is a fresh
; copy of the cell (rule 20: every load is a bus load), and -O1's `tmp * 2` = shl 1 is an _hl shl template on it.
; THE STORE IS KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3): its tape slot stays for the shot and so does its value rail, the sum x + c,
; which is therefore never uncomputed. The load copy's last reader is the shl, whose result is measured (no _unc to
; wait for); no memory version change follows, so the copy is un-copied right after the shl, before the measurement

; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).

; 100 (x a rail, c and n classical, left to right): the formal c stays the C ptr, and nothing about the pointee crosses
; the call. The memory, capture and purity facts of the original (memory(argmem: read), nocapture, readonly, nofree,
; nosync) are dropped from the clone, from its call and from the lowered own symbol callee_with_loop (§1.4).

; each c[i] is qram_load_i32_hl(m, address) at the run-time address (ptrtoint of c once at entry, ptrtoint of the

; to free in the other two: every rail is a user register.
; Kept: second_rotation: x (%4, measured); rotate_derived: y (%6, rotated then measured); rotate_double: x (%4, measured).
; Rotations: second_rotation: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, 1). rotate_derived: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, y = x + c, t2, 1).
; rotate_double: (Ry_f64, x, t1, 1); (Ry_f64, x, t2, 1).
; A second cq_theta on a register that is already a handle is a second Ry on the same rail (rule 2: a rotation of an
; existing handle is in place). A cq_theta on a derived value (y = x + c, an out-of-place _hl add into a fresh rail by
; rule 4) rotates that fresh rail, which is a user register from then on. x is dead after the add and y = x + c is a
; bijection in x for fixed c, so rule 6 cleans the old x rail BEFORE the Ry on y: t = y - c recomputes x, copy_i32 zeroes
; x, t is uncomputed. Keeping x would leave a which-path record of y: the Ry(t2) would act on a dephased y (1-bit view,
; t1 = t2 = pi/2, c = 1: cleaned, y = X Ry(pi/2)|0> and Ry(pi/2) gives |1> with probability 1; kept, 1/2).

; 8 cells at &ip after the call, measured).
; Clean: every clone-internal SSA rail that no kept store holds: the bit view chain bits, bits >> 52, its trunc, e;
; the arm-2 predicate e > k+51; the hoisted arm rails x - x, e - k, its zext, mask >> (e - k), its complement, the
; bit view i of t, x - i; both rails of the return select ladder. Each is uncomputed by its _unc and freed.
; Kept: x (the rotated register, a source of both results and the value rail of arm 2's store); f (the clone's result
; rail, measured; the clone writes memory, so it has no twin) and the load copy of ip (measured, rule 2). By rule 5
; sentence 3, the three kept stores to ip in split: each one's tape slot, its value rail (z = bits & mask for arm 1,
; x for arm 2, t = bits & ~(mask >> (e - k)) for arm 3) and its control rail (the arm-1 flag e < k, the arm-2
; conjunction !(e < k) & (e > k+51), the arm-3 conjunction !(e < k) & !(e > k+51)).
; Rotations: (Ry_f64, x, th, 1).
; THE OUT-PARAMETER IS BUS MEMORY (rules 20, 21, 18). `double ip` is an alloca passed to a callee, a user that is
; not on rule 20 (b)'s list, so it is bus-resident: __cq_alloc(8, 8) at the alloca's program point, no alloca remains
; and the lifetime markers are dropped. Its address is a classical ptr, so split's clone keeps the pointer formal as
; the C ptr (mask digit 0: __cq_q_split_1000, nothing about the pointee crosses the call) and every access through it
; is an _hl bus access at its run-time i64 (ptrtoint once at entry, after __cq_mem()).

; arm-3 conjunction over both negated flags in one double bracket; the conjunctions are kept, their operand a2 is not

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 8, 7, 5, 2.
; Checked: y = x_K * c (the copied-out product of the carried x after K trips, %29, measured as %63).
; Clean: every trip rail except a_K: the path flags, products, the second compare, cont, the two candidate updates,
; the inner and carried selects, the chain predicates a_0..a_{K-1} (trips K..1 popped and uncomputed by the reverse
; loop; trip 0's test and a_0 uncomputed after it), and the |1> seed (%7) freed directly.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register); y (%29, measured); a_K (%27 of the K-th trip, %38 of the first reverse trip), the
; output rail of rule 14: the continue test evaluated after the K-th body, 1 iff the retry loop would run a (K+1)-th trip.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Both gotos reach the header through one latch block (%12) that merges the two continue paths, so this is one rolled
; K-bounded loop (as example 05) whose CONTINUE predicate is the disjunction of the two path conditions:
; cont = (x > k) | (x*c > m), one or_i1 into a fresh |0> flag (rule 8; the second goto's own path predicate
; !(x > k) & (x*c > m) is not materialised, the OR absorbs it). -O1 tests at the header with no pre-header guard, so the
; loop is re-rolled to body-then-test (rule 14): the FIRST header evaluation (x_0 > k, x_0 * c, x_0 * c > m, cont_0) is
; computed before the loop as trip 0 of the chain, a_0 = seed & cont_0 from the |1> seed; trip j (j = 1..K) runs the
; body under a_{j-1} (the latch value x' = p1 ? x-k : x>>1 on the path flag of the CURRENT x, selected into the carried
; x only where a_{j-1} = 1) and then the NEXT header evaluation on the new x, a_j = a_{j-1} & cont_j. The path flag and
; the product of each test are carried into the next trip (the body's inner select reads the flag; the product of the
; last test is y). K = 4 (the literal 4 below).
; Output rail (rule 14): after the K-th body the chain ends in cont_K, the test admitting trip K + 1; a_K = a_{K-1} &
; cont_K is kept allocated, neither uncomputed nor freed: a_K = 1 means the retry loop would still continue after K
; trips; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0. y is the value of x*c at the exit: the carried x stops
; changing once the loop has exited, so y = x_K * c, the product of the K-th test, copied out (alloc + copy) and
; measured. The reverse loop pops trips K..1 and skips the predicate uncompute on its first iteration (reverse index 0)
; by a classical branch; trip 0's test and a_0 are uncomputed after it and the |1> seed is freed directly (rule 7).

  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching recompute the first time (always 1)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %8, %2 at recompute the first time: trip 0 of the chain  [path 1 predicate, block %10]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %3)    ; IR: %15 = mul nsw i32 %8, %3  (block %14, pure, hoisted)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %9, i32 %4)    ; IR: %16 = icmp sgt i32 %15, %4
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: block %12 is reached = path 1 OR path 2: cont = %9 | %16 (rule 8)

  %16 = phi i32 [ %12, %5 ], [ %27, %13 ]    ; IR: a_{j-1}: predicate of this trip's body (the back edge that reaches it)
  %17 = phi i32 [ %8, %5 ], [ %23, %13 ]    ; IR: %9 of the current x (path 1 flag, computed by the previous test)
  %18 = phi i32 [ %9, %5 ], [ %24, %13 ]    ; IR: %15 of the current x (computed by the previous test)

  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %22, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = icmp sgt i32 %8, %2 at the next recompute: the test after this body
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %22, i32 %3)    ; IR: %15 = mul nsw i32 %8, %3 of the next header
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %24, i32 %4)    ; IR: %16 = icmp sgt i32 %15, %4
  %26 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: cont of the next header = %9 | %16 (rule 8)
  call void @cqrt_or_i1(i32 %23, i32 %25, i32 %26)    ; IR: cont ^= %9 | %16
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_j = predicate of the next back edge (after trip K: a_K, the output rail)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %16, i32 %26, i32 %27)    ; IR: br label %7 from %12 taken once more
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %19)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %20)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %25)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %26)

  %33 = phi i32 [ 0, %30 ], [ %50, %49 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %34 = phi i32 [ %22, %30 ], [ %46, %49 ]    ; IR: %8 written by this trip
  %35 = phi i32 [ %27, %30 ], [ %45, %49 ]    ; IR: a_j, the predicate computed by this trip's test
  %36 = phi i32 [ %23, %30 ], [ %44, %49 ]    ; IR: %9 computed by this trip's test
  %37 = phi i32 [ %24, %30 ], [ %43, %49 ]    ; IR: %15 computed by this trip's test
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %42 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %43 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %44 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %46 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release %16 (|0>)

  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release next %8 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %40, i32 %44, i32 %42, i32 %41)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 22, 21, 16, 14 (a_K kept), 5, 7, 8, 4, 2.
; Checked: a[m - 1] after the K-bounded loop a[i] = i * c, i = 0..m (the load copy at the address rail, measured,
; %35 -> %43); the cells of a at exit, read from the bus at the block's address: a[j] = j * c where trip j ran (j <= m,
; j < K), else 0.
; Clean: the hoisted bound m + 1 and its zext (%16, %17); every trip's latch flag (%27, pushed, popped and uncomputed by
; the reverse loop); the address chain of &a[m - 1] (the index m - 1, its sext, the scaled index, the address rail:
; %31..%34), uncomputed right after the load (the load copy is measured, so the load is the rail's last reader).
; Kept: the user register m (%7); the load copy a[m - 1] (%35, measured: rule 2, never un-copied); by rule 5: the 16
; tape slots of the memset's byte stores and their one value seed i8 0 (%8, rule 7); per trip j the tape slot of the
; store a[j] = j * c, its value seed j * c (%23) and its control rail, the trip predicate a_j (%20: a_0 is the guard
; flag %15 inside its X bracket, a_1..a_{K-1} are %28 of trips 0..K-2), none of them pushed (rule 14: a trip rail rule
; 5 keeps is not pushed); the LAST trip predicate a_K (%28 of trip K - 1; rule 14: a_K = 1 means the loop had not
; exited after K trips, which is observable; the trip count m + 1 has no range bound, so B is unknown and a_K is kept).
; Rotations: (Ry, m, th, 1).
; ONE BUS (rule 20). a is BUS-RESIDENT: the loop's store through it is under a quantum predicate (the trip predicate)
; and the read a[m - 1] goes through a getelementptr with a tainted index, so rule 20 (b) fails for it: __cq_alloc(16,
; 16) at the alloca's program point (rules 16, 20: one zeroed block, no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are
; dropped and the end of the lifetime undoes nothing). m = __cq_mem() once at entry. Nothing is known about the block
; at compile time: its address is a classical i64 (ptrtoint), and no index is narrowed, bounded or checked (rule 21).
; THE INITIALIZER (rule 22). `= {0, 0, 0, 0}` is -O1's llvm.memset(a, 0, 16): ONE host loop of 16 kept byte stores
; qram_store_i8_hl at the classical addresses a + j, all of one value seed alloc_i8(0) (rule 7). It is emitted although
; the block is already zero (§0). Value, address and control are classical-valued, so the cells stay HOST.
; THE LOOP. The bound is quantum (m + 1 trips), so it is the rolled K-bounded loop of example 05 (rule 14), unchanged:
; its first predicate is NOT (m < 0) (an X bracket on the guard flag) and the next predicate is a_j & NOT (j + 1 ==
; m + 1). Inside trip j the store a[i] = i * c has the CLASSICAL address &a[j] (an affine induction with a classical
; start, recomputed from the trip index by a getelementptr without inbounds, never carried or pushed) and the
; classical value j * c, minted as the seed alloc_i32(j * c) (rule 7). It is ONE kept store
; qram_store_i32_hl_controlled(a_j, m, &a[j], seed) (rule 14: every bus access of trip j is under a_j): under a_j = 0
; nothing is touched and its slot stays |0>; under a_j = 1 the cell becomes QUANTUM (§1.3). The store is never popped
; (rule 5 sentence 3), so its control a_j and its value seed stay; the reverse loop pops only the latch flags.
; THE READ (rules 20, 21). a[m - 1] is one qram_load_i32 at an ADDRESS RAIL: the index m - 1 (add template), -O1's
; sext to i64 (sext template), scaled by mul_i64_hl(., 4) and added to the classical base by add_i64_hl. An address
; outside the block reads whatever the bus holds there (HOST bytes, or 0 where unreadable, §2): nothing is checked.
; Basis check (driver array_in_quantum_loop(1, .5, 3)): Ry(.5) flips each of the 32 bits of m0 = 1 with p = sin^2(.25)
; = 0.061209. On the unflipped branch ((1 - p)^32 = 0.132498) m = 1: trips 0 and 1 run (a_0 = a_1 = 1, a_2 = a_3 =
; a_K = 0), a = {0, 3, 0, 0} and a[0] = 0 is measured. m = 3 (bit 1 flipped): four trips, a = {0, 3, 6, 9}, a[2] = 6,
; a_K = 0 (the loop exits after exactly K trips). m = 5 (bit 2 flipped): four trips, a_K = 1, and a[4] reads the bytes
; just past the block.
; SPEC GAP: rule 8 closes the X bracket of a flag; the guard flag %15 here is trip 0's predicate and so the control of a
; kept store (rule 5), never uncomputed. Chosen: the bracket is still closed (not_i1 after the loop, where the old
; construction closed it before the flag's _unc), so the kept rail holds the IR's %6 = (m < 0).

define i32 @array_in_quantum_loop(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; the bus M, once at function entry (§5)
  %5 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 16, i64 16)    ; IR: %4 = alloca [4 x i32], align 16  [bus-resident (rule 20): one zeroed block, no alloca remains (rule 16)]
  %6 = ptrtoint ptr %5 to i64    ; IR: %4 as its run-time address (classical, rule 21)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register m]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %7, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: call @llvm.memset(%4, i8 0, 16): the byte value as ONE seed rail (rules 7, 22), kept with its stores; llvm.lifetime.start dropped (rule 16)
  br label %9

9:
  %10 = phi i64 [ 0, %3 ], [ %12, %9 ]    ; IR: call @llvm.memset(%4, i8 0, 16): byte j of the classical length 16 (host loop, rule 22)
  %11 = add i64 %6, %10    ; IR: the classical address a + j
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %4, i64 %11, i32 %8)    ; IR: call @llvm.memset(%4, i8 0, 16): byte store j  (kept store, rule 5; classical-valued, the cell stays HOST)
  %12 = add nuw nsw i64 %10, 1
  %13 = icmp eq i64 %12, 16
  br i1 %13, label %14, label %9

14:
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 0)    ; IR: %6 = icmp slt i32 %5, 0  [guard]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %15)    ; IR: bracket: the loop is entered under NOT %6 (used as trip 0's predicate)
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 1)    ; IR: %8 = add nuw i32 %5, 1  (pure, hoisted out of block %7)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64(i32 %16)    ; IR: %9 = zext i32 %8 to i64
  br label %18

18:
  %19 = phi i64 [ 0, %14 ], [ %26, %18 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i64 [ 0, %7 ], [ %21, %16 ]  (classical trip index, bounded by K)  [K]
  %20 = phi i32 [ %15, %14 ], [ %28, %18 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip (trip 0: NOT %6)
  %21 = trunc i64 %19 to i32    ; IR: %19 = trunc i64 %17 to i32  (classical)
  %22 = mul i32 %21, %2    ; IR: %20 = mul i32 %19, %2  (classical)
  %23 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %22)    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %18: the classical value i*c of this trip as a seed (rule 7), the store's value rail, kept with it
  %24 = getelementptr [4 x i32], ptr %5, i64 0, i64 %19    ; IR: %18 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 %17  [affine induction, classical start: recomputed from the trip index, not carried]
  %25 = ptrtoint ptr %24 to i64    ; IR: &a[i], the _hl address
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl_controlled(i32 %20, i32 %4, i64 %25, i32 %23)    ; IR: store i32 %20, ptr %18: a[i] = i*c under this trip's predicate  [kept store (rule 5): its slot, its value seed and its control a_j stay]
  %26 = add nuw nsw i64 %19, 1    ; IR: %21 = add nuw nsw i64 %17, 1  (classical)
  %27 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl(i32 %17, i64 %26)    ; IR: %22 = icmp eq i64 %21, %9
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next trip = a & NOT %22
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %20, i32 %27, i32 %28)    ; IR: br i1 %22 not taken
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %27)    ; IR: %22 of this trip, for the reverse loop (a_j and the value seed are kept, not pushed: rule 14)
  %29 = icmp ult i64 %26, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %22, label %10, label %16  [K]
  br i1 %29, label %18, label %30

30:
  %31 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %7, i32 -1)    ; IR: %11 = add nsw i32 %5, -1
  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_sext_i32_to_i64(i32 %31)    ; IR: %12 = sext i32 %11 to i64
  %33 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %32, i64 4)    ; IR: %13 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %4, i64 0, i64 %12  [the tainted index scaled by the element size (rule 20)]
  %34 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %33, i64 %6)    ; IR: %13 = getelementptr  [+ the classical base: the address rail of &a[m - 1]]
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32(i32 %4, i32 %34)    ; IR: %14 = load i32, ptr %13: a[m - 1]  [a load at an address rail; measured below, so never un-copied (rules 2, 5)]  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_hl_unc(i32 %34, i32 %33, i64 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %13  [the address rail: its load is its last reader (rule 20)]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %34)    ; IR: release the %13 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %33, i32 %32, i64 4)    ; IR: uncompute %13 (the scaled index)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %33)    ; IR: release the scaled-index rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sext_i32_to_i64_unc(i32 %32, i32 %31)    ; IR: uncompute %12
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %32)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %31, i32 %7, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %11
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %31)    ; IR: release the %11 rail (|0>)
  br label %36

36:
  %37 = phi i64 [ 3, %30 ], [ %40, %36 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index (K - 1 down to 0)  [K]
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %22 of that trip
  %39 = add nuw nsw i64 %37, 1    ; IR: %21 of that trip (classical)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl_unc(i32 %38, i32 %17, i64 %39)    ; IR: uncompute %22
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %38)    ; IR: release %22 (|0>)
  %40 = add nsw i64 %37, -1
  %41 = icmp sgt i64 %40, -1    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %41, label %36, label %42

42:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %15)    ; IR: bracket closed: %6 back; the flag is trip 0's store control and stays (rule 5)
  call void @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64_unc(i32 %17, i32 %16)    ; IR: uncompute %9
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %17)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %7, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %16)
  %43 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %35)    ; IR: %15 = cq_measure_si32(%14)
  ret i32 %43    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.end(16, %4) dropped (rule 16); ret i32 %15
}

; each trip, popped as %33..%41 in the reverse loop) and the two |0> seed rails for s and q (%6, %7 / %42, %43), all freed.

; predicate and hence no a_K output rail, the arm flag t > ix of each trip is uncomputed. -O1 already turned the arm into

; IR %33/%34 -> %35). The cells of the block on the bus at exit: the low bit of q[i] holds the measured outcome of q[i]
; (its high 7 bits 0), 0 <= i < n.
; Clean: per rotate trip, the swap rail of the in-place form (|0> after the swap-in, freed).
; Kept: the cells q[0..n-1] themselves (the registers live in memory: rotated in place, read and measured through load
; copies); by rule 5 sentence 3, the n tape slots of the memset's byte stores and their ONE value seed alloc_i8(0) (rules
; 7, 22; classical-valued, no qubit); by rule 5 sentence 1, the n angle load copies theta[i] (IR %22: each is un-copied
; right after its last reader, the Ry, and left allocated, since the in-place form's swap-out, a memory version change,
; lies between the load and that point (it is placed after the swap-in: no bus access between the form's swaps); HOST cells, classical-valued, no qubit); by rule 2, the n measured i1 load
; copies (IR %33/%34).

; value loaded from the bus is a quantum angle, rule 3), each in place on cell i through the in-place form's swap rail.
; Driver register_array(coef, 3); register_array(coef, 4), coef = {1, 2, 3, 4} a host array: Ry(theta[i]) on |0> gives
; 1 with probability sin^2(theta[i] / 2) = 0.2298, 0.7081, 0.9950, 0.8268, so e is a sum of independent Bernoullis
; (mean 1.9329 for n = 3, 2.7597 for n = 4).

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 5, 8, 20, 21; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, qram_swap).
; Checked: nothing is measured here; the result is the n byte cells q + 0 .. q + n-1 of the bus (one _Bool each, the
;          state in its low bit).
; Clean: per outer trip, the swap rail of the in-place form on q[i] (|0> after its swap-in). Per inner trip, the Toffoli
;        flag q[j] & q[i] and the two load copies it reads: q[j] (un-copied) and q[i] (loaded under q[j], un-copied
;        under the same q[j]).
; Kept: nothing: no tape slot (the only cell update is an in-place form), no load copy (each is un-copied before the
;       next memory version change, the next trip's in-place form).
; Rotations: for i = 0..n-1: (Ry at width i1, the cell q + i, base, 1); then for j = i+1..n-1: (P, the flag
;            q[j] & q[i], base / 2^(j-i), 1).
; Expected: the QFT ladder on n qubits with base as the opening rotation and the controlled phases base/2^(j-i)
; between q[i] and every later q[j], without the final bit-reversal swaps.
; MEMORY (rule 20). `q` is an ordinary pointer: its cells are bytes on the one bus M, at the run-time address q + i
; (rule 21: a classical i64, the ptrtoint of the getelementptr); nothing is asked about what they hold. The caller
; passes a _Bool array; the cells start HOST (the caller's bytes) and become QUANTUM at their first in-place form.
; The outer loop's `cq_theta(&q[i], base)` is `load i8 %16; trunc nuw to i1; cq_theta_i1; zext; store i8 %16` on the
; same SSA pointer with nothing between: rule 5's in-place form through the Width-casts clause, at width i1 (rule 2):
; qram_swap_i1_hl, ry_i1, qram_swap_i1_hl, free. The rotated value has no other reader (-O1 reloads q[i] in the inner
; loop), so no plain load follows the swap-in.
; The inner loop's `if (q[j] && q[i])` is two nested branches (-O1 keeps the short-circuit): the first conjunct's load
; of q[j] is a plain bus load (no quantum predicate in scope), the second conjunct's reload of q[i] sits in the arm of
; the q[j] flag and is the _controlled load under it (rule 5: every bus access under a quantum predicate). The two are
; folded into ONE Toffoli flag (rule 8); the cq_phi with its classically computed angle is a kickback on that flag; the
; flag is un-Toffoli'd and freed, then the q[i] copy is un-copied under q[j] and the q[j] copy un-copied (rule 5
; sentence 1: the inner loop makes no memory version change). Both loops are classical-bound: no predicate chain, no
; stack.
; SPEC GAP 1: each read of a _Bool cell is the program's own `load i8; trunc nuw i8 to i1`, no in-place form's Readers
; clause. Chosen as 117 and 205 (SPEC GAP 5): the load at the width i1 the value is used at (qram_load_i1_hl, §1.3: the
; low bit of the cell), not a qram_load_i8 and a trunc template (BACKEND_ABI lists no trunc i8 -> i1).

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 17, 2, 5 (in-place form; Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 18, 10, 20, 21, 16, 7, 8; §1.3 (the bus, qram_swap), §1.4.
; Checked: invert_theta: x (%4 -> %5). invert_call: x (the 4 cells at P, the address of the bus-resident x; read by
; the load copy %12 -> %13) and y (%11 -> %14), summed classically. The cells at P at exit hold x after both calls.
; Clean: in __cq_q_prep_01000: the swap rail of each in-place form (%8, %10: |0> after its swap-in) and the flag
; f = (y > k) (%9), uncomputed and freed after its last controlled gate (in the bracketed activation the backend
; recomputes and uncomputes it as the reversed list runs, rule 17).
; Kept: the user registers x (the cell at P) and y (rotated, measured). Rule 5 sentence 3: the tape slot of the store
; x = x0 and its value rail, the seed alloc_i32(x0) (%10 of invert_call). Rule 2: the load copy of x (%12), measured.
; Rotations: invert_theta: (Ry, x, th, 1); then the region as the backend emits it: (Ry, x, -t2, 1).
; invert_call: (Ry, y, ty, 1); (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, y > k); then the region: (Ry, x, -t2, y > k); (Ry, x, -t1, 1).
; cq_invert is the run-time pair cqrt_invert_begin()/cqrt_invert_end() (rule 17, §1.3): the code between the markers is
; lowered as anywhere else, and the backend emits the gates recorded between the two calls reversed with each gate
; inverted. invert_theta: the recorded list is [Ry(x, t2)], emitted as Ry(x, -t2).
; invert_call: `prep(&x, ...)` takes x's ADDRESS, a call user, so the alloca of x is bus-resident (rule 20 (b)):
; __cq_alloc(4, 4) at its program point, P = its run-time address (a classical i64), no alloca remains and the lifetime
; markers are dropped (rule 16). `x = x0` is a bus store of the seed alloc_i32(x0) at P, a kept store (rules 5, 7).
; THE CLONE (§1.4, rules 18, 21): a pointer is one scalar. &x is a classical ptr (not computed from a rail), digit 0,
; and the formal stays the C ptr; y is a quantum scalar, digit 1; the angles and k are classical: __cq_q_prep_01000.
; Nothing about the pointee crosses the call. In the clone, `*x = cq_theta(*x, t1)` is rule 5's in-place form at the
; classical address p = ptrtoint %0 (swap-out into a |0> rail, Ry, swap-in, free): the cell is the register. The
; conditional `*x = cq_theta(%7, t2)` rotates the value -O1 forwarded from the first store to the same SSA pointer
; (rule 5, Readers): its interval runs from that store and holds no memory version change (only the compare template),
; so it is a second in-place form, under the flag f = (y > k) read from the OTHER register y (rule 10 on a memory cell):
; the swaps are qram_swap_i32_hl_controlled(f, ...) and the gate ry_i32_controlled(f, ...). The clone's body is
; [swap; Ry(t1); swap; f = (y > k); swap|f; cRy(f, t2); swap|f; unc f; free f]. It writes memory (two in-place forms),
; so it has no twin and its calls are memory version changes (rules 5, 18); it has no result.
; The bracketed call is the SAME clone (no `_adj` kind exists, §1.4): rule 17's "Memory": an in-place form inverts
; exactly, so the backend's reversal of the gates it records is [unc f (= compute f); swap|f; cRy(f, -t2); swap|f;
; f's uncompute; swap; Ry(-t1); swap], with the frees performed after the reversed list. Had the condition read x
; itself (`if (*x > k) cq_theta(x, t2)`), the flag could not be uncomputed after the rotation changed x; that shape is
; example 66, where the flag stays allocated. After the region, `cq_measure(x)` reads x through a plain bus load at P
; (rule 3): the copy is the measured rail (rule 2, never un-copied).
; SPEC GAP (corpus convention, §5): §1.3 / rule 19 ask for a __cq_clone_register row (the _t clone, _t_ctl and their
; twins) per externally visible function. As in 200, 204, 211 and 212 nothing is registered for invert_theta and
; invert_call (their addresses are never taken here); the compiler emits the rows, and the omission is not part of the
; pinned lowering.
; Regenerated 2026-11-05 for the flat bus (the 2026-11-02 version kept x's handle in a classical slot, passed the slot
; to __cq_q_prep_11000 with a pointee digit and rotated the handle it loaded; the first version constructed
; __cq_q_prep_11000_adj at compile time).

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %11, double %2)    ; IR: %8 = cq_theta_ui32(%1, %2)  [Ry]
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_prep_01000(ptr noundef %8, i32 noundef %11, double noundef %3, double noundef %4, i32 noundef %5)    ; IR: call fastcc void @prep(%7, %8, %3, %4, %5): the clone of mask 01000 (classical ptr, y quantum); it writes memory, no twin (rule 18)
  call void @cqrt_invert_begin()    ; IR: call @__cq_invert_begin(); fence consumed (rule 17)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_prep_01000(ptr noundef %8, i32 noundef %11, double noundef %3, double noundef %4, i32 noundef %5)    ; IR: bracketed call @prep(%7, %8, %3, %4, %5): the same clone; the backend reverses and inverts the gates it records
  call void @cqrt_invert_end()    ; IR: call @__cq_invert_end(); fence consumed

  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %6, i64 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i32 %7, ptr %0: swap-in: the cell holds %7; the store closes form (1)

  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: block %9: %10 = cq_theta_ui32(%7, %3): in-place form (2) on the forwarded %7 (rule 5, Readers: no memory version change since store (1)), the swap rail (|0>)

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14, 9, 8, 4, 5, 7, 2.
; Checked: r = a^e mod N over the nbits low bits of e, then e (measured, summed classically).
; Clean: every trip's and, eq flag, product, remainder and merge rails (popped and uncomputed by the mirror) and the
; seed rail holding the classical 1 (never written, freed directly, rule 7).
; Kept: the user register e; the copied-out result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on e.
; Shor's controlled modular multiply: the exponent bit `(e >> i) & 1` is the condition of a value arm inside a
; classical-bound loop (rule 14); -O1 rewrites it to `(1 << i) & e`, so the and is a commutative Q+C op whose classical
; operand moves to the _hl slot (rule 4). The loop is classical (no predicate chain): each trip computes the and, the
; eq flag, the modular product into fresh rails and merges by one select (eq ? r : product, rule 9); r is loop-carried
; and seeded CLASSICAL (a rail holding 1 before trip 0). The classical recurrence `base = base*base % N` runs beside
; it. The reverse loop needs each trip's classical `base` and `1 << i`: the shift is recomputed from the trip index,
; the base is pushed on the classical handle stack beside the handles (the stack is classical; a classical word on it
; is ordinary, §1.3 push/pop). After the result is copied out and the loop mirrored, r is measured, then the user
; register e. nbits <= 0 takes the classical edge and measures the seed rail itself.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @modexp(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3, i32 noundef %4) {

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 1)    ; IR: incoming 1 of phi %16 / %9  [r before trip 0: a rail holding the classical 1]
  %8 = icmp sgt i32 %4, 0    ; IR: %7 = icmp sgt i32 %4, 0  (classical)

  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_ui32(%6)

  %15 = phi i32 [ %25, %13 ], [ 0, %5 ]    ; IR: %15 = phi i32 [ %27, %24 ], [ 0, %5 ]  (classical i)
  %16 = phi i32 [ %7, %5 ], [ %23, %13 ]    ; IR: %16 = phi i32 [ %25, %24 ], [ 1, %5 ]

  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %18)    ; IR: %19 = and i32 %18, %6  (commutative: classical operand moved to the _hl slot)
  %20 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %19, i32 0)    ; IR: %20 = icmp eq i32 %19, 0  [predicate of SKIPPING block %21]
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %16, i32 %17)    ; IR: %22 = mul i32 %17, %16  (block %21, hoisted: pure; commutative, classical operand to _hl)
  %22 = call i32 @cq_template_urem_i32_hl(i32 %21, i32 %3)    ; IR: %23 = urem i32 %22, %3  (block %21, hoisted)
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %20, i32 %16, i32 %22)    ; IR: %25 = phi i32 [ %23, %21 ], [ %16, %13 ] = %20 ? %16 : %23

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (b) (the union is a bus-resident alloca; union views and bit-fields need no rule), 16 (__cq_alloc),
; 5 (kept stores, the load un-copy), 2, 3, 4, 21, 25; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc).
; Checked: u.e after the exponent write-back (the load copy %17 of the 10 cells at &u, measured -> %18), and the cells of u
; read from the bus at exit: bytes 0..9 = the x87 pattern of x with bits 64..78 replaced by (exp(x) - k) & 0x7fff, bytes
; 10..11 = 0.
; Clean: the exponent arithmetic (%11 the sub, %12 the & 0x7fff, %13 the & -0x8000), uncomputed in LIFO order right after
; the or that reads them, and the load copy of the word at byte 8 (%10), un-copied after them, before the store of the new
; word (the next memory version change).
; Kept: x (%7, the rotated register, also the value rail of the kept store u.e = x); the new word (%14, the value rail of
; the kept store u.bits.exp = ...); the tape slots of the two stores (no handle: in the backend, holding the displaced
; cells); the load copy u.e (%17, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected for f80_union_slot(0, .5, 1): x starts as the all-zero x87 pattern and Ry(.5) flips each of its 80 bits
; independently with probability sin^2(.25) = 0.061209. The stored word at byte 8 is bits 64..79 of x zero-extended
; (bytes 10, 11 of the fresh block are 0); its low 15 bits (the exponent) are replaced by exp - 1 mod 2^15, the sign and
; the zero high half are kept. With probability cos^2(.25)^80 = 0.006390 no bit flipped: exp 0 - 1 = 0x7fff, sign 0,
; mantissa 0 (integer bit 0: the x87 pseudo-infinity pattern 0x7fff_0000000000000000, returned as it stands).
; THE UNION IS MEMORY (rule 20). The alloca of u has a store of a rail among its users (u.e = x), so it is bus-resident by
; rule 20 (b): __cq_alloc(12, 16) at the alloca's program point (rule 16; one zeroed block), no alloca remains and the
; lifetime markers are dropped. Every access is one bus access of the type and at the address its instruction names

name: 65_fenv_bracket
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 8, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_bracket: y = x * c; fenv_tested: y + (double)f, f = fetestexcept(FE_INEXACT) (y measured; f is classical
; by rule 2 and is a classical read).
; Clean: the compare flag y > k of each function; the flags rail select(y > k, 32, 0) of each function; fenv_tested's
; flags & 32 and host | quantum rails. All of them collapse after the measurement of y (rule 2).
; Kept: the user register x of each function; the result rail y (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; Classical reads (rule 2): 1 (fenv_tested's cq_measure(f): f is classical after y's measurement, no gate).
; This is the DEFAULT-ENVIRONMENT case of rule 23: without `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON` clang emits plain
; fadd/fmul/fcmp, which assume round-to-nearest and raise no flags, so every FP op lowers to its ordinary template;
; examples 80-82 are the full model (constrained ops). The fenv calls are classical calls on thread-global state and
; are kept exactly as clang emitted them (host calls on the real fenv_t slot); classical code is never deleted. The
; flags are split as in 81: the host register holds what classical code raises, the quantum FLAGS RAIL what quantum
; code raises. Plain ops raise nothing, so the only quantum write is an explicit feraiseexcept under a quantum
; predicate: flags' = flags | select(pred, m, 0), no host call (while the rail is empty, the select rail is the flags
; rail). fetestexcept(m) = host call | (flags & m). fenv_bracket: the feholdexcept/feupdateenv pair brackets no
; quantum flags (the rail is empty throughout), so it is host calls only. fenv_tested: fesetround(FE_UPWARD) is a host
; call but does not reach the plain fmul, which clang compiled for the default environment, so the template rounds to
; nearest exactly as the IR says.
; CLASSICAL COLLAPSE (rule 2, ruling 2026-10-29): both functions measure y, and every rail computed from y alone (the
; compare, the flags rail, fenv_tested's f chain) is a function of the outcome and classical values. Rule 2 is a
; data-flow condition, not a program-order one: those rails were computed BEFORE the measurement, and "while its
; sources still hold the outcome" is exactly that case (the _unc reads the measured rail, which still holds m). So each
; such rail is uncomputed right after the measurement (convention: as early as the invariant allows) and its value is
; recomputed by ordinary classical instructions from m. The flags rail is fenv state: its classical value is written to
; the HOST environment by feraiseexcept(v) at the collapse point (v = 0 raises nothing), so rule 23's "final flags rail
; is an output" has nothing left to keep. fenv_tested's cq_measure(f) measures a value rule 2 made classical: it is a
; classical read and emits no measurement (one measurement per call, y's). f's host part (%11) was read at its program
; point, before the write-back, exactly as the C program read it.
source_filename = "fenv_bracket.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

%struct.fenv_t = type { i16, i16, i32, [8 x i8] }    ; IR: %struct.fenv_t  (the host part keeps its real layout)

define double @fenv_bracket(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = alloca %struct.fenv_t, align 4    ; IR: %5 = alloca fenv_t  (env, host slot)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @fegetround()    ; IR: %7 = fegetround()  (host call)
  %8 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 0)    ; IR: %8 = fesetround(0)  (host call)
  %9 = call i32 @feholdexcept(ptr %5)    ; IR: %9 = feholdexcept(%5)  (host call; the quantum flags rail is empty)
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %6, double %2)    ; IR: %10 = fmul double %6, %2  [result rail y]  (plain op: raises nothing)
  %11 = call i32 @feupdateenv(ptr %5)    ; IR: %11 = feupdateenv(%5)  (host call; empty | empty)
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl(i32 %10, double %3)    ; IR: %12 = fcmp ogt double %10, %3  [predicate of block %13]
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %12, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: br i1 %12 -> block %13: %14 = feraiseexcept(32) under the predicate  [flags rail]
  %14 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 %7)    ; IR: %16 = fesetround(%7)  (host call)
  %15 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %10)    ; IR: %17 = cq_measure_f64(%10)  [outcome m; %10 holds it from here on]
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse: the flags rail is a function of y alone; uncompute it while %12 still holds its value
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the flags rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl_unc(i32 %12, i32 %10, double %3)    ; IR: uncompute %12 while %10 holds the outcome
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %12 rail (|0>)
  %16 = fcmp ogt double %15, %3    ; IR: %12 recomputed classically from the outcome (rule 2)
  %17 = select i1 %16, i32 32, i32 0    ; IR: the flags rail's classical value: select(y > k, 32, 0)
  %18 = call i32 @feraiseexcept(i32 %17)    ; IR: the collapsed flags written to the host environment (rule 23; raises nothing when %17 = 0)
  ret double %15    ; IR: ret double %17
}

define double @fenv_tested(double noundef %0, double noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_f64(double %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_f64(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_f64(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @fesetround(i32 2048)    ; IR: %6 = fesetround(2048)  (host call; does not reach the plain fmul)
  %7 = call i32 @feclearexcept(i32 32)    ; IR: %7 = feclearexcept(32)  (host call; the quantum flags rail is still empty)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_fmul_f64_hl(i32 %5, double %2)    ; IR: %8 = fmul double %5, %2  [result rail y]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl(i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: %9 = fcmp ogt double %8, %3  [predicate of block %10]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %9, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: br i1 %9 -> block %10: %11 = feraiseexcept(32) under the predicate  [flags rail]
  %11 = call i32 @fetestexcept(i32 32)    ; IR: %13 = fetestexcept(32): the host part, read at its program point
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 32)    ; IR: %13: the quantum part, flags & 32
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_or_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 %11)    ; IR: %13 = host | quantum  [f]
  %14 = call double @cqrt_measure_f64(i32 %8)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_f64(%8)  [outcome m; %8 holds it from here on]
  call void @cq_template_or_i32_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 2 collapse: f is a function of y alone; uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %12, i32 %10, i32 32)    ; IR: uncompute %13's quantum part
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_ll_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i32 32, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute the flags rail (a function of y alone)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_fcmp_ogt_f64_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, double %3)    ; IR: uncompute %9 while %8 holds the outcome
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  %15 = fcmp ogt double %14, %3    ; IR: %9 recomputed classically from the outcome (rule 2)
  %16 = select i1 %15, i32 32, i32 0    ; IR: the flags rail's classical value: select(y > k, 32, 0)
  %17 = and i32 %16, 32    ; IR: %13's quantum part, classical
  %18 = or i32 %17, %11    ; IR: %13 = host | quantum, classical  [f]
  %19 = call i32 @feraiseexcept(i32 %16)    ; IR: the collapsed flags written to the host environment (rule 23)
  %20 = sitofp i32 %18 to double    ; IR: %16 = sitofp i32 %15 to double  (%15 = cq_measure_si32(%13) is a classical read of f: no measurement)
  %21 = fadd double %14, %20    ; IR: %17 = fadd double %14, %16  (classical)
  ret double %21    ; IR: ret double %17
}

name: 66_self_conditioned_rotation
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 10 (a flag that read the rotated register stays allocated), 8, 2.
; Checked: x (%5 -> %7).
; Clean: none: nothing is freed.
; Kept: x (%5, the rotated register) and the flag f = (x > k) (%6): it was computed from x before the controlled rotation
; changed x, so it can no longer be uncomputed and stays allocated, entangled with x.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, t1, 1); (Ry, x, t2, x > k) with the predicate read from x before this rotation.
; The condition reads the register the arm rotates: the flag f = (x > k) is computed from x BEFORE the rotation, and after
; cRy(f, x, t2) it can no longer be uncomputed from x, because x has changed. We never decline: the flag is emitted, the
; rotation is controlled by it, and the flag simply STAYS ALLOCATED, entangled with x, like a user register (its which-branch
; record dephases later interference between the two arms: that is what the program says). C principle: the compiler does
; not stop the user shooting their own foot; it emits the program as written. Compare 39, where the condition reads a
; different register and the flag is uncomputed.
source_filename = "self_conditioned_rotation.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

define i32 @self_conditioned_rotation(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, double noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_sgt_i32_hl(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = icmp sgt i32 %5, %2  [path predicate of block %7, read from x before the rotation]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32_controlled(i32 %6, i32 %5, double %3)    ; IR: block %7: %8 = cq_theta_si32(%5, %3); %10 = phi [ %8, %7 ], [ %5, %4 ]  [Ry under the predicate, in place]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%10)  (%f is NOT uncomputed: x changed under it; the flag rail stays allocated)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %11
}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 5, 18, 16, 21, 4, 3, 2; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem).
; Checked: y + saved, saved = x * c, y = bump(saved) (measured); the cell `saved` = x * c (read from the bus at exit).
; Clean: the load copy of saved (%8, un-copied after the add: no memory version change follows it), the clone's result
; rail (%7, zeroed by the twin, then freed), and every rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register x (%5); the product x * c (%6: the value rail of the kept store `saved = x * c`, rule 5,
; sentence 3) and that store's tape slot (no handle: it is in the backend and holds the displaced `saved`); the result
; rail (%9, measured); the clone's tape rail and its tape field rail (never freed).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; A function-local `static` is a global with internal linkage (the casin shape: openlibm keeps `static double complex
; ca, ct, zz, z2;` and stores quantum values into them between calls to csqrt/clog, which is what stops -O1 from
; localizing them). ONE BUS (rule 20): the global lives at its host address, on the bus through the overlay; nothing is
; allocated, seeded or registered for it, it is not host-resident (it is not `isConstant()`), and nothing is known
; about it at compile time. `saved = x * c` is a KEPT bus store at the classical address `ptrtoint (ptr @saved to
; i64)` (rule 5, sentence 3: no _unc, its tape slot stays for the shot, and so does its value rail, the product, which
; is therefore no longer uncomputed). The callee is cloned for its quantum argument (rule 18); its printf is the output
; tape of example 47 (rule 16: one tape per function, the entry appended once). A format entry is no memory version
; change (rule 5), so bump does not write memory and keeps its twin; the twin recomputes the pure chain only (tape
; operations are write-once and are never replayed). The read back of `saved` after the call is a fresh bus load copy
; (rule 3: a rail, whatever the cell holds); its last reader is the add, and no memory version change follows, so it
; is un-copied right after the add (sentence 1) while the cells still hold what they held at the load. The call result
; is then zeroed by the twin, which reads the kept product as its argument.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]

  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %8, i32 %7)    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %7, %6  [result rail]  ; SPEC GAP: rule 6 'both operands dead' names a template result or an un-copied load copy as garbage; the clone result zeroed by its twin is read as such garbage too, so both operands are garbage and rule 6 has no trigger (198)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @static_global_slot.saved to i64))    ; IR: un-copy %7 (rule 5, sentence 1: its last reader is the add, no memory version change since the load)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_bump_1_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %9)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_si32(%8)
  ret i32 %10    ; IR: ret i32 %9
}

  %2 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the clone's output tape
  call void @cqrt_tape_fmt(i32 %2, ptr @.str)    ; IR: %2 = printf(@.str, %0): open the entry with its format string
  %3 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i32(i32 %2, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = printf(..., %0): field 0, a quantum value copied onto a fresh tape rail
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: %3 = add nsw i32 %0, 1

name: 68_nested_quantum_loops
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 14 (nested K-loops), 8, 7, 5.
; Checked: acc (the copied-out result %32 -> %66).
; Clean: every rail except a_K and the K rails b_K: every trip's values and intermediate predicates, popped and uncomputed
; by the mirror loops; a_0 through the guard compare; the |0> seed of acc (%62); the guard compare itself (%6).
; Kept: x (%4, the rotated register); the outer chain's last predicate a_K (%28 of outer trip K-1, popped as %36 on the first
; outer reverse trip); the K inner last predicates b_K (%22 of inner trip K-1 of each outer trip, popped as %38); the result
; %32 (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; A quantum-bounded loop nested inside a quantum-bounded loop, the k_rem_pio2 shape: this is example 05 composed with
; itself. -O1 made both loops bottom-tested (do-while) behind one guard x == 0. The outer loop runs K trips under the chain
; a_k (a_0 = NOT(x == 0), a_{k+1} = a_k & NOT(i - 1 == 0)); each outer trip runs an inner rolled loop of K trips under its
; own chain seeded from the outer predicate (b_0 = a_k, b_{m+1} = b_m & NOT(j + 1 == i)); the inner j is the classical trip
; index (it equals m whenever the trip is live), the outer i is quantum (it starts at x). Stack discipline: every inner trip
; pushes its handles, then the outer trip pushes its own (i, a_k, i - 1, the exit flag, the inner chain's final predicate).
; The reverse pops in stack order: an outer reverse trip pops its own handles, uncomputes them, then runs the inner reverse
; loop (popping the inner trips in reverse order); the pops match the pushes because the inner pushes of outer trip k sit
; above outer trip k's own pushes. This is not the exact gate mirror (forward ran the inner trips before the outer
; trip's i - 1, select, compare and a_{k+1}), and it need not be: rule 5 asks for dependency order, and those outer rails
; read only i and a_k, which the inner trips also only read, while no inner rail reads them; both groups' sources
; (i, a_k) stay live until the next reverse trip, so the two groups commute. K = 4 here; every literal K is tagged [K].
; Output rails (rule 14): the outer chain's last predicate a_K (a_K = 1 means the outer loop would have run past K trips) is
; kept allocated, neither uncomputed nor freed; the outer reverse loop skips its uncompute on reverse index 0 by a classical
; branch. Likewise each outer trip's inner chain keeps ITS last predicate b_K (pushed by the outer trip): K inner output
; rails in all, one per outer trip (b_K of a dead outer trip is |0>); the inner reverse loop skips the uncompute on reverse
; inner index K-1. Every other predicate is uncomputed as before; a_0 is uncomputed through the guard compare.

define i32 @nested_quantum_loops(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %8 / %10
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 0)    ; IR: %5 = icmp eq i32 %4, 0  [guard]
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of entering the outer loop = NOT %5
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %5
  call void @cqrt_xor_i1(i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: a_0 = NOT %5  (CNOT into the |0> rail)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket
  br label %8

8:
  %9 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %29, %24 ]    ; IR: outer trip index, bounded by K
  %10 = phi i32 [ %4, %3 ], [ %26, %24 ]    ; IR: %7 = phi i32 [ %13, %12 ], [ %4, %3 ]
  %11 = phi i32 [ %5, %3 ], [ %19, %24 ]    ; IR: %8 = phi i32 [ %19, %12 ], [ 0, %3 ]
  %12 = phi i32 [ %7, %3 ], [ %28, %24 ]    ; IR: predicate of this outer trip (a_k)
  br label %13    ; IR: br label %15

13:
  %14 = phi i32 [ 0, %8 ], [ %20, %13 ]    ; IR: %16 = phi i32 [ 0, %6 ], [ %20, %15 ]  (j: classical trip index)
  %15 = phi i32 [ %11, %8 ], [ %19, %13 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i32 [ %8, %6 ], [ %19, %15 ]
  %16 = phi i32 [ %12, %8 ], [ %22, %13 ]    ; IR: predicate of this inner trip (b_m; b_0 = a_k)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %15, i32 %2)    ; IR: %18 = mul i32 %17, %2
  %18 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 %14)    ; IR: %19 = add i32 %18, %16
  %19 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %16, i32 %18, i32 %15)    ; IR: next %17 / %8 = b_m ? %19 : %17
  %20 = add nuw i32 %14, 1    ; IR: %20 = add nuw i32 %16, 1  (classical)
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 %20)    ; IR: %21 = icmp eq i32 %20, %7  (commutative: quantum %7 in the _hl slot)
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next inner trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %21
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %16, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %21 not taken: b_{m+1} = b_m & NOT %21
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %15)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %16)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  %23 = icmp ult i32 %20, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %21, label %12, label %15  [K]
  br i1 %23, label %13, label %24

24:
  %25 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %10, i32 -1)    ; IR: %13 = add i32 %7, -1
  %26 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %12, i32 %25, i32 %10)    ; IR: next %7 = a_k ? %13 : %7
  %27 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %25, i32 0)    ; IR: %14 = icmp eq i32 %13, 0
  %28 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of the next outer trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %14
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %12, i32 %27, i32 %28)    ; IR: br i1 %14 not taken: a_{k+1} = a_k & NOT %14
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %27)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %10)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %12)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %25)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %27)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %22)    ; IR: the inner chain's final predicate b_K of this outer trip
  %29 = add nuw nsw i32 %9, 1
  %30 = icmp ult i32 %29, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %14, label %9, label %6  [K]
  br i1 %30, label %8, label %31

31:
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %10 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %19, %12 ]  [copied-out result]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %19, i32 %32)    ; IR: %10
  br label %33

33:
  %34 = phi i32 [ 0, %31 ], [ %63, %61 ]    ; IR: reverse outer trip index
  %35 = phi i32 [ %26, %31 ], [ %42, %61 ]    ; IR: %7 written by this outer trip
  %36 = phi i32 [ %28, %31 ], [ %41, %61 ]    ; IR: predicate of the next outer trip (a_{k+1})
  %37 = phi i32 [ %19, %31 ], [ %62, %61 ]    ; IR: acc after this outer trip
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %42 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %43 = icmp eq i32 %34, 0    ; IR: reverse index 0 is outer trip K-1: its a_{k+1} = a_K is an output rail (rule 14)
  br i1 %43, label %45, label %44

44:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %39)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %41, i32 %39, i32 %36)    ; IR: uncompute a_{k+1} (outer trips 0..K-2)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %39)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release a_{k+1} (|0>)
  br label %45

45:
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %35, i32 %41, i32 %40, i32 %42)    ; IR: uncompute next %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release next %7 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %39, i32 %40, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %14
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release %14 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %40, i32 %42, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %13
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release %13 (|0>)
  br label %46

46:
  %47 = phi i32 [ 3, %45 ], [ %59, %58 ]    ; IR: reverse inner trip index (K - 1 down to 0)  [K]
  %48 = phi i32 [ %38, %45 ], [ %51, %58 ]    ; IR: b_{m+1} of this inner trip
  %49 = phi i32 [ %37, %45 ], [ %54, %58 ]    ; IR: %17 / %8 written by this inner trip
  %50 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %51 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %52 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %53 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %54 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()
  %55 = add nuw i32 %47, 1    ; IR: %20 of this trip (classical)
  %56 = icmp eq i32 %47, 3    ; IR: reverse inner index K-1 is inner trip K-1: its b_{m+1} = b_K is an output rail (rule 14)  [K]
  br i1 %56, label %58, label %57

57:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %50)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %51, i32 %50, i32 %48)    ; IR: uncompute b_{m+1} (inner trips 0..K-2)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %50)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %48)    ; IR: release b_{m+1} (|0>)
  br label %58

58:
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %49, i32 %51, i32 %52, i32 %54)    ; IR: uncompute next %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %49)    ; IR: release next %17 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %50, i32 %42, i32 %55)    ; IR: uncompute %21
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %50)    ; IR: release %21 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %52, i32 %53, i32 %47)    ; IR: uncompute %19
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %52)    ; IR: release %19 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_hl_unc(i32 %53, i32 %54, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %53)    ; IR: release %18 (|0>)
  %59 = sub i32 %47, 1
  %60 = icmp sge i32 %59, 0
  br i1 %60, label %46, label %61

61:
  %62 = phi i32 [ %54, %58 ]    ; IR: acc at the start of this outer trip (the last popped %17 incoming)
  %63 = add nuw nsw i32 %34, 1
  %64 = icmp ult i32 %63, 4    ; IR: [K]
  br i1 %64, label %33, label %65

65:
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_xor_i1(i32 %6, i32 %41)    ; IR: uncompute a_0 (the last popped a_k is a_0)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %6)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; IR: release a_0 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 0)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release %5 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %62)    ; IR: release incoming 0 of phi %8 (never written, |0>)
  %66 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %32)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_ui32(%10)
  ret i32 %66    ; IR: ret i32 %11
}

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 26, 22, 20, 21, 18, 16, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2, 25; §1.4.
; Checked: creall(q) + cimagl(q), q = scale2(re + im*I) (measured): (re + im*0) * 2 + im * 2 in x87 extended
; arithmetic, re the rotated register; the cells of z's block and of the byval copy at exit (z.real = re + im*0 at
; offset 0, z.imag = im at offset 16, both blocks).
; Clean: the clone's two result rails (zeroed by the twin __cq_q_scale2_0_unc after their last consumer, the sum, then
; freed); every rail inside the clone and its twin (the two bus load copies of z.real and z.imag, un-copied after their
; templates' _unc, and the two fadd results).
; Kept: the user register re; by rule 5 the real part re + im*0 (the value rail of the kept f80 store into z.real), the
; seed im (the value rail of the kept store into z.imag), the tape slots of those two stores, the 32 byte load copies
; of the byval copy (each the value rail of a kept byte store) and the 32 tape slots of those byte stores; the sum
; (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, re, th, 1).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21, 26): on x86-64 a `long double complex` does not travel in registers: -O1 builds z in an
; `alloca { x86_fp80, x86_fp80 }` and passes it `byval`; the return comes back as the SSA aggregate
; { x86_fp80, x86_fp80 }. The alloca is BUS-RESIDENT (a store of a tainted value through it, and the call, are among
; its users), so it is __cq_alloc(32, 16) at its program point, no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped
; (rule 16). Its two stores are f80 bus stores (10 cells each, store size; the 6 padding bytes behind each are never
; touched) at the block's run-time address and at the untainted getelementptr + 16, which stays: the real part is the
; rail re + im*0, the imaginary part the classical im minted as a seed (rule 7). Both are kept stores (rule 5).
; THE BYVAL COPY (rules 26, 22): the caller makes the copy, a second block q = __cq_alloc(32, 16) and a bus copy of
; the 32 bytes of the byval type (padding included): one host loop of 32 qram_load_i8_hl at z's block, each byte rail
; pushed, then one host loop of 32 qram_store_i8_hl at q, popping, bytes 31 down to 0. Each byte store is kept with
; its value rail, the byte's load copy (rule 22). The call passes q as a plain ptr: no `byval` remains on it.
; THE CLONE (§1.4, rules 18, 26): the plain-ptr form of a function with a byval formal is spelled by the clone grammar
; even with the all-zero mask: q is a classical ptr, mask 0, so __cq_q_scale2_0(ptr). Nothing about the pointee
; crosses the call: the clone reads both fields from the bus at q and q + 16, and every load is a rail (rule 3), so
; z.imag, classical in C, is a rail inside the clone and both results are rails: the clone returns { i32, i32 }, each
; result copied into a fresh rail (rule 18), its SSA body uncomputed (the templates' _unc, then the load copies
; un-copied: no memory version change in the clone). The clone writes no memory, so it has a twin; its call is a
; load for rule 5: the twin runs after the results' last consumer, the caller's fadd, with no memory version change
; between, and the caller frees both result rails after it. scale2's own symbol is internal and has no caller left,
; so it is dropped (§1.4).
; SPEC GAP: rule 26 says the caller makes the byval copy but not at which program point; it is made immediately before
; the call (after z's two stores, which it must read).
; complex_long_double is externally visible and its address is never taken: by §5's example convention its clone-table
; row, _t clone, _t_ctl and their twins are omitted (the compiler emits them; they emit no gate and §6 does not compare
; them).

name: 71_extern_global_output
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20, 5 (Memory, sentence 3), 18, 9, 2; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem).
; Checked: r = body(x, k, &signflag) = x * x (measured, %5 -> %6); the cells of `signflag` at exit (read from the bus)
; hold select(x < k, -1, 1).
; Clean: inside the clone: the compare flag x < k (%4) and the product x * x (%6: copied out to %7, then uncomputed).
; Kept: the user register x (%4 of the caller: rotated); the result rail (%7 of the clone, %5 of the caller, measured,
; rule 2; body has no twin, rule 18); in the clone the sign rail
; select(x < k, -1, 1) (%5: the value rail of the kept store, rule 5 sentence 3) and the tape slot of the store
; `store i32 %4, ptr @signflag` (no handle: it holds the displaced content of `signflag`).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected for the driver extern_global_output(0, .5, 3) (analytic, not replayed): Ry(.5) flips each of the 32 bits of x
; independently with probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087; x = 0 (probability 0.132498) gives r = 0 and signflag = -1.
; The lgamma shape: lgamma(x) calls lgamma_r(x, &signgam) and signgam is an `extern int` with EXTERNAL linkage, readable
; by any translation unit and by the user after the call. -O1 promotes the pointer argument, so body stores straight
; into the global. ONE BUS (rule 20): `signflag` lives at its host address; nothing is allocated, seeded or registered
; for it, and the store is a bus store at the classical address `ptrtoint (ptr @signflag to i64)`. The clone accesses
; the bus, so it calls __cq_mem() once at its entry (§5); the caller makes no bus access. The store writes the VALUE of
; the sign into the four cells (they become QUANTUM, §1.3): it is a KEPT store (rule 5 sentence 3), no _unc exists, its
; tape slot stays for the shot and so does its value rail, the sign. A reader elsewhere loads the cells, never a handle.
; The sign is built by a select into a fresh rail (rule 9); its compare flag is uncomputed as usual (the sign rail no
; longer needs it). body writes memory (rule 5), so it has no twin (rule 18) and its result rail is KEPT by the caller;
; that result is measured anyway (as 51). The clone keeps -O1's `internal fastcc` (§1.4) and its mask 10 (arg 0 quantum).
source_filename = "extern_global_output.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@signflag = local_unnamed_addr global i32 0, align 4    ; IR: @signflag  (external linkage: lives at its host address on the bus, nothing allocated for it)

define i32 @extern_global_output(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_body_10(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = call @body(%4, %2), quantum clone (arg 0 quantum; a memory version change: body writes memory, no twin)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %6 = cq_measure_si32(%5)
  ret i32 %6    ; IR: ret i32 %6
}

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_body_10(i32 %0, i32 %1) unnamed_addr {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus m (§5: once, at function entry)
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: %3 = icmp slt i32 %0, %1
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_ll(i32 %4, i32 -1, i32 1)    ; IR: %4 = select i1 %3, i32 -1, i32 1  [the sign, a fresh rail]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %3, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @signflag to i64), i32 %5)    ; IR: store i32 %4, ptr @signflag  (a kept store at a classical address: its tape slot and its value rail %4 stay, no _unc)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %3 (the sign rail does not depend on the flag any more)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %5 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (the same rail in both operand slots)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %6, i32 %7)    ; IR: copy the result out
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %6, i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %5
}
