name: 72_memset_array
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 22, 20, 21, 16, 14, 5, 7, 4, 2.
; Checked: memset_over_quantum: before + a[1] (the add rail, measured), before = a[k & 3] read before the memset;
; memset_quantum_byte: b[0] + b[3] (the add rail, measured). The cells of the two blocks are not named outputs.
; Clean: memset_over_quantum: the address chain of &a[x & 3] (x & 3, its zext, the scaled index, the address rail),
; each uncomputed by its template's _unc right after the store and freed; the load copy a[1], un-copied after the add,
; before the measurement (no memory version change lies between the load and its _unc) and freed; the load copy
; before = a[k & 3], un-copied after the add, its last reader, and left allocated (rule 5 sentence 1: the memset, a
; memory version change, lies between the load and that point).
; memset_quantum_byte: the address chain of &b[y & 3] (y & 3, its zext, the address rail; size 1, no scale),
; uncomputed right after the store and freed; the load copies b[0] and b[3] and their zexts, uncomputed after the add,
; before the measurement, and freed.
; Kept: memset_over_quantum: x (rotated register); the four fill-value rails x + i (each the value rail of its trip's
; kept store, rule 5); the i8 seed 0 (the value rail of the memset's 16
; kept byte stores, rules 7, 22); the i32 seed c (the value rail of the store a[x & 3] = c); the tape slots of the 4
; fill stores, the 16 memset byte stores and the quantum-address store (rule 5); the sum (measured).
; memset_quantum_byte: x and y (rotated registers); the fill byte rail (char)x (the value rail of the memset's 4 kept
; byte stores, rule 22); the i8 seed 7 (value rail of the store b[y & 3] = 7); the tape slots of the 4 memset byte
; stores and of the quantum-address store; the sum (measured).
; Rotations: memset_over_quantum: (Ry, x, th, 1). memset_quantum_byte: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21): a[] and b[] are written at a QUANTUM address (a[x & 3] = c, b[y & 3] = 7: a getelementptr with
; a tainted index) and take quantum values, so each alloca is BUS-RESIDENT: __cq_alloc(size, align) at its program
; point, one zeroed block, no alloca remains, and the lifetime markers emit nothing (rule 16). m = __cq_mem() once at
; function entry (§5). Every access is ONE bus call at the run-time address: _hl with the classical i64 (ptrtoint of
; the block or of a getelementptr that stays because nothing in it is tainted), the plain form with a 64-bit address
; rail (x & 3, zext as -O1 wrote it, mul_i64_hl by the element size, add_i64_hl of the classical base). Every load is a
; bus load whose result is a rail; every store is a KEPT store (rule 5 sentence 3: no pop, the tape slot and the value
; rail stay; a classical value is first a seed, rule 7).
; MEMSET (rule 22): llvm.memset is ONE host loop of n byte stores qram_store_i8_hl at the classical addresses
; base + j of ONE i8 value rail, never unrolled although n is a constant (16 for a[], 4 for b[]), never widened into
; word stores, and emitted although the __cq_alloc block is already zero (memset_over_quantum's fill 0: the seed
; alloc_i8(0)); memset_quantum_byte's fill is the quantum rail trunc (char)x, kept with its stores.
; THE FILL LOOP (rule 14, classical bound): it stays the classical loop. Trip i's only rail, x + i, is the value rail of
; a kept store and is kept, so nothing is pushed and there is no reverse loop (as 204).
; before = a[k & 3] is a bus load at a classical address taken before the memset: it is un-copied after the add, its
; last reader, and stays allocated, not freed (rule 5 sentence 1: overtaken by the memset). a[1] is loaded after the quantum-address store and un-copied before the
; measurement. A load copy is never cleaned by rule 6, so the add's operands are not cleaned by it.
source_filename = "memset_array.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  br label %9    ; IR: llvm.lifetime.start(16, %5) dropped (rule 16); br label %19

  %13 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %6, i64 0, i64 %10    ; IR: %23 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %5, i64 0, i64 %20  (nothing tainted: the getelementptr stays)

  %15 = add nuw nsw i64 %10, 1    ; IR: %24 = add nuw nsw i64 %20, 1  (classical)
  %16 = icmp eq i64 %15, 4    ; IR: %25 = icmp eq i64 %24, 4  (classical bound)

  %20 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %6, i64 0, i64 %19    ; IR: %10 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %5, i64 0, i64 %9  (nothing tainted: stays)

  %32 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %31, i64 4)    ; IR: %14 = getelementptr inbounds [4 x i32], ptr %5, i64 0, i64 %13  [the tainted index scaled by the element size (rule 20)]
  %33 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %32, i64 %7)    ; IR: %14: plus the classical base address  [the address rail of &a[x & 3]]
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %14: the classical value c as a seed (rule 7), kept with its store
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32(i32 %5, i32 %33, i32 %34)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %14: a[x & 3] = c  [kept store at an address rail (rule 5)]
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_hl_unc(i32 %33, i32 %32, i64 %7)    ; IR: uncompute %14  [the address rail: a template result, uncomputed after the store (rule 5)]

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 14, 16, 20, 21, 3, 7; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc).
; Checked: a[x % n] (the load copy at the address rail, %28, measured -> %29); the cells of the block on the bus at
; exit: a[i] = i * c, 0 <= i < n.
; Clean: the address chain of &a[x % n]: the index rail x % n (%24), its zext to i64 (%25), the scaled index (%26) and
; the address rail (%27), uncomputed and freed right after the load (the load copy is measured, so the load is the
; address rail's last reader, rule 20).
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register: urem is no bijection, so rule 6 has no trigger); rule 5 sentence 3, per fill
; trip: the tape slot of the store a[i] = i * c (it holds the displaced zero bytes of the block) and its value rail,
; the seed alloc_i32(i * c) (%20, rule 7; classical-valued, so no qubit, §0); the load copy a[x % n] (%28, measured,
; rule 2).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Driver vla_array(0, .5, 5, 3): Ry(.5) flips each of the 32 bits of x0 = 0 with probability s = sin^2(.25) =
; 0.061209, independently. The cells are a = {0, 3, 6, 9, 12} and the measured value is 3*(x mod 5): 0 with
; probability 0.263952 (x = 0 alone contributes (1 - s)^32 = 0.132498), and 3, 6, 9, 12 with 0.184012 each.
; ONE BUS (rules 16, 20, 21). The VLA's users are the fill loop's stores through a getelementptr with an untainted index
; and the load through a getelementptr with the TAINTED index x % n: that user is none rule 20 (b) allows, so the alloca
; is BUS-RESIDENT. It is __cq_alloc(n * 4, 16) at the alloca's program point (rule 16: a variable-length alloca alike;
; the alignment is the alloca's 16; zeroed host memory at an address never reused, its size in the 8 bytes before it),
; and no alloca remains. The size is classical (n is a parameter), so no K2 and no overflow predicate. At -O1 a VLA at
; function scope has no llvm.stacksave/stackrestore; inside a loop or a block they would be dropped (rule 16). m =
; __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). Nothing is known about the block at compile time: its base is its run-time
; address, a classical i64.
; The fill loop has a classical bound (rule 14) and classical contents. Its getelementptr has an untainted index and
; stays; the store's address is its ptrtoint, and every store is a bus store: cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl of the seed
; alloc_i32(i * c) (a store's value is always a handle). Each is a KEPT store (rule 5 sentence 3): its tape slot and its
; seed stay for the shot, so no trip rail is pushed and there is no reverse loop. Value, address and control are all
; classical-valued, so the stores write the host bytes and the cells stay HOST (§1.3).
; The quantum-index read is ONE bus load at an ADDRESS RAIL (rule 20; QROM is retired): urem_i32_hl(x, n) is the index
; rail, -O1's zext to i64 is the zext template, the getelementptr is mul_i64_hl by the element size 4 and add_i64_hl of
; the classical base, and qram_load_i32 reads the 4 cells at that address. No index is narrowed, bounded or checked
; (rule 21): for n > 0, x % n lies in [0, n) and the load reads a cell the fill loop wrote. n == 0 is undefined
; behaviour in C; the lowering is total all the same: urem(x, 0) = x (§2), the block has size 0, and the load reads
; whatever the bus holds at base + 4x (§2: an unreadable HOST cell reads 0, never a fault). The load copy is measured,
; so it is never un-copied (rule 5 sentence 1); the address chain is template garbage, uncomputed in reverse order
; right after the load and before the measurement.

; of a on the bus at exit: a[i] = (i == (x & 3)) ? 2y + i : y + i, mod 2^32.
; Clean: the address chain of a[x & 3] (x & 3 %16, its zext %17, the scaled index %18, the address rail %19),
; uncomputed after the second swap of the in-place form; the in-place form's rails (the swapped-out old a[x & 3] %20,
; cleaned by rule 6 through the inverse t = sum - y %22; the sum rail %21, |0> after the swap-in); the four
; fixed-address load copies (%23, %24, %26, %28, un-copied: no memory version change follows them) and the two inner
; xors (%25, %27).
; Kept: the user registers x and y (%8, %9; y is also the value rail of the kept store a[0] = y). Rule 5 sentence 3:
; the tape slots of the four initializer stores and their value rails y + 1, y + 2, y + 3 (%11, %13, %15). The result
; rail (%29, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, tx, 1); (Ry, y, ty, 1).
; ONE BUS (rule 20): the alloca is BUS-RESIDENT (a tainted value is stored through it and a getelementptr with a
; tainted index reaches it), so no alloca remains: its block is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at the alloca's program point (rule
; 16) and both lifetime markers are dropped. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry. Nothing is known about an address
; at compile time: the base is the block's run-time address, a classical i64 (ptrtoint), and the constant-offset geps
; are classical i64 adds. The initializer is four kept i32 stores at classical addresses (qram_store_i32_hl): no _unc
; exists, the tape slots stay, and so do the value rails (y, and the template results y + 1, y + 2, y + 3, which are
; therefore no longer uncomputed).
; THE READ-MODIFY-WRITE (rules 5 and 6, "a memory cell"): `a[x & 3] += y` is load %16, add, store %16 on the same SSA
; pointer with no memory version change between them, and the add is a rule-6 bijection in the loaded value, so it is
; the in-place form at the address rail: the gep with the tainted index is 64-bit template arithmetic (-O1's zext,
; mul_i64_hl by 4, add_i64_hl of the run-time base), then at the store's position a |0> rail is swapped with the four
; cells (qram_swap_i32), the sum is computed into a fresh rail, the old value is cleaned by rule 6 (t = sum - y,
; copy, un-t), the sum rail is swapped into the cells, and the rail that receives the cells' |0> is freed. No copy, no
; tape slot and no old value remains. The address rail is template garbage, uncomputed after the second swap.
; THE FIXED-ADDRESS LOADS: four qram_load_i32_hl at the classical addresses of a[0..3], copy-outs into fresh rails;
; the xors go into fresh rails. No memory version change follows the loads, so each copy is un-copied (its _unc, same
; arguments) after its last reader and that reader's uncompute where it has one (a[3]'s reader is the measured result,
; which has none), before the measurement: the inner xors first, then the
; copies of a[3], a[2], a[1], a[0]. The end of a's lifetime undoes nothing (rule 20).

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 20 (witness: a classical table read at a quantum index is a bus load at an address rail; no
; QROM), 21, 5, 4, 3, 2.
; Checked: p[x & 7].v + p[x & 7].k, the returned double (the fadd rail %15 -> %16).
; Clean: the index rail x & 7 (%7), its zext (%8), the scaled index (%9), the two address rails (%10 = &p[x & 7] for k,
; %11 = &p[x & 7].v for v), the two load copies (%12 for v, %13 for k) and the sitofp of k (%14), uncomputed in LIFO
; order and freed before the measurement.
; Kept: x (%6, the rotated register) and the sum (%15, measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected for the driver array_of_structs(0, .5, P8): element i holds k = i + 1, v = i + .5, so the sum is 2i + 1.5 at
; i = x & 7.
; ONE BUS (rule 20): nothing is known about an address, so the classical table behind the parameter p is not told apart
; from any other memory: its cells are HOST and each load reads the host bytes at the access (§1.3); nothing is
; allocated, seeded or registered for it. p is not a constant global or an alloca, so it is not host-resident, and the
; index is a rail anyway. No QROM exists.
; ADDRESS ARITHMETIC (rules 20, 21): the classical base is p's run-time address, ptrtoint of the argument, placed once
; at function entry after __cq_mem() (as 206). -O1's zext of the index to i64 is a tainted cast and is the zext
; template. The getelementptr %struct.P (size 16) is mul_i64_hl(., 16) and add_i64_hl(., p): the address rail of
; p[x & 7], which is also the address of field k (offset 0). The getelementptr i8 (+8) has a tainted base and only a
; constant offset: add_i64_hl(., 8), no scale, the address rail of field v. Each getelementptr emits its own template;
; the struct layout enters only as the stride 16 and the byte offset 8 that -O1 already wrote. No index is narrowed,
; bounded or checked. -O1 reads v before k; the lowering keeps that order: ONE qram_load_f64 at the v rail and ONE
; qram_load_i32 at the k rail (rule 20: one call per access of store-size S cells, 8 and 4).
; UNCOMPUTE (rule 5 sentence 1): no memory version change follows the loads, and their last reader, the fadd (through
; the sitofp for k), is measured and never uncomputed, so both copies are un-copied right after the sitofp's _unc,
; before the measurement, while the cells still hold what was loaded; each address rail outlives its load's _unc
; (rule 20), the v rail before the k rail it was computed from, then the scale, the zext and the and.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: fenv_rounding: w + (double)m, w = ((x * c) + c) * c under the three modes, m the quantum mode;
; quantum_mode_classical_op: s = a + b rounded under the quantum mode (measured).
; Clean: fenv_rounding: the product y, the compare flag, the sum z; quantum_mode_classical_op: the compare flag and
; the mode rail.
; Kept: the user register x of each function; fenv_rounding's mode rail (measured as m) and result rail w;
; quantum_mode_classical_op's result rail s.
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; Full floating-point environment, part 1 of 3: the ROUNDING MODE (rule 23). Under `#pragma STDC FENV_ACCESS ON`
; clang -O1 emits llvm.experimental.constrained.* with round.dynamic: every such op reads the current mode. The fenv
; is program state (as the escaping global of 71), split in two: the HOST part, kept exactly by the real fenv calls
; for classical ops, and the QUANTUM part, the mode and flags as rails. The mode is classical (an i32 value the
; compiler tracks: the last classical fesetround argument, or fegetround() at entry) until a quantum value is written
; into it; then it is a handle and no host call is made. Template grammar (§1.2), one rule for all three fenv
; examples: cq_template_<op>[_<pred>]_<W>[_hl|_lh|_ll][_rm|_rmq][_exc][_unc]
;   _rm  = the mode is a classical i32 operand, last; _rmq = the mode is a handle, last; _exc = see example 81.
; A constrained op whose operands are all classical but whose mode is quantum is QUANTUM (its result depends on the
; mode): quantum_mode_classical_op shows it, `a + b` becomes cq_template_fadd_f64_ll_rmq. fegetround() under a quantum
; mode returns the mode handle itself. fpexcept.ignore here (`#pragma clang fp exceptions(ignore)`): no exception
; bits; 81 has them. Mode constants are the x86-64 host's: FE_TONEAREST 0, FE_DOWNWARD 1024, FE_UPWARD 2048,
; FE_TOWARDZERO 3072.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 23, 18, 26, 5.
; Checked: inexact (%17 -> %31) and w (%27 -> %32), summed classically.
; Clean: every dropped flags rail (the held flags %14 after feupdateenv, scale's returned flags %23 after fesetexceptflag,
; the FE_UPWARD flags %29 after fesetenv), the exception-bit rails %11 and %28, the quantum part of inexact's test (%16),
; p (%10), y (%13), scale's result rail %22, and inside the clone its whole chain.
; Kept: x (%8, the rotated register); the final flags rail %19 (restored | held, an output of rule 23, never freed);
; inexact (%17) and w (%27), measured.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Full floating-point environment, part 3 of 3: SAVED ENVIRONMENTS and CALLS. Mode and flags are split into a host part
; and a quantum part as in 80 and 81. A fenv_t or fexcept_t object keeps its host part through the real calls on the real
; alloca; its quantum part (the flags rail, and the mode when it is a handle) is known statically at every fenv call, so it
; is carried as SSA values exactly as -O1 carries a promoted slot (an object that escapes or is written in a loop is a
; classical slot of handles, as 31/70). feholdexcept(&env): save {mode, flags}, clear the flags (the rail becomes empty).
; feupdateenv: restore the saved part, then OR the current flags in. fegetexceptflag/fesetexceptflag(FE_ALL_EXCEPT): save /
; reinstate the flags handle itself (a narrower mask would and/or it). fegetenv/fesetenv: save / reinstate both. A flags
; rail that stops being current state (dropped by fesetexceptflag or fesetenv) is uncomputed; the final one is an output
; and stays. CALLS: a clone of a function that does constrained FP work takes the caller's mode (literal or handle) and
; quantum flags handle as two trailing parameters and returns { result, flags' } (the aggregate ABI of 64), BOTH copied
; into fresh rails before the body is uncomputed (rule 18); its _unc twin takes both returned handles first, then the same
; operands, and zeroes both; the caller frees both after the twin. scale's v * c + c is a constrained llvm.fmuladd, which is

name: 84_multi_origin_pointer
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 5, 9, 8, 7, 16, 4, 2.
; Checked: a[0] + b[1], the returned sum (the add rail %26 -> %27). The store reaches a[0] iff B and x & 1 == 1 and
; (x >> 1) & 1 == 0, b[1] iff B and x & 1 == 0 and (x >> 1) & 1 == 1 (B = x > 5; a[1] and b[0] are not read), so the sum
; is 1 + 4 = 5, v + 4 or 1 + v.
; Clean: the arm's pure chain: x & 1 (%13), the flag (x & 1) == 0 (%14), the address rail p = select(flag, b, a) (%15),
; x >> 1 (%16), the index (%17) and the gep chain zext / mul / add (%18..%20), all uncomputed and freed right after the
; store, their last reader (rule 20); the two fixed-address load copies a[0] and b[1] (%22, %25), un-copied after the add
; (no memory version change follows them, rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: x (%9, the rotated register); the sum (%26, measured); the predicate B = x > 5 (%12), the control rail of the
; kept store (rules 5, 8); the seed v (%21, the value rail of the kept store); the seeds 8589934593 and 17179869187
; (%10, %11, the value rails of the two kept initializer stores, rule 7); the tape slots of the three stores (store i64
; 8589934593, ptr %4; store i64 17179869187, ptr %5; store i32 %2, ptr %15).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; ONE BUS (rules 20, 21). Both allocas are BUS-RESIDENT: a select of their addresses under a quantum flag is among
; their users, which no clause of rule 20 (b) allows. So each is __cq_alloc(8, 8) at its program point (rule 16), no
; alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped; m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry (§5). The initializers
; are the -O1 i64 stores, each ONE qram_store_i64_hl at the block's classical run-time address, its value the seed
; alloc_i64(lit) (rules 7, 20); every value, address and control is classical-valued, so the cells stay HOST.
; A POINTER IS AN INTEGER (rule 21): p = (x & 1) ? a : b is select_i64_ll on the quantum flag (IR %10, lowered %14) over the two blocks'
; classical i64 addresses, ONE 64-bit address rail; nothing about a, b, objects or origins belongs to it. The arm's
; pure code is hoisted and computed unguarded (rule 9): the index chain and the gep, 64-bit template arithmetic into an
; address rail (rule 20): -O1's zext to i64, mul_i64_hl by the element size 4, add_i64 of the address rail p (a rail,
; so no _hl). The store p[(x >> 1) & 1] = v is ONE bus access, qram_store_i32_controlled under the block predicate B
; (rule 5: a bus access is never hoisted), with no guard per origin and no bounds check (rule 21); the classical v is
; first the seed alloc_i32(v). The store is KEPT: its tape slot, its value rail and its control rail B stay (rule 5
; sentence 3, rule 8), so B is never uncomputed. The address rail and its whole chain are template garbage, uncomputed
; right after the store. After the join no quantum predicate is in scope: a[0] and b[1] are plain bus loads at the
; classical addresses a and b + 4 (qram_load_i32_hl; &b[1] is the untainted gep, which stays, and its ptrtoint, %23 and
; %24, rule 20), un-copied by their _unc after the add, their last reader.

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 18, 9, 8, 5, 4, 2, 7, 16; §1.3, §1.4.
; Checked: r = p ? *p : -1 with p = pick(a, x) (the merge rail, measured): x & 1 ? a0 + ((x >> 1) & 3) : -1; the
; cells of a at exit: a[i] = a0 + i (only the initializer stores them). For the driver ptr_return(0, .5, 7) (Ry(.5)
; on every bit of x, a bit flips with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209): r = -1 with 0.938791, 7 with 0.053945, 8 and 9 with
; 0.003517 each, 10 with 0.000229.
; Clean: the address rail p that __cq_q_pick_01 returned, zeroed by its twin __cq_q_pick_01_unc after its last reader
; (the NULL flag's _unc, after the load's _unc) and freed; the NULL flag p == 0; the load copy *p, un-copied under its X-bracketed control right
; after the merge (no memory version change since the load) and freed; every rail inside the clone and its twin.
; Kept: the user register x; the merge rail r (measured); by rule 5 the tape slots of the four initializer stores
; and their value seeds (i32 a0, a0 + 1, a0 + 2, a0 + 3; classical-valued, no qubit, §0).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; A POINTER IS ITS ADDRESS (rule 21): pick returns a pointer computed from the rail k, so it is ONE i32 handle to a
; 64-bit address rail. Inside the clone the gep with a tainted index is rule 20's 64-bit template arithmetic: -O1's
; zext nneg to i64, mul_i64_hl by the element size 4, add_i64_hl of the classical run-time address of the pointer
; formal; the NULL arm of the select is the literal 0 (select_i64_lh). The pointer formal a is classical at the call,
; so the mask over pick's two scalar formals (ptr a, i32 k) is 01: __cq_q_pick_01(ptr, i32); nothing about the
; pointee crosses the call (§1.4, rule 18). pick has no bus access, so its twin exists and the caller runs it after the
; address rail's last reader. pick's own symbol has no caller left and is dropped (§1.4).
; Caller: the NULL test is icmp_eq_i64_hl(p, 0) (rule 21: null is the literal 0), a tainted br and so a flag (rule 8).
; The load *p sits on the flag's FALSE edge: it is ONE bus access at the address rail (rule 20), never hoisted, the
; _controlled form under NOT flag, an X bracket (not_i1) around it (rules 8, 9); under flag = 1 nothing is touched and
; the copy stays |0>. There is no object, guard, tag or bound: an address is not resolved at compile time (§0). The
; phi is one select_i32_lh(flag, -1, copy) (rule 9). The copy is un-copied by the _controlled_unc inside the same X
; bracket (rule 5).
; THE ALLOCA IS BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b)): a is passed to a call, a user that is not in the host-resident list, so it
; is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at its program point, no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Its

; bytes (§1.3). The constant geps &a[1..3] stay (nothing tainted) and are spelled ptrtoint for the _hl address.
; Everything else is uncomputed in reverse.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 22, 16, 7, 5, 4, 3, 2; §1.3.
; Checked: ptrdiff_q: q - p in elements (%11 -> %12). ptr_less: p < q, the unsigned compare of the two addresses
; (%21 -> %22 -> %23). ptr_eq_two_objects: p == q, the equality of the two addresses (%36 -> %37 -> %38); the 32 cells
; of a and b at exit, all 0 (HOST cells: every memset store is classical-valued, so it writes the host byte, §1.3).
; Clean: every rail but the registers, the result rails and what rule 5 keeps: the byte-offset chains of ptrdiff_q
; (%5..%10); in ptr_less the condition chain (%8, %9), the base address rail select(flag, b, a) (%10), the index chains
; with their widened and scaled forms (%11..%14, %16..%19), the address rails p (%15) and q (%20) and the compare %21;
; in ptr_eq_two_objects the same chains (%23..%35) and the compare %36; all uncomputed in LIFO order after the
; result's zext, before the measurement, and freed.
; Kept: the register x of each function (%4 / %7 / %8, rotated) and each result rail (measured); in
; ptr_eq_two_objects by rule 5 (rules 7, 22): the seed i8 0 of a's memset (%9) with the 16 tape slots of its byte
; stores, and the seed i8 0 of b's memset (%16) with the 16 tape slots of its byte stores.
; Rotations: ptrdiff_q: (Ry, x, th, 1). ptr_less: (Ry, x, th, 1). ptr_eq_two_objects: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; A POINTER IS AN INTEGER, ITS ADDRESS (rule 21): a classical ptr/i64 or ONE 64-bit address rail. Three shapes.
; ptrdiff_q: -O1 already folds p = a + i, q = a + j, q - p into integer IR (p's byte offset (x & 3) * 4 = %6, q's byte
; offset ((x >> 2) & 3) * 4 = %8, sub, ashr exact by the stride); no pointer survives, so that IR is lowered as the
; integer ops it is (the readnone ptr parameter is unused).
; ptr_less: p = ((x & 1) ? a : b) + ((x >> 1) & 3) is a pointer select under a quantum flag, select_i64_ll of the two
; classical run-time addresses (rule 21 Merge: both incomings classical, entering as their i64 values, the ptrtoint of
; the parameters at function entry), then rule 20's address arithmetic for the gep with a tainted index: the zext -O1
; wrote, mul_i64_hl by the element size 4, add_i64 to the base rail. q = a + ((x >> 3) & 3) is the same arithmetic on a
; classical base: add_i64_hl with a's address as the literal. icmp ult on pointers is icmp_ult_i64 of the two address
; rails (rule 21 Compare). a and b may alias; nothing about them is asked: the compare is of addresses only.
; ptr_eq_two_objects: a and b are local arrays whose addresses are selected under a quantum flag and indexed by a rail,
; so both allocas are BUS-RESIDENT (rule 20 (b): a select and a gep with a tainted index are not among the
; host-resident users): each is __cq_alloc(16, 16) at its program point (one zeroed block, an address never reused),
; no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Each memset is rule 22's host loop of 16 kept byte
; stores of one i8 seed at the classical addresses base + j; it is emitted although the block is already zero (§0).
; The pointers p and q are built exactly as in ptr_less, and icmp eq on pointers is icmp_eq_i64 of the two address
; rails: at run time p (in b's block) never equals q (in a's block) because the blocks are distinct, which the
; addresses decide with no compile-time knowledge of objects. No pointer is dereferenced, so no bus load occurs.

name: 87_pointer_induction
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 14 (re-rolled; a_K kept), 16, 5, 8, 9, 4, 7, 2.
; Checked: n = the number of leading nonzero bytes of s = {c, c + 1, c ^ 3, 0}, over at most K = 4 trips (measured
; through the copied-out rail %32 -> %47); the cells of s at exit, read from the bus at the block's address:
; {c, c + 1, c ^ 3, 0}.
; Clean: every trip's load copy *p (%20, un-copied by the reverse loop under the control it was loaded with: no memory
; version change follows the initializer stores), its flag (%21), n + 1 (%23), the select merge of n (%24) and the trip
; predicate a_0..a_{K-1} (%22, uncomputed by the reverse loop: a_{K-1} enters it through %36, a_0..a_{K-2} are popped
; as %40; a_K is a separate kept rail); the after-trip-K exit test (its
; load %29 and flag %30, undone at once); the |1> seed (%14) and the |0> seed of n (%13) (rule 7).
; Kept: the user register c (%6, also the value rail of the kept store s[0]); the value rails of the other three kept
; stores (rule 5 sentence 3): c + 1 (%7), c ^ 3 (%9) and the seed of the literal 0 (%11; rule 7, a basis state, no
; qubit); the four stores' tape slots (backend rails); the copied-out result rail (%32, measured); a_K (%31: the exit
; test *p != 0 evaluated after the K-th body, ANDed with trip K's predicate; rule 14: a_K = 1 iff the loop would run
; a (K+1)-th trip, which is observable; a loop that exits after exactly K trips reads 0). No range fact bounds the
; trip count (it depends on memory contents; the array's extent and the inbounds gep are never a bound, rule 21), so
; the cutoff is K and a_K is kept.
; Rotations: (Ry, c, th, 1).
; Expected: count_nonzero(0, .5). Ry(.5) flips each of the 8 bits of c with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209 and everything
; after it is a basis permutation, so n is distributed as the C program on the flipped c: c = 0 gives n = 0
; (0.603326), c = 255 gives n = 1 (s[1] = 0; 1.97e-10), c = 3 gives n = 2 (s[2] = 0; 0.002565), every other c n = 3
; (0.394109, s[3] = 0 stops it). n never reaches K, so a_K = 0 on every branch.
; A POINTER AS THE LOOP INDUCTION of a rolled loop whose exit depends on quantum data (rules 21, 14). ONE BUS (rule 20):
; the alloca s is BUS-RESIDENT, because a store through it of a tainted value (s[0] = c) is among its users, so no
; alloca remains: its block is __cq_alloc(4, 1) at the alloca's program point (rule 16, zeroed) and the lifetime
; markers are dropped. m = __cq_mem() is called once, at entry. The block's run-time address is a classical i64
; (rule 21) and every address below is that i64 plus a classical offset: nothing is known about what it points to.
; THE INITIALIZER: four bus stores at the classical addresses s + 0..3, in program order (two bus accesses never
; commute, rule 5), each ONE qram_store_i8_hl whose value is always a handle: the register c itself, the template
; results c + 1 and c ^ 3, and for s[3] = 0 the seed alloc_i8(0) (rules 7, 20; the store is emitted although the
; fresh block already holds 0: that is never asked, §0). Every store is KEPT (rule 5 sentence 3): no pop, its tape
; slot and its value rail stay, so c + 1 and c ^ 3 are never uncomputed. The s[3] store has classical-valued address,
; value and control, so it writes the host byte and that cell stays HOST (§1.3).
; THE POINTER p: -O1 carries it as phi ptr [s, +1]. Its SCEV is {s,+,1}: a loop-invariant classical start and an
; unconditional classical step, so it is an AFFINE INDUCTION (rule 14) and is NOT carried: in trip j it is the
; classical i64 s + j, recomputed from the trip index in the forward and in the reverse loop (arithmetic without
; inbounds/nuw/nsw) and never pushed. Its exit value is never read after the loop, so no carried address rail
; exists. Every *p is therefore an _hl access at a classical address.
; Re-rolled (rule 14): -O1's pre-header test *s != 0 is the latch test *(p + 1) != 0 one trip earlier (the same i8
; load at the SCEV-equal address s, no memory version change between the guard and the loop header), so it is trip
; 0. Trip j loads *p = s[j] (ONE cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_controlled, copy-out, cells preserved) under the predicate of
; REACHING its test (a_{j-1}; the |1> seed for trip 0): a trip C would not run touches no cell and no host byte. It
; tests the copy and forms a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT(*p == 0) (the IR's flag is the exit edge, so the conjunction sits in
; an X bracket, rule 8); n++ is select-merged on a_j (rule 9; the arm's pure add runs unguarded). The literal 4 is K
; [K]. After trip K the exit test is evaluated once more at s + K under a_{K-1} (one cell past the block, read only on
; the branch where C reads it too; no bound is checked, rule 21; it reads 0 by §2 or whatever the address holds) and
; a_K = a_{K-1} & NOT(*p == 0) is kept; that load and flag are undone at once. After n is copied out the reverse loop
; pops each trip and uncomputes it, the load's controlled _unc un-copying against the preserved cell at the address
; recomputed from the trip index. Nothing is popped or freed for the block: a store is never popped and a block is
; never freed (rules 5, 16).

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"

define i32 @count_nonzero(i8 noundef zeroext %0, double noundef %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; the bus M, once at function entry
  %4 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 4, i64 1)    ; IR: %3 = alloca [4 x i8], align 1  [bus-resident (a tainted value is stored through it): one zeroed block, no alloca remains (rules 16, 20)]
  %5 = ptrtoint ptr %4 to i64    ; the block's run-time address s, a classical i64 (rule 21)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [register c]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i8(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [Ry]; llvm.lifetime.start(4, %3) dropped (rule 16)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i64 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: store i8 %4, ptr %3: s[0] = c  [kept store at a classical address; the value rail is the register c]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i8_hl(i32 %6, i8 1)    ; IR: %5 = add i8 %4, 1
  %8 = add i64 %5, 1    ; IR: %6 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %3, i64 1  (classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i64 %8, i32 %7)    ; IR: store i8 %5, ptr %6: s[1] = c + 1  [kept store; %5's rail is its value rail, KEPT]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_xor_i8_hl(i32 %6, i8 3)    ; IR: %7 = xor i8 %4, 3
  %10 = add i64 %5, 2    ; IR: %8 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %3, i64 2  (classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i64 %10, i32 %9)    ; IR: store i8 %7, ptr %8: s[2] = c ^ 3  [kept store; %7's rail is its value rail, KEPT]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 0)    ; IR: store i8 0, ptr %9  [the seed of the literal 0: the store's value rail, KEPT with it (rules 5, 7)]
  %12 = add i64 %5, 3    ; IR: %9 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %3, i64 3  (classical)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %3, i64 %12, i32 %11)    ; IR: store i8 0, ptr %9: s[3] = 0  [kept store; classical-valued, so the host byte is written and the cell stays HOST]
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: incoming 0 of phi %17 / %13
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: predicate of reaching the loop guard in %2 (always 1)
  br label %15

15:
  %16 = phi i64 [ 0, %2 ], [ %25, %15 ]    ; IR: trip index j, bounded by K; p = s + j (%16 = phi ptr: an affine induction, not carried)  [K]
  %17 = phi i32 [ %13, %2 ], [ %24, %15 ]    ; IR: %17 = phi i32 [ %18, %15 ], [ 0, %2 ]
  %18 = phi i32 [ %14, %2 ], [ %22, %15 ]    ; IR: predicate of reaching this trip's test
  %19 = add i64 %5, %16    ; IR: p: %3 (trip 0) / %19 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %16, i64 1  [the classical address s + j]
  %20 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_controlled(i32 %18, i32 %3, i64 %19)    ; IR: %10 = load i8, ptr %3 (trip 0) / %20 = load i8, ptr %19: *p, ONE bus access under the predicate of reaching the test
  %21 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl(i32 %20, i8 0)    ; IR: %11 = icmp eq i8 %10, 0 (trip 0) / %21 = icmp eq i8 %20, 0
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket: the loop body runs when the test is false
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %18, i32 %21, i32 %22)    ; IR: br i1 %11 (trip 0) / br i1 %21 not taken: a_j = a_{j-1} & NOT test
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %21)    ; IR: bracket
  %23 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %17, i32 1)    ; IR: %18 = add nuw nsw i32 %17, 1
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %22, i32 %23, i32 %17)    ; IR: next %17 / %13 = a ? %18 : %17
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %17)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %20)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %21)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %23)
  %25 = add nuw nsw i64 %16, 1    ; IR: p++ is j + 1 (no gate)
  %26 = icmp ult i64 %25, 4    ; IR: K-bounded br i1 %21, label %12, label %15  [K]
  br i1 %26, label %15, label %27

27:
  %28 = add i64 %5, 4    ; IR: %19 = getelementptr after trip K: the classical address s + K  [K]
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_controlled(i32 %22, i32 %3, i64 %28)    ; IR: %20 = load i8, ptr %19 after trip K, under the predicate of trip K: *p for the exit test that would admit a (K+1)-th trip
  %30 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl(i32 %29, i8 0)    ; IR: %21 = icmp eq i8 %20, 0 after trip K
  %31 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: a_K = predicate of trip K & NOT that test  [output rail, kept]
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %30)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %22, i32 %30, i32 %31)    ; IR: br i1 %21 not taken once more (rule 14)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %30)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl_unc(i32 %30, i32 %29, i8 0)    ; IR: uncompute that test
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %30)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_controlled_unc(i32 %29, i32 %22, i32 %3, i64 %28)    ; IR: un-copy that load under the same control (rule 5)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %29)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %32 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %13 = phi i32 [ 0, %2 ], [ %18, %15 ]  [copied-out result]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %24, i32 %32)    ; IR: %13
  br label %33

33:
  %34 = phi i64 [ 0, %27 ], [ %44, %33 ]    ; IR: reverse trip index
  %35 = phi i32 [ %24, %27 ], [ %41, %33 ]    ; IR: %17 written by this trip
  %36 = phi i32 [ %22, %27 ], [ %40, %33 ]    ; IR: predicate of this trip
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %18 (n + 1)
  %38 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the test flag %11 / %21
  %39 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: the load %10 / %20
  %40 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: predicate of the previous trip (trip 0: the |1> seed)
  %41 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; IR: %17 incoming
  %42 = sub i64 3, %34    ; IR: this trip's index j = K - 1 - reverse index  [K]
  %43 = add i64 %5, %42    ; IR: p = s + j, recomputed from the trip index
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %35, i32 %36, i32 %37, i32 %41)    ; IR: uncompute next %17
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %35)    ; IR: release next %17 (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %37, i32 %41, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %18
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %37)    ; IR: release %18 (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %38)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %40, i32 %38, i32 %36)    ; IR: uncompute the predicate of this trip (every trip 1..K; a_K is a separate rail)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %38)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release the predicate (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i8_hl_unc(i32 %38, i32 %39, i8 0)    ; IR: uncompute %11 / %21
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %38)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i8_hl_controlled_unc(i32 %39, i32 %40, i32 %3, i64 %43)    ; IR: un-copy %10 / %20 under the control it was loaded with (rule 5: no memory version change since the load)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %39)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  %44 = add nuw nsw i64 %34, 1
  %45 = icmp ult i64 %44, 4    ; IR: K  [K]
  br i1 %45, label %33, label %46

46:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; IR: release the |1> seed directly (rule 7: known basis state)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; IR: release incoming 0 of phi %17 (never written, |0>)
  %47 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %32)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_si32(%13); llvm.lifetime.end(4, %3) dropped: the block is never freed (rule 16)
  ret i32 %47    ; IR: ret i32 %14
}

name: 88_nested_pointer
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 21, 20, 5 (Memory, sentences 1 and 3), 16, 7, 4, 3, 2; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc).
; Checked: a[0] + b[1] + *q (the add rail %47, measured -> %48) after p[(x >> 1) & 1] = v through p = tab[x & 1] and
; tab[(x >> 2) & 1] = &s.g, q = tab[1]; and the cells of a, b, s and tab read from the bus at exit. With b0, b1, b2 the
; low three bits of x: p = b0 ? &b : &a, the cell p[b1] = v; tab[b2] = &s.g; q = b2 ? &s.g : &b, so
; a[0] = (b0 == 0 && b1 == 0) ? v : 1, b[1] = (b0 == 1 && b1 == 1) ? v : 4, *q = b2 ? 6 : b[1].
; Clean: the three address chains (x & 1, its zext, the scaling by 8, the add of tab's address: %21..%24, uncomputed
; right after the un-copy of the load p it addresses; x >> 1, & 1, zext, the scaling by 4, the add of p: %26..%30, uncomputed right
; after the store p[j] = v; x >> 2, & 1, zext, the scaling by 8, the add of tab's address: %34..%38, uncomputed right
; after the store tab[k] = &s.g); the load copies q = tab[1] (%40), a[0] (%41), b[1] (%44) and *q (%46) and the sum
; a[0] + b[1] (%45), all uncomputed before the measurement: no memory version change follows the load of q.

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 4, 9, 5, 2.
; Checked: mul_overflow: r + o, r = x * c wrapped, o its overflow flag; add_overflow_qq: overflow ? INT_MAX : x + y;
; add_sat: uadd_sat(x, c) (each measured).
; Clean: mul_overflow's overflow flag; add_overflow_qq's wrapped sum and overflow flag.
; Kept: the user registers (x; x and y; x); the measured result rails (mul_overflow: the product and the zext'd flag).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (mul_overflow, add_sat); Ry(tx) on x and Ry(ty) on y (add_overflow_qq).
; The with.overflow intrinsics return the aggregate { iN, i1 }: the wrapped result and the overflow flag. The handle
; ABI gives one rail per template, so the aggregate is TWO templates over the same operands (rule 4; the convention of
; 81's op / op_exc twins): the value is the ordinary wrapping opcode template (mul_i32 for umul, add_i32 for sadd:
; that IS the wrapped result) and the flag is cq_template_<u|s><op>_overflow_<W>[_hl|_lh], an i1 rail, each with its
; own _unc. extractvalue selects the rail; zext i1 -> i32 is the cast template. llvm.uadd.sat (clang's fold of
; s = x + c; if (s < x) s = ~0u) is the single saturating template cq_template_uadd_sat_<W> (§1.2).
source_filename = "overflow_intrinsics.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5 = umul.with.overflow(%4, %2): element 0, the wrapped product (%7)  [measured]
  %6 = call i32 @cq_template_umul_overflow_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: %5: element 1, the overflow flag (%6)
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i1_to_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %8 = zext i1 %6 to i32  [measured]
  call void @cq_template_umul_overflow_i32_hl_unc(i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %6

  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %5)    ; IR: %9 = cq_measure_ui32(%7)
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %7)    ; IR: %10 = cq_measure_si32(%8)
  %10 = add i32 %9, %8    ; IR: %11 = add i32 %10, %9  (classical)

define i32 @add_overflow_qq(i32 noundef %0, i32 noundef %1, double noundef %2, double noundef %3) {

  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %7 = sadd.with.overflow(%5, %6): element 0, the wrapped sum (%9)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_sadd_overflow_i32(i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: %7: element 1, the overflow flag (%8)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %8, i32 2147483647, i32 %7)    ; IR: %10 = select i1 %8, i32 2147483647, i32 %9  [result rail]
  call void @cq_template_sadd_overflow_i32_unc(i32 %8, i32 %5, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %8
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %8 rail (|0>)

  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_ui32(%0, %1)  [register x]

; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 25, 4, 5, 2.
; Checked: mul_i128: (((x | 1 << 64) * c) >> 64) as 64 bits; div_i128: ((hi << 64 | lo) / (x | 1 << 64)) as 64 bits

; Kept: the user register x of each function; the truncated result rail (measured).
; Rotations: Ry(th) on x (each function).
; 128-bit integers are a WIDTH VARIANT (rule 25): every i128 opcode is the same template family at W = 128
; (zext_i64_to_i128, or_i128_hl, mul_i128_hl, lshr_i128_hl, udiv_i128_lh, trunc_i128_to_i64), with classical i128
; operands passed as i128 values. Note on division: at -O1 the IR still holds `udiv i128` (the __udivti3 libcall
; appears only at codegen, below the IR), so it lowers as the udiv template like 11's i32 udiv (rule 4; §2 fixes
; udiv(a, 0)); the backend's circuit reference for it is compiler-rt's __udivti3 (udivmodti4.c), which is in the
; source bundle for lifting if a direct 128-bit divider is not provided. -O1 rewrote p + (c << 64) in mul_i128 into

target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

; Clean: the three rails of the atomicrmw's in-place form (the swap rail %11, the rule-6 inverse t = (h + c) - c %13,
; the updated rail %12, |0> after the swap-in); the cmpxchg equality flag %15 (uncomputed against the measured copy %14).
; Kept: x (%8: rotated register, and the value rail of the kept store `store atomic i32 %6, ptr %5`, rule 5 sentence 3,
; so rule 6 does not clean it); by rule 5, for the shot: the tape slots of the three bus stores (`store i32 %2, ptr %5`,
; `store atomic i32 %6, ptr %5`, and the cmpxchg's store of the select %16); the seed %9 holding c (rule 7: the value rail of the
; kept store `int cell = c`); the load copy old = %10 (the atomicrmw's result, read after the in-place form, which
; overtakes it: sentence 1 un-copies it right after its last reader, the select %16, and does not free it); the
; cmpxchg's select %16 (the value rail of its kept store). Rule 2: the load copies %14
; (expected) and %18 (now) and the zext %17 (ok), measured.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected for the driver atomics(0, .5, 3, 5): Ry(.5) flips each of the 32 bits of x = 0 independently with
; probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.0612087. The cell holds x + 3 after the fetch-add, so expected = x + 3 and the exchange
; succeeds iff x + 3 == 5, i.e. x == 2: then now = old = x = 2, ok = 1, expected = 5, result 8 (probability
; s (1 - s)^31 = 0.008639). Otherwise now = expected = x + 3, ok = 0, result 2x + 6: x = 0 gives 6 with probability
; (1 - s)^32 = 0.132498; each other single-bit flip x = 2^i (i != 1, 30, 31) gives 2^(i+1) + 6 with probability
; 0.008639 (i = 0 also gives 8, so 8 has probability 0.017278 in all). i = 30 and i = 31 overflow the final signed add
; %23 (nsw: undefined in C): under the trace's wraparound i = 30 gives -2^31 + 6 and i = 31 (x = INT_MIN) gives 6, so
; the trace's 6 has probability 0.132498 + 0.008639 = 0.141137.
; THREADS ARE OUT OF THE MODEL (rule 24): a reversible circuit is sequential, so every atomic op has single-thread
; semantics and lowers as the plain op it wraps: store atomic = store, load atomic = load, atomicrmw add = load + add +
; store returning the old value, cmpxchg = load + icmp eq + select + store returning { loaded, equal } as two rails
; (rule 26's aggregate), fence = nothing (no gate, no host call).
; ONE BUS (rule 20). cell's alloca has a store of a rail among its users, so it is bus-resident (rule 20 (b)): one
; zeroed block __cq_alloc(4, 4) at the alloca's program point, no alloca remains and the lifetime markers are dropped
; (rule 16). Its run-time address %7 is the _hl operand of every access; nothing asks what the cell holds. `int cell =
; c` stores the seed alloc_i32(c) (rule 7), and it and the store atomic of x are KEPT stores (rule 5 sentence 3).
; atomicrmw add is `y = load; y' = y + c; store y'` on the same pointer with nothing between: rule 5's IN-PLACE FORM with
; a rule-6 bijection as its step (rule 6, "a memory cell"), at the store's position: swap-out into a fresh |0> rail,
; y' = h + c with rule 6's clean of h, swap-in, free. Its result, the old value y, has another reader (the cmpxchg's new
; value), so it is a plain load taken before the swap-out (rule 5, Readers); the form is a memory version change before
; that reader, so the copy is overtaken (sentence 1): un-copied after the select, left allocated.
; SPEC GAP (rule 4): `cmpxchg` and `atomicrmw` are first read as a bus load, the compare and `select` (or the
; operation's) templates and a bus store on the same pointer (rules 20, 24); that expansion is then lowered by rule 5
; like any written load/update/store, so an `atomicrmw` whose operation is a rule-6 bijection in the cell (`add`, `sub`,
; `xor`) is rule 5's in-place form, and its result, the old value, is the Readers clause's plain load taken before the
; swap-out.
; cmpxchg is not the in-place form (the select's condition reads the cell and its true arm is not an update of it, rule
; 6): a plain load (element 0, measured as `expected`), the compare (element 1), the select and a kept store of it. The
; load atomic of `now` is a plain load at the classical address, measured. The flag %15 is uncomputed after its last
; consumer (the zext); its _unc reads the measured copy %14, which stays allocated.

define i32 @atomics(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2, i32 noundef %3) {
  %5 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus m (§5: once, at function entry)
  %6 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 4, i64 4)    ; IR: %5 = alloca i32, align 4: cell is bus-resident (a rail is stored through it): a zeroed block, no alloca remains
  %7 = ptrtoint ptr %6 to i64    ; IR: the run-time address of cell as the _hl operand (classical)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %8, double %1)    ; IR: %6 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %2)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: the value seed c (rule 7; kept with the store; llvm.lifetime.start is dropped)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %9)    ; IR: store i32 %2, ptr %5: int cell = c  (kept store, classical address)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store atomic i32 %6, ptr %5 seq_cst: single-thread, a kept store of x
  %10 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: %7 = atomicrmw add ptr %5, i32 %2: the old value, a plain load before the swap-out (rule 5, Readers; the form overtakes it: un-copied after the select, not freed)
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = atomicrmw add: in-place form, the swap rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %11)    ; IR: %7 = atomicrmw add: swap-out: the rail holds the cell, the cell |0>
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %11, i32 %2)    ; IR: %7 = atomicrmw add: old + %2  [the new cell]
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_hl(i32 %12, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: t = (old + c) - c recomputes the swapped-out cell
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %13, i32 %11)    ; IR: rule 6: the swap rail ^= t: |0>
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_hl_unc(i32 %13, i32 %12, i32 %2)    ; IR: rule 6: uncompute t
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release t (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the old cell rail (|0> after the copy)
  call void @cqrt_qram_swap_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %12)    ; IR: %7 = atomicrmw add: swap-in: the cell holds old + c, the rail the cell's |0>
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the rail (|0>): nothing remains of the update
  ; IR: fence seq_cst: no gate (single thread)
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: %8 = cmpxchg ptr %5, i32 %3, i32 %7: the loaded value, element 0 (%10)  [measured]
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl(i32 %14, i32 %3)    ; IR: %8: element 1 (%9), loaded == expected
  %16 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %15, i32 %10, i32 %14)    ; IR: %8: cell = equal ? %7 (the old value) : loaded  [the new cell]
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: un-copy %7 (the old value) after its last reader, the select; the in-place form came between, so it stays allocated (overtaken, rule 5 sentence 1)
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7, i32 %16)    ; IR: %8: the store of the new cell (kept store: its tape slot and its value rail %8's select stay)
  %17 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i1_to_i32(i32 %15)    ; IR: %11 = zext i1 %9 to i32  [measured]
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i32_hl(i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: %12 = load atomic i32, ptr %5 seq_cst: a plain bus load  [measured]
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i32_hl_unc(i32 %15, i32 %14, i32 %3)    ; IR: uncompute %9 (its last consumer, the zext, is done; the select is kept)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  %19 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %18)    ; IR: %13 = cq_measure_si32(%12)
  %20 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %17)    ; IR: %14 = cq_measure_si32(%11)
  %21 = add nsw i32 %20, %19    ; IR: %15 = add nsw i32 %14, %13  (classical)
  %22 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %14)    ; IR: %16 = cq_measure_si32(%10)
  %23 = add nsw i32 %21, %22    ; IR: %17 = add nsw i32 %15, %16  (classical)
  ret i32 %23    ; IR: ret i32 %17  (llvm.lifetime.end is dropped, rule 16)
}

; Checked: sum3(1, a, x, b) = a + x + b + 1 (the clone's result rail, the rule-6 image s + 1, measured in the caller as
; %6 -> %7). The cells of the two blocks are not named outputs.
; Clean: in __cq_q_sum3_00, per trip: the address chain of the register-slot arm (the zext of gp_offset, the address
; rail reg_save_area + gp_offset) and the merged slot address, each uncomputed after the un-copy of the load through
; it; the load copy of the argument (va_arg's load, un-copied in the trip: no memory version change lies between the
; load and its _unc); the old s and its rule-6 rail t (rule 6 in the body, as 27 and 204; trip 0's old s is the |0>
; seed). After the loop: the last s, cleaned by rule 6 from the result s + 1, and its rail t; the gp_offset
; after-values (IR %24) and the overflow_arg_area after-values (IR %23) of trips 0..2, uncomputed by the reverse loop
; (rule 14) from the per-trip handles it pops.
; Kept: varargs: x (%5, the rotated register; also the value rail of the block store of slot 1) and the result rail
; (%6, measured); by rule 5 the three tape slots of the caller's block stores and the seeds a and b (their value
; rails). __cq_q_sum3_00: by rule 5 the four tape slots of va_start's stores with their seeds (48, 176, the block
; address, 0); per trip the tape slots of the two va_arg stores (gp_offset, overflow_arg_area) with their value rails
; (gp_offset + 8, overflow_arg_area + 8) and their control, the flag gp_offset < 41 (rule 8); the load copies of
; ap->gp_offset, ap->reg_save_area and ap->overflow_arg_area (rule 5 sentence 1: each is un-copied after its last
; reader, reg_save_area after the loop, gp_offset and overflow_arg_area after the reverse loop, and left allocated,
; since trip 0's store comes between the load and that point). No _unc twin: the clone writes memory (rule 18), and the caller measures its result.
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: the bus run is classical-valued apart from x: gp_offset reads 48, so the flag is 0 on every trip, the slot
; is the overflow area, and the three trips load a, x, b from the block at offsets 0, 8, 16. The measured value is
; a + x + b + 1 with x = x0 ^ e, each bit of x flipped independently with p = sin^2(th / 2).
; THE VARIADIC BLOCK (rule 16, §1.4). The caller stores every variadic argument into one __cq_alloc(24, 16) block in
; the SysV overflow-area layout (8-byte slots at the promoted type, here three i32 at offsets 0, 8, 16) and passes the
; block's address as the clone's last formal: __cq_q_sum3_00(i32 n, ptr block), mask digit 0 for the dead n (passed as
; poison) and digit 0 for the block pointer. No per-signature clone exists. The classical a and b are stored as seeds
; (rule 7), x as its handle; all three are kept stores (rule 5) at classical addresses.
; VA_START IS FOUR BUS STORES (rule 16). ap (the alloca of the va_list) has va_start, va_end and stores of loaded values
; among its users, so it is bus-resident (rule 20 (b)): __cq_alloc(24, 16), no alloca remains, the lifetime markers are
; dropped. va_start writes {gp_offset = 48, fp_offset = 176, overflow_arg_area = block, reg_save_area = 0} by four kept
; stores of seeds. va_arg and va_end are -O1's code as it stands: every load from ap is a bus load and its result is a
; rail (rule 3; over-taint is accepted, §0), so gp_offset and both area pointers are rails, the va_arg branch on

; gp_offset + 8, overflow_arg_area + 8) is hoisted, each arm's store to ap stays in its arm as the _controlled store
; under the flag (the ¬flag arm inside an X bracket), and the three phis are select templates under the flag. The
; argument slot is an address rail, so va_arg's load is qram_load_i32 at that rail (rule 20). llvm.va_end is nothing.
; THE LOOP (rule 14, classical bound: i < 3). The accumulator s' = v + s is a bijection in s whose other operand is a

low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19 (classical function pointer, clone table), 18, 16, 21, 9, 4, 5, 7, 2, 14; §1.3 (clone table), §1.4
; (table clones, activation counter).
; Checked: fp(x) with fp = which ? dbl : sq (the copy of the table clone's result, measured): x + x where which != 0,
; x * x where which = 0.
; Clean: inside whichever table clone runs: its arm value (copied out, then uncomputed and freed); the clone's
; result rail, zeroed and freed by its table twin (__cq_q_<fn>_1_t_unc, resolved as kind 2; the caller frees no
; result of a table clone, §1.4); on the host branch (never taken here) the |1> seed of the effect entry (rule 7).
; Kept: the user register x; the copy of the call's result (measured; rule 18: a measured result is copied before the
; twin runs); the function's tape (allocated at entry on every path, rule 16). On the host branch (never taken here):
; the tape field rail of x and the entry's result rail r_e (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; An INDIRECT CALL through a CLASSICAL function pointer with a quantum argument (rule 19). Which functions fp can
; denote is never analysed (clang's !callees metadata is not read): fp is resolved at run time through the clone
; table. The module constructor registers one row for each address-taken function (dbl, sq: their addresses are the
; select's operands): its host address, the type string "i32 (i32)", its table clone and that clone's _ctl, _unc and
; _ctl_unc (§1.3). The call is __cq_clone_resolve(fp, 0), the forward table clone, with the table ABI: every formal a
; handle (x), then K = 4, the K of this function (§0). The caller has no record of the callee, so the call is a memory
; version change, and its twin (__cq_clone_resolve(fp, 2)) is called exactly once at its rule-18 position: the result
; is measured, so it is first copied into a fresh rail, the twin zeroes and frees the clone's own result, and the
; copy is measured (rule 18). A null resolve means fp is host code: the call is rule 16's effect entry with a null
; name, fp's address as its first field (a classical i64, a _lit field) and x as its second, under an alloc_i1(true)
; seed; its result rail r_e is measured. The two results merge by a classical phi of handles (the branch is
; classical). No predicate is in scope, so no _ctl clone is called here; the _ctl forms exist because every row
; names them.
; THE TABLE CLONES (§1.4). Each takes the handle and K and returns one handle; neither function mints a register, so
; nothing is pushed and the twins pop nothing. Their bodies keep the copy-out form of rule 18 (compute, copy the
; result out, uncompute, free). dbl and sq write no memory and do not measure, so the table twins are rule 18's twin:
; recompute, XOR the result out with copy_i32, uncompute, then free both rails (§1.4: a table twin frees the results
; it zeroes). A _ctl table clone whose body is only templates computes unguarded and reads its predicate only for the
; cut: it and its twin read the function's activation counter d on entry, add 1 and subtract 1 at the return; at
; d >= K the clone returns a |0> rail and keeps a copy_i1 of its predicate as the overflow rail, and the twin frees
; that |0> rail (rule 14). The _ctl forms are not called in this program.
; THE OWN SYMBOLS. dbl and sq have no bus access, no cq_* call and no call: each is its own lowering (rule 19), and
; their host addresses are the table's keys. The per-mask clones __cq_q_dbl_1 / __cq_q_sq_1 have no call by name and
; are dropped (§1.4).
; Corpus convention (§5): the clone-table row, table clone, _t_ctl and twins of the externally visible indirect_call
; (type i32 (i32, double, i32)), whose address is never taken, are omitted; the compiler emits them (§1.3, rule 19).
; SPEC GAP: CR fixes no module-internal name: as in 205, 211 and 212 the constructor is internal void @__cq_register()
; at priority 65535, the sig string is private @.cq.sig, the activation counters are internal i32 @__cq_act_<fn>.
; The host branch is rule 16's effect entry, not the instruction as it stands: its argument x is a rail, so it is not
; an ordinary host call (rule 16: every argument classical). The _i32 form is used because the program reads the result.
; SPEC GAP: rule 18 lets a one-template body return its rail directly (211's inc); the copy-out form of the previous
; lowering is kept here, which rule 18 also allows.
source_filename = "indirect_call.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@.cq.sig = private unnamed_addr constant [10 x i8] c"i32 (i32)\00", align 1    ; the LLVM function type of dbl, sq and the indirect call, as a C string (§1.3)
@__cq_act_dbl = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; live _ctl activations of dbl (§1.4: it has a table clone)
@__cq_act_sq = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; live _ctl activations of sq (§1.4)
@llvm.global_ctors = appending global [1 x { i32, ptr, ptr }] [{ i32, ptr, ptr } { i32 65535, ptr @__cq_register, ptr null }]

define internal void @__cq_register() {
  call void @__cq_clone_register(ptr @dbl, ptr @.cq.sig, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_unc, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl_unc)    ; row of dbl (address taken by the select): fn, sig, table clone, _ctl, _unc, _ctl_unc (rule 19)
  call void @__cq_clone_register(ptr @sq, ptr @.cq.sig, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_unc, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl_unc)    ; row of sq (address taken by the select)
  ret void
}

define i32 @indirect_call(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; the function's tape (one tape_alloc at entry, on every path; the host branch's effect entry records on it, rule 16)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %5, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %6 = icmp eq i32 %2, 0    ; IR: %5 = icmp eq i32 %2, 0  (classical)
  %7 = select i1 %6, ptr @sq, ptr @dbl    ; IR: %6 = select i1 %5, ptr @sq, ptr @dbl  (classical function pointer: a host address)
  %8 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %7, i32 0)    ; IR: %7 = call %6(%4)  [the table clone of fp (kind 0), from the clone table at run time (rule 19)]
  %9 = icmp eq ptr %8, null    ; IR: %7: no row, fp is host code
  br i1 %9, label %14, label %10    ; IR: %7: classical branch

10:
  %11 = call i32 %8(i32 %5, i32 4)    ; IR: %7 = call %6(%4)  [the table clone: the argument rail x, K; a memory version change (rule 19)]  [K]
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %7  [the copy of the result that is measured (rule 18)]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %11, i32 %12)    ; IR: %7  [copy the result out before the twin]
  %13 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %7, i32 2)    ; IR: %7  [the table twin of fp (kind 2)]
  call void %13(i32 %11, i32 %5, i32 4)    ; IR: %7  [the twin, exactly once: the result, the argument, K; it zeroes and frees the result (§1.4)]  [K]
  br label %19    ; IR: %7

14:
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: %7 = call %6(%4)  [host code: no predicate in scope, the |1> seed (rule 16)]
  %16 = ptrtoint ptr %7 to i64    ; IR: %6 as a classical i64 (rule 21)
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i64_lit(i32 %4, i64 %16)    ; IR: %7  [field 0: the callee's address, classical (rule 19)]
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i32(i32 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: %7  [field 1: the argument rail x (KEPT tape rail)]
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_effect_i32_controlled(i32 %15, i32 %4, ptr null, i32 2)    ; IR: %7  [the effect entry with a null name: r_e, its result rail, KEPT (rule 16)]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the seed (|1>, never written: freed directly, rule 7)
  br label %19    ; IR: %7

19:
  %20 = phi i32 [ %12, %10 ], [ %18, %14 ]    ; IR: %7  [result handle, classical phi of handles]
  %21 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %20)    ; IR: %8 = cq_measure_si32(%7)
  ret i32 %21    ; IR: ret i32 %8
}

define internal i32 @dbl(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (the own symbol: its own lowering, rule 19; its address is the table key)
  ret i32 %2    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal i32 @sq(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0    ; IR: %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (the own symbol: its own lowering, rule 19; its address is the table key)
  ret i32 %2    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal i32 @__cq_q_dbl_1_t(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (table clone: the handle, then K)
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %2  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %3, i32 %4)    ; IR: ret i32 %2  [copy the result out]
  call void @cq_template_shl_i32_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %2
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %2 rail (|0>)
  ret i32 %4    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal void @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (twin: recompute; the result, the argument, K)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %4, i32 %0)    ; IR: ret i32 %2  [XOR the result out: it is |0>]
  call void @cq_template_shl_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %2
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %2 rail (|0>)

  %5 = add i32 %4, 1
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; one more live _ctl activation of dbl
  %6 = icmp ult i32 %4, %2    ; d below K: the body runs (rule 14)

  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %2  [result rail of the call]

  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %0, i32 %14)    ; a copy of the predicate
