name: 97_quantum_fnptr
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 19, 2, 4, 5, 7, 8, 9, 13, 14, 16, 18, 20, 21; §1.3 (clone table), §1.4 (table clones).
; Checked: r = fps[x & 1](c + x) (the copied-out result of the merge, measured): 2(c + x) where x & 1 = 0 (dbl),
; (c + x)^2 where x & 1 = 1 (sq); the cells of fps are unchanged.
; Clean: the address chain of &fps[x & 1] (the and %5, its zext %6, the scaled index, the address rail %7), uncomputed
; right after fp's un-copy and freed; the argument c + x (%9), uncomputed after its last reader, the effect entry's field;
; per candidate: the flag f_i (fp == a_i), the complement rail p_{i+1} and the select rail out_{i+1}, popped and
; uncomputed by the reverse loop and freed; the outer select rail (after the copy-out); the seeds p_0 (|1>) and out_0
; (|0>), never written and freed directly (rule 7); dbl's and sq's result rails (2(c + x), (c + x)^2), zeroed and freed
; by their twins __cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl_unc and __cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl_unc; fp, the load copy of fps[x & 1], un-copied after
; the reverse loop (its last reader is the last flag's _unc) and left allocated (rule 5 sentence 1: the dispatch, a
; memory version change, overtakes it).
; Kept: x (the rotated register); per candidate the copy c_i of its result (rule
; 19: the result is kept across the next memory version change as a copy); the result rail r_e of the complement's
; effect entry, its two tape field rails and the tape (rule 16); the copied-out result R (measured).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: quantum_fnptr(0, .5, 3). Ry acts on all 32 qubits of x: each bit flips with p = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209.
; x & 1 = 0 (dbl) with 0.938791 and 1 (sq) with 0.061209; r = 2(3 + x) on the dbl branch and (3 + x)^2 on the sq
; branch. P(r = 6) = 0.141137 (dbl with x = 0: 0.132498; with x = 2^31: 0.008639; no square is 6 mod 2^32). Both cells
; of fps hold registered functions of type i32 (i32), so one flag is 1 on every branch, the complement predicate is 0
; and the effect entry is never performed (deferred by the backend, its r_e is |0>).
; A FUNCTION POINTER LOADED AT AN ADDRESS RAIL (rules 19, 20, 21). fps is a constant global at its host address: HOST
; cells seen through the overlay, nothing seeded and no derived table. Its index is tainted, so the access is not the
; host-resident plain load of rule 20 (a): the gep is 64-bit template arithmetic (the zext as -O1 wrote it, mul by the
; element size 8, add of the classical base) and the load is ONE qram_load_i64 at the address rail: fp is a 64-bit rail
; holding the callee's host address.
; THE DISPATCH (as 211). Which functions fp can denote is never analysed: the candidates are the registered functions of
; the call's function type, read from the clone table at run time. The module constructor registers one row for each
; address-taken function (dbl, sq): its host address, the type string "i32 (i32)", its table clone and that clone's
; _ctl, _unc and _ctl_unc. The dispatch is a classical loop (rule 14: i < __cq_clone_count(sig), registration order).
; Trip i takes a_i = __cq_clone_at(sig, i), the flag f_i = icmp_eq_i64_hl(fp, a_i), and calls the _t_ctl clone of a_i
; (kind 1) under f_i with the table ABI: predicate first, every formal a handle (the argument rail c + x), then K = 4,
; the K of this function. The caller has no record of a callee: every call is a memory version change, so the result is
; copied into a fresh rail c_i that is KEPT, and the twin (kind 3, same flag) is called right after, before the next
; memory version change (the next candidate's call, or the effect entry). The trip then extends the complement p_{i+1} =
; p_i & NOT f_i (an X bracket on f_i around and_i1 into a fresh rail, rule 8; p_0 is a |1> seed, no predicate being in
; scope) and the merge out_{i+1} = select_i32(f_i, c_i, out_i) (rule 9; out_0 is a |0> seed), and pushes p_i, out_i,
; c_i and f_i. After the loop p_n says "fp is no registered function": fp is host code there, and p_n itself is the
; predicate of the effect entry with a null name, fp its first field and c + x its second, result rail r_e. The call's
; value is select_i32(p_n, r_e, out_n). It is copied out (rule 14), the outer select is uncomputed, the reverse loop
; pops the trips and uncomputes each select, each p_{i+1} and each flag (a_i again from the table), the seeds are freed
; and the copy is measured.
; THE TABLE CLONES (§1.4). Each takes handles and K, returns one handle and pushes nothing (neither function mints a
; register). dbl and sq are one template each: their clones return the template's rail, their twins are that
; template's _unc and the free (the caller frees no result of a table clone). A _ctl clone guards gates, and neither
; body has one, so the _t_ctl clones compute unguarded (rule 9) and the caller's select does the rest. Every _t_ctl
; clone and _t_ctl_unc twin reads its function's activation counter d on entry, adds 1 and subtracts 1 at its return
; (§1.4); at d >= K the clone returns a |0> rail and keeps a copy_i1 of its predicate as the overflow rail, and the twin
; frees that |0> rail (rule 14). Nothing re-enters here, so d is 0 at every call and no activation is cut.
; THE OWN SYMBOLS. dbl and sq stay, at the host addresses the cells of fps hold (the table's keys): neither has a bus
; access, a cq_* call or a call, so each is its own lowering. No clone of either is called by name, so there is no
; rule-18 clone __cq_q_dbl_1 / __cq_q_sq_1.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 / §1.3 ask for a clone-table row per externally visible function too. quantum_fnptr gets none here
; (as in 211, §5): its type is not the call's, so the dispatch does not see the difference.
; SPEC GAP: rule 19 does not say how the complement predicate and the select chain are built for a candidate count
; known only at run time. Chosen, as in 211 and 212: ONE loop and its reverse; the complement is an arm of one outer
; select on p_n, not the innermost arm of one chain. The flags are pairwise exclusive (distinct addresses), so the
; value is the same on every branch.
; SPEC GAP: neither rule 16 nor BACKEND_ABI §1.11 says that an effect entry captures its predicate. p_n is uncomputed
; and freed after the entry like any flag (138, 211, 212), so the backend must capture it at the call.
; SPEC GAP: no name is fixed for the module constructor, the type-string global or the activation counters beyond
; §1.3/§1.4's spellings; the counters are plain module-internal i32 globals, read and written by plain instructions.
source_filename = "quantum_fnptr.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@fps = internal unnamed_addr constant [2 x ptr] [ptr @dbl, ptr @sq], align 16    ; IR: @fps  (at its host address: HOST cells on the bus, rule 20)
@.cq.sig = private unnamed_addr constant [10 x i8] c"i32 (i32)\00", align 1    ; the LLVM function type of dbl, sq and the indirect call, as a C string (§1.3)
@__cq_act_dbl = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; live _ctl activations of dbl (§1.4)
@__cq_act_sq = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; live _ctl activations of sq (§1.4)
@llvm.global_ctors = appending global [1 x { i32, ptr, ptr }] [{ i32, ptr, ptr } { i32 65535, ptr @__cq_register, ptr null }]

define internal void @__cq_register() {
  call void @__cq_clone_register(ptr @dbl, ptr @.cq.sig, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_unc, ptr @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl_unc)    ; row of dbl (address taken in @fps): fn, sig, table clone, _ctl, _unc, _ctl_unc (rule 19)
  call void @__cq_clone_register(ptr @sq, ptr @.cq.sig, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_unc, ptr @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl_unc)    ; row of sq (address taken in @fps)
  ret void
}

define i32 @quantum_fnptr(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; the bus M, once at function entry (§5)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; the function's tape (the complement's effect entry, rule 16)
  %6 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %6, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: %5 = and i32 %4, 1
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64(i32 %7)    ; IR: %6 = zext nneg i32 %5 to i64
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i64_hl(i32 %8, i64 8)    ; IR: %7 = getelementptr inbounds [2 x ptr], ptr @fps, i64 0, i64 %6  [the tainted index scaled by the element size (rule 20)]
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i64_hl(i32 %9, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @fps to i64))    ; IR: %7 = getelementptr  [+ the classical base: the address rail of &fps[x & 1]]
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64(i32 %4, i32 %10)    ; IR: %8 = load ptr, ptr %7, align 8  [a load at an address rail: fp, a 64-bit rail holding the callee's address; overtaken by the dispatch, un-copied after the reverse loop (rule 5)]
  %12 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: %9 = add nsw i32 %4, %2  [the call's argument rail]
  %13 = call i32 @__cq_clone_count(ptr @.cq.sig)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [n, the number of registered functions of type i32 (i32): the candidates (rule 19)]
  %14 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; p_0: the complement of no flag (a |1> seed: no predicate in scope, rules 7, 16)
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; out_0: the merge of no candidate (a seed)
  br label %16    ; the dispatch: one trip per candidate, classical code (rules 14, 19)

16:
  %17 = phi i32 [ 0, %3 ], [ %31, %21 ]    ; candidate index i (classical)
  %18 = phi i32 [ %14, %3 ], [ %29, %21 ]    ; p_i: 1 iff fp is none of a_0 .. a_{i-1}
  %19 = phi i32 [ %15, %3 ], [ %30, %21 ]    ; out_i: the merge of candidates 0 .. i-1
  %20 = icmp ult i32 %17, %13
  br i1 %20, label %21, label %32

21:
  %22 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %17)    ; a_i: the host address of candidate i (registration order)
  %23 = ptrtoint ptr %22 to i64    ; a_i as a classical i64 (rule 21)
  %24 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl(i32 %11, i64 %23)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [flag f_i: fp == a_i (rule 13's compare)]
  %25 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %22, i32 1)    ; the _t_ctl clone of a_i (kind 1)
  %26 = call i32 %25(i32 %24, i32 %12, i32 4)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [candidate i under f_i: predicate, the argument rail c + x, K; a memory version change (rule 19)]  [K]
  %27 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; c_i: the copy that is KEPT in the result's place (rule 19)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %26, i32 %27)    ; c_i ^= the result, before the next memory version change
  %28 = call ptr @__cq_clone_resolve(ptr %22, i32 3)    ; the _t_ctl_unc twin of a_i (kind 3)
  call void %28(i32 %24, i32 %26, i32 %12, i32 4)    ; IR: the twin, exactly once, under the same flag: predicate, the result, the argument, K (it frees what it zeroes)  [K]
  %29 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; p_{i+1}
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %24)    ; X bracket: NOT f_i (rule 8)
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %18, i32 %24, i32 %29)    ; p_{i+1} = p_i & NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %24)    ; close the X bracket
  %30 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %24, i32 %27, i32 %19)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [merge: candidate i's result under f_i, else the merge so far (rule 9)]
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %18)    ; p_i, out_i, c_i and f_i, for the reverse loop (rule 14)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %19)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %27)
  call void @cqrt_push(i32 %24)
  %31 = add nuw i32 %17, 1
  br label %16

32:
  %33 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i64_controlled(i32 %18, i32 %5, i32 %11)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [under p_n, the complement of the flags: the entry's first field, the callee's address, the rail fp (rule 19)]
  %34 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i32_controlled(i32 %18, i32 %5, i32 %12)    ; the argument c + x
  %35 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_effect_i32_controlled(i32 %18, i32 %5, ptr null, i32 2)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [fp is host code: the effect entry with a null name; r_e, its result rail, KEPT (rule 16)]
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %12, i32 %6, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %9  [after its last reader, the entry's field (rule 5)]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  %36 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32(i32 %18, i32 %35, i32 %19)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [the call's value: the complement's r_e where p_n, else the candidates' merge]  ; SPEC GAP: the complement is an arm of this outer select (header)
  %37 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: %10 = call i32 %8(i32 %9)  [copied-out result R (rule 14)]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %36, i32 %37)    ; IR: %10
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %36, i32 %18, i32 %35, i32 %19)    ; IR: uncompute the outer select
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %36)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %38    ; the reverse loop: candidates n-1 .. 0 (the pop order)

38:
  %39 = phi i32 [ %13, %32 ], [ %44, %43 ]    ; trips left to undo (classical)
  %40 = phi i32 [ %18, %32 ], [ %48, %43 ]    ; p_{i+1} of the trip being undone
  %41 = phi i32 [ %19, %32 ], [ %47, %43 ]    ; out_{i+1} of the trip being undone
  %42 = icmp eq i32 %39, 0
  br i1 %42, label %51, label %43

43:
  %44 = add i32 %39, -1    ; the trip's candidate index i
  %45 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; f_i
  %46 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; c_i (kept: only its handle is read)
  %47 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; out_i
  %48 = call i32 @cqrt_pop()    ; p_i
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_unc(i32 %41, i32 %45, i32 %46, i32 %47)    ; IR: uncompute the merge of candidate i
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %45)    ; X bracket: NOT f_i
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %48, i32 %45, i32 %40)    ; uncompute p_{i+1} (after its last use: the uncompute of p_{i+2}, or for p_n the effect entry and the outer select)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %45)    ; close the X bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; release it (|0>)
  %49 = call ptr @__cq_clone_at(ptr @.cq.sig, i32 %44)    ; a_i again, from the trip index (rule 14)
  %50 = ptrtoint ptr %49 to i64
  call void @cq_template_icmp_eq_i64_hl_unc(i32 %45, i32 %11, i64 %50)    ; IR: uncompute the flag f_i (after its last use)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %45)    ; IR: release it (|0>)
  br label %38

51:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %40)    ; release p_0 (a |1> seed, never written: a known basis state, rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %41)    ; release out_0 (a seed, never written: |0>, rule 7)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_unc(i32 %11, i32 %4, i32 %10)    ; IR: un-copy %8  [fp, after its last reader (the last flag's _unc); overtaken by the dispatch, so it stays allocated (rule 5 sentence 1)]
  call void @cq_template_add_i64_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %9, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @fps to i64))    ; IR: uncompute %7  [the address rail, after the load's _unc (rule 5)]
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_mul_i64_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %8, i64 8)    ; IR: uncompute %7 (the scaled index)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the scaled-index rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_zext_i32_to_i64_unc(i32 %8, i32 %7)    ; IR: uncompute %6
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %6 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %7, i32 %6, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  %52 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %37)    ; IR: %11 = cq_measure_si32(%10)  [not in a _ctl clone: the result rail itself is measured (rule 2)]
  ret i32 %52    ; IR: ret i32 %11
}

define internal i32 @dbl(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (the own symbol: no bus access, no cq_* call, no call, so its own lowering, rule 19; its address is the cell value in @fps and the table key)
  ret i32 %2    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal i32 @sq(i32 noundef %0) {
  %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0    ; IR: %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (the own symbol, its own lowering, rule 19; the table key of the second cell of @fps)
  ret i32 %2    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal i32 @__cq_q_dbl_1_t(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (table clone: the handle, then K; a one-template body returns its rail, rule 18)
  ret i32 %3    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal void @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  call void @cq_template_shl_i32_hl_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %2  (twin: the result, the argument, K)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %0)    ; IR: release the result rail (|0>): a table clone's twin frees what it zeroes (§1.4)
  ret void
}

define internal i32 @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; d: this activation's depth (§1.4)
  %5 = add i32 %4, 1
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; one more live _ctl activation of dbl
  %6 = icmp ult i32 %4, %2    ; d below K: the body runs (rule 14)
  br i1 %6, label %7, label %11

7:
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_shl_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: %2 = shl nsw i32 %0, 1  (a template on an SSA value: computed unguarded, the caller merges by select, rule 9; the predicate %0 guards no gate here)
  %9 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4
  %10 = add i32 %9, -1
  store i32 %10, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; the activation ends
  ret i32 %8    ; IR: ret i32 %2

11:
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; the cut: the result is a |0> rail (rule 14)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; the overflow predicate of this cut activation, an output rail (KEPT)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %0, i32 %13)    ; a copy of the predicate
  %14 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4
  %15 = add i32 %14, -1
  store i32 %15, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; the activation ends
  ret i32 %12
}

define internal void @__cq_q_dbl_1_t_ctl_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %3) {
  %5 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4    ; d (§1.4): the twin makes the same cut
  %6 = add i32 %5, 1
  store i32 %6, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4
  %7 = icmp ult i32 %5, %3
  br i1 %7, label %8, label %9

8:
  call void @cq_template_shl_i32_hl_unc(i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %2  (twin: predicate, the result, the argument, K)
  br label %9

9:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %1)    ; IR: release the result rail (|0>: zeroed above, or the cut activation's |0> rail)
  %10 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4
  %11 = add i32 %10, -1
  store i32 %11, ptr @__cq_act_dbl, align 4
  ret void
}

define internal i32 @__cq_q_sq_1_t(i32 %0, i32 %1) {
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %0, i32 %0)    ; IR: %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (table clone: the handle, then K; a one-template body returns its rail, rule 18)
  ret i32 %3    ; IR: ret i32 %2
}

define internal void @__cq_q_sq_1_t_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: uncompute %2  (twin: the result, the argument, K)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %0)    ; IR: release the result rail (|0>): a table clone's twin frees what it zeroes (§1.4)
  ret void
}

define internal i32 @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {
  %4 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4    ; d: this activation's depth (§1.4)
  %5 = add i32 %4, 1
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4    ; one more live _ctl activation of sq
  %6 = icmp ult i32 %4, %2    ; d below K: the body runs (rule 14)
  br i1 %6, label %7, label %11

7:
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_mul_i32(i32 %1, i32 %1)    ; IR: %2 = mul nsw i32 %0, %0  (a template on SSA values: computed unguarded, the caller merges by select, rule 9; the predicate %0 guards no gate here)
  %9 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4
  %10 = add i32 %9, -1
  store i32 %10, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4    ; the activation ends
  ret i32 %8    ; IR: ret i32 %2

11:
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; the cut: the result is a |0> rail (rule 14)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; the overflow predicate of this cut activation, an output rail (KEPT)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %0, i32 %13)    ; a copy of the predicate
  %14 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4
  %15 = add i32 %14, -1
  store i32 %15, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4    ; the activation ends
  ret i32 %12
}

define internal void @__cq_q_sq_1_t_ctl_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %3) {
  %5 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4    ; d (§1.4): the twin makes the same cut
  %6 = add i32 %5, 1
  store i32 %6, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4
  %7 = icmp ult i32 %5, %3
  br i1 %7, label %8, label %9

8:
  call void @cq_template_mul_i32_unc(i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %2)    ; IR: uncompute %2  (twin: predicate, the result, the argument, K)
  br label %9

9:
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %1)    ; IR: release the result rail (|0>: zeroed above, or the cut activation's |0> rail)
  %10 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4
  %11 = add i32 %10, -1
  store i32 %11, ptr @__cq_act_sq, align 4
  ret void
}

name: 98_quantum_depth_recursion
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 2, 4, 5, 8, 9, 14, 18, 19; §1.4 (Recursion: one _ctl clone, the activation counter).
; Checked: chain(n & 3, a) with the recursion cut at K = 4 (the copied-out result %6, measured -> %7).
; Clean: the scrutinee n & 3; in __cq_q_chain_10_b3, in every activation of __cq_q_chain_10_ctl that runs its body and of
;        its twin: the base-case flag c, n - 1, the conjunction p & !c (_ctl and twin only), the callee's result (zeroed
;        by the twin, then freed; a |0> rail at the cut), the difference and the merge.
; Kept: the user register n (%4); the result rail of __cq_q_chain_10_b3 (%6, measured); ONE overflow rail per cut
;       activation of __cq_q_chain_10_ctl (rule 14): each a copy_i1 of that activation's predicate, [(n & 3) >= 5] = |0>
;       on every branch (B = 3 < K: rule 14's recursion clause has no B condition); 2^K = 16 of them in one call of the entry.
; Rotations: (Ry, n, th, 1).
; Expected (Ry(th) acts on every qubit of a rail, so each bit flips with probability s(th) = sin^2(th/2), independently):
;   quantum_depth_recursion(0, .5, 2): m = n & 3 is the two low bits of n, each flipped from 0 with s = 0.0612087.
;     chain(m, 2) is 2 for m = 0, -1 for m = 1, 3 for m = 2, -2 for m = 3 (the cut never binds: m <= 3, so at most
;     three activations of the _ctl clone run their base case or recurse with a predicate that can be 1). Measured: 2
;     with probability 0.881329, -1 with 0.057462, 3 with 0.057462, -2 with 0.003747. Every overflow rail reads 0.
; TRUE RECURSION WITH QUANTUM DEPTH, ONE CLONE (§1.4, rule 14). clang cannot loop-convert chain (the result is used
; non-associatively), so the clone recurses. chain's base-case test reads the rail n, and its recursive call sits in the
; arm n > 0: a call under a quantum predicate of a function on a call cycle, so the callee is the _ctl clone (rule 19),
; __cq_q_chain_10_ctl(pred, n, a): mask 10 at every depth (a + 1 stays classical), ONE clone whatever the depth, and no
; depth is passed. The entry calls chain with no predicate in scope: __cq_q_chain_10_b3(n & 3, a), the rule-18 clone of
; mask 10 with the bound 3 of its quantum argument (§1.4 _bN: the range fact of `and %4, 3` at the call site). chain's
; own symbol has no remaining use and is dropped (§1.4).
; The clone body (all three definitions share it). c = (n < 1) is the base-case flag. The recursive arm's pure code
; (n - 1; a + 1 is classical) is hoisted and computed unguarded (rule 9); the call stays in its arm, under NOT c: an X
; bracket on c in __cq_q_chain_10_b3 (rule 8: the false edge), and in the _ctl clone the conjunction f = p & !c in a
; fresh rail (and_i1 inside the X bracket), which is the callee's predicate. The call is not tail: a - r is computed
; after it (sub_lh, unguarded: r is read by nothing when c holds), and the phi merges by select on c (rule 9). The clone
; copies the merge out, uncomputes select and sub, zeroes r by the callee's twin __cq_q_chain_10_ctl_unc(pred, r, n - 1,
; a + 1) under the same predicate value (the same bracket, or f before its teardown), frees r, and uncomputes f, n - 1
; and c. The twin recomputes the same chain, XORs the merge out of the result rail and uncomputes; the caller frees the
; result. __cq_q_chain_10_b3 has no twin (nobody calls one, §1.4): its result is measured by the entry. chain touches
; no memory: no bus, no __cq_mem.
; THE ACTIVATION COUNTER AND THE CUT. chain lies on a call cycle, so it has one module-internal classical counter of its
; live _ctl activations, @__cq_act_chain (§1.4). __cq_q_chain_10_ctl and its twin read it on entry (the depth d), add
; 1, and subtract 1 at their return. A classical branch on d decides: while d < K = 4 [K] the body runs; at d = K the
; clone returns at once, its result a |0> rail, and a copy_i1 of its predicate into a fresh rail is the kept overflow
; predicate (rule 14: one per cut activation). __cq_q_chain_10_b3 is no _ctl clone and does not count, so the
; activations are: __cq_q_chain_10_b3 on m = n & 3, then _ctl at d = 0..3 on m - 1..m - 4, and the cut at d = 4, whose
; predicate is m >= 1 & .. & m >= 5 = [m >= 5], |0> since m <= 3. The host recursion gives every activation its own
; rails. Cost: each body calls the next level's clone and its twin, so 2^(d+1) bodies run at depth d and 2^K = 16
; forward activations reach the cut.
; THE CUT. Rule 14's recursion clause cuts at K whatever decides the depth and keeps one overflow copy per cut
; activation (no B condition: that is the loop clause); §1.4 _bN bounds serve loop cutoffs only, and the one _ctl clone
; carries none. The forward clone that a twin calls to recompute keeps its copy at the cut; the twin's own cut mints
; nothing and calls no gate (rule 14).
source_filename = "quantum_depth_recursion.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@__cq_act_chain = internal global i32 0, align 4    ; §1.4: the counter of chain's live _ctl activations (compiler state, not program memory)

define i32 @quantum_depth_recursion(i32 noundef %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 %0)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [register n]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i32(i32 %4, double %1)    ; IR: %4 = cq_theta_si32(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  %5 = call i32 @cq_template_and_i32_hl(i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: %5 = and i32 %4, 3
  %6 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_b3(i32 %5, i32 %2)    ; IR: %6 = call @chain(%5, %2): the clone of mask 10 (arg 0 quantum, bound 3), no predicate in scope
  call void @cq_template_and_i32_hl_unc(i32 %5, i32 %4, i32 3)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %5)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  %7 = call i32 @cqrt_measure_i32(i32 %6)    ; IR: %7 = cq_measure_si32(%6)  (the clone's copied-out result rail stays allocated)
  ret i32 %7    ; IR: ret i32 %7
}

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_b3(i32 %0, i32 %1) {    ; IR: chain(n quantum, a classical), no predicate
  %3 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: %3 = icmp slt i32 %0, 1  [base-case flag c; block %6 runs under NOT c]
  %4 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %0, i32 -1)    ; IR: %7 = add nsw i32 %0, -1  (pure arm code, hoisted: rule 9)
  %5 = add nsw i32 %1, 1    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %1, 1  (classical)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %3)    ; IR: bracket: block %6 runs under NOT %3
  %6 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl(i32 %3, i32 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: %9 = call @chain(%7, %8) under the predicate n > 0: the _ctl clone (rule 19: a call cycle), depth d = 0; rule 14: no bound
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %3)    ; IR: bracket
  %7 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 %1, i32 %6)    ; IR: %10 = sub nsw i32 %1, %9  (after the call: not a tail call)
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %3, i32 %1, i32 %7)    ; IR: %5 = phi [ %10, %6 ], [ %1, %2 ]: c ? a : %10
  %9 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %8, i32 %9)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [copy the result out]
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %8, i32 %3, i32 %1, i32 %7)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_lh_unc(i32 %7, i32 %1, i32 %6)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %7)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %3)    ; IR: bracket: the twin runs under the predicate value the call had
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %6, i32 %4, i32 %5)    ; IR: uncompute %9 (the _ctl clone's twin, depth d = 0)  §1.4: _ctl_unc(pred, outs.., args..)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %3)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %6)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %4, i32 %0, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %4)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %3, i32 %0, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %3)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  ret i32 %9    ; IR: ret i32 %5
}

define internal fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2) {    ; IR: chain(n quantum, a classical) under the predicate %0: ONE clone for every depth
  %4 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the activation's depth d = the live _ctl activations of chain
  %5 = add i32 %4, 1    ; IR: §1.4: this activation is live
  store i32 %5, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter adds 1
  %6 = icmp ult i32 %4, 4    ; IR: rule 14: the classical branch on entry, d below the cutoff  [K]
  br i1 %6, label %7, label %16    ; IR: rule 14: the body runs while d < K; at d = K the activation is cut

7:
  %8 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: %3 = icmp slt i32 %0, 1  [base-case flag c; block %6 runs under NOT c]
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %1, i32 -1)    ; IR: %7 = add nsw i32 %0, -1  (pure arm code, hoisted: rule 9)
  %10 = add nsw i32 %2, 1    ; IR: %8 = add nsw i32 %1, 1  (classical)
  %11 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: the predicate of block %6: f = pred & NOT c (rule 8: a conjunction into a fresh |0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %3
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %0, i32 %8, i32 %11)    ; IR: br i1 %3 not taken under the clone's predicate: f = pred & NOT c
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket
  %12 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl(i32 %11, i32 %9, i32 %10)    ; IR: %9 = call @chain(%7, %8) under f: the same clone, depth d + 1
  %13 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 %2, i32 %12)    ; IR: %10 = sub nsw i32 %1, %9  (after the call: not a tail call)
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %8, i32 %2, i32 %13)    ; IR: %5 = phi [ %10, %6 ], [ %1, %2 ]: c ? a : %10
  %15 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [result rail of the call]
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %14, i32 %15)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [copy the result out, unguarded (§1.4 _ctl): not |0> where pred = 0; the caller merges by select and its twin XORs the same value back]
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %14, i32 %8, i32 %2, i32 %13)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_lh_unc(i32 %13, i32 %2, i32 %12)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl_unc(i32 %11, i32 %12, i32 %9, i32 %10)    ; IR: uncompute %9 (the twin under the same f, depth d + 1)  §1.4: _ctl_unc(pred, outs.., args..)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %3
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %0, i32 %8, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute f (after its last controlled call)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %8)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %11)    ; IR: release the f rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %1, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %8, i32 %1, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %8)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  br label %19    ; IR: to the return

16:
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: rule 14: the cut activation's overflow rail (fresh |0>)
  call void @cqrt_copy_i1(i32 %0, i32 %17)    ; IR: rule 14: copy_i1 of the predicate: the KEPT overflow predicate (one per cut activation; [m >= 5] = |0> here)  rule 14: a forward clone called from a twin keeps its copy too
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i32(i32 0)    ; IR: rule 14: the cut activation returns at once, its result a |0> rail
  br label %19    ; IR: to the return

19:
  %20 = phi i32 [ %15, %7 ], [ %18, %16 ]    ; IR: ret i32 %5  (classical choice of the handle: body or cut)
  %21 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter at the return
  %22 = add i32 %21, -1    ; IR: §1.4: this activation ends
  store i32 %22, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter subtracts 1
  ret i32 %20    ; IR: ret i32 %5
}

define internal fastcc void @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl_unc(i32 %0, i32 %1, i32 %2, i32 %3) {    ; IR: twin of __cq_q_chain_10_ctl: (pred, out, n, a)  §1.4
  %5 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the activation's depth d (the twin counts like its clone)
  %6 = add i32 %5, 1    ; IR: §1.4: this activation is live
  store i32 %6, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter adds 1
  %7 = icmp ult i32 %5, 4    ; IR: rule 14: the twin makes the same cut  [K]
  br i1 %7, label %8, label %16    ; IR: rule 14: at d = K the result is |0> already: nothing to zero, no overflow rail (rule 14: the twin's cut mints nothing and calls no gate)

8:
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl(i32 %2, i32 1)    ; IR: recompute %3
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i32_hl(i32 %2, i32 -1)    ; IR: recompute %7
  %11 = add nsw i32 %3, 1    ; IR: %8  (classical)
  %12 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 false)    ; IR: recompute f = pred & NOT c (fresh |0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %9)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %3
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %0, i32 %9, i32 %12)    ; IR: f = pred & NOT c
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %9)    ; IR: bracket
  %13 = call fastcc i32 @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl(i32 %12, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: recompute %9 = call @chain(%7, %8) under f (the clone, depth d + 1)
  %14 = call i32 @cq_template_sub_i32_lh(i32 %3, i32 %13)    ; IR: recompute %10
  %15 = call i32 @cq_template_select_i32_lh(i32 %9, i32 %3, i32 %14)    ; IR: recompute %5
  call void @cqrt_copy_i32(i32 %15, i32 %1)    ; IR: ret i32 %5  [xor the result out of the result rail: |0>]
  call void @cq_template_select_i32_lh_unc(i32 %15, i32 %9, i32 %3, i32 %14)    ; IR: uncompute %5
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %15)    ; IR: release the %5 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_sub_i32_lh_unc(i32 %14, i32 %3, i32 %13)    ; IR: uncompute %10
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %14)    ; IR: release the %10 rail (|0>)
  call fastcc void @__cq_q_chain_10_ctl_unc(i32 %12, i32 %13, i32 %10, i32 %11)    ; IR: uncompute %9 (the twin under the same f, depth d + 1)
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %13)    ; IR: release the %9 rail (|0>)
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %9)    ; IR: bracket: NOT %3
  call void @cqrt_and_i1(i32 %0, i32 %9, i32 %12)    ; IR: uncompute f
  call void @cqrt_not_i1(i32 %9)    ; IR: bracket
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %12)    ; IR: release the f rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_add_i32_hl_unc(i32 %10, i32 %2, i32 -1)    ; IR: uncompute %7
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %10)    ; IR: release the %7 rail (|0>)
  call void @cq_template_icmp_slt_i32_hl_unc(i32 %9, i32 %2, i32 1)    ; IR: uncompute %3
  call void @cqrt_free(i32 %9)    ; IR: release the %3 rail (|0>)
  br label %16    ; IR: to the return

16:
  %17 = load i32, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter at the return
  %18 = add i32 %17, -1    ; IR: §1.4: this activation ends
  store i32 %18, ptr @__cq_act_chain, align 4    ; IR: §1.4: the counter subtracts 1
  ret void
}

name: 99_byte_tape
low:
; HAND-WRITTEN. Rules: 16, 20, 21, 5, 7, 8, 4, 2; §1.3 (the bus, __cq_mem, __cq_alloc); BACKEND_ABI §1.11.
; Checked: x (%8, measured -> %22, returned zero-extended).
; Clean: the zext of x (%9) and the predicate flag x > k (%19), uncomputed after the fputs entry; the |1> predicate seed
; of the fwrite entry (%17: never written, freed directly, rule 7); both load copies of stdout (%16, %20: un-copied
; right after their tape field, before their entry, the next memory version change: rule 5 sentence 1).
; Kept: the user register x (%8: rotated, measured, and the value rail of the kept store buf[0] = x); the rail x + 1
; (%10, the value rail of the kept store buf[1] = x + 1, rule 5 sentence 3); the seed 'z' (%13, the value rail of the
; kept store buf[2] = 'z', rule 7); the tape slots of those three stores (in the backend); the tape (%5) and its two
; write-only tape rails, the stream fields of the fwrite (%18) and fputs (%21) entries. Neither entry has a result rail
; (the program reads neither result: the bare form).
; Rotations: (Ry, x, th, 1).
; Expected: byte_tape(0, .5, 1): Ry(.5) acts on every qubit of the i8 rail x = 0, so each bit flips independently with
; probability s = sin^2(.25) = 0.061209; the measured value v is 0 with probability (1 - s)^8 = 0.603326. The output
; of the shot is the three bytes v, v + 1 (mod 256), 'z' (the fwrite), then "hi\n" iff v > 1, i.e. iff one of bits
; 1..7 of v is set: probability 1 - (1 - s)^7 = 0.357337. Both entries are deferred and performed at the end of the
; shot in sequence order; the bytes of buf the backend captured at the fwrite entry are copies of x and x + 1, so the
; printed bytes agree with the returned v on every shot.
; BUF (rule 20). The alloca [3 x i8] has stores of tainted values and a call among its users, so it is bus-resident
; (rule 20 b): __cq_alloc(3, 1) at the alloca's program point (align 1, the alloca's), no alloca remains, and the
; lifetime markers are dropped (rule 16). Its three byte stores are bus stores at classical addresses
; (qram_store_i8_hl; the getelementptrs have nothing tainted and stay, the address is the ptrtoint): buf[0] = x and
; buf[1] = x + 1 with their rails as values, buf[2] = 'z' with the seed alloc_i8(122). Every one is a KEPT store (rule 5
; sentence 3): its tape slot stays and so does its value rail, so the rail x + 1 is never uncomputed.
; STDOUT (rules 20, 21). `stdout` is `load ptr, ptr @__stdoutp`: @__stdoutp is a global that is not constant, so the
; load is a bus load at its host address ptrtoint (ptr @__stdoutp to i64) (nothing is allocated or seeded for it) and
; its result is a rail, the stream's address (a 64-bit rail, rule 21), although the cells are HOST. The load in block
; %13 lies under the quantum predicate x > k and is the _hl_controlled load; its un-copy takes the same control.
; HOST EFFECTS (rule 16). fwrite and fputs are stream calls with pointer arguments, so neither is an ordinary host
; call: each is ONE effect entry on the function's tape (one tape_alloc at entry). Its fields are its arguments in
; order: a pointer is its address (buf's run-time i64 and the constant @.str as _lit fields; the stream rail as a
; tape_write_i64 field), the classical sizes as i64 _lit fields. A buffer or string is never expanded into fields:
; what the backend reads from buf (two QUANTUM cells, one HOST cell holding 'z') and from @.str is BACKEND_ABI §1.11's
; capture at the entry. fwrite has no predicate in scope: a cqrt_alloc_i1(true) seed, freed right after the effect
; call. fputs is in block %13: its entry is under the flag x > k, which is uncomputed after the entry like any flag.
; SPEC GAP (rule 16, effect entry name): the -O1 callees are @"\01_fwrite" and @"\01_fputs" (Darwin's asm-label
; spellings), and "the callee's symbol name" does not say which spelling. Used: the C identifier the callee is declared
; by, i.e. the LLVM name with the leading "\01" asm-label marker and the target's global symbol prefix ("_" on Mach-O)
; removed: @.cq.effect.fwrite = "fwrite", @.cq.effect.fputs = "fputs".
source_filename = "byte_tape.c"
target datalayout = "e-m:o-p270:32:32-p271:32:32-p272:64:64-i64:64-i128:128-f80:128-n8:16:32:64-S128"
target triple = "x86_64-apple-macosx16.0.0"

@__stdoutp = external local_unnamed_addr global ptr, align 8    ; IR: @__stdoutp  (stdout: a host global, on the bus at its host address)
@.str = private unnamed_addr constant [4 x i8] c"hi\0A\00", align 1    ; IR: @.str
@.cq.effect.fwrite = private unnamed_addr constant [7 x i8] c"fwrite\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for fwrite (a host string): @.cq.effect.<name>, one per host callee, after the module's own globals  ; SPEC GAP: name of @"\01_fwrite" (header)
@.cq.effect.fputs = private unnamed_addr constant [6 x i8] c"fputs\00", align 1    ; IR: effect entry name for fputs  ; SPEC GAP: name of @"\01_fputs" (header)

define i32 @byte_tape(i8 noundef zeroext %0, double noundef %1, i32 noundef %2) {
  %4 = call i32 @__cq_mem()    ; IR: the bus m (once, at function entry)
  %5 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_alloc()    ; IR: the function's tape: one per function that records an entry, at function entry (the fwrite and fputs entries, one event sequence)
  %6 = call ptr @__cq_alloc(i64 3, i64 1)    ; IR: %4 = alloca [3 x i8], align 1: buf is bus-resident (tainted stores, a call argument): a zeroed block, no alloca remains (llvm.lifetime.start is dropped)
  %7 = ptrtoint ptr %6 to i64    ; IR: %4 as its run-time address: the _hl operand of buf[0] and the fwrite buffer field (classical)
  %8 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 %0)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [register x]
  call void @cqrt_ry_i8(i32 %8, double %1)    ; IR: %5 = cq_theta_ui8(%0, %1)  [Ry]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %4, i64 %7, i32 %8)    ; IR: store i8 %5, ptr %4: buf[0] = x  (kept store at a classical address: tape slot and value rail x stay, no _unc)
  %9 = call i32 @cq_template_zext_i8_to_i32(i32 %8)    ; IR: %7 = zext i8 %5 to i32
  %10 = call i32 @cq_template_add_i8_hl(i32 %8, i8 1)    ; IR: %8 = add i8 %5, 1
  %11 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 1    ; IR: %6 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %4, i64 1  [nothing tainted: the gep stays]
  %12 = ptrtoint ptr %11 to i64    ; IR: store i8 %8, ptr %6  [the classical address as its run-time i64]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %4, i64 %12, i32 %10)    ; IR: store i8 %8, ptr %6: buf[1] = x + 1  (kept store: tape slot and value rail %8 stay, so %8 is never uncomputed)
  %13 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i8(i8 122)    ; IR: store i8 122, ptr %9: the classical value as a seed rail (rule 7), kept with its store
  %14 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %6, i64 2    ; IR: %9 = getelementptr inbounds i8, ptr %4, i64 2  [nothing tainted: the gep stays]
  %15 = ptrtoint ptr %14 to i64    ; IR: store i8 122, ptr %9  [the classical address as its run-time i64]
  call void @cqrt_qram_store_i8_hl(i32 %4, i64 %15, i32 %13)    ; IR: store i8 122, ptr %9: buf[2] = 'z'  (kept store; classical-valued address and content: the cell stays HOST)
  %16 = call i32 @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl(i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @__stdoutp to i64))    ; IR: %10 = load ptr, ptr @__stdoutp: stdout  (a bus load at the global's host address: a rail, the stream's address)
  %17 = call i32 @cqrt_alloc_i1(i1 true)    ; IR: %11 = fwrite(%4, 1, 3, %10): no predicate in scope, the |1> seed
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i64_lit(i32 %5, i64 %7)    ; IR: %11 = fwrite(%4, ...): argument 0, the buffer: a pointer is its address, classical: a _lit field (the buffer is not expanded into fields)
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i64_lit(i32 %5, i64 1)    ; IR: %11 = fwrite(..., 1, ...): argument 1, the size: a classical i64 _lit field
  call void @cqrt_tape_write_i64_lit(i32 %5, i64 3)    ; IR: %11 = fwrite(..., 3, ...): argument 2, the count: a classical i64 _lit field
  %18 = call i32 @cqrt_tape_write_i64(i32 %5, i32 %16)    ; IR: %11 = fwrite(..., %10): argument 3, the stream: the address rail copied onto a fresh tape rail (kept)
  call void @cqrt_qram_load_i64_hl_unc(i32 %16, i32 %4, i64 ptrtoint (ptr @__stdoutp to i64))    ; IR: un-copy %10 (rule 5 sentence 1: its last reader is the tape field, before the entry, the next memory version change)
